items.quote: A crane is a machine for lifting and lowering a load and moving it horizontally, with the hoisting mechanism an integral part of the machine.
items.statement: A crane is a machine for lifting and lowering a load and moving it horizontally, with the hoisting mechanism an integral part of the machine.

items.quote: Cranes whether fixed or mobile are driven manually or by power.
items.statement: Cranes, whether fixed or mobile, are driven manually or by power.

items.quote: An automatic crane is a crane which when activated operates through a preset cycle or cycles.
items.statement: An automatic crane is a crane which, when activated, operates through a preset cycle or cycles.

items.quote: A cab-operated crane is a crane controlled by an operator in a cab located on the bridge or trolley.
items.statement: A cab-operated crane is a crane controlled by an operator in a cab located on the bridge or trolley.

items.quote: Cantilever gantry crane means a gantry or semigantry crane in which the bridge girders or trusses extend transversely beyond the crane runway on one or both sides.
items.statement: A cantilever gantry crane is a gantry or semigantry crane in which the bridge girders or trusses extend transversely beyond the crane runway on one or both sides.

items.quote: Floor-operated crane means a crane which is pendant or nonconductive rope controlled by an operator on the floor or an independent platform.
items.statement: A floor-operated crane is a crane that is pendant or nonconductive rope controlled by an operator on the floor or an independent platform.

items.quote: Gantry crane means a crane similar to an overhead crane except that the bridge for carrying the trolley or trolleys is rigidly supported on two or more legs running on fixed rails or other runway.
items.statement: A gantry crane is similar to an overhead crane except that the bridge carrying the trolley or trolleys is rigidly supported on two or more legs running on fixed rails or other runway.

items.quote: Hot metal handling crane means an overhead crane used for transporting or pouring molten material.
items.statement: A hot metal handling crane is an overhead crane used for transporting or pouring molten material.

items.quote: Overhead crane means a crane with a movable bridge carrying a movable or fixed hoisting mechanism and traveling on an overhead fixed runway structure.
items.statement: An overhead crane is a crane with a movable bridge carrying a movable or fixed hoisting mechanism and traveling on an overhead fixed runway structure.

items.quote: Power-operated crane means a crane whose mechanism is driven by electric, air, hydraulic, or internal combustion means.
items.statement: A power-operated crane is a crane whose mechanism is driven by electric, air, hydraulic, or internal combustion means.

items.quote: A pulpit-operated crane is a crane operated from a fixed operator station not attached to the crane.
items.statement: A pulpit-operated crane is a crane operated from a fixed operator station not attached to the crane.

items.quote: A remote-operated crane is a crane controlled by an operator not in a pulpit or in the cab attached to the crane, by any method other than pendant or rope control.
items.statement: A remote-operated crane is controlled by an operator not in a pulpit or in the cab attached to the crane, by any method other than pendant or rope control.

items.quote: A semigantry crane is a gantry crane with one end of the bridge rigidly supported on one or more legs that run on a fixed rail or runway, the other end of the bridge being supported by a truck running on an elevated rail or runway.
items.statement: A semigantry crane is a gantry crane with one end of the bridge rigidly supported on one or more legs running on a fixed rail or runway, and the other end supported by a truck running on an elevated rail or runway.

items.quote: Storage bridge crane means a gantry type crane of long span usually used for bulk storage of material; the bridge girders or trusses are rigidly or nonrigidly supported on one or more legs.
items.statement: A storage bridge crane is a long-span gantry type crane usually used for bulk storage of material, with bridge girders or trusses rigidly or nonrigidly supported on one or more legs.

items.quote: It may have one or more fixed or hinged cantilever ends.
items.statement: A storage bridge crane may have one or more fixed or hinged cantilever ends.

items.quote: Wall crane means a crane having a jib with or without trolley and supported from a side wall or line of columns of a building.
items.statement: A wall crane is a crane having a jib, with or without trolley, supported from a side wall or line of columns of a building.

items.quote: It is a traveling type and operates on a runway attached to the side wall or columns.
items.statement: A wall crane is a traveling type that operates on a runway attached to the side wall or columns.

items.quote: Appointed means assigned specific responsibilities by the employer or the employer's representative.
items.statement: Appointed means assigned specific responsibilities by the employer or the employer's representative.

items.quote: ANSI means the American National Standards Institute.
items.statement: ANSI means the American National Standards Institute.

items.quote: An auxiliary hoist is a supplemental hoisting unit of lighter capacity and usually higher speed than provided for the main hoist.
items.statement: An auxiliary hoist is a supplemental hoisting unit of lighter capacity and usually higher speed than provided for the main hoist.

items.quote: A brake is a device used for retarding or stopping motion by friction or power means.
items.statement: A brake is a device used for retarding or stopping motion by friction or power means.

items.quote: A drag brake is a brake which provides retarding force without external control.
items.statement: A drag brake is a brake that provides retarding force without external control.

items.quote: A holding brake is a brake that automatically prevents motion when power is off.
items.statement: A holding brake is a brake that automatically prevents motion when power is off.

items.quote: Bridge means that part of a crane consisting of girders, trucks, end ties, footwalks, and drive mechanism which carries the trolley or trolleys.
items.statement: The bridge is the part of a crane, consisting of girders, trucks, end ties, footwalks, and drive mechanism, which carries the trolley or trolleys.

items.quote: Bridge travel means the crane movement in a direction parallel to the crane runway.
items.statement: Bridge travel is crane movement in a direction parallel to the crane runway.

items.quote: A bumper (buffer) is an energy absorbing device for reducing impact when a moving crane or trolley reaches the end of its permitted travel; or when two moving cranes or trolleys come in contact.
items.statement: A bumper (buffer) is an energy absorbing device for reducing impact when a moving crane or trolley reaches the end of its permitted travel, or when two moving cranes or trolleys come in contact.

items.quote: The cab is the operator's compartment on a crane.
items.statement: The cab is the operator's compartment on a crane.

items.quote: Clearance means the distance from any part of the crane to a point of the nearest obstruction.
items.statement: Clearance is the distance from any part of the crane to a point of the nearest obstruction.

items.quote: Collectors current are contacting devices for collecting current from runway or bridge conductors.
items.statement: Current collectors are contacting devices for collecting current from runway or bridge conductors.

items.quote: Conductors, bridge are the electrical conductors located along the bridge structure of a crane to provide power to the trolley.
items.statement: Bridge conductors are the electrical conductors located along the bridge structure of a crane to provide power to the trolley.

items.quote: Conductors, runway (main) are the electrical conductors located along a crane runway to provide power to the crane.
items.statement: Runway (main) conductors are the electrical conductors located along a crane runway to provide power to the crane.

items.quote: The control braking means is a method of controlling crane motor speed when in an overhauling condition.
items.statement: Control braking means is a method of controlling crane motor speed when in an overhauling condition.

items.quote: Countertorque means a method of control by which the power to the motor is reversed to develop torque in the opposite direction.
items.statement: Countertorque is a method of control in which power to the motor is reversed to develop torque in the opposite direction.

items.quote: Dynamic means a method of controlling crane motor speeds when in the overhauling condition to provide a retarding force.
items.statement: Dynamic means a method of controlling crane motor speeds in the overhauling condition to provide a retarding force.

items.quote: Regenerative means a form of dynamic braking in which the electrical energy generated is fed back into the power system.
items.statement: Regenerative means a form of dynamic braking in which the electrical energy generated is fed back into the power system.

items.quote: Mechanical means a method of control by friction.
items.statement: Mechanical means a method of control by friction.

items.quote: Controller, spring return means a controller which when released will return automatically to a neutral position.
items.statement: A spring return controller is a controller which, when released, returns automatically to a neutral position.

items.quote: Designated means selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.
items.statement: Designated means selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.

items.quote: A drift point means a point on a travel motion controller which releases the brake while the motor is not energized.
items.statement: A drift point is a point on a travel motion controller which releases the brake while the motor is not energized.

items.quote: This allows for coasting before the brake is set.
items.statement: A drift point allows for coasting before the brake is set.

items.quote: The drum is the cylindrical member around which the ropes are wound for raising or lowering the load.
items.statement: The drum is the cylindrical member around which the ropes are wound for raising or lowering the load.

items.quote: An equalizer is a device which compensates for unequal length or stretch of a rope.
items.statement: An equalizer is a device that compensates for unequal length or stretch of a rope.

items.quote: Exposed means capable of being contacted inadvertently.
items.statement: Exposed means capable of being contacted inadvertently.

items.quote: Applied to hazardous objects not adequately guarded or isolated.
items.statement: The term exposed is applied to hazardous objects not adequately guarded or isolated.

items.quote: Fail-safe means a provision designed to automatically stop or safely control any motion in which a malfunction occurs.
items.statement: Fail-safe means a provision designed to automatically stop or safely control any motion in which a malfunction occurs.

items.quote: Footwalk means the walkway with handrail, attached to the bridge or trolley for access purposes.
items.statement: A footwalk is the walkway with handrail, attached to the bridge or trolley for access purposes.

items.quote: A hoist is an apparatus which may be a part of a crane, exerting a force for lifting or lowering.
items.statement: A hoist is an apparatus, which may be part of a crane, that exerts a force for lifting or lowering.

items.quote: Hoist chain means the load bearing chain in a hoist.
items.statement: Hoist chain means the load bearing chain in a hoist.

items.quote: Chain properties do not conform to those shown in ANSI B30.9-1971, Safety Code for Slings.
items.statement: A note states that chain properties do not conform to those shown in ANSI B30.9-1971, Safety Code for Slings.

items.quote: Hoist motion means that motion of a crane which raises and lowers a load.
items.statement: Hoist motion is the motion of a crane which raises and lowers a load.

items.quote: Load means the total superimposed weight on the load block or hook.
items.statement: Load means the total superimposed weight on the load block or hook.

items.quote: The load block is the assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, bearing, sheaves, pins, and frame suspended by the hoisting rope.
items.statement: The load block is the assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, bearing, sheaves, pins, and frame suspended by the hoisting rope.

items.quote: Magnet means an electromagnetic device carried on a crane hook to pick up loads magnetically.
items.statement: A magnet is an electromagnetic device carried on a crane hook to pick up loads magnetically.

items.quote: Main hoist means the hoist mechanism provided for lifting the maximum rated load.
items.statement: The main hoist is the hoist mechanism provided for lifting the maximum rated load.

items.quote: A man trolley is a trolley having an operator's cab attached thereto.
items.statement: A man trolley is a trolley having an operator's cab attached to it.

items.quote: Rated load means the maximum load for which a crane or individual hoist is designed and built by the manufacturer and shown on the equipment nameplate(s).
items.statement: Rated load is the maximum load for which a crane or individual hoist is designed and built by the manufacturer and shown on the equipment nameplate(s).

items.quote: Rope refers to wire rope, unless otherwise specified.
items.statement: Rope refers to wire rope unless otherwise specified.

items.quote: Running sheave means a sheave which rotates as the load block is raised or lowered.
items.statement: A running sheave is a sheave which rotates as the load block is raised or lowered.

items.quote: Runway means an assembly of rails, beams, girders, brackets, and framework on which the crane or trolley travels.
items.statement: A runway is an assembly of rails, beams, girders, brackets, and framework on which the crane or trolley travels.

items.quote: Side pull means that portion of the hoist pull acting horizontally when the hoist lines are not operated vertically.
items.statement: Side pull is the portion of the hoist pull acting horizontally when the hoist lines are not operated vertically.

items.quote: Span means the horizontal distance center to center of runway rails.
items.statement: Span is the horizontal distance center to center of runway rails.

items.quote: Standby crane means a crane which is not in regular service but which is used occasionally or intermittently as required.
items.statement: A standby crane is a crane not in regular service but used occasionally or intermittently as required.

items.quote: A stop is a device to limit travel of a trolley or crane bridge.
items.statement: A stop is a device to limit travel of a trolley or crane bridge.

items.quote: This device normally is attached to a fixed structure and normally does not have energy absorbing ability.
items.statement: A stop is normally attached to a fixed structure and normally does not have energy absorbing ability.

items.quote: A switch is a device for making, breaking, or for changing the connections in an electric circuit.
items.statement: A switch is a device for making, breaking, or changing the connections in an electric circuit.

items.quote: An emergency stop switch is a manually or automatically operated electric switch to cut off electric power independently of the regular operating controls.
items.statement: An emergency stop switch is a manually or automatically operated electric switch that cuts off electric power independently of the regular operating controls.

items.quote: A limit switch is a switch which is operated by some part or motion of a power-driven machine or equipment to alter the electric circuit associated with the machine or equipment.
items.statement: A limit switch is operated by some part or motion of a power-driven machine or equipment to alter the electric circuit associated with that machine or equipment.

items.quote: A main switch is a switch controlling the entire power supply to the crane.
items.statement: A main switch is a switch controlling the entire power supply to the crane.

items.quote: A master switch is a switch which dominates the operation of contactors, relays, or other remotely operated devices.
items.statement: A master switch is a switch which dominates the operation of contactors, relays, or other remotely operated devices.

items.quote: The trolley is the unit which travels on the bridge rails and carries the hoisting mechanism.
items.statement: The trolley is the unit which travels on the bridge rails and carries the hoisting mechanism.

items.quote: Trolley travel means the trolley movement at right angles to the crane runway.
items.statement: Trolley travel is trolley movement at right angles to the crane runway.

items.quote: Truck means the unit consisting of a frame, wheels, bearings, and axles which supports the bridge girders or trolleys.
items.statement: A truck is the unit consisting of a frame, wheels, bearings, and axles which supports the bridge girders or trolleys.

items.quote: This section applies to overhead and gantry cranes, including semigantry, cantilever gantry, wall cranes, storage bridge cranes, and others having the same fundamental characteristics.
items.statement: §1910.179 applies to overhead and gantry cranes, including semigantry, cantilever gantry, wall cranes, storage bridge cranes, and others with the same fundamental characteristics.

items.quote: All new overhead and gantry cranes constructed and installed on or after August 31, 1971, shall meet the design specifications of the American National Standard Safety Code for Overhead and Gantry Cranes, ANSI B30.2.0-1967
items.statement: All new overhead and gantry cranes constructed and installed on or after August 31, 1971, must meet the design specifications of ANSI B30.2.0-1967.

items.quote: Cranes may be modified and rerated provided such modifications and the supporting structure are checked thoroughly for the new rated load by a qualified engineer or the equipment manufacturer.
items.statement: Cranes may be modified and rerated only if a qualified engineer or the equipment manufacturer thoroughly checks the modifications and the supporting structure for the new rated load.

items.quote: The crane shall be tested in accordance with paragraph (k)(2) of this section.
items.statement: A modified and rerated crane must be tested in accordance with paragraph (k)(2).

items.quote: New rated load shall be displayed in accordance with subparagraph (5) of this paragraph.
items.statement: The new rated load of a modified and rerated crane must be displayed in accordance with subparagraph (5).

items.quote: Outdoor storage bridges shall be provided with automatic rail clamps.
items.statement: Outdoor storage bridges must have automatic rail clamps.

items.quote: A wind-indicating device shall be provided which will give a visible or audible alarm to the bridge operator at a predetermined wind velocity.
items.statement: A wind-indicating device must be provided that gives the bridge operator a visible or audible alarm at a predetermined wind velocity.

items.quote: If the clamps act on the rail heads, any beads or weld flash on the rail heads shall be ground off.
items.statement: If rail clamps act on the rail heads, any beads or weld flash on the rail heads must be ground off.

items.quote: The rated load of the crane shall be plainly marked on each side of the crane
items.statement: The crane's rated load must be plainly marked on each side of the crane.

items.quote: if the crane has more than one hoisting unit, each hoist shall have its rated load marked on it or its load block and this marking shall be clearly legible from the ground or floor.
items.statement: If a crane has more than one hoisting unit, each hoist must have its rated load marked on it or its load block, clearly legible from the ground or floor.

items.quote: Minimum clearance of 3 inches overhead
items.statement: A minimum overhead clearance of 3 inches must be provided and maintained between the crane and obstructions, in conformity with CMAA Specification No. 61.

items.quote: Minimum clearance of 3 inches overhead and 2 inches laterally shall be provided and maintained between crane and obstructions
items.statement: A minimum lateral clearance of 2 inches must be provided and maintained between the crane and obstructions, in conformity with CMAA Specification No. 61.

items.quote: Where passageways or walkways are provided obstructions shall not be placed so that safety of personnel will be jeopardized by movements of the crane.
items.statement: Where passageways or walkways are provided, obstructions must not be placed so that crane movements jeopardize personnel safety.

items.quote: If the runways of two cranes are parallel, and there are no intervening walls or structure, there shall be adequate clearance provided and maintained between the two bridges.
items.statement: If two cranes' runways are parallel with no intervening walls or structure, adequate clearance must be provided and maintained between the two bridges.

items.quote: Only designated personnel shall be permitted to operate a crane covered by this section.
items.statement: Only designated personnel may be permitted to operate a crane covered by this section.

items.quote: The general arrangement of the cab and the location of control and protective equipment shall be such that all operating handles are within convenient reach of the operator when facing the area to be served by the load hook, or while facing the direction of travel of the cab.
items.statement: The cab arrangement and the location of control and protective equipment must put all operating handles within the operator's convenient reach when facing the area served by the load hook or the cab's direction of travel.

items.quote: The arrangement shall allow the operator a full view of the load hook in all positions.
items.statement: The cab arrangement must allow the operator a full view of the load hook in all positions.

items.quote: The cab shall be located to afford a minimum of 3 inches clearance from all fixed structures within its area of possible movement.
items.statement: The cab must be located to give at least 3 inches of clearance from all fixed structures within its area of possible movement.

items.quote: Access to the car and/or bridge walkway shall be by a conveniently placed fixed ladder, stairs, or platform requiring no step over any gap exceeding 12 inches (30 cm).
items.statement: Access to the car and/or bridge walkway must be by a conveniently placed fixed ladder, stairs, or platform that requires no step over any gap exceeding 12 inches (30 cm).

items.quote: Fixed ladders must comply with subpart D of this part.
items.statement: Fixed ladders for crane access must comply with subpart D.

items.quote: Carbon tetrachloride extinguishers shall not be used.
items.statement: Carbon tetrachloride fire extinguishers must not be used.

items.quote: Light in the cab shall be sufficient to enable the operator to see clearly enough to perform his work.
items.statement: Cab lighting must be sufficient for the operator to see clearly enough to perform his work.

items.quote: If sufficient headroom is available on cab-operated cranes, a footwalk shall be provided on the drive side along the entire length of the bridge of all cranes having the trolley running on the top of the girders.
items.statement: If sufficient headroom is available on cab-operated cranes, a footwalk must be provided on the drive side along the entire bridge length of all cranes whose trolley runs on top of the girders.

items.quote: Where footwalks are located in no case shall less than 48 inches of headroom be provided.
items.statement: Where footwalks are located, headroom must in no case be less than 48 inches.

items.quote: Footwalks shall be of rigid construction
items.statement: Footwalks must be of rigid construction.

items.quote: designed to sustain a distributed load of at least 50 pounds per square foot.
items.statement: Footwalks must be designed to sustain a distributed load of at least 50 pounds per square foot.

items.quote: Footwalks shall have a walking surface of antislip type.
items.statement: Footwalks must have an antislip walking surface.

items.quote: Wood will meet this requirement.
items.statement: A note states that wood will meet the requirement, appearing after the antislip footwalk surface provision.

items.quote: The inner edge shall extend at least to the line of the outside edge of the lower cover plate or flange of the girder.
items.statement: The inner edge of a footwalk must extend at least to the line of the outside edge of the girder's lower cover plate or flange.

items.quote: Toeboards and handrails must comply with subpart D of this part.
items.statement: Footwalk toeboards and handrails must comply with subpart D.

items.quote: Gantry cranes shall be provided with ladders or stairways extending from the ground to the footwalk or cab platform.
items.statement: Gantry cranes must have ladders or stairways extending from the ground to the footwalk or cab platform.

items.quote: Stairways shall be equipped with rigid and substantial metal handrails.
items.statement: Stairways must have rigid and substantial metal handrails.

items.quote: Walking surfaces shall be of an antislip type.
items.statement: Under the ladders and stairways provision, walking surfaces must be of an antislip type.

items.quote: Ladders shall be permanently and securely fastened in place
items.statement: Ladders must be permanently and securely fastened in place.

items.quote: constructed in compliance with subpart D of this part.
items.statement: Ladders must be constructed in compliance with subpart D.

items.quote: Stops shall be provided at the limits of travel of the trolley.
items.statement: Stops must be provided at the limits of trolley travel.

items.quote: Stops shall be fastened to resist forces applied when contacted.
items.statement: Trolley stops must be fastened to resist the forces applied when contacted.

items.quote: A stop engaging the tread of the wheel shall be of a height at least equal to the radius of the wheel.
items.statement: A trolley stop that engages the wheel tread must be at least as high as the wheel's radius.

items.quote: A crane shall be provided with bumpers or other automatic means providing equivalent effect
items.statement: A crane must have bumpers or other automatic means of equivalent effect, except as excepted for certain slow-travel, restricted-operation or similar conditions.

items.quote: unless the crane travels at a slow rate of speed and has a faster deceleration rate due to the use of sleeve bearings, or is not operated near the ends of bridge and trolley travel, or is restricted to a limited distance by the nature of the crane operation and there is no hazard of striking any object in this limited distance, or is used in similar operating conditions.
items.statement: Crane bumpers or equivalent means are not required if the crane travels slowly and has a faster deceleration rate due to sleeve bearings, is not operated near the ends of bridge and trolley travel, is restricted by the nature of the operation to a limited distance with no hazard of striking any object in it, or is used in similar operating conditions.

items.quote: The bumpers shall be capable of stopping the crane (not including the lifted load) at an average rate of deceleration not to exceed 3 ft/s/s when traveling in either direction at 20 percent of the rated load speed.
items.statement: Bridge bumpers must be able to stop the crane (not including the lifted load) at an average deceleration not exceeding 3 ft/s/s when traveling in either direction at 20 percent of rated load speed.

items.quote: The bumpers shall have sufficient energy absorbing capacity to stop the crane when traveling at a speed of at least 40 percent of rated load speed.
items.statement: Bridge bumpers must have enough energy-absorbing capacity to stop the crane traveling at a speed of at least 40 percent of rated load speed.

items.quote: The bumper shall be so mounted that there is no direct shear on bolts.
items.statement: A bridge bumper must be mounted so that there is no direct shear on bolts.

items.quote: Bumpers shall be so designed and installed as to minimize parts falling from the crane in case of breakage.
items.statement: Bridge bumpers must be designed and installed to minimize parts falling from the crane if breakage occurs.

items.quote: A trolley shall be provided with bumpers or other automatic means of equivalent effect
items.statement: A trolley must have bumpers or other automatic means of equivalent effect, except as excepted for certain slow-travel, restricted-operation or similar conditions.

items.quote: unless the trolley travels at a slow rate of speed, or is not operated near the ends of bridge and trolley travel, or is restricted to a limited distance of the runway and there is no hazard of striking any object in this limited distance, or is used in similar operating conditions.
items.statement: Trolley bumpers or equivalent means are not required if the trolley travels slowly, is not operated near the ends of bridge and trolley travel, is restricted to a limited runway distance with no hazard of striking any object in it, or is used in similar operating conditions.

items.quote: The bumpers shall be capable of stopping the trolley (not including the lifted load) at an average rate of deceleration not to exceed 4.7 ft/s/s when traveling in either direction at one-third of the rated load speed.
items.statement: Trolley bumpers must be able to stop the trolley (not including the lifted load) at an average deceleration not exceeding 4.7 ft/s/s when traveling in either direction at one-third of rated load speed.

items.quote: When more than one trolley is operated on the same bridge, each shall be equipped with bumpers or equivalent on their adjacent ends.
items.statement: When more than one trolley is operated on the same bridge, each must have bumpers or equivalent on their adjacent ends.

items.quote: Bumpers or equivalent shall be designed and installed to minimize parts falling from the trolley in case of age.
items.statement: Trolley bumpers or equivalent must be designed and installed to minimize parts falling from the trolley "in case of age" (the source's wording).

items.quote: Bridge trucks shall be equipped with sweeps which extend below the top of the rail and project in front of the truck wheels.
items.statement: Bridge trucks must have rail sweeps that extend below the top of the rail and project in front of the truck wheels.

items.quote: If hoisting ropes run near enough to other parts to make fouling or chafing possible, guards shall be installed to prevent this condition.
items.statement: If hoisting ropes run close enough to other parts to make fouling or chafing possible, guards must be installed to prevent it.

items.quote: A guard shall be provided to prevent contact between bridge conductors and hoisting ropes if they could come into contact.
items.statement: If bridge conductors and hoisting ropes could come into contact, a guard must be provided to prevent it.

items.quote: Exposed moving parts such as gears, set screws, projecting keys, chains, chain sprockets, and reciprocating components which might constitute a hazard under normal operating conditions shall be guarded.
items.statement: Exposed moving parts, such as gears, set screws, projecting keys, chains, chain sprockets and reciprocating components, that might be a hazard under normal operating conditions must be guarded.

items.quote: Guards shall be securely fastened.
items.statement: Guards for moving parts must be securely fastened.

items.quote: Each guard shall be capable of supporting without permanent distortion the weight of a 200-pound person unless the guard is located where it is impossible for a person to step on it.
items.statement: Each moving-part guard must support the weight of a 200-pound person without permanent distortion, unless it is located where a person cannot step on it.

items.quote: Each independent hoisting unit of a crane shall be equipped with at least one self-setting brake, hereafter referred to as a holding brake, applied directly to the motor shaft or some part of the gear train.
items.statement: Each independent hoisting unit of a crane must have at least one self-setting brake (holding brake) applied directly to the motor shaft or some part of the gear train.

items.quote: Each independent hoisting unit of a crane, except worm-geared hoists, the angle of whose worm is such as to prevent the load from accelerating in the lowering direction shall, in addition to a holding brake, be equipped with control braking means to prevent overspeeding.
items.statement: In addition to a holding brake, each independent hoisting unit of a crane must have control braking means to prevent overspeeding, except worm-geared hoists whose worm angle prevents the load from accelerating in the lowering direction.

items.quote: 125 percent when used with a control braking means other than mechanical.
items.statement: A hoist motor holding brake used with a control braking means other than mechanical must have at least 125 percent of full load hoisting torque at the point where the brake is applied.

items.quote: 100 percent when used in conjunction with a mechanical control braking means.
items.statement: A hoist motor holding brake used with a mechanical control braking means must have at least 100 percent of full load hoisting torque at the point where the brake is applied.

items.quote: 100 percent each if two holding brakes are provided.
items.statement: If two holding brakes are provided for a hoist motor, each must have at least 100 percent of full load hoisting torque at the point where the brake is applied.

items.quote: Holding brakes on hoists shall have ample thermal capacity for the frequency of operation required by the service.
items.statement: Holding brakes on hoists must have ample thermal capacity for the frequency of operation required by the service.

items.quote: Holding brakes on hoists shall be applied automatically when power is removed.
items.statement: Holding brakes on hoists must be applied automatically when power is removed.

items.quote: Where necessary holding brakes shall be provided with adjustment means to compensate for wear.
items.statement: Where necessary, holding brakes must have adjustment means to compensate for wear.

items.quote: The wearing surface of all holding-brake drums or discs shall be smooth.
items.statement: The wearing surface of all holding-brake drums or discs must be smooth.

items.quote: Each independent hoisting unit of a crane handling hot metal and having power control braking means shall be equipped with at least two holding brakes.
items.statement: Each independent hoisting unit of a crane that handles hot metal and has power control braking means must have at least two holding brakes.

items.quote: A power control braking means such as regenerative, dynamic or countertorque braking, or a mechanically controlled braking means shall be capable of maintaining safe lowering speeds of rated loads.
items.statement: A power control braking means (such as regenerative, dynamic or countertorque braking) or a mechanically controlled braking means must be capable of maintaining safe lowering speeds of rated loads.

items.quote: The control braking means shall have ample thermal capacity for the frequency of operation required by service.
items.statement: The control braking means must have ample thermal capacity for the frequency of operation required by service.

items.quote: Foot-operated brakes shall not require an applied force of more than 70 pounds to develop manufacturer's rated brake torque.
items.statement: Foot-operated trolley and bridge brakes must not require more than 70 pounds of applied force to develop the manufacturer's rated brake torque.

items.quote: Brakes may be applied by mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, or gravity means.
items.statement: Trolley and bridge brakes may be applied by mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, or gravity means.

items.quote: Where necessary brakes shall be provided with adjustment means to compensate for wear.
items.statement: Where necessary, trolley and bridge brakes must have adjustment means to compensate for wear.

items.quote: The wearing surface of all brakedrums or discs shall be smooth.
items.statement: The wearing surface of all trolley and bridge brake drums or discs must be smooth.

items.quote: All foot-brake pedals shall be constructed so that the operator's foot will not easily slip off the pedal.
items.statement: All foot-brake pedals must be constructed so that the operator's foot will not easily slip off.

items.quote: Foot-operated brakes shall be equipped with automatic means for positive release when pressure is released from the pedal.
items.statement: Foot-operated brakes must have automatic means for positive release when pressure is released from the pedal.

items.quote: stop the trolley or bridge within a distance in feet equal to 10 percent of full load speed in feet per minute when traveling at full speed with full load.
items.statement: Trolley or bridge brakes must be large enough to stop the trolley or bridge, traveling at full speed with full load, within a distance in feet equal to 10 percent of full load speed in feet per minute.

items.quote: If holding brakes are provided on the bridge or trolleys, they shall not prohibit the use of a drift point in the control circuit.
items.statement: Holding brakes on the bridge or trolleys, if provided, must not prohibit the use of a drift point in the control circuit.

items.quote: Brakes on trolleys and bridges shall have ample thermal capacity for the frequency of operation required by the service to prevent impairment of functions from overheating.
items.statement: Trolley and bridge brakes must have ample thermal capacity for the frequency of operation required by the service, to prevent impairment of functions from overheating.

items.quote: On cab-operated cranes with cab on trolley, a trolley brake shall be required as specified under paragraph (f)(4) of this section.
items.statement: Cab-operated cranes with the cab on the trolley require a trolley brake as specified in paragraph (f)(4).

items.quote: A drag brake may be applied to hold the trolley in a desired position on the bridge and to eliminate creep with the power off.
items.statement: A drag brake may be applied to hold the trolley in a desired position on the bridge and to eliminate creep with the power off.

items.quote: On cab-operated cranes with cab on bridge, a bridge brake is required as specified under paragraph (f)(4) of this section.
items.statement: Cab-operated cranes with the cab on the bridge require a bridge brake as specified in paragraph (f)(4).

items.quote: On cab-operated cranes with cab on trolley, a bridge brake of the holding type shall be required.
items.statement: Cab-operated cranes with the cab on the trolley require a holding-type bridge brake.

items.quote: On all floor, remote and pulpit-operated crane bridge drives, a brake of noncoasting mechanical drive shall be provided.
items.statement: All floor, remote and pulpit-operated crane bridge drives must have a brake of noncoasting mechanical drive.

items.quote: Wiring and equipment shall comply with subpart S of this part.
items.statement: Crane wiring and electrical equipment must comply with subpart S of Part 1910.

items.quote: The control circuit voltage shall not exceed 600 volts for a.c. or d.c. current.
items.statement: Control circuit voltage must not exceed 600 volts for a.c. or d.c. current.

items.quote: The voltage at pendant push-buttons shall not exceed 150 volts for a.c.
items.statement: AC voltage at pendant push-buttons must not exceed 150 volts.

items.quote: The voltage at pendant push-buttons shall not exceed 150 volts for a.c. and 300 volts for d.c.
items.statement: DC voltage at pendant push-buttons must not exceed 300 volts.

items.quote: Where multiple conductor cable is used with a suspended pushbutton station, the station must be supported in some satisfactory manner that will protect the electrical conductors against strain.
items.statement: Where multiple conductor cable is used with a suspended pushbutton station, the station must be supported in a satisfactory manner that protects the electrical conductors against strain.

items.quote: Pendant control boxes shall be constructed to prevent electrical shock
items.statement: Pendant control boxes must be constructed to prevent electrical shock.

items.quote: shall be clearly marked for identification of functions.
items.statement: Pendant control boxes must be clearly marked to identify functions.

items.quote: Electrical equipment shall be so located or enclosed that live parts will not be exposed to accidental contact under normal operating conditions.
items.statement: Electrical equipment must be located or enclosed so live parts are not exposed to accidental contact under normal operating conditions.

items.quote: Electric equipment shall be protected from dirt, grease, oil, and moisture.
items.statement: Electric equipment must be protected from dirt, grease, oil, and moisture.

items.quote: Guards for live parts shall be substantial and so located that they cannot be accidently deformed so as to make contact with the live parts.
items.statement: Guards for live parts must be substantial and located so they cannot be accidentally deformed into contact with the live parts.

items.quote: Cranes not equipped with spring-return controllers or momentary contact pushbuttons shall be provided with a device which will disconnect all motors from the line on failure of power
items.statement: Cranes without spring-return controllers or momentary contact pushbuttons must have a device that disconnects all motors from the line on power failure.

items.quote: will not permit any motor to be restarted until the controller handle is brought to the “off” position, or a reset switch or button is operated.
items.statement: On cranes without spring-return controllers or momentary contact pushbuttons, the power-failure disconnect device must not permit any motor to restart until the controller handle is brought to "off" or a reset switch or button is operated.

items.quote: Lever operated controllers shall be provided with a notch or latch which in the “off” position prevents the handle from being inadvertently moved to the “on” position. An “off” detent or spring return arrangement is acceptable.
items.statement: Lever operated controllers must have a notch or latch that, in the "off" position, prevents the handle from being inadvertently moved to "on"; an "off" detent or spring return arrangement is acceptable.

items.quote: The controller operating handle shall be located within convenient reach of the operator.
items.statement: The controller operating handle must be within convenient reach of the operator.

items.quote: As far as practicable, the movement of each controller handle shall be in the same general directions as the resultant movements of the load.
items.statement: As far as practicable, each controller handle must move in the same general directions as the resultant load movements.

items.quote: The control for the bridge and trolley travel shall be so located that the operator can readily face the direction of travel.
items.statement: The bridge and trolley travel control must be located so the operator can readily face the direction of travel.

items.quote: For floor-operated cranes, the controller or controllers if rope operated, shall automatically return to the “off” position when released by the operator.
items.statement: On floor-operated cranes, rope-operated controllers must automatically return to "off" when released by the operator.

items.quote: Pushbuttons in pendant stations shall return to the “off” position when pressure is released by the crane operator.
items.statement: Pendant station pushbuttons must return to "off" when the crane operator releases pressure.

items.quote: Automatic cranes shall be so designed that all motions shall fail-safe if any malfunction of operation occurs.
items.statement: Automatic cranes must be designed so all motions fail-safe if any malfunction of operation occurs.

items.quote: Remote-operated cranes shall function so that if the control signal for any crane motion becomes ineffective the crane motion shall stop.
items.statement: On remote-operated cranes, if the control signal for any crane motion becomes ineffective, that motion must stop.

items.quote: Enclosures for resistors shall have openings to provide adequate ventilation
items.statement: Resistor enclosures must have openings that provide adequate ventilation.

items.quote: shall be installed to prevent the accumulation of combustible matter too near to hot parts.
items.statement: Resistor enclosures must be installed to prevent combustible matter from accumulating too near hot parts.

items.quote: Resistor units shall be supported so as to be as free as possible from vibration.
items.statement: Resistor units must be supported so they are as free as possible from vibration.

items.quote: Provision shall be made to prevent broken parts or molten metal falling upon the operator or from the crane.
items.statement: For resistors, provision must be made to prevent broken parts or molten metal from falling upon the operator or from the crane.

items.quote: The power supply to the runway conductors shall be controlled by a switch or circuit breaker located on a fixed structure, accessible from the floor, and arranged to be locked in the open position.
items.statement: Power to the runway conductors must be controlled by a switch or circuit breaker that is on a fixed structure, accessible from the floor, and arranged to be locked open.

items.quote: On cab-operated cranes a switch or circuit breaker of the enclosed type, with provision for locking in the open position, shall be provided in the leads from the runway conductors.
items.statement: Cab-operated cranes must have an enclosed switch or circuit breaker, lockable in the open position, in the leads from the runway conductors.

items.quote: A means of opening this switch or circuit breaker shall be located within easy reach of the operator.
items.statement: On cab-operated cranes, a means of opening the runway-lead switch or circuit breaker must be within easy reach of the operator.

items.quote: On floor-operated cranes, a switch or circuit breaker of the enclosed type, with provision for locking in the open position, shall be provided in the leads from the runway conductors.
items.statement: Floor-operated cranes must have an enclosed switch or circuit breaker, lockable in the open position, in the leads from the runway conductors.

items.quote: This disconnect shall be mounted on the bridge or footwalk near the runway collectors.
items.statement: On floor-operated cranes, the runway-lead disconnect must be mounted on the bridge or footwalk near the runway collectors.

items.quote: One of the following types of floor-operated disconnects shall be provided:
items.statement: Floor-operated cranes must have one of these disconnect types: a nonconductive rope attached to the main disconnect switch, an undervoltage trip for the main circuit breaker operated by a pendant emergency stop button, or a main line contactor operated by a pendant switch or pushbutton.

items.quote: The hoisting motion of all electric traveling cranes shall be provided with an overtravel limit switch in the hoisting direction.
items.statement: The hoisting motion of all electric traveling cranes must have an overtravel limit switch in the hoisting direction.

items.quote: All cranes using a lifting magnet shall have a magnet circuit switch of the enclosed type with provision for locking in the open position.
items.statement: All cranes using a lifting magnet must have an enclosed magnet circuit switch that can be locked in the open position.

items.quote: Means for discharging the inductive load of the magnet shall be provided.
items.statement: Cranes using a lifting magnet must have means for discharging the magnet's inductive load.

items.quote: Conductors of the open type mounted on the crane runway beams or overhead shall be so located or so guarded that persons entering or leaving the cab or crane footwalk normally could not come into contact with them.
items.statement: Open-type conductors on crane runway beams or overhead must be located or guarded so that persons entering or leaving the cab or crane footwalk normally could not contact them.

items.quote: If a service receptacle is provided in the cab or on the bridge of cab-operated cranes, it shall be a grounded three-prong type permanent receptacle
items.statement: A service receptacle, if provided in the cab or on the bridge of a cab-operated crane, must be a grounded three-prong type permanent receptacle.

items.quote: it shall be a grounded three-prong type permanent receptacle, not exceeding 300 volts.
items.statement: A service receptacle in the cab or on the bridge of a cab-operated crane must not exceed 300 volts.

items.quote: Sheave grooves shall be smooth and free from surface defects which could cause rope damage.
items.statement: Sheave grooves must be smooth and free from surface defects that could damage rope.

items.quote: Sheaves carrying ropes which can be momentarily unloaded shall be provided with close-fitting guards or other suitable devices to guide the rope back into the groove when the load is applied again.
items.statement: Sheaves carrying ropes that can be momentarily unloaded must have close-fitting guards or other suitable devices to guide the rope back into the groove when the load is applied again.

items.quote: The sheaves in the bottom block shall be equipped with close-fitting guards that will prevent ropes from becoming fouled when the block is lying on the ground with ropes loose.
items.statement: Bottom block sheaves must have close-fitting guards that prevent ropes from becoming fouled when the block is lying on the ground with ropes loose.

items.quote: Pockets and flanges of sheaves used with hoist chains shall be of such dimensions that the chain does not catch or bind during operation.
items.statement: Pockets and flanges of sheaves used with hoist chains must be dimensioned so the chain does not catch or bind during operation.

items.quote: All running sheaves shall be equipped with means for lubrication.
items.statement: All running sheaves must be equipped with a means for lubrication.

items.quote: Permanently lubricated, sealed and/or shielded bearings meet this requirement.
items.statement: Permanently lubricated, sealed and/or shielded bearings meet the lubrication-means requirement for running sheaves.

items.quote: In using hoisting ropes, the crane manufacturer's recommendation shall be followed.
items.statement: The crane manufacturer's recommendation must be followed in using hoisting ropes.

items.quote: The rated load divided by the number of parts of rope shall not exceed 20 percent of the nominal breaking strength of the rope.
items.statement: The rated load divided by the number of parts of rope must not exceed 20 percent of the rope's nominal breaking strength.

items.quote: Socketing shall be done in the manner specified by the manufacturer of the assembly.
items.statement: Socketing must be done in the manner specified by the manufacturer of the assembly.

items.quote: No less than two wraps of rope shall remain on the drum when the hook is in its extreme low position.
items.statement: At least two wraps of rope must remain on the drum when the hook is in its extreme low position.

items.quote: Rope end shall be anchored by a clamp securely attached to the drum, or by a socket arrangement approved by the crane or rope manufacturer.
items.statement: The rope end must be anchored to the drum by a securely attached clamp or by a socket arrangement approved by the crane or rope manufacturer.

items.quote: Rope clips attached with U-bolts shall have the U-bolts on the dead or short end of the rope.
items.statement: Rope clips attached with U-bolts must have the U-bolts on the dead or short end of the rope.

items.quote: Spacing and number of all types of clips shall be in accordance with the clip manufacturer's recommendation.
items.statement: Spacing and number of all types of rope clips must follow the clip manufacturer's recommendation.

items.quote: Clips shall be drop-forged steel in all sizes manufactured commercially.
items.statement: Rope clips must be drop-forged steel in all sizes manufactured commercially.

items.quote: When a newly installed rope has been in operation for an hour, all nuts on the clip bolts shall be retightened.
items.statement: When a newly installed rope has been in operation for an hour, all nuts on the clip bolts must be retightened.

items.quote: Swaged or compressed fittings shall be applied as recommended by the rope or crane manufacturer.
items.statement: Swaged or compressed fittings must be applied as recommended by the rope or crane manufacturer.

items.quote: Wherever exposed to temperatures, at which fiber cores would be damaged, rope having an independent wirerope or wire-strand core, or other temperature-damage resistant core shall be used.
items.statement: Wherever rope is exposed to temperatures that would damage fiber cores, rope with an independent wire-rope or wire-strand core, or another temperature-damage resistant core, must be used.

items.quote: Replacement rope shall be the same size, grade, and construction as the original rope furnished by the crane manufacturer, unless otherwise recommended by a wire rope manufacturer due to actual working condition requirements.
items.statement: Replacement rope must be the same size, grade and construction as the original rope furnished by the crane manufacturer, unless a wire rope manufacturer recommends otherwise due to actual working condition requirements.

items.quote: If a load is supported by more than one part of rope, the tension in the parts shall be equalized.
items.statement: If a load is supported by more than one part of rope, the tension in the parts must be equalized.

items.quote: Hooks shall meet the manufacturer's recommendations
items.statement: Hooks must meet the manufacturer's recommendations.

items.quote: Hooks shall meet the manufacturer's recommendations and shall not be overloaded.
items.statement: Hooks must not be overloaded.

items.quote: Except for floor-operated cranes a gong or other effective warning signal shall be provided for each crane equipped with a power traveling mechanism.
items.statement: Each crane with a power traveling mechanism, except floor-operated cranes, must have a gong or other effective warning signal.

items.quote: Prior to initial use all new and altered cranes shall be inspected to insure compliance with the provisions of this section.
items.statement: All new and altered cranes must be inspected before initial use to ensure compliance with this section.

items.quote: The intervals in turn are dependent upon the nature of the critical components of the crane and the degree of their exposure to wear, deterioration, or malfunction. The two general classifications are herein designated as “frequent” and “periodic”
items.statement: Inspections of cranes in regular service are classed as frequent or periodic by interval, which depends on the nature of the critical components and their degree of exposure to wear, deterioration or malfunction.

items.quote: Frequent inspection—Daily to monthly intervals.
items.statement: Frequent inspection is done at daily to monthly intervals.

items.quote: Periodic inspection—1 to 12-month intervals.
items.statement: Periodic inspection is done at 1 to 12-month intervals.

items.quote: The following items shall be inspected for defects at intervals as defined in paragraph (j)(1)(ii) of this section or as specifically indicated, including observation during operation for any defects which might appear between regular inspections.
items.statement: Frequent inspection items must be inspected for defects at the defined or specifically indicated intervals, including observation during operation for defects that might appear between regular inspections.

items.quote: All deficiencies such as listed shall be carefully examined and determination made as to whether they constitute a safety hazard
items.statement: All listed frequent-inspection deficiencies must be carefully examined and a determination made whether they are a safety hazard.

items.quote: All functional operating mechanisms for maladjustment interfering with proper operation. Daily.
items.statement: All functional operating mechanisms must be inspected daily for maladjustment that interferes with proper operation.

items.quote: Deterioration or leakage in lines, tanks, valves, drain pumps, and other parts of air or hydraulic systems. Daily.
items.statement: Lines, tanks, valves, drain pumps and other parts of air or hydraulic systems must be inspected daily for deterioration or leakage.

items.quote: Hooks with deformation or cracks. Visual inspection daily
items.statement: Hooks must be visually inspected daily for deformation or cracks.

items.quote: monthly inspection with a certification record which includes the date of inspection, the signature of the person who performed the inspection and the serial number, or other identifier, of the hook inspected.
items.statement: Hooks must be inspected monthly for deformation or cracks, with a certification record that includes the inspection date, the inspector's signature and the hook's serial number or other identifier.

items.quote: For hooks with cracks or having more than 15 percent in excess of normal throat opening or more than 10° twist from the plane of the unbent hook refer to paragraph (l)(3)(iii)(a) of this section.
items.statement: For hooks with cracks, more than 15 percent over normal throat opening, or more than 10° twist from the plane of the unbent hook, paragraph (l)(3)(iii)(a) applies.

items.quote: Hoist chains, including end connections, for excessive wear, twist, distorted links interfering with proper function, or stretch beyond manufacturer's recommendations. Visual inspection daily
items.statement: Hoist chains, including end connections, must be visually inspected daily for excessive wear, twist, distorted links interfering with proper function, or stretch beyond the manufacturer's recommendations.

items.quote: monthly inspection with a certification record which includes the date of inspection, the signature of the person who performed the inspection and an identifier of the chain which was inspected.
items.statement: Hoist chains must be inspected monthly, with a certification record that includes the inspection date, the inspector's signature and an identifier of the chain inspected.

items.quote: All functional operating mechanisms for excessive wear of components.
items.statement: Frequent inspection must check all functional operating mechanisms for excessive wear of components.

items.quote: Rope reeving for noncompliance with manufacturer's recommendations.
items.statement: Frequent inspection must check rope reeving for noncompliance with the manufacturer's recommendations.

items.quote: Complete inspections of the crane shall be performed at intervals as generally defined in paragraph (j)(1)(ii)(b) of this section, depending upon its activity, severity of service, and environment, or as specifically indicated below.
items.statement: Complete crane inspections must be performed at the periodic intervals, depending on the crane's activity, severity of service and environment, or as specifically indicated.

items.quote: These inspections shall include the requirements of paragraph (j)(2) of this section and in addition, the following items.
items.statement: Periodic inspections must include the frequent inspection requirements of paragraph (j)(2) in addition to the periodic items.

items.quote: Any deficiencies such as listed shall be carefully examined and determination made as to whether they constitute a safety hazard
items.statement: All listed periodic-inspection deficiencies must be carefully examined and a determination made whether they are a safety hazard.

items.quote: Deformed, cracked, or corroded members.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for deformed, cracked or corroded members.

items.quote: Loose bolts or rivets.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for loose bolts or rivets.

items.quote: Cracked or worn sheaves and drums.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for cracked or worn sheaves and drums.

items.quote: Worn, cracked or distorted parts such as pins, bearings, shafts, gears, rollers, locking and clamping devices.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for worn, cracked or distorted parts such as pins, bearings, shafts, gears, rollers, and locking and clamping devices.

items.quote: Excessive wear on brake system parts, linings, pawls, and ratchets.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for excessive wear on brake system parts, linings, pawls and ratchets.

items.quote: Load, wind, and other indicators over their full range, for any significant inaccuracies.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check load, wind and other indicators over their full range for significant inaccuracies.

items.quote: Gasoline, diesel, electric, or other powerplants for improper performance or noncompliance with applicable safety requirements.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check gasoline, diesel, electric or other powerplants for improper performance or noncompliance with applicable safety requirements.

items.quote: Excessive wear of chain drive sprockets and excessive chain stretch.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for excessive wear of chain drive sprockets and excessive chain stretch.

items.quote: Electrical apparatus, for signs of pitting or any deterioration of controller contactors, limit switches and pushbutton stations.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check electrical apparatus for signs of pitting or any deterioration of controller contactors, limit switches and pushbutton stations.

items.quote: A crane which has been idle for a period of 1 month or more, but less than 6 months, shall be given an inspection conforming with requirements of paragraph (j)(2) of this section and paragraph (m)(2) of this section before placing in service.
items.statement: A crane idle for 1 month or more but less than 6 months must, before being placed in service, be inspected per paragraphs (j)(2) and (m)(2).
items.value: 1 month or more, but less than 6 months

items.quote: A crane which has been idle for a period of over 6 months shall be given a complete inspection conforming with requirements of paragraphs (j) (2) and (3) of this section and paragraph (m)(2) of this section before placing in service.
items.statement: A crane idle for over 6 months must, before being placed in service, be given a complete inspection per paragraphs (j)(2), (j)(3) and (m)(2).

items.quote: Standby cranes shall be inspected at least semi-annually in accordance with requirements of paragraph (j)(2) of this section and paragraph (m)(2) of this section.
items.statement: Standby cranes must be inspected at least semi-annually per paragraphs (j)(2) and (m)(2).

items.quote:
Prior to initial use all new and altered cranes shall be tested to insure compliance with this section including the following functions:
[29cfr1910.179(k)(1)(i)(a)] (a) Hoisting and lowering.
items.statement: Before initial use, all new and altered cranes must be tested to ensure compliance with this section, including the hoisting and lowering functions.

items.quote: Trolley travel.
items.statement: The pre-initial-use operational test of new and altered cranes must include trolley travel.

items.quote: Bridge travel.
items.statement: The pre-initial-use operational test of new and altered cranes must include bridge travel.

items.quote: Limit switches, locking and safety devices.
items.statement: The pre-initial-use operational test of new and altered cranes must include limit switches, locking and safety devices.

items.quote: The trip setting of hoist limit switches shall be determined by tests with an empty hook traveling in increasing speeds up to the maximum speed.
items.statement: The hoist limit switch trip setting must be determined by tests with an empty hook traveling at increasing speeds up to maximum speed.

items.quote: The actuating mechanism of the limit switch shall be located so that it will trip the switch, under all conditions, in sufficient time to prevent contact of the hook or hook block with any part of the trolley.
items.statement: The limit switch actuating mechanism must be located so it trips the switch, under all conditions, in time to prevent the hook or hook block from contacting any part of the trolley.

items.quote: Test loads shall not be more than 125 percent of the rated load unless otherwise recommended by the manufacturer.
items.statement: Rated load test loads must not exceed 125 percent of rated load unless the manufacturer recommends otherwise.

items.quote: The test reports shall be placed on file where readily available to appointed personnel.
items.statement: Rated load test reports must be filed where readily available to appointed personnel.

items.quote: A preventive maintenance program based on the crane manufacturer's recommendations shall be established.
items.statement: A preventive maintenance program based on the crane manufacturer's recommendations must be established.

items.quote: The crane to be repaired shall be run to a location where it will cause the least interference with other cranes and operations in the area.
items.statement: Before adjustments and repairs are started, the crane to be repaired must be run to where it will cause the least interference with other cranes and operations in the area.

items.quote: All controllers shall be at the off position.
items.statement: Before adjustments and repairs are started on a crane, all controllers must be at the off position.

items.quote: The main or emergency switch shall be open and locked in the open position.
items.statement: Before adjustments and repairs are started on a crane, the main or emergency switch must be open and locked in the open position.

items.quote: Warning or “out of order” signs shall be placed on the crane, also on the floor beneath or on the hook where visible from the floor.
items.statement: Before adjustments and repairs are started, warning or "out of order" signs must be placed on the crane, and also on the floor beneath or on the hook where visible from the floor.

items.quote: Where other cranes are in operation on the same runway, rail stops or other suitable means shall be provided to prevent interference with the idle crane.
items.statement: Before adjustments and repairs are started, where other cranes are operating on the same runway, rail stops or other suitable means must be provided to prevent interference with the idle crane.

items.quote: After adjustments and repairs have been made the crane shall not be operated until all guards have been reinstalled, safety devices reactivated and maintenance equipment removed.
items.statement: After adjustments and repairs, the crane must not be operated until all guards have been reinstalled, safety devices reactivated and maintenance equipment removed.

items.quote: Any unsafe conditions disclosed by the inspection requirements of paragraph (j) of this section shall be corrected before operation of the crane is resumed.
items.statement: Any unsafe conditions disclosed by the inspections required by paragraph (j) must be corrected before crane operation is resumed.

items.quote: Adjustments and repairs shall be done only by designated personnel.
items.statement: Adjustments and repairs must be done only by designated personnel.

items.quote: Adjustments shall be maintained to assure correct functioning of components.
items.statement: Adjustments must be maintained to assure correct functioning of components, with examples including all functional operating mechanisms, limit switches, control systems, brakes and power plants.

items.quote: Repairs or replacements shall be provided promptly as needed for safe operation.
items.statement: Repairs or replacements must be provided promptly as needed for safe operation.

items.quote: Crane hooks showing defects described in paragraph (j)(2)(iii) of this section shall be discarded.
items.statement: Crane hooks showing defects described in paragraph (j)(2)(iii) must be discarded.

items.quote: Repairs by welding or reshaping are not generally recommended. If such repairs are attempted they shall only be done under competent supervision
items.statement: Crane hook repairs by welding or reshaping are not generally recommended, but if attempted they must be done only under competent supervision.

items.quote: the hook shall be tested to the load requirements of paragraph (k)(2) of this section before further use.
items.statement: If a crane hook is repaired by welding or reshaping, it must be tested to the load requirements of paragraph (k)(2) before further use.

items.quote: Load attachment chains and rope slings showing defects described in paragraph (j)(2) (iv) and (v) of this section respectively.
items.statement: Load attachment chains and rope slings showing the defects described in paragraph (j)(2)(iv) and (v), respectively, are examples of items needing prompt repair or replacement for safe operation.

items.quote: All critical parts which are cracked, broken, bent, or excessively worn.
items.statement: All critical parts that are cracked, broken, bent or excessively worn are examples of items needing prompt repair or replacement for safe operation.

items.quote: Pendant control stations shall be kept clean
items.statement: Pendant control stations must be kept clean.

items.quote: Pendant control stations shall be kept clean and function labels kept legible.
items.statement: Function labels on pendant control stations must be kept legible.

items.quote: A thorough inspection of all ropes shall be made at least once a month
items.statement: A thorough inspection of all running ropes must be made at least once a month.

items.quote: a certification record which includes the date of inspection, the signature of the person who performed the inspection and an identifier for the ropes which were inspected
items.statement: A certification record of the running rope inspection must include the inspection date, the signature of the person who performed it and an identifier for the ropes inspected.

items.quote: shall be kept on file where readily available to appointed personnel.
items.statement: The running rope certification record must be kept on file where readily available to appointed personnel.

items.quote: Any deterioration, resulting in appreciable loss of original strength, shall be carefully observed and determination made as to whether further use of the rope would constitute a safety hazard.
items.statement: Any rope deterioration resulting in appreciable loss of original strength must be carefully observed, and it must be determined whether further use of the rope would be a safety hazard.

items.quote: Reduction of rope diameter below nominal diameter due to loss of core support, internal or external corrosion, or wear of outside wires.
items.statement: A condition that could cause appreciable rope strength loss is reduced diameter below nominal due to loss of core support, internal or external corrosion, or wear of outside wires.

items.quote: A number of broken outside wires and the degree of distribution or concentration of such broken wires.
items.statement: A condition that could cause appreciable rope strength loss involves the number of broken outside wires and how they are distributed or concentrated.

items.quote: Worn outside wires.
items.statement: Worn outside wires are a condition that could cause appreciable rope strength loss.

items.quote: Corroded or broken wires at end connections.
items.statement: Corroded or broken wires at end connections are a condition that could cause appreciable rope strength loss.

items.quote: Corroded, cracked, bent, worn, or improperly applied end connections.
items.statement: Corroded, cracked, bent, worn or improperly applied end connections are a condition that could cause appreciable rope strength loss.

items.quote: Severe kinking, crushing, cutting, or unstranding.
items.statement: Severe kinking, crushing, cutting or unstranding is a condition that could cause appreciable rope strength loss.

items.quote: All rope which has been idle for a period of a month or more due to shutdown or storage of a crane on which it is installed shall be given a thorough inspection before it is used.
items.statement: Rope idle for a month or more because the crane it is installed on was shut down or stored must be thoroughly inspected before use.

items.quote: This inspection shall be for all types of deterioration
items.statement: The inspection of idle rope must cover all types of deterioration.

items.quote: shall be performed by an appointed person whose approval shall be required for further use of the rope.
items.statement: The idle rope inspection must be performed by an appointed person, whose approval is required for further use of the rope.

items.quote: A certification record shall be available for inspection which includes the date of inspection, the signature of the person who performed the inspection and an identifier for the rope which was inspected.
items.statement: A certification record of the idle rope inspection must be available for inspection and include the inspection date, the inspector's signature and an identifier for the rope inspected.

items.quote: The crane shall not be loaded beyond its rated load except for test purposes as provided in paragraph (k) of this section.
items.statement: The crane must not be loaded beyond its rated load, except for test purposes as provided in paragraph (k).

items.quote: The hoist chain or hoist rope shall be free from kinks or twists
items.statement: When attaching the load, the hoist chain or hoist rope must be free from kinks or twists.

items.quote: The hoist chain or hoist rope shall be free from kinks or twists and shall not be wrapped around the load.
items.statement: The hoist chain or hoist rope must not be wrapped around the load.

items.quote: The load shall be attached to the load block hook by means of slings or other approved devices.
items.statement: The load must be attached to the load block hook by slings or other approved devices.

items.quote: Care shall be taken to make certain that the sling clears all obstacles.
items.statement: Care must be taken to make certain that the sling clears all obstacles.

items.quote: The load shall be well secured and properly balanced in the sling or lifting device before it is lifted more than a few inches.
items.statement: The load must be well secured and properly balanced in the sling or lifting device before it is lifted more than a few inches.

items.quote: Hoist rope shall not be kinked.
items.statement: Before starting to hoist, it must be noted that the hoist rope is not kinked.

items.quote: Multiple part lines shall not be twisted around each other.
items.statement: Before starting to hoist, it must be noted that multiple part lines are not twisted around each other.

items.quote: The hook shall be brought over the load in such a manner as to prevent swinging.
items.statement: Before starting to hoist, it must be noted that the hook is to be brought over the load in a way that prevents swinging.

items.quote: There is no sudden acceleration or deceleration of the moving load.
items.statement: During hoisting, care must be taken that there is no sudden acceleration or deceleration of the moving load.

items.quote: The load does not contact any obstructions.
items.statement: During hoisting, care must be taken that the load does not contact any obstructions.

items.quote: Cranes shall not be used for side pulls except when specifically authorized by a responsible person who has determined that the stability of the crane is not thereby endangered and that various parts of the crane will not be overstressed.
items.statement: Cranes must not be used for side pulls unless specifically authorized by a responsible person who has determined that crane stability is not thereby endangered and that various crane parts will not be overstressed.

items.quote: While any employee is on the load or hook, there shall be no hoisting, lowering, or traveling.
items.statement: There must be no hoisting, lowering or traveling while any employee is on the load or hook.

items.quote: The employer shall require that the operator avoid carrying loads over people.
items.statement: The employer must require that the operator avoid carrying loads over people.

items.quote: The operator shall test the brakes each time a load approaching the rated load is handled.
items.statement: The operator must test the brakes each time a load approaching the rated load is handled.

items.quote: The brakes shall be tested by raising the load a few inches and applying the brakes.
items.statement: For the brake test on a load approaching rated load, the brakes must be tested by raising the load a few inches and applying the brakes.

items.quote: The load shall not be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on the hoisting drum.
items.statement: The load must not be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on the hoisting drum.

items.quote: When two or more cranes are used to lift a load one qualified responsible person shall be in charge of the operation.
items.statement: When two or more cranes are used to lift a load, one qualified responsible person must be in charge of the operation.

items.quote: He shall analyze the operation and instruct all personnel involved in the proper positioning, rigging of the load, and the movements to be made.
items.statement: In a lift using two or more cranes, the person in charge must analyze the operation and instruct all personnel involved in proper positioning, rigging of the load and the movements to be made.

items.quote: The employer shall insure that the operator does not leave his position at the controls while the load is suspended.
items.statement: The employer must ensure that the operator does not leave the position at the controls while the load is suspended.

items.quote: When starting the bridge and when the load or hook approaches near or over personnel, the warning signal shall be sounded.
items.statement: The warning signal must be sounded when starting the bridge and when the load or hook approaches near or over personnel.
