items.quote: At the beginning of each operator's shift, the upper limit switch of each hoist shall be tried out under no load.
items.statement: At the beginning of each operator's shift, the upper limit switch of each hoist must be tried out under no load.

items.quote: Extreme care shall be exercised; the block shall be “inched” into the limit or run in at slow speed.
items.statement: When trying out the upper limit switch, extreme care must be used, and the block must be inched into the limit or run in at slow speed.

items.quote: If the switch does not operate properly, the appointed person shall be immediately notified.
items.statement: If the upper limit switch does not operate properly during the tryout, the appointed person must be notified immediately.

items.quote: The hoist limit switch which controls the upper limit of travel of the load block shall never be used as an operating control.
items.statement: The hoist limit switch that controls the upper limit of load block travel must never be used as an operating control.

items.quote: The employer shall insure that hands are free from encumbrances while personnel are using ladders.
items.statement: The employer must ensure that personnel's hands are free from encumbrances while they use ladders.

items.quote: Articles which are too large to be carried in pockets or belts shall be lifted and lowered by hand line.
items.statement: Articles too large to be carried in pockets or belts must be lifted and lowered by hand line.

items.quote: Necessary clothing and personal belongings shall be stored in such a manner as not to interfere with access or operation.
items.statement: Necessary clothing and personal belongings in the cab must be stored so they do not interfere with access or operation.

items.quote: Tools, oil cans, waste, extra fuses, and other necessary articles shall be stored in the tool box
items.statement: Tools, oil cans, waste, extra fuses and other necessary articles must be stored in the tool box.

items.quote: Tools, oil cans, waste, extra fuses, and other necessary articles shall be stored in the tool box, and shall not be permitted to lie loose in or about the cab.
items.statement: Tools, oil cans, waste, extra fuses and other necessary articles must not be permitted to lie loose in or about the cab.

items.quote: The employer shall insure that operators are familiar with the operation and care of fire extinguishers provided.
items.statement: The employer must ensure that operators are familiar with the operation and care of the fire extinguishers provided.

items.quote: A crawler crane consists of a rotating superstructure with power plant, operating machinery, and boom, mounted on a base, equipped with crawler treads for travel.
items.statement: A crawler crane consists of a rotating superstructure with power plant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on a base equipped with crawler treads for travel.

items.quote: Its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.
items.statement: The function of a crawler crane is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.

items.quote: A locomotive crane consists of a rotating superstructure with power-plant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on a base or car equipped for travel on railroad track.
items.statement: A locomotive crane consists of a rotating superstructure with power plant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on a base or car equipped for travel on railroad track.

items.quote: It may be self-propelled or propelled by an outside source.
items.statement: A locomotive crane may be self-propelled or propelled by an outside source.

items.quote: Its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.
items.statement: The function of a locomotive crane is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.

items.quote: A truck crane consists of a rotating superstructure with powerplant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on an automotive truck equipped with a powerplant for travel.
items.statement: A truck crane consists of a rotating superstructure with powerplant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on an automotive truck equipped with a powerplant for travel.

items.quote: Its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.
items.statement: The function of a truck crane is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.

items.quote: A wheel mounted crane (wagon crane) consists of a rotating superstructure with powerplant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on a base or platform equipped with axles and rubber-tired wheels for travel.
items.statement: A wheel mounted crane (wagon crane) consists of a rotating superstructure with powerplant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on a base or platform equipped with axles and rubber-tired wheels for travel.

items.quote: The base is usually propelled by the engine in the superstructure, but it may be equipped with a separate engine controlled from the superstructure.
items.statement: A wheel mounted crane's base is usually propelled by the engine in the superstructure, but it may have a separate engine controlled from the superstructure.

items.quote: Its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.
items.statement: The function of a wheel mounted crane is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.

items.quote: An accessory is a secondary part or assembly of parts which contributes to the overall function and usefulness of a machine.
items.statement: An accessory is a secondary part or assembly of parts that contributes to the overall function and usefulness of a machine.

items.quote: Appointed means assigned specific responsibilities by the employer or the employer's representative.
items.statement: Appointed means assigned specific responsibilities by the employer or the employer's representative.

items.quote: ANSI means the American National Standards Institute.
items.statement: ANSI means the American National Standards Institute.

items.quote: An angle indicator (boom) is an accessory which measures the angle of the boom to the horizontal.
items.statement: A boom angle indicator is an accessory that measures the angle of the boom to the horizontal.

items.quote: The axis of rotation is the vertical axis around which the crane superstructure rotates.
items.statement: The axis of rotation is the vertical axis around which the crane superstructure rotates.

items.quote: Axle means the shaft or spindle with which or about which a wheel rotates.
items.statement: An axle is the shaft or spindle with which or about which a wheel rotates.

items.quote: On truck- and wheel-mounted cranes it refers to an automotive type of axle assembly including housings, gearing, differential, bearings, and mounting appurtenances.
items.statement: On truck- and wheel-mounted cranes, axle refers to an automotive type of axle assembly including housings, gearing, differential, bearings and mounting appurtenances.

items.quote: Axle (bogie) means two or more automotive-type axles mounted in tandem in a frame so as to divide the load between the axles and permit vertical oscillation of the wheels.
items.statement: An axle bogie is two or more automotive-type axles mounted in tandem in a frame so as to divide the load between the axles and permit vertical oscillation of the wheels.

items.quote: The base (mounting) is the traveling base or carrier on which the rotating superstructure is mounted such as a car, truck, crawlers, or wheel platform.
items.statement: The base (mounting) is the traveling base or carrier, such as a car, truck, crawlers or wheel platform, on which the rotating superstructure is mounted.

items.quote: The boom (crane) is a member hinged to the front of the rotating superstructure with the outer end supported by ropes leading to a gantry or A-frame and used for supporting the hoisting tackle.
items.statement: The crane boom is a member hinged to the front of the rotating superstructure, with its outer end supported by ropes leading to a gantry or A-frame, and used to support the hoisting tackle.

items.quote: The boom angle is the angle between the longitudinal centerline of the boom and the horizontal.
items.statement: The boom angle is the angle between the longitudinal centerline of the boom and the horizontal.

items.quote: The boom longitudinal centerline is a straight line between the boom foot pin (heel pin) centerline and boom point sheave pin centerline.
items.statement: The boom longitudinal centerline is a straight line between the boom foot pin (heel pin) centerline and the boom point sheave pin centerline.

items.quote: The boom hoist is a hoist drum and rope reeving system used to raise and lower the boom.
items.statement: The boom hoist is a hoist drum and rope reeving system used to raise and lower the boom.

items.quote: The rope system may be all live reeving or a combination of live reeving and pendants.
items.statement: The boom hoist rope system may be all live reeving or a combination of live reeving and pendants.

items.quote: The boom stop is a device used to limit the angle of the boom at the highest position.
items.statement: A boom stop is a device used to limit the angle of the boom at the highest position.

items.quote: A brake is a device used for retarding or stopping motion by friction or power means.
items.statement: A brake is a device used to retard or stop motion by friction or power means.

items.quote: A cab is a housing which covers the rotating superstructure machinery and/or operator's station.
items.statement: A cab is a housing that covers the rotating superstructure machinery and/or the operator's station.

items.quote: On truck-crane trucks a separate cab covers the driver's station.
items.statement: On truck-crane trucks, a separate cab covers the driver's station.

items.quote: The clutch is a friction, electromagnetic, hydraulic, pneumatic, or positive mechanical device for engagement or disengagement of power.
items.statement: A clutch is a friction, electromagnetic, hydraulic, pneumatic or positive mechanical device for engaging or disengaging power.

items.quote: The counterweight is a weight used to supplement the weight of the machine in providing stability for lifting working loads.
items.statement: The counterweight is a weight used to supplement the machine's weight in providing stability for lifting working loads.

items.quote: Designated means selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.
items.statement: Designated means selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.

items.quote: The drum is the cylindrical members around which ropes are wound for raising and lowering the load or boom.
items.statement: The drum is the cylindrical members around which ropes are wound to raise and lower the load or boom.

items.quote: Dynamic (loading) means loads introduced into the machine or its components by forces in motion.
items.statement: Dynamic loading means loads introduced into the machine or its components by forces in motion.

items.quote: The gantry (A-frame) is a structural frame, extending above the superstructure, to which the boom support ropes are reeved.
items.statement: The gantry (A-frame) is a structural frame extending above the superstructure, to which the boom support ropes are reeved.

items.quote: A jib is an extension attached to the boom point to provide added boom length for lifting specified loads.
items.statement: A jib is an extension attached to the boom point to provide added boom length for lifting specified loads.

items.quote: The jib may be in line with the boom or offset to various angles.
items.statement: A jib may be in line with the boom or offset to various angles.

items.quote: Load (working) means the external load, in pounds, applied to the crane, including the weight of load-attaching equipment such as load blocks, shackles, and slings.
items.statement: The working load is the external load, in pounds, applied to the crane, including the weight of load-attaching equipment such as load blocks, shackles and slings.

items.quote: Load block (upper) means the assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, sheaves, pins, and frame suspended from the boom point.
items.statement: The upper load block is the assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, sheaves, pins and frame suspended from the boom point.

items.quote: Load block (lower) means the assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, sheaves, pins, and frame suspended by the hoisting ropes.
items.statement: The lower load block is the assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, sheaves, pins and frame suspended by the hoisting ropes.

items.quote: A load hoist is a hoist drum and rope reeving system used for hoisting and lowering loads.
items.statement: A load hoist is a hoist drum and rope reeving system used for hoisting and lowering loads.

items.quote: Load ratings are crane ratings in pounds established by the manufacturer in accordance with paragraph (c) of this section.
items.statement: Load ratings are crane ratings in pounds established by the manufacturer in accordance with paragraph (c) of this section.

items.quote: Outriggers are extendable or fixed metal arms, attached to the mounting base, which rest on supports at the outer ends.
items.statement: Outriggers are extendable or fixed metal arms attached to the mounting base, which rest on supports at the outer ends.

items.quote: Rail clamp means a tong-like metal device, mounted on a locomotive crane car, which can be connected to the track.
items.statement: A rail clamp is a tong-like metal device mounted on a locomotive crane car that can be connected to the track.

items.quote: Reeving means a rope system in which the rope travels around drums and sheaves.
items.statement: Reeving is a rope system in which the rope travels around drums and sheaves.

items.quote: Rope refers to a wire rope unless otherwise specified.
items.statement: Rope refers to a wire rope unless otherwise specified.

items.quote: Side loading means a load applied at an angle to the vertical plane of the boom.
items.statement: Side loading is a load applied at an angle to the vertical plane of the boom.

items.quote: A standby crane is a crane which is not in regular service but which is used occasionally or intermittently as required.
items.statement: A standby crane is one that is not in regular service but is used occasionally or intermittently as required.

items.quote: A standing (guy) rope is a supporting rope which maintains a constant distance between the points of attachment to the two components connected by the rope.
items.statement: A standing (guy) rope is a supporting rope that maintains a constant distance between the points of attachment to the two components it connects.

items.quote: Structural competence means the ability of the machine and its components to withstand the stresses imposed by applied loads.
items.statement: Structural competence is the ability of the machine and its components to withstand the stresses imposed by applied loads.

items.quote: Superstructure means the rotating upper frame structure of the machine and the operating machinery mounted thereon.
items.statement: The superstructure is the rotating upper frame structure of the machine and the operating machinery mounted on it.

items.quote: Swing means the rotation of the superstructure for movement of loads in a horizontal direction about the axis of rotation.
items.statement: Swing is the rotation of the superstructure about the axis of rotation to move loads horizontally.

items.quote: Swing mechanism means the machinery involved in providing rotation of the superstructure.
items.statement: The swing mechanism is the machinery involved in rotating the superstructure.

items.quote: Tackle is an assembly of ropes and sheaves arranged for hoisting and pulling.
items.statement: Tackle is an assembly of ropes and sheaves arranged for hoisting and pulling.

items.quote: Transit means the moving or transporting of a crane from one jobsite to another.
items.statement: Transit is moving or transporting a crane from one jobsite to another.

items.quote: Travel means the function of the machine moving from one location to another, on a jobsite.
items.statement: Travel is the function of the machine moving from one location to another on a jobsite.

items.quote: The travel mechanism is the machinery involved in providing travel.
items.statement: The travel mechanism is the machinery involved in providing travel.

items.quote: Wheelbase means the distance between centers of front and rear axles.
items.statement: Wheelbase is the distance between the centers of the front and rear axles.

items.quote: For a multiple axle assembly the axle center for wheelbase measurement is taken as the midpoint of the assembly.
items.statement: For a multiple axle assembly, the axle center used for wheelbase measurement is the midpoint of the assembly.

items.quote: The whipline (auxiliary hoist) is a separate hoist rope system of lighter load capacity and higher speed than provided by the main hoist.
items.statement: The whipline (auxiliary hoist) is a separate hoist rope system with lighter load capacity and higher speed than the main hoist.

items.quote: A winch head is a power driven spool for handling of loads by means of friction between fiber or wire rope and spool.
items.statement: A winch head is a power-driven spool for handling loads by friction between fiber or wire rope and the spool.

items.quote: This section applies to crawler cranes, locomotive cranes, wheel mounted cranes of both truck and self-propelled wheel type, and any variations thereof which retain the same fundamental characteristics.
items.statement: The section applies to crawler cranes, locomotive cranes, wheel mounted cranes of both truck and self-propelled wheel type, and variations that retain the same fundamental characteristics.

items.quote: This section includes only cranes of the above types, which are basically powered by internal combustion engines or electric motors and which utilize drums and ropes.
items.statement: The section includes only cranes of the listed types that are basically powered by internal combustion engines or electric motors and use drums and ropes.

items.quote: Cranes designed for railway and automobile wreck clearances are excepted.
items.statement: Cranes designed for railway and automobile wreck clearances are excepted from the section.

items.quote: The requirements of this section are applicable only to machines when used as lifting cranes.
items.statement: The section's requirements apply to machines only when they are used as lifting cranes.

items.quote: All new crawler, locomotive, and truck cranes constructed and utilized on or after August 31, 1971, shall meet the design specifications of the American National Standard Safety Code for Crawler, Locomotive, and Truck Cranes, ANSI B30.5-1968
items.statement: All new crawler, locomotive and truck cranes constructed and utilized on or after August 31, 1971, must meet the design specifications of ANSI B30.5-1968, incorporated by reference as specified in § 1910.6.

items.quote: Crawler, locomotive, and truck cranes constructed prior to August 31, 1971, should be modified to conform to those design specifications by February 15, 1972, unless it can be shown that the crane cannot feasibly or economically be altered and that the crane substantially complies with the requirements of this section.
items.statement: Crawler, locomotive and truck cranes constructed before August 31, 1971, should be modified to conform to the ANSI B30.5-1968 design specifications by February 15, 1972, except where it can be shown that the crane cannot feasibly or economically be altered and that it substantially complies with the section's requirements.

items.quote: Only designated personnel shall be permitted to operate a crane covered by this section.
items.statement: No one other than designated personnel may be permitted to operate a crane covered by the section.

items.quote: The margin of stability for determination of load ratings, with booms of stipulated lengths at stipulated working radii for the various types of crane mountings, is established by taking a percentage of the loads which will produce a condition of tipping or balance with the boom in the least stable direction, relative to the mounting.
items.statement: Where stability governs lifting performance, the stability margin for load ratings (for stipulated boom lengths and working radii for each mounting type) is set as a percentage of the loads that produce tipping or balance with the boom in the least stable direction relative to the mounting.

items.quote:
Maximum load ratings (percent of tipping loads)
Locomotive, without outriggers: |
Booms 60 feet or less | 1 85
items.statement: For locomotive cranes without outriggers and booms 60 feet or less, load ratings must not exceed 85 percent of tipping loads, unless this gives less than 30,000 pound-feet net stabilizing moment about the rail, which is the minimum for such booms.

items.quote:
Maximum load ratings (percent of tipping loads)
Locomotive, without outriggers: |
Booms 60 feet or less | 1 85
Booms over 60 feet | 1 85
items.statement: For locomotive cranes without outriggers and booms over 60 feet, load ratings must not exceed 85 percent of tipping loads, unless this gives less than 30,000 pound-feet net stabilizing moment about the rail, which is the minimum for such booms.

items.quote:
Maximum load ratings (percent of tipping loads)
Locomotive, without outriggers: |
Booms 60 feet or less | 1 85
Booms over 60 feet | 1 85
Locomotive, using outriggers fully extended | 80
items.statement: For locomotive cranes using fully extended outriggers, load ratings must not exceed 80 percent of tipping loads.

items.quote:
Maximum load ratings (percent of tipping loads)
Locomotive, without outriggers: |
Booms 60 feet or less | 1 85
Booms over 60 feet | 1 85
Locomotive, using outriggers fully extended | 80
Crawler, without outriggers | 75
items.statement: For crawler cranes without outriggers, load ratings must not exceed 75 percent of tipping loads.

items.quote:
Maximum load ratings (percent of tipping loads)
Locomotive, without outriggers: |
Booms 60 feet or less | 1 85
Booms over 60 feet | 1 85
Locomotive, using outriggers fully extended | 80
Crawler, without outriggers | 75
Crawler, using outriggers fully extended | 85
items.statement: For crawler cranes using fully extended outriggers, load ratings must not exceed 85 percent of tipping loads.

items.quote:
Maximum load ratings (percent of tipping loads)
Locomotive, without outriggers: |
Booms 60 feet or less | 1 85
Booms over 60 feet | 1 85
Locomotive, using outriggers fully extended | 80
Crawler, without outriggers | 75
Crawler, using outriggers fully extended | 85
Truck and wheel mounted without outriggers or using outriggers fully extended | 85
items.statement: For truck and wheel-mounted cranes without outriggers or with fully extended outriggers, load ratings must not exceed 85 percent of tipping loads.

items.quote: Unless this results in less than 30,000 pound-feet net stabilizing moment about the rail, which shall be minimum with such booms.
items.statement: For locomotive cranes without outriggers, if the 85 percent rating would give less than 30,000 pound-feet net stabilizing moment about the rail, 30,000 pound-feet is the minimum for those booms.

items.quote: Tipping with or without the use of outriggers occurs when half of the wheels farthest from the load leave the rail.
items.statement: For locomotive crane load ratings, tipping, with or without outriggers, occurs when half of the wheels farthest from the load leave the rail.

items.quote: The crane shall be standing on track which is level within 1 percent grade.
items.statement: For applying locomotive crane stability percentages, the crane must stand on track that is level within 1 percent grade.

items.quote: Radius of the load is the horizontal distance from a projection of the axis of rotation to the rail support surface, before loading, to the center of vertical hoist line or tackle with load applied.
items.statement: For locomotive cranes, load radius is the horizontal distance from a projection of the axis of rotation to the rail support surface, before loading, to the center of the vertical hoist line or tackle with load applied.

items.quote: Tipping loads from which ratings are determined shall be applied under static conditions only, i.e., without dynamic effect of hoisting, lowering, or swinging.
items.statement: Tipping loads used to determine locomotive crane ratings must be applied only under static conditions, without the dynamic effect of hoisting, lowering or swinging.

items.quote: The weight of all auxiliary handling devices such as hoist blocks, hooks, and slings shall be considered a part of the load rating.
items.statement: For locomotive cranes, the weight of all auxiliary handling devices, such as hoist blocks, hooks and slings, must be considered part of the load rating.

items.quote: for crawler, truck, and wheel-mounted cranes shall be in accordance with Crane Load-Stability Test Code, Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) J765
items.statement: Stipulations for applying the stability percentages to crawler, truck and wheel-mounted cranes must accord with SAE J765, Crane Load-Stability Test Code, incorporated by reference in § 1910.6.

items.quote: such additional factors as freely suspended loads, track, wind, or ground conditions, condition and inflation of rubber tires, boom lengths, proper operating speeds for existing conditions, and, in general, careful and competent operation. All of these shall be taken into account by the user.
items.statement: The user must take into account factors that influence the stability factors, such as freely suspended loads, track, wind or ground conditions, rubber tire condition and inflation, boom lengths, proper operating speeds for existing conditions, and careful and competent operation.

items.quote: A substantial and durable rating chart with clearly legible letters and figures shall be provided with each crane
items.statement: Each crane must have a substantial, durable load rating chart with clearly legible letters and figures.

items.quote: securely fixed to the crane cab in a location easily visible to the operator while seated at his control station
items.statement: The load rating chart must be securely fixed to the crane cab where the operator can easily see it while seated at the control station.

items.quote: Prior to initial use all new and altered cranes shall be inspected to insure compliance with provisions of this section.
items.statement: All new and altered cranes must be inspected before initial use to ensure compliance with this section.

items.quote: Inspection procedure for cranes in regular service is divided into two general classifications based upon the intervals at which inspection should be performed. The intervals in turn are dependent upon the nature of the critical components of the crane and the degree of their exposure to wear, deterioration, or malfunction.
items.statement: Regular inspection is divided into frequent and periodic classes based on intervals, which depend on the nature of the crane's critical components and their exposure to wear, deterioration or malfunction.

items.quote: Frequent inspection: Daily to monthly intervals.
items.statement: Frequent inspection is done at daily to monthly intervals.

items.quote: Periodic inspection: 1- to 12-month intervals, or as specifically recommended by the manufacturer.
items.statement: Periodic inspection is done at 1- to 12-month intervals, or as the manufacturer specifically recommends.

items.quote: Items such as the following shall be inspected for defects at intervals as defined in paragraph (d)(2)(i) of this section or as specifically indicated including observation during operation for any defects which might appear between regular inspections.
items.statement: Items such as those listed for frequent inspection must be inspected for defects at frequent intervals or as specifically indicated, including observation during operation for defects that might appear between regular inspections.

items.quote: Any deficiencies such as listed shall be carefully examined and determination made as to whether they constitute a safety hazard:
items.statement: Deficiencies found in frequent inspection, such as those listed, must be carefully examined and a determination made whether they are a safety hazard.

items.quote: All control mechanisms for maladjustment interfering with proper operation: Daily.
items.statement: All control mechanisms must be inspected daily for maladjustment that interferes with proper operation.

items.quote: All control mechanisms for excessive wear of components and contamination by lubricants or other foreign matter.
items.statement: Frequent inspection must check all control mechanisms for excessive component wear and contamination by lubricants or other foreign matter.

items.quote: All safety devices for malfunction.
items.statement: Frequent inspection must check all safety devices for malfunction.

items.quote: Deterioration or leakage in air or hydraulic systems: Daily.
items.statement: Air or hydraulic systems must be inspected daily for deterioration or leakage.

items.quote: Crane hooks with deformations or cracks.
items.statement: Frequent inspection must check crane hooks for deformations or cracks.

items.quote: more than 15 percent in excess of normal throat opening
items.statement: The hook inspection item singles out hooks with more than 15 percent in excess of normal throat opening.

items.quote: more than 10° twist from the plane of the unbent hook
items.statement: The hook inspection item singles out hooks with more than 10° twist from the plane of the unbent hook.

items.quote: Rope reeving for noncompliance with manufacturer's recommendations.
items.statement: Frequent inspection must check rope reeving for noncompliance with the manufacturer's recommendations.

items.quote: Electrical apparatus for malfunctioning, signs of excessive deterioration, dirt, and moisture accumulation.
items.statement: Frequent inspection must check electrical apparatus for malfunction, signs of excessive deterioration, dirt and moisture accumulation.

items.quote: Complete inspections of the crane shall be performed at intervals as generally defined in paragraph (d)(2)(ii) of this section depending upon its activity, severity of service, and environment, or as specifically indicated below.
items.statement: Complete crane inspections must be performed at periodic intervals, depending on the crane's activity, severity of service and environment, or as specifically indicated.

items.quote: These inspections shall include the requirements of paragraph (d)(3) of this section
items.statement: Periodic inspections must include the frequent inspection requirements of paragraph (d)(3) in addition to the periodic items.

items.quote: Any deficiencies such as listed shall be carefully examined and determination made as to whether they constitute a safety hazard:
items.statement: Deficiencies found in periodic inspection, such as those listed, must be carefully examined and a determination made whether they are a safety hazard.

items.quote: Deformed, cracked, or corroded members in the crane structure and boom.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for deformed, cracked or corroded members in the crane structure and boom.

items.quote: Loose bolts or rivets.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for loose bolts or rivets.

items.quote: Cracked or worn sheaves and drums.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for cracked or worn sheaves and drums.

items.quote: Worn, cracked, or distorted parts such as pins, bearings, shafts, gears, rollers and locking devices.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for worn, cracked or distorted parts such as pins, bearings, shafts, gears, rollers and locking devices.

items.quote: Excessive wear on brake and clutch system parts, linings, pawls, and ratchets.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for excessive wear on brake and clutch system parts, linings, pawls and ratchets.

items.quote: Load, boom angle, and other indicators over their full range, for any significant inaccuracies.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check load, boom angle and other indicators over their full range for significant inaccuracies.

items.quote: Gasoline, diesel, electric, or other power plants for improper performance or noncompliance with safety requirements.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check gasoline, diesel, electric or other power plants for improper performance or noncompliance with safety requirements.

items.quote: Excessive wear of chain-drive sprockets and excessive chain stretch.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for excessive wear of chain-drive sprockets and excessive chain stretch.

items.quote: Travel steering, braking, and locking devices, for malfunction.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check travel steering, braking and locking devices for malfunction.

items.quote: Excessively worn or damaged tires.
items.statement: Periodic inspection must check for excessively worn or damaged tires.

items.quote: A crane which has been idle for a period of one month or more, but less than 6 months, shall be given an inspection conforming with requirements of paragraph (d)(3) of this section and paragraph (g)(2)(ii) of this section before placing in service.
items.statement: A crane idle for one month or more but less than 6 months must be inspected under paragraphs (d)(3) and (g)(2)(ii) before being placed in service.
items.value: one month or more, but less than 6

items.quote: A crane which has been idle for a period of six months shall be given a complete inspection conforming with requirements of paragraphs (d) (3) and (4) of this section and paragraph (g)(2)(ii) of this section before placing in service.
items.statement: A crane idle for six months must get a complete inspection under paragraphs (d)(3), (d)(4) and (g)(2)(ii) before being placed in service.

items.quote: Standby cranes shall be inspected at least semiannually in accordance with requirements of paragraph (d)(3) of this section and paragraph (g)(2)(ii) of this section.
items.statement: Standby cranes must be inspected at least semiannually under paragraphs (d)(3) and (g)(2)(ii).

items.quote: Such cranes which are exposed to adverse environment should be inspected more frequently.
items.statement: Standby cranes exposed to an adverse environment should (advisory) be inspected more frequently than semiannually.

items.quote: shall be made monthly on critical items in use such as brakes, crane hooks, and ropes
items.statement: Certification records must be made monthly on critical items in use, such as brakes, crane hooks and ropes.

items.quote: Certification records which include the date of inspection, the signature of the person who performed the inspection and the serial number, or other identifier, of the crane which was inspected
items.statement: Inspection certification records must include the inspection date, the signature of the person who inspected, and the serial number or other identifier of the crane.

items.quote: This certification record shall be kept readily available.
items.statement: The inspection certification record must be kept readily available.

items.quote: each new production crane shall be tested by the manufacturer to the extent necessary to insure compliance with the operational requirements of this paragraph including functions such as the following:
items.statement: In addition to prototype tests and quality-control measures, the manufacturer must test each new production crane as needed to ensure compliance with the operational requirements, including functions such as those listed.

items.quote: Load hoisting and lowering mechanisms.
items.statement: Manufacturer operational testing of new production cranes includes functions such as load hoisting and lowering mechanisms.

items.quote: Boom hoisting and lower mechanisms.
items.statement: Manufacturer operational testing of new production cranes includes functions such as boom hoisting and lowering mechanisms.

items.quote: Swinging mechanism.
items.statement: Manufacturer operational testing of new production cranes includes functions such as the swinging mechanism.

items.quote: Travel mechanism.
items.statement: Manufacturer operational testing of new production cranes includes functions such as the travel mechanism.

items.quote: Safety devices.
items.statement: Manufacturer operational testing of new production cranes includes functions such as safety devices.

items.quote: Where the complete production crane is not supplied by one manufacturer such tests shall be conducted at final assembly.
items.statement: Where one manufacturer does not supply the complete production crane, the operational tests must be conducted at final assembly.

items.quote: Certified production-crane test results shall be made available.
items.statement: Certified production-crane test results must be made available.

items.quote: Written reports shall be available showing test procedures and confirming the adequacy of repairs or alterations.
items.statement: Written reports showing test procedures and confirming the adequacy of repairs or alterations must be available.

items.quote: Test loads shall not exceed 110 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius.
items.statement: Rated load test loads must not exceed 110 percent of the rated load at any selected working radius.

items.quote: Crawler, truck, and wheel-mounted cranes shall be tested in accordance with SAE Recommended Practice, Crane Load Stability Test Code J765 (April 1961).
items.statement: Where rerating is necessary, crawler, truck and wheel-mounted cranes must be tested under SAE Recommended Practice, Crane Load Stability Test Code J765 (April 1961).

items.quote: Locomotive cranes shall be tested in accordance with paragraph (c)(1) (i) and (ii) of this section.
items.statement: Where rerating is necessary, locomotive cranes must be tested under paragraph (c)(1)(i) and (ii).

items.quote: Rerating test report shall be readily available.
items.statement: Where rerating is necessary, the rerating test report must be readily available.

items.quote: No cranes shall be rerated in excess of the original load ratings unless such rating changes are approved by the crane manufacturer or final assembler.
items.statement: No crane may be rerated above its original load ratings unless the crane manufacturer or final assembler approves the change.

items.quote: After adjustments and repairs have been made the crane shall not be operated until all guards have been reinstalled
items.statement: After adjustments and repairs, the crane must not be operated until all guards have been reinstalled.

items.quote: the crane shall not be operated until all guards have been reinstalled, safety devices reactivated
items.statement: After adjustments and repairs, the crane must not be operated until safety devices have been reactivated.

items.quote: the crane shall not be operated until all guards have been reinstalled, safety devices reactivated, and maintenance equipment removed
items.statement: After adjustments and repairs, the crane must not be operated until maintenance equipment has been removed.

items.quote: A thorough inspection of all ropes in use shall be made at least once a month
items.statement: All ropes in use must be thoroughly inspected at least once a month.

items.quote: a certification record which includes the date of inspection, the signature of the person who performed the inspection and an identifier for the ropes shall be prepared
items.statement: A certification record of the monthly rope inspection must be prepared, including the inspection date, the signature of the person who performed it and an identifier for the ropes.

items.quote: kept on file where readily available
items.statement: The certification record for the monthly rope inspection must be kept on file where it is readily available.

items.quote: All inspections shall be performed by an appointed or authorized person.
items.statement: All running rope inspections must be performed by an appointed or authorized person.

items.quote: Any deterioration, resulting in appreciable loss of original strength shall be carefully observed and detemination made as to whether further use of the rope would constitute a safety hazard.
items.statement: Any rope deterioration resulting in appreciable loss of original strength must be carefully observed, and a determination made as to whether further use of the rope would be a safety hazard.

items.quote: Reduction of rope diameter below nominal diameter due to loss of core support, internal or external corrosion, or wear of outside wires.
items.statement: A condition that could cause appreciable loss of rope strength is reduction of diameter below nominal due to loss of core support, internal or external corrosion, or wear of outside wires.

items.quote: A number of broken outside wires and the degree of distribution of concentration of such broken wires.
items.statement: A condition that could cause appreciable loss of rope strength is a number of broken outside wires, considered with how those broken wires are distributed or concentrated.

items.quote: Worn outside wires.
items.statement: Worn outside wires are a condition that could cause appreciable loss of rope strength.

items.quote: Corroded or broken wires at end connections.
items.statement: Corroded or broken wires at end connections are a condition that could cause appreciable loss of rope strength.

items.quote: Corroded, cracked, bent, worn, or improperly applied end connections.
items.statement: Corroded, cracked, bent, worn or improperly applied end connections are a condition that could cause appreciable loss of rope strength.

items.quote: Severe kinking, crushing, cutting, or unstranding.
items.statement: Severe kinking, crushing, cutting or unstranding is a condition that could cause appreciable loss of rope strength.

items.quote: Particular care shall be taken to inspect ropes at these locations.
items.statement: Particular care must be taken to inspect ropes where they contact saddles, equalizer sheaves or other sheaves with limited rope travel, because heavy wear and/or broken wires may occur there.

items.quote: All rope which has been idle for a period of a month or more due to shutdown or storage of a crane on which it is installed shall be given a thorough inspection before it is used.
items.statement: Rope idle for a month or more because its crane was shut down or stored must be thoroughly inspected before it is used.

items.quote: This inspection shall be for all types of deterioration
items.statement: The inspection of idle rope must cover all types of deterioration.

items.quote: shall be performed by an appointed or authorized person whose approval shall be required for further use of the rope
items.statement: The idle rope inspection must be performed by an appointed or authorized person, whose approval is required for further use of the rope.

items.quote: A certification record which includes the date of inspection, the signature of the person who performed the inspection, and an identifier for the rope which was inspected shall be prepared and kept readily available.
items.statement: A certification record of the idle rope inspection, with the inspection date, the inspector's signature and an identifier for the rope, must be prepared and kept readily available.

items.quote: Particular care shall be taken in the inspection of nonrotating rope.
items.statement: Particular care must be taken when inspecting nonrotating rope.

items.quote: No crane shall be loaded beyond the rated load, except for test purposes as provided in paragraph (e) of this section.
items.statement: No crane may be loaded beyond its rated load, except for test purposes as provided in paragraph (e).

items.quote: it shall be ascertained that the weight of the load has been determined within plus or minus 10 percent before it is lifted
items.statement: For loads limited by structural competence rather than stability, it must be ascertained before lifting that the load weight has been determined within plus or minus 10 percent.

items.quote: The hoist rope shall not be wrapped around the load.
items.statement: The hoist rope must not be wrapped around the load.

items.quote: The load shall be attached to the hook by means of slings or other approved devices.
items.statement: The load must be attached to the hook by slings or other approved devices.

items.quote: The crane is level and where necessary blocked properly.
items.statement: The employer must assure that the crane is level and, where necessary, properly blocked.

items.quote: The load is well secured and properly balanced in the sling or lifting device before it is lifted more than a few inches.
items.statement: The employer must assure that the load is well secured and properly balanced in the sling or lifting device before it is lifted more than a few inches.

items.quote: Hoist rope shall not be kinked.
items.statement: Before hoisting starts, it must be noted that the hoist rope is not kinked.

items.quote: Multiple part lines shall not be twisted around each other.
items.statement: Before hoisting starts, it must be noted that multiple part lines are not twisted around each other.

items.quote: The hook shall be brought over the load in such a manner as to prevent swinging.
items.statement: Before hoisting, the hook must be brought over the load in a way that prevents swinging.

items.quote: There is no sudden acceleration or deceleration of the moving load.
items.statement: During hoisting, care must be taken that the moving load is not suddenly accelerated or decelerated.

items.quote: The load does not contact any obstructions.
items.statement: During hoisting, care must be taken that the load does not contact any obstructions.

items.quote: Side loading of booms shall be limited to freely suspended loads.
items.statement: Side loading of booms must be limited to freely suspended loads.

items.quote: Cranes shall not be used for dragging loads sideways.
items.statement: Cranes must not be used to drag loads sideways.

items.quote: No hoisting, lowering, swinging, or traveling shall be done while anyone is on the load or hook.
items.statement: No hoisting, lowering, swinging or traveling may be done while anyone is on the load or hook.

items.quote: The operator should avoid carrying loads over people.
items.statement: The operator should avoid carrying loads over people.

items.quote: On truck-mounted cranes, no loads shall be lifted over the front area except as approved by the crane manufacturer.
items.statement: On truck-mounted cranes, no loads may be lifted over the front area except as approved by the crane manufacturer.

items.quote: The operator shall test the brakes each time a load approaching the rated load is handled by raising it a few inches and applying the brakes.
items.statement: Each time a load approaching the rated load is handled, the operator must test the brakes by raising the load a few inches and applying them.

items.quote: Outriggers shall be used when the load to be handled at that particular radius exceeds the rated load without outriggers as given by the manufacturer for that crane.
items.statement: Outriggers must be used when the load at a particular radius exceeds the manufacturer's rated load without outriggers for that crane.

items.quote: Where floats are used they shall be securely attached to the outriggers.
items.statement: Where outrigger floats are used, they must be securely attached to the outriggers.

items.quote: Be strong enough to prevent crushing.
items.statement: Wood blocks used to support outriggers must be strong enough to prevent crushing.

items.quote: Be free from defects.
items.statement: Wood blocks used to support outriggers must be free from defects.

items.quote: Be of sufficient width and length to prevent shifting or toppling under load.
items.statement: Wood blocks used to support outriggers must be wide and long enough to prevent shifting or toppling under load.

items.quote: Neither the load nor the boom shall be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on their respective drums.
items.statement: Neither the load nor the boom may be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on their drums.

items.quote: Before lifting loads with locomotive cranes without using outriggers, means shall be applied to prevent the load from being carried by the truck springs.
items.statement: Before a locomotive crane lifts loads without outriggers, means must be applied to keep the truck springs from carrying the load.

items.quote: When two or more cranes are used to lift one load, one designated person shall be responsible for the operation.
items.statement: When two or more cranes lift one load, one designated person must be responsible for the operation.

items.quote: He shall be required to analyze the operation and instruct all personnel involved in the proper positioning, rigging of the load, and the movements to be made.
items.statement: In a lift of one load by two or more cranes, the responsible designated person must analyze the operation and instruct all personnel involved on positioning, rigging of the load and the movements to be made.

items.quote: The boom shall be carried in line with the direction of motion.
items.statement: In transit, the boom must be carried in line with the direction of motion.

items.quote: The superstructure shall be secured against rotation, except when negotiating turns when there is an operator in the cab or the boom is supported on a dolly.
items.statement: In transit, the superstructure must be secured against rotation, except when negotiating turns when there is an operator in the cab or the boom is supported on a dolly.

items.quote: The empty hook shall be lashed or otherwise restrained so that it cannot swing freely.
items.statement: In transit, the empty hook must be lashed or otherwise restrained so it cannot swing freely.

items.quote: Before traveling a crane with load, a designated person shall be responsible for determining and controlling safety.
items.statement: Before a crane travels with a load, a designated person must be responsible for determining and controlling safety.

items.quote: Decisions such as position of load, boom location, ground support, travel route, and speed of movement shall be in accord with his determinations.
items.statement: When a crane travels with a load, decisions such as load position, boom location, ground support, travel route and speed must accord with the designated person's determinations.

items.quote: A crane with or without load shall not be traveled with the boom so high that it may bounce back over the cab.
items.statement: A crane, with or without load, must not travel with the boom so high that it may bounce back over the cab.

items.quote: When rotating the crane, sudden starts and stops shall be avoided.
items.statement: Sudden starts and stops must be avoided when rotating the crane.

items.quote: Rotational speed shall be such that the load does not swing out beyond the radii at which it can be controlled.
items.statement: Crane rotational speed must be such that the load does not swing out beyond the radii at which it can be controlled.

items.quote: A tag or restraint line shall be used when rotation of the load is hazardous.
items.statement: A tag or restraint line must be used when rotating the load is hazardous.

items.quote: When a crane is to be operated at a fixed radius, the boom-hoist pawl or other positive locking device shall be engaged.
items.statement: When a crane is to be operated at a fixed radius, the boom-hoist pawl or other positive locking device must be engaged.

items.quote: Ropes shall not be handled on a winch head without the knowledge of the operator.
items.statement: Ropes must not be handled on a winch head without the operator's knowledge.

items.quote: While a winch head is being used, the operator shall be within convenient reach of the power unit control lever.
items.statement: While a winch head is in use, the operator must be within convenient reach of the power unit control lever.

items.quote: The operator shall not be permitted to leave his position at the controls while the load is suspended.
items.statement: The operator must not be permitted to leave the controls while the load is suspended.

items.quote: No person should be permitted to stand or pass under a load on the hook.
items.statement: No person should be permitted to stand or pass under a load on the hook.

items.quote: If the load must remain suspended for any considerable length of time, the operator shall hold the drum from rotating in the lowering direction by activating the positive controllable means of the operator's station.
items.statement: If a load must stay suspended for any considerable time, the operator must keep the drum from rotating in the lowering direction by activating the positive controllable means at the operator's station.

items.quote: Rail clamps shall not be used as a means of restraining tipping of a locomotive crane.
items.statement: Rail clamps must not be used to restrain tipping of a locomotive crane.

items.quote: Cranes shall not be operated without the full amount of any ballast or counterweight in place as specified by the maker
items.statement: Cranes must not be operated without the full ballast or counterweight specified by the maker in place, subject to the temporary exception for truck cranes that have dropped it.

items.quote: truck cranes that have dropped the ballast or counterweight may be operated temporarily with special care and only for light loads without full ballast or counterweight in place
items.statement: As an exception, truck cranes that have dropped their ballast or counterweight may be operated temporarily without the full amount in place, only with special care and for light loads.

items.quote: The ballast or counterweight in place specified by the manufacturer shall not be exceeded.
items.statement: The ballast or counterweight in place must not exceed what the manufacturer specifies.

items.quote: Necessary clothing and personal belongings shall be stored in such a manner as to not interfere with access or operation.
items.statement: Necessary clothing and personal belongings in cabs must be stored so they do not interfere with access or operation.

items.quote: Tools, oil cans, waste, extra fuses, and other necessary articles shall be stored in the tool box
items.statement: Tools, oil cans, waste, extra fuses and other necessary articles must be stored in the tool box.

items.quote: shall not be permitted to lie loose in or about the cab
items.statement: Tools, oil cans, waste, extra fuses and other necessary articles must not lie loose in or about the cab.

items.quote: Refueling with small portable containers shall be done with an approved safety type can equipped with an automatic closing cap and flame arrester.
items.statement: Refueling with small portable containers must use an approved safety type can with an automatic closing cap and flame arrester.

items.quote: Machines shall not be refueled with the engine running.
items.statement: Machines must not be refueled with the engine running.

items.quote: A carbon dioxide, dry chemical, or equivalent fire extinguisher shall be kept in the cab or vicinity of the crane.
items.statement: A carbon dioxide, dry chemical or equivalent fire extinguisher must be kept in the cab or vicinity of the crane.

items.quote: Operating and maintenance personnel shall be made familiar with the use and care of the fire extinguishers provided.
items.statement: Operating and maintenance personnel must be made familiar with the use and care of the fire extinguishers provided.

items.quote: A locomotive crane shall not be swung into a position where railway cars on an adjacent track might strike it, until it has been ascertained that cars are not being moved on the adjacent track and proper flag protection has been established.
items.statement: A locomotive crane must not be swung where adjacent-track railway cars might strike it until it is ascertained that cars are not being moved on that track and proper flag protection is established.

items.quote: For operations near overhead electric lines, see § 1910.333(c)(3).
items.statement: For operations near overhead electric lines, § 1910.333(c)(3) applies by reference.

items.quote: This section applies to slings used in conjunction with other material handling equipment for the movement of material by hoisting, in employments covered by this part.
items.statement: Section 1910.184 applies to slings used with other material handling equipment to move material by hoisting, in employments covered by Part 1910.

items.quote: The types of slings covered are those made from alloy steel chain, wire rope, metal mesh, natural or synthetic fiber rope (conventional three strand construction), and synthetic web (nylon, polyester, and polypropylene).
items.statement: The covered sling types are alloy steel chain, wire rope, metal mesh, natural or synthetic fiber rope of conventional three strand construction, and synthetic web (nylon, polyester and polypropylene).

items.quote: Angle of loading is the inclination of a leg or branch of a sling measured from the horizontal or vertical plane as shown in Fig. N-184-5
items.statement: Angle of loading is the inclination of a sling leg or branch measured from the horizontal or vertical plane, as shown in Fig. N-184-5.

items.quote: an angle of loading of five degrees or less from the vertical may be considered a vertical angle of loading
items.statement: An angle of loading of five degrees or less from the vertical may be considered a vertical angle of loading.

items.quote: Basket hitch is a sling configuration whereby the sling is passed under the load and has both ends, end attachments, eyes or handles on the hook or a single master link.
items.statement: A basket hitch is a configuration in which the sling passes under the load and has both ends, end attachments, eyes or handles on the hook or a single master link.

items.quote: Braided wire rope is a wire rope formed by plaiting component wire ropes.
items.statement: Braided wire rope is a wire rope formed by plaiting component wire ropes.

items.quote: Bridle wire rope sling is a sling composed of multiple wire rope legs with the top ends gathered in a fitting that goes over the lifting hook.
items.statement: A bridle wire rope sling has multiple wire rope legs with the top ends gathered in a fitting that goes over the lifting hook.

items.quote: Cable laid endless sling-mechanical joint is a wire rope sling made endless by joining the ends of a single length of cable laid rope with one or more metallic fittings.
items.statement: A cable laid endless sling-mechanical joint is a wire rope sling made endless by joining the ends of a single length of cable laid rope with one or more metallic fittings.

items.quote: Cable laid grommet-hand tucked is an endless wire rope sling made from one length of rope wrapped six times around a core formed by hand tucking the ends of the rope inside the six wraps.
items.statement: A hand tucked cable laid grommet is an endless wire rope sling made from one length of rope wrapped six times around a core formed by hand tucking the rope ends inside the six wraps.

items.quote: Cable laid rope is a wire rope composed of six wire ropes wrapped around a fiber or wire rope core.
items.statement: Cable laid rope is a wire rope composed of six wire ropes wrapped around a fiber or wire rope core.

items.quote: Cable laid rope sling-mechanical joint is a wire rope sling made from a cable laid rope with eyes fabricated by pressing or swaging one or more metal sleeves over the rope junction.
items.statement: A cable laid rope sling-mechanical joint is a wire rope sling made from cable laid rope with eyes fabricated by pressing or swaging one or more metal sleeves over the rope junction.

items.quote: Choker hitch is a sling configuration with one end of the sling passing under the load and through an end attachment, handle or eye on the other end of the sling.
items.statement: A choker hitch is a configuration with one end of the sling passing under the load and through an end attachment, handle or eye on the other end.

items.quote: Coating is an elastomer or other suitable material applied to a sling or to a sling component to impart desirable properties.
items.statement: Coating is an elastomer or other suitable material applied to a sling or sling component to impart desirable properties.

items.quote: Cross rod is a wire used to join spirals of metal mesh to form a complete fabric.
items.statement: A cross rod is a wire used to join spirals of metal mesh to form a complete fabric.

items.quote: Designated means selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.
items.statement: Designated means selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.

items.quote: Equivalent entity is a person or organization (including an employer) which, by possession of equipment, technical knowledge and skills, can perform with equal competence the same repairs and tests as the person or organization with which it is equated.
items.statement: An equivalent entity is a person or organization, including an employer, which by possessing equipment, technical knowledge and skills can perform the same repairs and tests with equal competence as the one it is equated with.

items.quote: Fabric (metal mesh) is the flexible portion of a metal mesh sling consisting of a series of transverse coils and cross rods.
items.statement: Fabric (metal mesh) is the flexible portion of a metal mesh sling, consisting of a series of transverse coils and cross rods.

items.quote: Female handle (choker) is a handle with a handle eye and a slot of such dimension as to permit passage of a male handle thereby allowing the use of a metal mesh sling in a choker hitch.
items.statement: A female handle (choker) has a handle eye and a slot sized to let a male handle pass through, allowing a metal mesh sling to be used in a choker hitch.

items.quote: Handle is a terminal fitting to which metal mesh fabric is attached.
items.statement: A handle is a terminal fitting to which metal mesh fabric is attached.

items.quote: Handle eye is an opening in a handle of a metal mesh sling shaped to accept a hook, shackle or other lifting device.
items.statement: A handle eye is an opening in a metal mesh sling handle shaped to accept a hook, shackle or other lifting device.

items.quote: Hitch is a sling configuration whereby the sling is fastened to an object or load, either directly to it or around it.
items.statement: A hitch is a configuration in which the sling is fastened to an object or load, either directly to it or around it.

items.quote: Link is a single ring of a chain.
items.statement: A link is a single ring of a chain.

items.quote: Male handle (triangle) is a handle with a handle eye.
items.statement: A male handle (triangle) is a handle with a handle eye.

items.quote: Master coupling link is an alloy steel welded coupling link used as an intermediate link to join alloy steel chain to master links.
items.statement: A master coupling link is an alloy steel welded coupling link used as an intermediate link to join alloy steel chain to master links.

items.quote: Master link or gathering ring is a forged or welded steel link used to support all members (legs) of an alloy steel chain sling or wire rope sling.
items.statement: A master link or gathering ring is a forged or welded steel link used to support all legs of an alloy steel chain sling or wire rope sling.

items.quote: Mechanical coupling link is a nonwelded, mechanically closed steel link used to attach master links, hooks, etc., to alloy steel chain.
items.statement: A mechanical coupling link is a nonwelded, mechanically closed steel link used to attach items such as master links and hooks to alloy steel chain.

items.quote: Proof load is the load applied in performance of a proof test.
items.statement: Proof load is the load applied in performing a proof test.

items.quote: Proof test is a nondestructive tension test performed by the sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity to verify construction and workmanship of a sling.
items.statement: A proof test is a nondestructive tension test performed by the sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity to verify a sling's construction and workmanship.

items.quote: Rated capacity or working load limit is the maximum working load permitted by the provisions of this section.
items.statement: Rated capacity or working load limit is the maximum working load permitted by the provisions of this section.

items.quote: Reach is the effective length of an alloy steel chain sling measured from the top bearing surface of the upper terminal component to the bottom bearing surface of the lower terminal component.
items.statement: Reach is the effective length of an alloy steel chain sling, measured from the top bearing surface of the upper terminal component to the bottom bearing surface of the lower terminal component.

items.quote: Selvage edge is the finished edge of synthetic webbing designed to prevent unraveling.
items.statement: A selvage edge is the finished edge of synthetic webbing designed to prevent unraveling.

items.quote: Sling is an assembly which connects the load to the material handling equipment.
items.statement: A sling is an assembly that connects the load to the material handling equipment.

items.quote: Sling manufacturer is a person or organization that assembles sling components into their final form for sale to users.
items.statement: A sling manufacturer is a person or organization that assembles sling components into their final form for sale to users.

items.quote: Spiral is a single transverse coil that is the basic element from which metal mesh is fabricated.
items.statement: A spiral is a single transverse coil that is the basic element from which metal mesh is fabricated.

items.quote: Strand laid endless sling-mechanical joint is a wire rope sling made endless from one length of rope with the ends joined by one or more metallic fittings.
items.statement: A strand laid endless sling-mechanical joint is a wire rope sling made endless from one length of rope with the ends joined by one or more metallic fittings.

items.quote: Strand laid grommet-hand tucked is an endless wire rope sling made from one length of strand wrapped six times around a core formed by hand tucking the ends of the strand inside the six wraps.
items.statement: A hand tucked strand laid grommet is an endless wire rope sling made from one length of strand wrapped six times around a core formed by hand tucking the strand ends inside the six wraps.

items.quote: Strand laid rope is a wire rope made with strands (usually six or eight) wrapped around a fiber core, wire strand core, or independent wire rope core (IWRC).
items.statement: Strand laid rope is a wire rope made with strands, usually six or eight, wrapped around a fiber core, wire strand core or independent wire rope core (IWRC).

items.quote: Vertical hitch is a method of supporting a load by a single, vertical part or leg of the sling.
items.statement: A vertical hitch is a method of supporting a load by a single, vertical part or leg of the sling.

items.quote: Slings that are damaged or defective shall not be used.
items.statement: Damaged or defective slings must not be used.

items.quote: Slings shall not be shortened with knots or bolts or other makeshift devices.
items.statement: Slings must not be shortened with knots, bolts or other makeshift devices.

items.quote: Sling legs shall not be kinked.
items.statement: Sling legs must not be kinked.

items.quote: Slings shall not be loaded in excess of their rated capacities.
items.statement: Slings must not be loaded beyond their rated capacities.

items.quote: Slings used in a basket hitch shall have the loads balanced to prevent slippage.
items.statement: Loads on slings used in a basket hitch must be balanced to prevent slippage.

items.quote: Slings shall be securely attached to their loads.
items.statement: Slings must be securely attached to their loads.

items.quote: Slings shall be padded or protected from the sharp edges of their loads.
items.statement: Slings must be padded or protected from the sharp edges of their loads.

items.quote: Suspended loads shall be kept clear of all obstructions.
items.statement: Suspended loads must be kept clear of all obstructions.

items.quote: All employees shall be kept clear of loads about to be lifted and of suspended loads.
items.statement: Whenever any sling is used, all employees must be kept clear of loads about to be lifted and of suspended loads.

items.quote: Hands or fingers shall not be placed between the sling and its load while the sling is being tightened around the load.
items.statement: Hands or fingers must not be placed between the sling and its load while the sling is being tightened around the load.

items.quote: Shock loading is prohibited.
items.statement: Shock loading of slings is prohibited.

items.quote: A sling shall not be pulled from under a load when the load is resting on the sling.
items.statement: A sling must not be pulled from under a load while the load is resting on it.

items.quote: Employers must not load a sling in excess of its recommended safe working load as prescribed by the sling manufacturer on the identification markings permanently affixed to the sling.
items.statement: Employers must not load a sling beyond the recommended safe working load that the sling manufacturer prescribes on its permanently affixed identification markings.

items.quote: Employers must not use slings without affixed and legible identification markings.
items.statement: Employers must not use slings that lack affixed and legible identification markings.

items.quote: Each day before being used, the sling and all fastenings and attachments shall be inspected for damage or defects by a competent person designated by the employer.
items.statement: Each day before use, a competent person designated by the employer must inspect the sling and all fastenings and attachments for damage or defects.

items.quote: Additional inspections shall be performed during sling use, where service conditions warrant.
items.statement: Additional inspections must be performed during sling use where service conditions warrant.

items.quote: Damaged or defective slings shall be immediately removed from service.
items.statement: Damaged or defective slings must be immediately removed from service.

items.quote: Alloy steel chain slings shall have permanently affixed durable identification stating size, grade, rated capacity, and reach.
items.statement: Alloy steel chain slings must have permanently affixed, durable identification stating size, grade, rated capacity and reach.

items.quote: Hooks, rings, oblong links, pear shaped links, welded or mechanical coupling links or other attachments shall have a rated capacity at least equal to that of the alloy steel chain with which they are used or the sling shall not be used in excess of the rated capacity of the weakest component.
items.statement: Hooks, rings, oblong links, pear shaped links, welded or mechanical coupling links or other attachments must have a rated capacity at least equal to that of the alloy steel chain they are used with, or the sling must not be used above the rated capacity of the weakest component.

items.quote: Makeshift links or fasteners formed from bolts or rods, or other such attachments, shall not be used.
items.statement: Makeshift links or fasteners formed from bolts or rods, or other such attachments, must not be used on alloy steel chain slings.

items.quote: In addition to the inspection required by paragraph (d) of this section, a thorough periodic inspection of alloy steel chain slings in use shall be made on a regular basis
items.statement: In addition to the inspection required by paragraph (d), alloy steel chain slings in use must get a thorough periodic inspection on a regular basis.

items.quote: to be determined on the basis of (A) frequency of sling use; (B) severity of service conditions; (C) nature of lifts being made; and (D) experience gained on the service life of slings used in similar circumstances.
items.statement: The frequency of thorough periodic inspections of alloy steel chain slings must be based on frequency of sling use, severity of service conditions, nature of lifts, and experience with the service life of slings used in similar circumstances.

items.quote: Such inspections shall in no event be at intervals greater than once every 12 months.
items.statement: The interval between thorough periodic inspections of alloy steel chain slings must never be greater than once every 12 months.

items.quote: The employer shall make and maintain a record of the most recent month in which each alloy steel chain sling was thoroughly inspected
items.statement: The employer must make and maintain a record of the most recent month in which each alloy steel chain sling was thoroughly inspected.

items.quote: shall make such record available for examination.
items.statement: The employer must make the record of the most recent thorough inspection of each alloy steel chain sling available for examination.

items.quote: The thorough inspection of alloy steel chain slings shall be performed by a competent person designated by the employer
items.statement: The thorough inspection of alloy steel chain slings must be performed by a competent person designated by the employer.

items.quote: shall include a thorough inspection for wear, defective welds, deformation and increase in length.
items.statement: The thorough inspection of alloy steel chain slings must include a thorough inspection for wear, defective welds, deformation and increase in length.

items.quote: Where such defects or deterioration are present, the sling shall be immediately removed from service.
items.statement: An alloy steel chain sling must be immediately removed from service when the defects or deterioration covered by the thorough inspection are present.

items.quote: The employer shall ensure that before use, each new, repaired, or reconditioned alloy steel chain sling, including all welded components in the sling assembly, shall be proof tested by the sling manufacturer or equivalent entity, in accordance with paragraph 5.2 of the American Society of Testing and Materials Specification A391-65
items.statement: The employer must ensure that each new, repaired or reconditioned alloy steel chain sling, including all welded components in the assembly, is proof tested before use by the sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity, in accordance with paragraph 5.2 of ASTM A391-65 (ANSI G61.1-1968).

items.quote: The employer shall retain a certificate of the proof test and shall make it available for examination.
items.statement: The employer must retain a certificate of the alloy steel chain sling proof test and make it available for examination.

items.quote: Employers must permanently remove an alloy steel-chain slings from service if it is heated above 1000 degrees F.
items.statement: Employers must permanently remove an alloy steel chain sling from service if it is heated above 1000 degrees F.

items.quote: When exposed to service temperatures in excess of 600 degrees F, employers must reduce the maximum working-load limits permitted by the chain manufacturer in accordance with the chain or sling manufacturer's recommendations.
items.statement: When alloy steel chain slings are exposed to service temperatures above 600 degrees F, employers must reduce the chain manufacturer's permitted maximum working-load limits according to the chain or sling manufacturer's recommendations.

items.quote: Worn or damaged alloy steel chain slings or attachments shall not be used until repaired.
items.statement: Worn or damaged alloy steel chain slings or attachments must not be used until repaired.

items.quote: When welding or heat testing is performed, slings shall not be used unless repaired, reconditioned and proof tested by the sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity.
items.statement: When welding or heat testing is performed, alloy steel chain slings must not be used unless repaired, reconditioned and proof tested by the sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity.

items.quote: Mechanical coupling links or low carbon steel repair links shall not be used to repair broken lengths of chain.
items.statement: Mechanical coupling links or low carbon steel repair links must not be used to repair broken lengths of chain.

items.quote: If the chain size at any point of the link is less than that stated in Table N-184-1, the employer must remove the chain from service.
items.statement: The employer must remove a chain from service if the chain size at any point of a link is less than that stated in Table N-184-1.
For 1⁄4-inch chain, the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 13⁄64 inch.
For 3⁄8-inch chain, the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 19⁄64 inch.
For 1⁄2-inch chain, the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 25⁄64 inch.
For 5⁄8-inch chain, the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 31⁄64 inch.
For 3⁄4-inch chain, the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 19⁄32 inch.
For 7⁄8-inch chain, the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 45⁄64 inch.
For 1-inch chain, the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 13⁄16 inch.
For 1-1⁄8-inch chain (printed as "11⁄8"), the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 29⁄32 inch.
For 1-1⁄4-inch chain (printed as "11⁄4"), the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 1 inch.
For 1-3⁄8-inch chain (printed as "13⁄8"), the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 1-3⁄32 inches (printed as "13⁄32").
For 1-1⁄2-inch chain (printed as "11⁄2"), the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 1-3⁄16 inches (printed as "13⁄16").
For 1-3⁄4-inch chain (printed as "13⁄4"), the minimum allowable chain size at any point of a link is 1-13⁄32 inches (printed as "113⁄32").

items.quote: Alloy steel chain slings with cracked or deformed master links, coupling links or other components shall be removed from service.
items.statement: Alloy steel chain slings with cracked or deformed master links, coupling links or other components must be removed from service.

items.quote: Slings shall be removed from service if hooks are cracked
items.statement: Alloy steel chain slings must be removed from service if hooks are cracked.

items.quote: have been opened more than 15 percent of the normal throat opening measured at the narrowest point
