items.statement: Alloy steel chain slings must be removed from service if hooks have been opened more than 15 percent of the normal throat opening, measured at the narrowest point.

items.quote: twisted more than 10 degrees from the plane of the unbent hook.
items.statement: Alloy steel chain slings must be removed from service if hooks are twisted more than 10 degrees from the plane of the unbent hook.

items.quote: Employers must use only wire-rope slings that have permanently affixed and legible identification markings as prescribed by the manufacturer, and that indicate the recommended safe working load for the type(s) of hitch(es) used, the angle upon which it is based, and the number of legs if more than one.
items.statement: Employers must use only wire-rope slings with permanently affixed, legible identification markings, as prescribed by the manufacturer, showing the recommended safe working load for the hitch type(s) used, the angle it is based on, and the number of legs if more than one.

items.quote: Cable laid and 6 × 19 and 6 × 37 slings shall have a minimum clear length of wire rope 10 times the component rope diameter between splices, sleeves or end fittings.
items.statement: Cable laid, 6 × 19 and 6 × 37 slings must have a minimum clear length of wire rope between splices, sleeves or end fittings of 10 times the component rope diameter.

items.quote: Braided slings shall have a minimum clear length of wire rope 40 times the component rope diameter between the loops or end fittings.
items.statement: Braided slings must have a minimum clear length of wire rope between the loops or end fittings of 40 times the component rope diameter.

items.quote: Cable laid grommets, strand laid grommets and endless slings shall have a minimum circumferential length of 96 times their body diameter.
items.statement: Cable laid grommets, strand laid grommets and endless slings must have a minimum circumferential length of 96 times their body diameter.

items.quote: Fiber core wire rope slings of all grades shall be permanently removed from service if they are exposed to temperatures in excess of 200 °F.
items.statement: Fiber core wire rope slings of all grades must be permanently removed from service if exposed to temperatures above 200 °F.

items.quote: When nonfiber core wire rope slings of any grade are used at temperatures above 400 °F or below minus 60 °F, recommendations of the sling manufacturer regarding use at that temperature shall be followed.
items.statement: When nonfiber core wire rope slings of any grade are used above 400 °F or below minus 60 °F, the sling manufacturer's recommendations for use at that temperature must be followed.

items.quote: Welding of end attachments, except covers to thimbles, shall be performed prior to the assembly of the sling.
items.statement: Welding of wire-rope sling end attachments, except covers to thimbles, must be performed before the sling is assembled.

items.quote: All welded end attachments shall not be used unless proof tested by the manufacturer or equivalent entity at twice their rated capacity prior to initial use.
items.statement: Welded end attachments must not be used unless the manufacturer or an equivalent entity proof tested them at twice their rated capacity before initial use.

items.quote: The employer shall retain a certificate of the proof test, and make it available for examination.
items.statement: The employer must retain a certificate of the welded end attachment proof test and make it available for examination.

items.quote: Ten randomly distributed broken wires in one rope lay
items.statement: A wire rope sling must be immediately removed from service if it has ten randomly distributed broken wires in one rope lay.
items.unit: broken wires in one rope lay

items.quote: five broken wires in one strand in one rope lay.
items.statement: A wire rope sling must be immediately removed from service if it has five broken wires in one strand in one rope lay.
items.unit: broken wires in one strand in one rope lay

items.quote: Wear or scraping of one-third the original diameter of outside individual wires.
items.statement: A wire rope sling must be immediately removed from service if outside individual wires have wear or scraping of one-third their original diameter.

items.quote: Kinking, crushing, bird caging or any other damage resulting in distortion of the wire rope structure.
items.statement: A wire rope sling must be immediately removed from service if kinking, crushing, bird caging or any other damage has distorted the wire rope structure.

items.quote: Evidence of heat damage.
items.statement: A wire rope sling must be immediately removed from service if there is evidence of heat damage.

items.quote: End attachments that are cracked, deformed or worn.
items.statement: A wire rope sling must be immediately removed from service if end attachments are cracked, deformed or worn.

items.quote: Hooks that have been opened more than 15 percent of the normal throat opening measured at the narrowest point
items.statement: A wire rope sling must be immediately removed from service if hooks have been opened more than 15 percent of the normal throat opening, measured at the narrowest point.

items.quote: twisted more than 10 degrees from the plane of the unbent hook.
items.statement: A wire rope sling must be immediately removed from service if hooks are twisted more than 10 degrees from the plane of the unbent hook.

items.quote: Corrosion of the rope or end attachments.
items.statement: A wire rope sling must be immediately removed from service if the rope or end attachments are corroded.

items.quote: Each metal mesh sling shall have permanently affixed to it a durable marking that states the rated capacity for vertical basket hitch and choker hitch loadings.
items.statement: Each metal mesh sling must have a permanently affixed durable marking stating the rated capacity for vertical basket hitch and choker hitch loadings.

items.quote: Handles shall have a rated capacity at least equal to the metal fabric
items.statement: Metal mesh sling handles must have a rated capacity at least equal to that of the metal fabric.

items.quote: exhibit no deformation after proof testing.
items.statement: Metal mesh sling handles must show no deformation after proof testing.

items.quote: The rated capacity of the sling is not reduced.
items.statement: The fabric and handles of a metal mesh sling must be joined so that the sling's rated capacity is not reduced.

items.quote: The load is evenly distributed across the width of the fabric.
items.statement: The fabric and handles of a metal mesh sling must be joined so that the load is evenly distributed across the width of the fabric.

items.quote: Sharp edges will not damage the fabric.
items.statement: The fabric and handles of a metal mesh sling must be joined so that sharp edges will not damage the fabric.

items.quote: Coatings which diminish the rated capacity of a sling shall not be applied.
items.statement: Coatings that diminish the rated capacity of a metal mesh sling must not be applied.

items.quote: All new and repaired metal mesh slings, including handles, shall not be used unless proof tested by the manufacturer or equivalent entity at a minimum of 1 1/2 times their rated capacity.
items.statement: New and repaired metal mesh slings, including handles, must not be used unless the manufacturer or an equivalent entity proof tested them at a minimum of 1 1/2 times their rated capacity.

items.quote: Elastomer impregnated slings shall be proof tested before coating.
items.statement: Elastomer impregnated metal mesh slings must be proof tested before coating.

items.quote: Metal mesh slings which are not impregnated with elastomers may be used in a temperature range from minus 20 °F to plus 550 °F without decreasing the working load limit.
items.statement: Metal mesh slings not impregnated with elastomers may be used from minus 20 °F to plus 550 °F without decreasing the working load limit.

items.quote: Metal mesh slings impregnated with polyvinyl chloride or neoprene may be used only in a temperature range from zero degrees to plus 200 °F.
items.statement: Metal mesh slings impregnated with polyvinyl chloride or neoprene may be used only from zero degrees to plus 200 °F.

items.quote: For operations outside these temperature ranges or for metal mesh slings impregnated with other materials, the sling manufacturer's recommendations shall be followed.
items.statement: For operations outside the stated metal mesh sling temperature ranges, or for slings impregnated with other materials, the sling manufacturer's recommendations must be followed.

items.quote: Metal mesh slings which are repaired shall not be used unless repaired by a metal mesh sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity.
items.statement: Repaired metal mesh slings must not be used unless repaired by a metal mesh sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity.

items.quote: Once repaired, each sling shall be permanently marked or tagged, or a written record maintained, to indicate the date and nature of the repairs and the person or organization that performed the repairs.
items.statement: Once repaired, each metal mesh sling must be permanently marked or tagged, or a written record kept, showing the date and nature of the repairs and who (person or organization) performed them.

items.quote: Records of repairs shall be made available for examination.
items.statement: Records of metal mesh sling repairs must be made available for examination.

items.quote: A broken weld or broken brazed joint along the sling edge.
items.statement: A metal mesh sling must be immediately removed from service if there is a broken weld or broken brazed joint along the sling edge.

items.quote: Reduction in wire diameter of 25 per cent due to abrasion
items.statement: A metal mesh sling must be immediately removed from service if wire diameter is reduced by 25 percent due to abrasion.

items.quote: Reduction in wire diameter of 25 per cent due to abrasion or 15 per cent due to corrosion.
items.statement: A metal mesh sling must be immediately removed from service if wire diameter is reduced by 15 percent due to corrosion.

items.quote: Lack of flexibility due to distortion of the fabric.
items.statement: A metal mesh sling must be immediately removed from service if it lacks flexibility due to distortion of the fabric.

items.quote: Distortion of the female handle so that the depth of the slot is increased more than 10 per cent.
items.statement: A metal mesh sling must be immediately removed from service if the female handle is distorted so that the slot depth is increased more than 10 percent.

items.quote: Distortion of either handle so that the width of the eye is decreased more than 10 per cent.
items.statement: A metal mesh sling must be immediately removed from service if either handle is distorted so that the eye width is decreased more than 10 percent.

items.quote: A 15 percent reduction of the original cross sectional area of metal at any point around the handle eye.
items.statement: A metal mesh sling must be immediately removed from service if the original cross sectional area of metal is reduced by 15 percent at any point around the handle eye.

items.quote: Distortion of either handle out of its plane.
items.statement: A metal mesh sling must be immediately removed from service if either handle is distorted out of its plane.

items.quote: Employers must use natural and synthetic fiber-rope slings that have permanently affixed and legible identification markings stating the rated capacity for the type(s) of hitch(es) used
items.statement: Employers must use natural and synthetic fiber-rope slings with permanently affixed and legible identification markings stating the rated capacity for the type(s) of hitch(es) used.

items.quote: identification markings stating the rated capacity for the type(s) of hitch(es) used and the angle upon which it is based
items.statement: Fiber-rope sling identification markings must state the angle on which the rated capacity is based.

items.quote: identification markings stating the rated capacity for the type(s) of hitch(es) used and the angle upon which it is based, type of fiber material
items.statement: Fiber-rope sling identification markings must state the type of fiber material.

items.quote: and the number of legs if more than one.
items.statement: Fiber-rope sling identification markings must state the number of legs if there is more than one.

items.quote: Natural and synthetic fiber rope slings, except for wet frozen slings, may be used in a temperature range from minus 20 °F to plus 180 °F without decreasing the working load limit.
items.statement: Natural and synthetic fiber rope slings, except wet frozen slings, may be used from minus 20 °F to plus 180 °F without decreasing the working load limit.

items.quote: For operations outside this temperature range and for wet frozen slings, the sling manufacturer's recommendations shall be followed.
items.statement: For fiber rope sling operations outside the minus 20 °F to plus 180 °F range, and for wet frozen slings, the sling manufacturer's recommendations must be followed.

items.quote: Spliced fiber rope slings shall not be used unless they have been spliced in accordance with the following minimum requirements and in accordance with any additional recommendations of the manufacturer
items.statement: Spliced fiber rope slings must not be used unless spliced according to the listed minimum requirements and any additional manufacturer recommendations.

items.quote: In manila rope, eye splices shall consist of at least three full tucks
items.statement: Eye splices in manila rope must have at least three full tucks.

items.quote: short splices shall consist of at least six full tucks, three on each side of the splice center line.
items.statement: Short splices in manila rope must have at least six full tucks, three on each side of the splice center line.
items.value: at least six (three on each side)

items.quote: In synthetic fiber rope, eye splices shall consist of at least four full tucks
items.statement: Eye splices in synthetic fiber rope must have at least four full tucks.

items.quote: short splices shall consist of at least eight full tucks, four on each side of the center line.
items.statement: Short splices in synthetic fiber rope must have at least eight full tucks, four on each side of the center line.
items.value: at least eight (four on each side)

items.quote: Strand end tails shall not be trimmed flush with the surface of the rope immediately adjacent to the full tucks. This applies to all types of fiber rope and both eye and short splices.
items.statement: For all types of fiber rope and both eye and short splices, strand end tails must not be trimmed flush with the rope surface immediately adjacent to the full tucks.

items.quote: For fiber rope under one inch in diameter, the tail shall project at least six rope diameters beyond the last full tuck.
items.statement: For fiber rope under one inch in diameter, the splice tail must project at least six rope diameters beyond the last full tuck.

items.quote: For fiber rope one inch in diameter and larger, the tail shall project at least six inches beyond the last full tuck.
items.statement: For fiber rope one inch in diameter and larger, the splice tail must project at least six inches beyond the last full tuck.

items.quote: Where a projecting tail interferes with the use of the sling, the tail shall be tapered and spliced into the body of the rope using at least two additional tucks (which will require a tail length of approximately six rope diameters beyond the last full tuck).
items.statement: Where a projecting tail interferes with use of a fiber rope sling, it must be tapered and spliced into the rope body with at least two additional tucks, which requires a tail length of about six rope diameters beyond the last full tuck.

items.quote: Fiber rope slings shall have a minimum clear length of rope between eye splices equal to 10 times the rope diameter.
items.statement: Fiber rope slings must have a minimum clear length of rope between eye splices equal to 10 times the rope diameter.

items.quote: Knots shall not be used in lieu of splices.
items.statement: Knots must not be used in place of splices in fiber rope slings.

items.quote: Clamps not designed specifically for fiber ropes shall not be used for splicing.
items.statement: Clamps not designed specifically for fiber ropes must not be used for splicing.

items.quote: the eye shall be of such size to provide an included angle of not greater than 60 degrees at the splice when the eye is placed over the load or support.
items.statement: All fiber rope eye splices must have an eye sized so the included angle at the splice is not greater than 60 degrees when the eye is placed over the load or support.

items.quote: Fiber rope slings shall not be used if end attachments in contact with the rope have sharp edges or projections.
items.statement: Fiber rope slings must not be used if end attachments in contact with the rope have sharp edges or projections.

items.quote: (i) Abnormal wear.
items.statement: Natural and synthetic fiber rope slings must be immediately removed from service if abnormal wear is present.

items.quote: Powdered fiber between strands.
items.statement: Natural and synthetic fiber rope slings must be immediately removed from service if there is powdered fiber between strands.

items.quote: Broken or cut fibers.
items.statement: Natural and synthetic fiber rope slings must be immediately removed from service if there are broken or cut fibers.

items.quote: Variations in the size or roundness of strands.
items.statement: Natural and synthetic fiber rope slings must be immediately removed from service if there are variations in the size or roundness of strands.

items.quote: Discoloration or rotting.
items.statement: Natural and synthetic fiber rope slings must be immediately removed from service if there is discoloration or rotting.

items.quote: Distortion of hardware in the sling.
items.statement: Natural and synthetic fiber rope slings must be immediately removed from service if hardware in the sling is distorted.

items.quote: Only fiber rope slings made from new rope shall be used.
items.statement: Only fiber rope slings made from new rope may be used.

items.quote: Use of repaired or reconditioned fiber rope slings is prohibited.
items.statement: Using repaired or reconditioned fiber rope slings is prohibited.

items.quote: Each sling shall be marked or coded to show the rated capacities for each type of hitch
items.statement: Each synthetic web sling must be marked or coded to show the rated capacities for each type of hitch.

items.quote: Each sling shall be marked or coded to show the rated capacities for each type of hitch and type of synthetic web material.
items.statement: Each synthetic web sling must be marked or coded to show the type of synthetic web material.

items.quote: Synthetic webbing shall be of uniform thickness and width
items.statement: Synthetic webbing must be of uniform thickness and width.

items.quote: selvage edges shall not be split from the webbing's width.
items.statement: Selvage edges of synthetic webbing must not be split from the webbing's width.

items.quote: Of a minimum breaking strength equal to that of the sling
items.statement: Synthetic web sling fittings must have a minimum breaking strength equal to that of the sling.

items.quote: Free of all sharp edges that could in any way damage the webbing.
items.statement: Synthetic web sling fittings must be free of all sharp edges that could in any way damage the webbing.

items.quote: Stitching shall be the only method used to attach end fittings to webbing and to form eyes.
items.statement: Stitching must be the only method used to attach end fittings to synthetic webbing and to form eyes.

items.quote: The thread shall be in an even pattern
items.statement: The stitching thread must be in an even pattern.

items.quote: contain a sufficient number of stitches to develop the full breaking strength of the sling.
items.statement: The stitching must contain enough stitches to develop the full breaking strength of the sling.

items.quote: Nylon web slings shall not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of acids or phenolics are present.
items.statement: Nylon web slings must not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of acids or phenolics are present.

items.quote: Polyester and polypropylene web slings shall not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of caustics are present.
items.statement: Polyester and polypropylene web slings must not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of caustics are present.

items.quote: Web slings with aluminum fittings shall not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of caustics are present.
items.statement: Web slings with aluminum fittings must not be used where fumes, vapors, sprays, mists or liquids of caustics are present.

items.quote: Synthetic web slings of polyester and nylon shall not be used at temperatures in excess of 180 °F.
items.statement: Polyester and nylon synthetic web slings must not be used at temperatures above 180 °F.

items.quote: Polypropylene web slings shall not be used at temperatures in excess of 200 °F.
items.statement: Polypropylene web slings must not be used at temperatures above 200 °F.

items.quote: Synthetic web slings which are repaired shall not be used unless repaired by a sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity.
items.statement: Repaired synthetic web slings must not be used unless repaired by a sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity.

items.quote: Each repaired sling shall be proof tested by the manufacturer or equivalent entity to twice the rated capacity prior to its return to service.
items.statement: Each repaired synthetic web sling must be proof tested by the manufacturer or equivalent entity to twice the rated capacity before returning to service.

items.quote: The employer shall retain a certificate of the proof test and make it available for examination.
items.statement: The employer must retain a certificate of the repaired sling's proof test and make it available for examination.

items.quote: Slings, including webbing and fittings, which have been repaired in a temporary manner shall not be used.
items.statement: Synthetic web slings, including webbing and fittings, that have been repaired in a temporary manner must not be used.

items.quote: Acid or caustic burns;
items.statement: Synthetic web slings must be immediately removed from service if there are acid or caustic burns.

items.quote: Melting or charring of any part of the sling surface;
items.statement: Synthetic web slings must be immediately removed from service if any part of the sling surface is melted or charred.

items.quote: Snags, punctures, tears or cuts;
items.statement: Synthetic web slings must be immediately removed from service if there are snags, punctures, tears or cuts.

items.quote: Broken or worn stitches
items.statement: Synthetic web slings must be immediately removed from service if there are broken or worn stitches.

items.quote: Distortion of fittings.
items.statement: Synthetic web slings must be immediately removed from service if fittings are distorted.

items.quote: This standard applies to power-operated equipment, when used in construction, that can hoist, lower and horizontally move a suspended load.
items.statement: This standard applies to power-operated equipment, when used in construction, that can hoist, lower and horizontally move a suspended load, except for the items excluded in paragraph (c).

items.quote: Such equipment includes, but is not limited to: Articulating cranes (such as knuckle-boom cranes); crawler cranes; floating cranes; cranes on barges; locomotive cranes;
items.statement: Covered equipment includes, but is not limited to, articulating, crawler, floating, locomotive, mobile, industrial, tower, pedestal, portal, overhead and gantry, straddle and sideboom cranes, cranes on barges, dedicated pile drivers, service/mechanic trucks with a hoisting device, a crane on a monorail, derricks, and variations of such equipment, except items excluded in paragraph (c).

items.quote: multi-purpose machines when configured to hoist and lower (by means of a winch or hook) and horizontally move a suspended load
items.statement: Multi-purpose machines are covered equipment when configured to hoist and lower (by means of a winch or hook) and horizontally move a suspended load.

items.quote: This standard applies to equipment included in paragraph (a) of this section when used with attachments. Such attachments, whether crane-attached or suspended include, but are not limited to:
items.statement: The standard applies to covered equipment when used with attachments, whether crane-attached or suspended, including but not limited to hooks, magnets, grapples, buckets, drag lines, personnel platforms, augers or drills and pile driving equipment.

items.quote: Machinery included in paragraph (a) of this section while it has been converted or adapted for a non-hoisting/lifting use.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover otherwise included machinery while it has been converted or adapted for a non-hoisting/lifting use, such as power shovels, excavators and concrete pumps.

items.quote: Power shovels, excavators, wheel loaders, backhoes, loader backhoes, track loaders.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover power shovels, excavators, wheel loaders, backhoes, loader backhoes and track loaders.

items.quote: This machinery is also excluded when used with chains, slings or other rigging to lift suspended loads.
items.statement: Power shovels, excavators, wheel loaders, backhoes, loader backhoes and track loaders remain excluded even when used with chains, slings or other rigging to lift suspended loads.

items.quote: Automotive wreckers and tow trucks when used to clear wrecks and haul vehicles.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover automotive wreckers and tow trucks when used to clear wrecks and haul vehicles.

items.quote: Digger derricks when used for augering holes for poles carrying electric or telecommunication lines, placing and removing the poles, and for handling associated materials for installation on, or removal from, the poles
items.statement: The subpart does not cover digger derricks when used for augering holes for poles carrying electric or telecommunication lines, placing and removing the poles, and handling associated materials for installation on or removal from the poles.

items.quote: or when used for any other work subject to subpart V of this part.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover digger derricks when used for any other work subject to subpart V of Part 1926.

items.quote: To be eligible for this exclusion, digger-derrick use in work subject to subpart V of this part must comply with all of the provisions of that subpart
items.statement: To be eligible for the digger-derrick exclusion, digger-derrick use in work subject to subpart V must comply with all provisions of that subpart.

items.quote: digger-derrick use in construction work for telecommunication service (as defined at § 1910.268(s)(40)) must comply with all of the provisions of § 1910.268.
items.statement: To be eligible for the digger-derrick exclusion, digger-derrick use in construction work for telecommunication service (as defined at § 1910.268(s)(40)) must comply with all provisions of § 1910.268.

items.quote: Machinery originally designed as vehicle-mounted aerial devices (for lifting personnel) and self-propelled elevating work platforms.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover machinery originally designed as vehicle-mounted aerial devices for lifting personnel, or self-propelled elevating work platforms.

items.quote: Telescopic/hydraulic gantry systems.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover telescopic/hydraulic gantry systems.

items.quote: Stacker cranes.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover stacker cranes.

items.quote: Powered industrial trucks (forklifts), except when configured to hoist and lower (by means of a winch or hook) and horizontally move a suspended load.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover powered industrial trucks (forklifts), except when configured to hoist and lower (by means of a winch or hook) and horizontally move a suspended load.

items.quote: Mechanic's truck with a hoisting device when used in activities related to equipment maintenance and repair.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover a mechanic's truck with a hoisting device when used in activities related to equipment maintenance and repair.

items.quote: Machinery that hoists by using a come-a-long or chainfall.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover machinery that hoists by using a come-a-long or chainfall.

items.quote: Dedicated drilling rigs.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover dedicated drilling rigs.

items.quote: Gin poles when used for the erection of communication towers.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover gin poles when used for the erection of communication towers.

items.quote: Tree trimming and tree removal work.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover tree trimming and tree removal work.

items.quote: Anchor handling or dredge-related operations with a vessel or barge using an affixed A-frame.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover anchor handling or dredge-related operations with a vessel or barge using an affixed A-frame.

items.quote: Roustabouts.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover roustabouts.

items.quote: Helicopter cranes.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover helicopter cranes.

items.quote: Articulating/knuckle-boom truck cranes that deliver material to a construction site when used to transfer materials from the truck crane to the ground, without arranging the materials in a particular sequence for hoisting.
items.statement: The material delivery exclusion covers articulating/knuckle-boom truck cranes delivering material to a construction site when used to transfer materials from the truck crane to the ground without arranging them in a particular sequence for hoisting.

items.quote: when the crane is used to transfer building supply sheet goods or building supply packaged materials from the truck crane onto a structure, using a fork/cradle at the end of the boom, but only when the truck crane is equipped with a properly functioning automatic overload prevention device.
items.statement: The material delivery exclusion covers articulating/knuckle-boom truck cranes delivering to a construction site when used to transfer building supply sheet goods or packaged materials from the truck crane onto a structure with a fork/cradle at the end of the boom, but only when the truck crane has a properly functioning automatic overload prevention device.

items.quote: Such sheet goods or packaged materials include, but are not limited to: Sheets of sheet rock, sheets of plywood, bags of cement, sheets or packages of roofing shingles, and rolls of roofing felt.
items.statement: Building supply sheet goods or packaged materials include, but are not limited to, sheets of sheet rock or plywood, bags of cement, sheets or packages of roofing shingles, and rolls of roofing felt.

items.quote: The articulating/knuckle-boom crane is used to hold, support or stabilize the material to facilitate a construction activity, such as holding material in place while it is attached to the structure;
items.statement: The material delivery exclusion does not apply when the articulating/knuckle-boom crane is used to hold, support or stabilize material to facilitate a construction activity, such as holding it in place while it is attached to the structure.

items.quote: The material being handled by the articulating/knuckle-boom crane is a prefabricated component.
items.statement: The material delivery exclusion does not apply when the material handled by the articulating/knuckle-boom crane is a prefabricated component.

items.quote: Such prefabricated components include, but are not limited to: Precast concrete members or panels, roof trusses (wooden, cold-formed metal, steel, or other material), prefabricated building sections
items.statement: Prefabricated components include, but are not limited to, precast concrete members or panels, roof trusses of any material, and prefabricated building sections such as floor panels, wall panels, roof panels, roof structures or similar items.

items.quote: The material being handled by the crane is a structural steel member (for example, steel joists, beams, columns, steel decking (bundled or unbundled) or a component of a systems-engineered metal building (as defined in 29 CFR 1926 subpart R).
items.statement: The material delivery exclusion does not apply when the material handled by the crane is a structural steel member, such as steel joists, beams, columns, bundled or unbundled steel decking, or a component of a systems-engineered metal building (as defined in 29 CFR 1926 subpart R).

items.quote: The activity is not specifically excluded under § 1400(c)(17)(i) and (ii).
items.statement: As listed among the conditions where the material delivery exclusion does not apply, one is that the activity is not specifically excluded under § 1400(c)(17)(i) and (ii).

items.quote: Flash-butt welding trucks or other roadway maintenance machines not equipped with any hoisting device other than that used to suspend and move a welding device or workhead assembly.
items.statement: The subpart does not cover flash-butt welding trucks or other roadway maintenance machines not equipped with any hoisting device other than one used to suspend and move a welding device or workhead assembly.

items.quote: the terms flash-butt welding truck and roadway maintenance machine refer to railroad equipment that meets the definition of “roadway maintenance machine” in 49 CFR 214.7 and is used only for railroad track work.
items.statement: For paragraph (c)(18), flash-butt welding truck and roadway maintenance machine mean railroad equipment that meets the 49 CFR 214.7 definition of roadway maintenance machine and is used only for railroad track work.

items.quote: All sections of this subpart CC apply to the equipment covered by this standard unless specified otherwise.
items.statement: All sections of subpart CC apply to equipment covered by the standard unless specified otherwise.

items.quote: The duties of controlling entities under this subpart include, but are not limited to, the duties specified in §§ 1926.1402(c), 1926.1402(e) and 1926.1424(b).
items.statement: Controlling entities' duties under the subpart include, but are not limited to, those specified in §§ 1926.1402(c), 1926.1402(e) and 1926.1424(b).

items.quote: Where provisions of this standard direct an operator, crewmember, or other employee to take certain actions, the employer must establish, effectively communicate to the relevant persons, and enforce, work rules to ensure compliance with such provisions.
items.statement: Where the standard directs an operator, crewmember or other employee to take certain actions, the employer must establish work rules to ensure compliance with those provisions.

items.quote: the employer must establish, effectively communicate to the relevant persons, and enforce, work rules
items.statement: Where the standard directs an operator, crewmember or other employee to take certain actions, the employer must effectively communicate the compliance work rules to the relevant persons.

items.quote: and enforce, work rules to ensure compliance with such provisions.
items.statement: Where the standard directs an operator, crewmember or other employee to take certain actions, the employer must enforce work rules to ensure compliance with those provisions.

items.quote: For work covered by subpart V of this part, compliance with § 1926.959 is deemed compliance with §§ 1926.1407 through 1926.1411.
items.statement: For work covered by subpart V of Part 1926, compliance with § 1926.959 is deemed compliance with §§ 1926.1407 through 1926.1411.

items.quote: Section 1926.1402 does not apply to cranes designed for use on railroad tracks, when used on railroad tracks that are part of the general railroad system of transportation that is regulated pursuant to the Federal Railroad Administration under 49 CFR part 213, and that comply with applicable Federal Railroad Administration requirements.
items.statement: Section 1926.1402 does not apply to cranes designed for railroad tracks when used on tracks that are part of the general railroad system of transportation regulated by the FRA under 49 CFR part 213, provided they comply with applicable FRA requirements.

items.quote: A/D director (Assembly/Disassembly director) means an individual who meets this subpart's requirements for an A/D director, irrespective of the person's formal job title or whether the person is non-management or management personnel.
items.statement: An A/D (Assembly/Disassembly) director is an individual who meets this subpart's requirements for an A/D director, regardless of formal job title or whether the person is management or non-management.

items.quote: Articulating crane means a crane whose boom consists of a series of folding, pin connected structural members, typically manipulated to extend or retract by power from hydraulic cylinders.
items.statement: An articulating crane is a crane whose boom consists of a series of folding, pin-connected structural members, typically extended or retracted by power from hydraulic cylinders.

items.quote: Assembly/Disassembly means the assembly and/or disassembly of equipment covered under this standard.
items.statement: Assembly/Disassembly means the assembly and/or disassembly of equipment covered under this standard.

items.quote: With regard to tower cranes, “erecting and climbing” replaces the term “assembly,” and “dismantling” replaces the term “disassembly.”
items.statement: For tower cranes, "erecting and climbing" replaces the term "assembly" and "dismantling" replaces the term "disassembly."

items.quote: Regardless of whether the crane is initially erected to its full height or is climbed in stages, the process of increasing the height of the crane is an erection process.
items.statement: Increasing a tower crane's height is an erection process, whether the crane is first erected to full height or climbed in stages.

items.quote: Assist crane means a crane used to assist in assembling or disassembling a crane.
items.statement: An assist crane is a crane used to assist in assembling or disassembling a crane.

items.quote: Attachments means any device that expands the range of tasks that can be done by the equipment. Examples include, but are not limited to: An auger, drill, magnet, pile-driver, and boom-attached personnel platform.
items.statement: An attachment is any device that expands the range of tasks the equipment can do, such as an auger, drill, magnet, pile-driver or boom-attached personnel platform.

items.quote: Audible signal means a signal made by a distinct sound or series of sounds. Examples include, but are not limited to, sounds made by a bell, horn, or whistle.
items.statement: An audible signal is a signal made by a distinct sound or series of sounds, such as from a bell, horn or whistle.

items.quote: Blocking (also referred to as “cribbing”) is wood or other material used to support equipment or a component and distribute loads to the ground.
items.statement: Blocking (also called cribbing) is wood or other material used to support equipment or a component and distribute loads to the ground.

items.quote: Boatswain's chair means a single-point adjustable suspension scaffold consisting of a seat or sling (which may be incorporated into a full body harness) designed to support one employee in a sitting position.
items.statement: A boatswain's chair is a single-point adjustable suspension scaffold consisting of a seat or sling (which may be incorporated into a full body harness) designed to support one employee in a sitting position.

items.quote: Bogie means “travel bogie,” which is defined below.
items.statement: "Bogie" means "travel bogie."

items.quote: Boom (equipment other than tower crane) means an inclined spar, strut, or other long structural member which supports the upper hoisting tackle on a crane or derrick.
items.statement: For equipment other than tower cranes, a boom is an inclined spar, strut or other long structural member that supports the upper hoisting tackle on a crane or derrick.

items.quote: On tower cranes, if the “boom” (i.e., principal horizontal structure) is fixed, it is referred to as a jib
items.statement: On tower cranes, a fixed principal horizontal structure ("boom") is referred to as a jib.

items.quote: if it is moveable up and down, it is referred to as a boom.
items.statement: On tower cranes, a principal horizontal structure that is moveable up and down is referred to as a boom.

items.quote: Boom angle indicator means a device which measures the angle of the boom relative to horizontal.
items.statement: A boom angle indicator is a device that measures the boom's angle relative to horizontal.

items.quote: Boom hoist limiting device includes boom hoist disengaging device, boom hoist shut-off, boom hoist disconnect, boom hoist hydraulic relief, boom hoist kick-outs, automatic boom stop device, or derricking limiter.
items.statement: Boom hoist limiting devices include the boom hoist disengaging device, shut-off, disconnect, hydraulic relief and kick-outs, the automatic boom stop device and the derricking limiter.

items.quote: This type of device disengages boom hoist power when the boom reaches a predetermined operating angle.
items.statement: A boom hoist limiting device disengages boom hoist power when the boom reaches a predetermined operating angle.

items.quote: It also sets brakes or closes valves to prevent the boom from lowering after power is disengaged.
items.statement: A boom hoist limiting device also sets brakes or closes valves to keep the boom from lowering after power is disengaged.

items.quote: Boom length indicator indicates the length of the permanent part of the boom (such as ruled markings on the boom) or, as in some computerized systems, the length of the boom with extensions/attachments.
items.statement: A boom length indicator indicates the length of the permanent part of the boom or, in some computerized systems, the boom length including extensions/attachments.

items.quote: Boom stop includes boom stops, (belly straps with struts/standoff), telescoping boom stops, attachment boom stops, and backstops.
items.statement: Boom stops include boom stops (belly straps with struts/standoff), telescoping boom stops, attachment boom stops and backstops.

items.quote: These devices restrict the boom from moving above a certain maximum angle and toppling over backward.
items.statement: Boom stops restrict the boom from moving above a certain maximum angle and toppling over backward.

items.quote: Boom suspension system means a system of pendants, running ropes, sheaves, and other hardware which supports the boom tip and controls the boom angle.
items.statement: A boom suspension system is a system of pendants, running ropes, sheaves and other hardware that supports the boom tip and controls the boom angle.

items.quote: Builder means the builder/constructor of equipment.
items.statement: A builder is the builder/constructor of equipment.

items.quote: The center of gravity of any object is the point in the object around which its weight is evenly distributed.
items.statement: An object's center of gravity is the point in the object around which its weight is evenly distributed.

items.quote: Certified welder means a welder who meets nationally recognized certification requirements applicable to the task being performed.
items.statement: A certified welder is a welder who meets nationally recognized certification requirements applicable to the task being performed.

items.quote: Climbing means the process in which a tower crane is raised to a new working height, either by adding additional tower sections to the top of the crane (top climbing), or by a system in which the entire crane is raised inside the structure (inside climbing).
items.statement: Climbing is raising a tower crane to a new working height, either by adding tower sections to the top (top climbing) or by a system that raises the entire crane inside the structure (inside climbing).

items.quote: Come-a-long means a mechanical device typically consisting of a chain or cable attached at each end that is used to facilitate movement of materials through leverage.
items.statement: A come-a-long is a mechanical device, typically a chain or cable attached at each end, used to facilitate movement of materials through leverage.

items.quote: Competent person means one who is capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards in the surroundings or working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous to employees, and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.
items.statement: A competent person can identify existing and predictable hazards in surroundings or working conditions that are unsanitary, hazardous or dangerous to employees, and has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.

items.quote: Controlled load lowering means lowering a load by means of a mechanical hoist drum device that allows a hoisted load to be lowered with maximum control using the gear train or hydraulic components of the hoist mechanism.
items.statement: Controlled load lowering is lowering a load with a mechanical hoist drum device that allows maximum control using the hoist mechanism's gear train or hydraulic components.

items.quote: Controlled load lowering requires the use of the hoist drive motor, rather than the load hoist brake, to lower the load.
items.statement: Controlled load lowering requires using the hoist drive motor, rather than the load hoist brake, to lower the load.

items.quote: Controlling entity means an employer that is a prime contractor, general contractor, construction manager or any other legal entity which has the overall responsibility for the construction of the project—its planning, quality and completion.
items.statement: A controlling entity is an employer that is a prime contractor, general contractor, construction manager or other legal entity with overall responsibility for the construction project's planning, quality and completion.

items.quote: Counterweight means a weight used to supplement the weight of equipment in providing stability for lifting loads by counterbalancing those loads.
items.statement: A counterweight is a weight used to supplement the equipment's weight in providing stability for lifting loads by counterbalancing them.

items.quote: Crane/derrick includes all equipment covered by this subpart.
items.statement: "Crane/derrick" includes all equipment covered by this subpart.

items.quote: Crawler crane means equipment that has a type of base mounting which incorporates a continuous belt of sprocket driven track.
items.statement: A crawler crane is equipment with a base mounting that incorporates a continuous belt of sprocket-driven track.

items.quote: Crossover points means locations on a wire rope which is spooled on a drum where one layer of rope climbs up on and crosses over the previous layer.
items.statement: Crossover points are locations on drum-spooled wire rope where one layer climbs up on and crosses over the previous layer.

items.quote: Dedicated channel means a line of communication assigned by the employer who controls the communication system to only one signal person and crane/derrick or to a coordinated group of cranes/derricks/signal person(s).
items.statement: A dedicated channel is a communication line assigned by the employer controlling the communication system to only one signal person and crane/derrick, or to a coordinated group of cranes/derricks/signal persons.

items.quote: Dedicated pile-driver is a machine that is designed to function exclusively as a pile-driver.
items.statement: A dedicated pile-driver is a machine designed to function exclusively as a pile-driver.

items.quote: To be considered a dedicated spotter, the requirements of § 1926.1428 (Signal person qualifications) must be met
items.statement: To be considered a dedicated spotter (power lines), a person must meet the requirements of § 1926.1428 (Signal person qualifications).

items.quote: his/her sole responsibility is to watch the separation between the power line and the equipment, load line and load (including rigging and lifting accessories), and ensure through communication with the operator that the applicable minimum approach distance is not breached.
items.statement: A dedicated spotter's sole responsibility must be to watch the separation between the power line and the equipment, load line and load (including rigging and lifting accessories), and ensure through communication with the operator that the minimum approach distance is not breached.

items.quote: Directly under the load means a part or all of an employee is directly beneath the load.
items.statement: "Directly under the load" means part or all of an employee is directly beneath the load.

items.quote: Dismantling includes partial dismantling (such as dismantling to shorten a boom or substitute a different component).
items.statement: Dismantling includes partial dismantling, such as to shorten a boom or substitute a different component.

items.quote: Drum rotation indicator means a device on a crane or hoist which indicates in which direction and at what relative speed a particular hoist drum is turning.
items.statement: A drum rotation indicator is a device on a crane or hoist that indicates the direction and relative speed at which a particular hoist drum is turning.

items.quote: Electrical contact occurs when a person, object, or equipment makes contact or comes in close proximity with an energized conductor or equipment that allows the passage of current.
items.statement: Electrical contact occurs when a person, object or equipment contacts or comes in close proximity with an energized conductor or equipment that allows the passage of current.

items.quote: Employer-made equipment means floating cranes/derricks designed and built by an employer for the employer's own use.
items.statement: Employer-made equipment means floating cranes/derricks designed and built by an employer for its own use.

items.quote: Encroachment is where any part of the crane, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) breaches a minimum clearance distance that this subpart requires to be maintained from a power line.
items.statement: Encroachment is when any part of the crane, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) breaches a minimum clearance distance from a power line required by this subpart.

items.quote: Equipment means equipment covered by this subpart.
items.statement: "Equipment" means equipment covered by this subpart.

items.quote: Equipment criteria means instructions, recommendations, limitations and specifications.
items.statement: Equipment criteria means instructions, recommendations, limitations and specifications.

items.quote: Fall protection equipment means guardrail systems, safety net systems, personal fall arrest systems, positioning device systems or fall restraint systems.
items.statement: Fall protection equipment means guardrail systems, safety net systems, personal fall arrest systems, positioning device systems or fall restraint systems.

items.quote: Fall restraint system means a fall protection system that prevents the user from falling any distance.
items.statement: A fall restraint system is a fall protection system that prevents the user from falling any distance.

items.quote: The system is comprised of either a body belt or body harness, along with an anchorage, connectors and other necessary equipment. The other components typically include a lanyard, and may also include a lifeline and other devices.
items.statement: A fall restraint system comprises a body belt or body harness along with an anchorage, connectors and other necessary equipment, typically including a lanyard and possibly a lifeline and other devices.

items.quote: Fall zone means the area (including but not limited to the area directly beneath the load) in which it is reasonably foreseeable that partially or completely suspended materials could fall in the event of an accident.
items.statement: The fall zone is the area, including but not limited to directly beneath the load, where it is reasonably foreseeable that partially or completely suspended materials could fall in an accident.

items.quote: Flange points are points of contact between rope and drum flange where the rope changes layers.
items.statement: Flange points are points of contact between rope and drum flange where the rope changes layers.

items.quote: Floating cranes/derricks means equipment designed by the manufacturer (or employer) for marine use by permanent attachment to a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation.
items.statement: Floating cranes/derricks are equipment designed by the manufacturer or employer for marine use by permanent attachment to a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation.

items.quote: For example means “one example, although there are others.”
items.statement: "For example" means one example, although there are others.

items.quote: Free fall (of the load line) means that only the brake is used to regulate the descent of the load line (the drive mechanism is not used to drive the load down faster or retard its lowering).
items.statement: Free fall of the load line means only the brake regulates its descent; the drive mechanism is not used to drive the load down faster or retard its lowering.

items.quote: Free surface effect is the uncontrolled transverse movement of liquids in compartments which reduce a vessel's transverse stability.
items.statement: Free surface effect is the uncontrolled transverse movement of liquids in compartments, which reduces a vessel's transverse stability.

items.quote: Hoist means a mechanical device for lifting and lowering loads by winding a line onto or off a drum.
items.statement: A hoist is a mechanical device for lifting and lowering loads by winding a line onto or off a drum.

items.quote: Hoisting is the act of raising, lowering or otherwise moving a load in the air with equipment covered by this standard.
items.statement: Hoisting is raising, lowering or otherwise moving a load in the air with equipment covered by this standard.

items.quote: As used in this standard, “hoisting” can be done by means other than wire rope/hoist drum equipment.
items.statement: Under this standard, hoisting can be done by means other than wire rope/hoist drum equipment.

items.quote: Include/including means “including, but not limited to.”
items.statement: "Include/including" means including, but not limited to.

items.quote: Insulating link/device means an insulating device listed, labeled, or accepted by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.7.
items.statement: An insulating link/device is an insulating device listed, labeled or accepted by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.7.

items.quote: Jib stop (also referred to as a jib backstop), is the same type of device as a boom stop but is for a fixed or luffing jib.
items.statement: A jib stop (jib backstop) is the same type of device as a boom stop but is for a fixed or luffing jib.

items.quote: Land crane/derrick is equipment not originally designed by the manufacturer for marine use by permanent attachment to barges, pontoons, vessels, or other means of floatation.
items.statement: A land crane/derrick is equipment not originally designed by the manufacturer for marine use by permanent attachment to barges, pontoons, vessels or other means of floatation.

items.quote: List means the angle of inclination about the longitudinal axis of a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of floatation.
items.statement: List is the angle of inclination about the longitudinal axis of a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of floatation.

items.quote: Load refers to the object(s) being hoisted and/or the weight of the object(s); both uses refer to the object(s) and the load-attaching equipment, such as, the load block, ropes, slings, shackles, and any other ancillary attachment.
items.statement: "Load" refers to the hoisted object(s) and/or their weight, and both uses include the load-attaching equipment such as the load block, ropes, slings, shackles and any other ancillary attachment.

items.quote: Load moment (or rated capacity) indicator means a system which aids the equipment operator by sensing (directly or indirectly) the overturning moment on the equipment, i.e., load multiplied by radius.
items.statement: A load moment (or rated capacity) indicator is a system that aids the equipment operator by sensing, directly or indirectly, the overturning moment on the equipment (load multiplied by radius).

items.quote: It compares this lifting condition to the equipment's rated capacity, and indicates to the operator the percentage of capacity at which the equipment is working.
items.statement: A load moment indicator compares the lifting condition to the equipment's rated capacity and shows the operator the percentage of capacity at which the equipment is working.

items.quote: Lights, bells, or buzzers may be incorporated as a warning of an approaching overload condition.
items.statement: A load moment indicator may incorporate lights, bells, or buzzers to warn of an approaching overload.

items.quote: Load moment (or rated capacity) limiter means a system which aids the equipment operator by sensing (directly or indirectly) the overturning moment on the equipment, i.e., load multiplied by radius.
items.statement: A load moment (or rated capacity) limiter is a system that aids the equipment operator by sensing, directly or indirectly, the overturning moment on the equipment (load multiplied by radius).

items.quote: when the rated capacity is reached, it shuts off power to those equipment functions which can increase the severity of loading on the equipment, e.g., hoisting, telescoping out, or luffing out.
items.statement: When rated capacity is reached, a load moment limiter shuts off power to equipment functions that can increase loading severity, such as hoisting, telescoping out, or luffing out.

items.quote: Typically, those functions which decrease the severity of loading on the equipment remain operational, e.g., lowering, telescoping in, or luffing in.
items.statement: With a load moment limiter, functions that decrease loading severity, such as lowering, telescoping in, or luffing in, typically remain operational.

items.quote: Locomotive crane means a crane mounted on a base or car equipped for travel on a railroad track.
items.statement: A locomotive crane is a crane mounted on a base or car equipped for travel on a railroad track.

items.quote: Luffing jib limiting device is similar to a boom hoist limiting device, except that it limits the movement of the luffing jib.
items.statement: A luffing jib limiting device is similar to a boom hoist limiting device, except that it limits the movement of the luffing jib.

items.quote: Marine hoisted personnel transfer device means a device, such as a “transfer net,” that is designed to protect the employees being hoisted during a marine transfer and to facilitate rapid entry into and exit from the device.
items.statement: A marine hoisted personnel transfer device is a device, such as a transfer net, designed to protect employees hoisted during a marine transfer and to facilitate rapid entry into and exit from the device.

items.quote: Such devices do not include boatswain's chairs when hoisted by equipment covered by this standard.
items.statement: Boatswain's chairs hoisted by equipment covered by this standard are excluded from marine hoisted personnel transfer devices.

items.quote: Marine worksite means a construction worksite located in, on or above the water.
items.statement: A marine worksite is a construction worksite located in, on or above the water.

items.quote: Mobile crane means a lifting device incorporating a cable suspended latticed boom or hydraulic telescopic boom designed to be moved between operating locations by transport over the road.
items.statement: A mobile crane is a lifting device with a cable suspended latticed boom or hydraulic telescopic boom, designed to be moved between operating locations by transport over the road.

items.quote: Moving point-to-point means the times during which an employee is in the process of going to or from a work station.
items.statement: Moving point-to-point means the times when an employee is in the process of going to or from a work station.

items.quote: Multi-purpose machine means a machine that is designed to be configured in various ways, at least one of which allows it to hoist (by means of a winch or hook) and horizontally move a suspended load.
items.statement: A multi-purpose machine is designed to be configured in various ways, at least one of which allows it to hoist (by winch or hook) and horizontally move a suspended load.

items.quote: When configured with the forks/tongs, it is not covered by this subpart.
items.statement: A multi-purpose machine configured with forks or tongs is not covered by this subpart.

items.quote: When configured with a winch pack, jib (with a hook at the end) or jib used in conjunction with a winch, it is covered by this subpart.
items.statement: A multi-purpose machine configured with a winch pack, a jib with a hook at the end, or a jib used with a winch is covered by this subpart.

items.quote: Nationally recognized accrediting agency is an organization that, due to its independence and expertise, is widely recognized as competent to accredit testing organizations.
items.statement: A nationally recognized accrediting agency is an organization that, due to its independence and expertise, is widely recognized as competent to accredit testing organizations.

items.quote: Examples of such accrediting agencies include, but are not limited to, the National Commission for Certifying Agencies and the American National Standards Institute.
items.statement: Examples of nationally recognized accrediting agencies include, but are not limited to, the National Commission for Certifying Agencies and the American National Standards Institute.

items.quote: Nonconductive means that, because of the nature and condition of the materials used, and the conditions of use (including environmental conditions and condition of the material), the object in question has the property of not becoming energized
items.statement: Nonconductive means that, because of the materials' nature and condition and the conditions of use (including environment and material condition), the object has the property of not becoming energized (high resistance to current under the conditions of use).

items.quote: Operational aids are devices that assist the operator in the safe operation of the crane by providing information or automatically taking control of a crane function.
items.statement: Operational aids are devices that help the operator operate the crane safely by providing information or automatically taking control of a crane function.

items.quote: These include, but are not limited to, the devices listed in § 1926.1416 (“listed operational aids”).
items.statement: Operational aids include, but are not limited to, the listed operational aids in § 1926.1416.

items.quote: Operational controls means levers, switches, pedals and other devices for controlling equipment operation.
items.statement: Operational controls are levers, switches, pedals and other devices for controlling equipment operation.

items.quote: Operator means a person who is operating the equipment.
items.statement: An operator is a person who is operating the equipment.

items.quote: Overhead and gantry cranes includes overhead/bridge cranes, semigantry, cantilever gantry, wall cranes, storage bridge cranes, launching gantry cranes, and similar equipment, irrespective of whether it travels on tracks, wheels, or other means.
items.statement: Overhead and gantry cranes include overhead/bridge, semigantry, cantilever gantry, wall, storage bridge and launching gantry cranes and similar equipment, whether it travels on tracks, wheels or other means.

items.quote: Paragraph refers to a paragraph in the same section of this subpart that the word “paragraph” is used, unless otherwise specified.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, "paragraph" refers to a paragraph in the same section of this subpart where the word is used.

items.quote: Pendants includes both wire and bar types.
items.statement: Pendants include both wire and bar types.

items.quote: Wire type: A fixed length of wire rope with mechanical fittings at both ends for pinning segments of wire rope together.
items.statement: A wire-type pendant is a fixed length of wire rope with mechanical fittings at both ends for pinning segments of wire rope together.

items.quote: Bar type: Instead of wire rope, a bar is used.
items.statement: A bar-type pendant uses a bar instead of wire rope.

items.quote: Pendants are typically used in a latticed boom crane system to easily change the length of the boom suspension system without completely changing the rope on the drum when the boom length is increased or decreased.
items.statement: Pendants are typically used in latticed boom crane systems to easily change boom suspension system length without completely changing the drum rope when boom length is increased or decreased.

items.quote: Personal fall arrest system means a system used to arrest an employee in a fall from a working level.
items.statement: A personal fall arrest system is a system used to arrest an employee in a fall from a working level.

items.quote: It consists of an anchorage, connectors, a body harness and may include a lanyard, deceleration device, lifeline, or suitable combination of these.
items.statement: A personal fall arrest system consists of an anchorage, connectors and a body harness, and may include a lanyard, deceleration device, lifeline, or a suitable combination of these.

items.quote: Portal crane is a type of crane consisting of a rotating upperstructure, hoist machinery, and boom mounted on top of a structural gantry which may be fixed in one location or have travel capability.
items.statement: A portal crane has a rotating upperstructure, hoist machinery and boom mounted on top of a structural gantry that may be fixed in one location or able to travel.

items.quote: The gantry legs or columns usually have portal openings in between to allow passage of traffic beneath the gantry.
items.statement: A portal crane's gantry legs or columns usually have portal openings between them to let traffic pass beneath the gantry.

items.quote: Power lines means electric transmission and distribution lines.
items.statement: Power lines are electric transmission and distribution lines.

items.quote: Procedures include, but are not limited to: Instructions, diagrams, recommendations, warnings, specifications, protocols and limitations.
items.statement: Procedures include, but are not limited to, instructions, diagrams, recommendations, warnings, specifications, protocols and limitations.

items.quote: Proximity alarm is a device that provides a warning of proximity to a power line and that has been listed, labeled, or accepted by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.7.
items.statement: A proximity alarm is a device that warns of proximity to a power line and has been listed, labeled, or accepted by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.7.

items.quote: Qualified evaluator (not a third party) means a person employed by the signal person's employer who has demonstrated that he/she is competent in accurately assessing whether individuals meet the Qualification Requirements in this subpart for a signal person.
items.statement: A qualified evaluator (not a third party) is a person employed by the signal person's employer who has demonstrated competence in accurately assessing whether individuals meet this subpart's signal person qualification requirements.

items.quote: Qualified evaluator (third party) means an entity that, due to its independence and expertise, has demonstrated that it is competent in accurately assessing whether individuals meet the Qualification Requirements in this subpart for a signal person.
items.statement: A qualified evaluator (third party) is an entity that, due to its independence and expertise, has demonstrated competence in accurately assessing whether individuals meet this subpart's signal person qualification requirements.

items.quote: Qualified person means a person who, by possession of a recognized degree, certificate, or professional standing, or who by extensive knowledge, training and experience, successfully demonstrated the ability to solve/resolve problems relating to the subject matter, the work, or the project.
items.statement: A qualified person is one who, by a recognized degree, certificate or professional standing, or by extensive knowledge, training and experience, has successfully demonstrated the ability to solve problems relating to the subject matter, work, or project.

items.quote: Qualified rigger is a rigger who meets the criteria for a qualified person.
items.statement: A qualified rigger is a rigger who meets the criteria for a qualified person.

items.quote: Range control limit device is a device that can be set by an equipment operator to limit movement of the boom or jib tip to a plane or multiple planes.
items.statement: A range control limit device can be set by an equipment operator to limit boom or jib tip movement to a plane or multiple planes.

items.quote: Range control warning device is a device that can be set by an equipment operator to warn that the boom or jib tip is at a plane or multiple planes.
items.statement: A range control warning device can be set by an equipment operator to warn that the boom or jib tip is at a plane or multiple planes.

items.quote: Rated capacity means the maximum working load permitted by the manufacturer under specified working conditions.
items.statement: Rated capacity is the maximum working load the manufacturer permits under specified working conditions.

items.quote: Such working conditions typically include a specific combination of factors such as equipment configuration, radii, boom length, and other parameters of use.
items.statement: The working conditions for rated capacity typically include a specific combination of factors such as equipment configuration, radii, boom length and other parameters of use.

items.quote: Rated capacity indicator: See load moment indicator.
items.statement: "Rated capacity indicator" refers to the definition of load moment indicator.

items.quote: Rated capacity limiter: See load moment limiter.
items.statement: "Rated capacity limiter" refers to the definition of load moment limiter.

items.quote: Repetitive pickup points refer to, when operating on a short cycle operation, the rope being used on a single layer and being spooled repetitively over a short portion of the drum.
items.statement: Repetitive pickup points means that, in short cycle operation, the rope is used on a single layer and spooled repetitively over a short portion of the drum.

items.quote: Running wire rope means a wire rope that moves over sheaves or drums.
items.statement: Running wire rope is wire rope that moves over sheaves or drums.

items.quote: Runway means a firm, level surface designed, prepared and designated as a path of travel for the weight and configuration of the crane being used to lift and travel with the crane suspended platform.
items.statement: A runway is a firm, level surface designed, prepared and designated as a travel path for the weight and configuration of the crane used to lift and travel with the crane suspended platform.

items.quote: An existing surface may be used as long as it meets these criteria.
items.statement: An existing surface may be used as a runway as long as it meets the runway criteria.

items.quote: Section means a section of this subpart, unless otherwise specified.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, "section" means a section of this subpart.

items.quote: Sideboom crane means a track-type or wheel-type tractor having a boom mounted on the side of the tractor, used for lifting, lowering or transporting a load suspended on the load hook.
items.statement: A sideboom crane is a track-type or wheel-type tractor with a side-mounted boom, used to lift, lower or transport a load suspended on the load hook.

items.quote: The boom or hook can be lifted or lowered in a vertical direction only.
items.statement: A sideboom crane's boom or hook can be lifted or lowered only in a vertical direction.

items.quote: Special hazard warnings means warnings of site-specific hazards (for example, proximity of power lines).
items.statement: Special hazard warnings are warnings of site-specific hazards, such as proximity of power lines.

items.quote: Stability (flotation device) means the tendency of a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation to return to an upright position after having been inclined by an external force.
items.statement: Stability of a flotation device is the tendency of a barge, pontoons, vessel or other flotation means to return upright after being inclined by an external force.

items.quote: Standard Method means the protocol in appendix A of this subpart for hand signals.
items.statement: Standard Method is the hand signal protocol in appendix A of this subpart.

items.quote: Such as means “such as, but not limited to.”
items.statement: "Such as" means "such as, but not limited to."

items.quote: Superstructure: See Upperworks.
items.statement: "Superstructure" refers to the definition of Upperworks.

items.quote: Tagline means a rope (usually fiber) attached to a lifted load for purposes of controlling load spinning and pendular motions or used to stabilize a bucket or magnet during material handling operations.
items.statement: A tagline is a rope, usually fiber, attached to a lifted load to control load spinning and pendular motions, or used to stabilize a bucket or magnet during material handling.

items.quote: Tender means an individual responsible for monitoring and communicating with a diver.
items.statement: A tender is an individual responsible for monitoring and communicating with a diver.

items.quote: Tilt up or tilt down operation means raising/lowering a load from the horizontal to vertical or vertical to horizontal.
items.statement: A tilt up or tilt down operation is raising or lowering a load from horizontal to vertical or from vertical to horizontal.

items.quote: Tower crane is a type of lifting structure which utilizes a vertical mast or tower to support a working boom (jib) in an elevated position. Loads are suspended from the working boom.
items.statement: A tower crane is a lifting structure that uses a vertical mast or tower to support an elevated working boom (jib) from which loads are suspended.

items.quote: While the working boom may be of the fixed type (horizontal or angled) or have luffing capability, it can always rotate to swing loads, either by rotating on the top of the tower (top slewing) or by the rotation of the tower (bottom slewing).
items.statement: A tower crane's working boom may be fixed (horizontal or angled) or luffing, but can always rotate to swing loads, by top slewing or bottom slewing.

items.quote: The tower base may be fixed in one location or ballasted and moveable between locations.
items.statement: A tower crane's base may be fixed in one location or ballasted and moveable between locations.

items.quote: Mobile cranes that are configured with luffing jib and/or tower attachments are not considered tower cranes under this section.
items.statement: Mobile cranes configured with luffing jib and/or tower attachments are excluded from being considered tower cranes under this section.

items.quote: Travel bogie (tower cranes) is an assembly of two or more axles arranged to permit vertical wheel displacement and equalize the loading on the wheels.
items.statement: A tower crane travel bogie is an assembly of two or more axles arranged to permit vertical wheel displacement and equalize loading on the wheels.

items.quote: Trim means angle of inclination about the transverse axis of a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of floatation.
items.statement: Trim is the angle of inclination about the transverse axis of a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation.

items.quote: Two blocking means a condition in which a component that is uppermost on the hoist line such as the load block, hook block, overhaul ball, or similar component, comes in contact with the boom tip, fixed upper block or similar component.
items.statement: Two blocking is when the uppermost component on the hoist line, such as the load block, hook block or overhaul ball, contacts the boom tip, fixed upper block or similar component.

items.quote: This binds the system and continued application of power can cause failure of the hoist rope or other component.
items.statement: Two blocking binds the system, and continued application of power can cause failure of the hoist rope or another component.

items.quote: Unavailable procedures means procedures that are no longer available from the manufacturer, or have never been available, from the manufacturer.
items.statement: Unavailable procedures are procedures that are no longer available, or have never been available, from the manufacturer.

items.quote: Upperstructure: See Upperworks.
items.statement: "Upperstructure" refers to the definition of Upperworks.

items.quote: Upperworks means the revolving frame of equipment on which the operating machinery (and many cases the engine) are mounted along with the operator's cab.
items.statement: Upperworks is the revolving frame of equipment on which the operating machinery (and in many cases the engine) is mounted along with the operator's cab.

items.quote: The counterweight is typically supported on the rear of the upperstructure and the boom or other front end attachment is mounted on the front.
items.statement: The counterweight is typically supported on the rear of the upperstructure, and the boom or other front end attachment is mounted on the front.

items.quote: Up to means “up to and including.”
items.statement: "Up to" means "up to and including."

items.quote: Wire rope means a flexible rope constructed by laying steel wires into various patterns of multi-wired strands around a core system to produce a helically wound rope.
items.statement: Wire rope is a flexible rope made by laying steel wires into various patterns of multi-wired strands around a core system to produce a helically wound rope.

items.quote: “Ground conditions” means the ability of the ground to support the equipment (including slope, compaction, and firmness).
