items.statement: “Ground conditions” means the ability of the ground to support the equipment, including slope, compaction, and firmness.

items.quote: “Supporting materials” means blocking, mats, cribbing, marsh buggies (in marshes/wetlands), or similar supporting materials or devices.
items.statement: “Supporting materials” means blocking, mats, cribbing, marsh buggies (in marshes/wetlands), or similar supporting materials or devices.

items.quote: The equipment must not be assembled or used unless ground conditions are firm, drained, and graded to a sufficient extent so that, in conjunction (if necessary) with the use of supporting materials, the equipment manufacturer's specifications for adequate support and degree of level of the equipment are met.
items.statement: The equipment must not be assembled or used unless ground conditions are firm, drained, and graded sufficiently so that, with supporting materials if necessary, the equipment manufacturer's specifications for adequate support and degree of level are met.

items.quote: The requirement for the ground to be drained does not apply to marshes/wetlands.
items.statement: As an exception, the requirement for the ground to be drained does not apply to marshes/wetlands.

items.quote:
The controlling entity must:
[29cfr1926.1402(c)(1)] (1) Ensure that ground preparations necessary to meet the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section are provided.
items.statement: The controlling entity must ensure that the ground preparations necessary to meet the ground condition requirements of paragraph (b) are provided.

items.quote: Inform the user of the equipment and the operator of the location of hazards beneath the equipment set-up area (such as voids, tanks, utilities) if those hazards are identified in documents (such as site drawings, as-built drawings, and soil analyses) that are in the possession of the controlling entity (whether at the site or off-site) or the hazards are otherwise known to that controlling entity.
items.statement: The controlling entity must inform the equipment user and the operator of the location of hazards beneath the equipment set-up area (such as voids, tanks, utilities) if those hazards are identified in documents in its possession, whether at the site or off-site (such as site drawings, as-built drawings, and soil analyses), or are otherwise known to it.

items.quote: If there is no controlling entity for the project, the requirement in paragraph (c)(1) of this section must be met by the employer that has authority at the site to make or arrange for ground preparations needed to meet paragraph (b) of this section.
items.statement: If the project has no controlling entity, the employer with authority at the site to make or arrange for the needed ground preparations must ensure that the preparations necessary to meet paragraph (b) are provided.

items.quote: If the A/D director or the operator determines that ground conditions do not meet the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section, that person's employer must have a discussion with the controlling entity regarding the ground preparations that are needed so that, with the use of suitable supporting materials/devices (if necessary), the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section can be met.
items.statement: If the A/D director or the operator determines that ground conditions do not meet paragraph (b), that person's employer must discuss with the controlling entity the ground preparations needed so that paragraph (b) can be met, using suitable supporting materials/devices if necessary.

items.quote: This section does not apply to cranes designed for use on railroad tracks when used on railroad tracks that are part of the general railroad system of transportation that is regulated pursuant to the Federal Railroad Administration under 49 CFR part 213 and that comply with applicable Federal Railroad Administration requirements.
items.statement: This section does not apply to cranes designed for use on railroad tracks when they are used on tracks that are part of the general railroad system of transportation regulated under the Federal Railroad Administration under 49 CFR part 213, and they comply with applicable Federal Railroad Administration requirements.

items.quote: When assembling or disassembling equipment (or attachments), the employer must comply with all applicable manufacturer prohibitions
items.statement: When assembling or disassembling equipment or attachments, the employer must comply with all applicable manufacturer prohibitions.

items.quote:
must comply with either:
[29cfr1926.1403(a)] (a) Manufacturer procedures applicable to assembly and disassembly, or
[29cfr1926.1403(b)] (b) Employer procedures for assembly and disassembly.
items.statement: When assembling or disassembling equipment or attachments, the employer must comply with either the applicable manufacturer assembly and disassembly procedures or employer procedures for assembly and disassembly.

items.quote: Employer procedures may be used only where the employer can demonstrate that the procedures used meet the requirements in § 1926.1406.
items.statement: The employer may use employer procedures for assembly and disassembly only where the employer can demonstrate that the procedures used meet the requirements in § 1926.1406.

items.quote: The employer must follow manufacturer procedures when an employer uses synthetic slings during assembly or disassembly rigging.
items.statement: The employer must follow manufacturer procedures when using synthetic slings during assembly or disassembly rigging.

items.quote: Assembly/disassembly must be directed by a person who meets the criteria for both a competent person and a qualified person, or by a competent person who is assisted by one or more qualified persons
items.statement: Assembly/disassembly must be directed by a person who meets the criteria for both a competent person and a qualified person, or by a competent person assisted by one or more qualified persons.

items.quote: directed by a person who meets the criteria for both a competent person and a qualified person, or by a competent person who is assisted by one or more qualified persons (“A/D director”)
items.statement: The "A/D director" is the person directing assembly/disassembly: either one who meets both the competent person and qualified person criteria, or a competent person assisted by one or more qualified persons.

items.quote: Where the assembly/disassembly is being performed by only one person, that person must meet the criteria for both a competent person and a qualified person.
items.statement: When only one person performs the assembly/disassembly, that person must meet the criteria for both a competent person and a qualified person.

items.quote: For purposes of this standard, that person is considered the A/D director.
items.statement: For purposes of this standard, a person who performs assembly/disassembly alone is considered the A/D director.

items.quote: The A/D director must understand the applicable assembly/disassembly procedures.
items.statement: The A/D director must understand the applicable assembly/disassembly procedures.

items.quote: The A/D director must review the applicable assembly/disassembly procedures immediately prior to the commencement of assembly/disassembly unless the A/D director understands the procedures and has applied them to the same type and configuration of equipment (including accessories, if any).
items.statement: The A/D director must review the applicable procedures immediately before assembly/disassembly begins, unless the director understands them and has applied them to the same type and configuration of equipment (including any accessories).

items.quote:
(1) Before commencing assembly/disassembly operations, the A/D director must ensure that the crew members understand all of the following:
[29cfr1926.1404(d)(1)(i)] (i) Their tasks.
items.statement: Before assembly/disassembly operations begin, the A/D director must ensure crew members understand their tasks.

items.quote: The hazards associated with their tasks.
items.statement: Before assembly/disassembly operations begin, the A/D director must ensure crew members understand the hazards associated with their tasks.

items.quote: The hazardous positions/locations that they need to avoid.
items.statement: Before assembly/disassembly operations begin, the A/D director must ensure crew members understand the hazardous positions/locations they need to avoid.

items.quote: During assembly/disassembly operations, before a crew member takes on a different task, or when adding new personnel during the operations, the requirements in paragraphs (d)(1)(i) through (d)(1)(iii) of this section must be met.
items.statement: During operations, before a crew member takes on a different task, the requirements that crew members understand their tasks, the associated hazards and the hazardous locations to avoid must be met.

items.quote: or when adding new personnel during the operations, the requirements in paragraphs (d)(1)(i) through (d)(1)(iii) of this section must be met.
items.statement: When new personnel are added during operations, the requirements that crew members understand their tasks, the associated hazards and the hazardous locations to avoid must be met.

items.quote: Before a crew member goes to a location that is out of view of the operator and is either in, on, or under the equipment, or near the equipment (or load) where the crew member could be injured by movement of the equipment (or load), the crew member must inform the operator that he/she is going to that location.
items.statement: A crew member must tell the operator before going to a location out of the operator's view that is in, on or under the equipment, or near the equipment or load where movement of either could injure the crew member.

items.quote: the operator must not move any part of the equipment (or load) until the operator is informed in accordance with a pre-arranged system of communication that the crew member is in a safe position.
items.statement: When the operator knows a crew member went to such an out-of-view hazardous location, the operator must not move any part of the equipment or load until informed through a pre-arranged communication system that the crew member is in a safe position.

items.quote: When pins (or similar devices) are being removed, employees must not be under the boom, jib, or other components, except where the requirements of paragraph (f)(2) of this section are met.
items.statement: Employees must not be under the boom, jib or other components while pins or similar devices are being removed, except where the site-constraint exception in paragraph (f)(2) is met.

items.quote: Where the employer demonstrates that site constraints require one or more employees to be under the boom, jib, or other components when pins (or similar devices) are being removed, the A/D director must implement procedures that minimize the risk of unintended dangerous movement
items.statement: Where the employer demonstrates that site constraints require employees to be under the boom, jib or other components during pin removal (an exception to the prohibition), the A/D director must implement procedures that minimize the risk of unintended dangerous movement.

items.quote: the A/D director must implement procedures that minimize the risk of unintended dangerous movement and minimize the duration and extent of exposure under the boom.
items.statement: Where the employer demonstrates that site constraints require employees to be under components during pin removal, the A/D director must implement procedures that minimize the duration and extent of exposure under the boom.

items.quote: During all phases of assembly/disassembly, rated capacity limits for loads imposed on the equipment, equipment components (including rigging), lifting lugs and equipment accessories, must not be exceeded for the equipment being assembled/disassembled.
items.statement: During all phases of assembly/disassembly, rated capacity limits for loads on the equipment, its components (including rigging), lifting lugs and accessories must not be exceeded for the equipment being assembled or disassembled.

items.quote: The A/D director supervising the assembly/disassembly operation must address the hazards associated with the operation
items.statement: The A/D director supervising the operation must address the hazards associated with it, including those listed in paragraph (h).

items.quote: Site and ground conditions must be adequate for safe assembly/disassembly operations
items.statement: Site and ground conditions must be adequate for safe assembly/disassembly operations.

items.quote: Site and ground conditions must be adequate for safe assembly/disassembly operations and to support the equipment during assembly/disassembly
items.statement: Site and ground conditions must be adequate to support the equipment during assembly/disassembly.

items.quote: The size, amount, condition and method of stacking the blocking must be sufficient to sustain the loads and maintain stability.
items.statement: The size, amount, condition and stacking method of blocking must be sufficient to sustain the loads and maintain stability.

items.quote:
When used to support lattice booms or components, blocking must be appropriately placed to:
[29cfr1926.1404(h)(3)(i)] (i) Protect the structural integrity of the equipment
items.statement: Blocking used to support lattice booms or components must be placed to protect the structural integrity of the equipment.

items.quote: Prevent dangerous movement and collapse.
items.statement: Blocking used to support lattice booms or components must be placed to prevent dangerous movement and collapse.

items.quote: When using an assist crane, the loads that will be imposed on the assist crane at each phase of assembly/disassembly must be verified in accordance with § 1926.1417(o)(3) before assembly/disassembly begins.
items.statement: When an assist crane is used, the loads it will bear at each phase must be verified under § 1926.1417(o)(3) before assembly/disassembly begins.

items.quote: The point(s) of attachment of rigging to a boom (or boom sections or jib or jib sections) must be suitable for preventing structural damage and facilitating safe handling of these components.
items.statement: Rigging attachment points on a boom, jib or their sections must be suitable for preventing structural damage and facilitating safe handling of these components.

items.quote: The center of gravity of the load must be identified if that is necessary for the method used for maintaining stability.
items.statement: The load's center of gravity must be identified if the method used for maintaining stability requires it.

items.quote: Where there is insufficient information to accurately identify the center of gravity, measures designed to prevent unintended dangerous movement resulting from an inaccurate identification of the center of gravity must be used.
items.statement: When information is insufficient to accurately identify the center of gravity, measures designed to prevent unintended dangerous movement from an inaccurate identification must be used.

items.quote: The boom sections, boom suspension systems (such as gantry A-frames and jib struts), and components must be rigged or supported to maintain stability upon the removal of the pins.
items.statement: Boom sections, boom suspension systems (such as gantry A-frames and jib struts) and components must be rigged or supported to stay stable when pins are removed.

items.quote: Suspension ropes and pendants must not be allowed to catch on the boom or jib connection pins or cotter pins (including keepers and locking pins).
items.statement: Suspension ropes and pendants must not be allowed to catch on boom or jib connection pins or cotter pins, including keepers and locking pins.

items.quote: The potential for unintended movement from inadequately supported counterweights
items.statement: The A/D director must address the potential for unintended movement from inadequately supported counterweights.

items.quote: The potential for unintended movement from inadequately supported counterweights and from hoisting counterweights.
items.statement: The A/D director must address the potential for unintended movement from hoisting counterweights.

items.quote: Each time reliance is to be placed on the boom hoist brake to prevent boom movement during assembly/disassembly, the brake must be tested prior to such reliance to determine if it is sufficient to prevent boom movement.
items.statement: Each time the boom hoist brake will be relied on to prevent boom movement during assembly/disassembly, it must be tested beforehand to determine whether it is sufficient.

items.quote: If it is not sufficient, a boom hoist pawl, other locking device/back-up braking device, or another method of preventing dangerous movement of the boom (such as blocking or using an assist crane) from a boom hoist brake failure must be used.
items.statement: If the boom hoist brake is not sufficient, a boom hoist pawl, other locking or back-up braking device, or another method (such as blocking or an assist crane) must be used to prevent dangerous boom movement from brake failure.

items.quote: Backward stability before swinging the upperworks, travel, and when attaching or removing equipment components.
items.statement: The A/D director must address loss of backward stability, considering it before swinging the upperworks, before travel, and when attaching or removing equipment components.

items.quote: The effect of wind speed and weather on the equipment.
items.statement: The A/D director must address the effect of wind speed and weather on the equipment.

items.quote: Manufacturer limitations on the maximum amount of boom supported only by cantilevering must not be exceeded.
items.statement: Manufacturer limitations on the maximum amount of boom supported only by cantilevering must not be exceeded.

items.quote: Where these are unavailable, a registered professional engineer familiar with the type of equipment involved must determine in writing this limitation
items.statement: When manufacturer cantilever limitations are unavailable, a registered professional engineer familiar with the type of equipment must determine the limitation in writing.

items.quote: must determine in writing this limitation, which must not be exceeded.
items.statement: The cantilever limitation that a registered professional engineer determines, when manufacturer limitations are unavailable, must not be exceeded.

items.quote: The weight of each of the components must be readily available.
items.statement: The weight of each component must be readily available.

items.quote: The selection of components, and configuration of the equipment, that affect the capacity or safe operation of the equipment must be in accordance with:
items.statement: Component selection and equipment configuration that affect capacity or safe operation must accord with either manufacturer instructions, prohibitions, limitations and specifications (or, if unavailable, a registered professional engineer's written approval) or approved modifications meeting § 1926.1434.

items.quote: Where these are unavailable, a registered professional engineer familiar with the type of equipment involved must approve, in writing, the selection and configuration of components
items.statement: When manufacturer instructions, prohibitions, limitations and specifications are unavailable, a registered professional engineer familiar with the type of equipment must approve the component selection and configuration in writing.

items.quote: Upon completion of assembly, the equipment must be inspected to ensure compliance with paragraph (m)(1) of this section
items.statement: When assembly is complete, the equipment must be inspected to ensure compliance with the component selection and configuration requirements of paragraph (m)(1).

items.quote: Reusable shipping pins, straps, links, and similar equipment must be removed.
items.statement: Reusable shipping pins, straps, links and similar equipment must be removed.

items.quote: Once they are removed they must either be stowed or otherwise stored so that they do not present a falling object hazard.
items.statement: Once removed, reusable shipping pins, straps, links and similar equipment must be stowed or stored so they do not present a falling object hazard.

items.quote: Equipment used for pile driving must not have a jib attached during pile driving operations.
items.statement: Equipment used for pile driving must not have a jib attached during pile driving operations.

items.quote: When the load to be handled and the operating radius require the use of outriggers or stabilizers, or at any time when outriggers or stabilizers are used, all of the following requirements must be met (except as otherwise indicated):
items.statement: The paragraph (q) outrigger and stabilizer requirements apply, except as otherwise indicated, when the load and operating radius require outriggers or stabilizers, and any time they are used.

items.quote: The outriggers or stabilizers must be either fully extended or, if manufacturer procedures permit, deployed as specified in the load chart.
items.statement: When outriggers or stabilizers are required or used, they must be fully extended or, if manufacturer procedures permit, deployed as specified in the load chart.

items.quote: The outriggers must be set to remove the equipment weight from the wheels, except for locomotive cranes
items.statement: When outriggers are required or used, they must be set to remove the equipment weight from the wheels, except on locomotive cranes.

items.quote: This provision does not apply to stabilizers.
items.statement: The requirement to set outriggers so the equipment weight is off the wheels does not apply to stabilizers.

items.quote: When outrigger floats are used, they must be attached to the outriggers.
items.statement: When outrigger floats are used, they must be attached to the outriggers.

items.quote: When stabilizer floats are used, they must be attached to the stabilizers.
items.statement: When stabilizer floats are used, they must be attached to the stabilizers.

items.quote: Each outrigger or stabilizer must be visible to the operator or to a signal person during extension and setting.
items.statement: Each outrigger or stabilizer must be visible to the operator or a signal person during extension and setting.

items.quote:
(5) Outrigger and stabilizer blocking must:
[29cfr1926.1404(q)(5)(i)] (i) Meet the requirements in paragraphs (h)(2) and (h)(3) of this section.
items.statement: Outrigger and stabilizer blocking must meet the blocking material and blocking location requirements of paragraphs (h)(2) and (h)(3).

items.quote: Be placed only under the outrigger or stabilizer float/pad of the jack or, where the outrigger or stabilizer is designed without a jack, under the outer bearing surface of the extended outrigger or stabilizer beam.
items.statement: Outrigger or stabilizer blocking must be placed only under the float/pad of the jack or, for designs without a jack, under the outer bearing surface of the extended outrigger or stabilizer beam.

items.quote: For locomotive cranes, when using outriggers or stabilizers to handle loads, the manufacturer's procedures must be followed.
items.statement: When a locomotive crane uses outriggers or stabilizers to handle loads, the manufacturer's procedures must be followed.

items.quote: When lifting loads without using outriggers or stabilizers, the manufacturer's procedures must be met regarding truck wedges or screws.
items.statement: When a locomotive crane lifts loads without outriggers or stabilizers, the manufacturer's procedures on truck wedges or screws must be met.

items.quote: In addition to following the requirements in 29 CFR 1926.251 and other requirements in this and other standards applicable to rigging
items.statement: Rigging used for assembly/disassembly is subject to 29 CFR 1926.251 and other rigging requirements in this and other standards, in addition to the requirements of paragraph (r).

items.quote: The rigging work is done by a qualified rigger.
items.statement: When rigging is used for assembly/disassembly, the employer must ensure the rigging work is done by a qualified rigger.

items.quote: Synthetic slings are protected from: Abrasive, sharp or acute edges
items.statement: For assembly/disassembly rigging, the employer must ensure synthetic slings are protected from abrasive, sharp or acute edges.

items.quote: configurations that could cause a reduction of the sling's rated capacity, such as distortion or localized compression.
items.statement: For assembly/disassembly rigging, the employer must ensure synthetic slings are protected from configurations that could reduce their rated capacity, such as distortion or localized compression.

items.quote: When synthetic slings are used, the synthetic sling manufacturer's instructions, limitations, specifications and recommendations must be followed.
items.statement: When synthetic slings are used in assembly/disassembly rigging, the employer must ensure the sling manufacturer's instructions, limitations, specifications and recommendations are followed.

items.quote: applies to both the use of manufacturer procedures and employer procedures
items.statement: The §1926.1405 additional requirements for dismantling booms and jibs apply both when manufacturer procedures are used and when employer procedures are used.

items.quote: Dismantling (including dismantling for changing the length of) booms and jibs.
items.statement: Dismantling of booms and jibs under §1926.1405 includes dismantling done to change their length.

items.quote: None of the pins in the pendants are to be removed (partly or completely) when the pendants are in tension.
items.statement: When dismantling booms and jibs, none of the pins in the pendants may be removed, partly or completely, when the pendants are in tension.

items.quote: None of the pins (top or bottom) on boom sections located between the pendant attachment points and the crane/derrick body are to be removed (partly or completely) when the pendants are in tension.
items.statement: When dismantling booms and jibs, none of the top or bottom pins on boom sections between the pendant attachment points and the crane/derrick body may be removed, partly or completely, when the pendants are in tension.

items.quote: None of the pins (top or bottom) on boom sections located between the uppermost boom section and the crane/derrick body are to be removed (partly or completely) when the boom is being supported by the uppermost boom section resting on the ground (or other support).
items.statement: When dismantling booms and jibs, none of the top or bottom pins on boom sections between the uppermost boom section and the crane/derrick body may be removed, partly or completely, when the boom is being supported by the uppermost boom section resting on the ground or other support.

items.quote: None of the top pins on boom sections located on the cantilevered portion of the boom being removed (the portion being removed ahead of the pendant attachment points) are to be removed (partly or completely) until the cantilevered section to be removed is fully supported.
items.statement: When dismantling booms and jibs, none of the top pins on boom sections in the cantilevered portion being removed (ahead of the pendant attachment points) may be removed, partly or completely, until the cantilevered section to be removed is fully supported.

items.quote: Prevent unintended dangerous movement, and prevent collapse, of any part of the equipment.
items.statement: When using employer procedures instead of manufacturer procedures for assembly/disassembly, the employer must ensure the procedures prevent unintended dangerous movement of any part of the equipment.

items.quote: prevent collapse, of any part of the equipment
items.statement: When using employer procedures instead of manufacturer procedures for assembly/disassembly, the employer must ensure the procedures prevent collapse of any part of the equipment.

items.quote: Provide adequate support and stability of all parts of the equipment.
items.statement: When using employer procedures instead of manufacturer procedures for assembly/disassembly, the employer must ensure the procedures provide adequate support of all parts of the equipment.

items.quote: Provide adequate support and stability of all parts of the equipment.
items.statement: When using employer procedures instead of manufacturer procedures for assembly/disassembly, the employer must ensure the procedures provide adequate stability of all parts of the equipment.

items.quote: Position employees involved in the assembly/disassembly operation so that their exposure to unintended movement or collapse of part or all of the equipment is minimized.
items.statement: When using employer procedures instead of manufacturer procedures for assembly/disassembly, the employer must ensure the procedures position employees involved in the operation so that their exposure to unintended movement or collapse of part or all of the equipment is minimized.

items.quote: Employer procedures must be developed by a qualified person.
items.statement: Employer assembly/disassembly procedures must be developed by a qualified person.

items.quote: Before assembling or disassembling equipment, the employer must determine if any part of the equipment, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) could get, in the direction or area of assembly/disassembly, closer than 20 feet to a power line during the assembly/disassembly process.
items.statement: Before assembling or disassembling equipment, the employer must determine whether any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) could get, in the direction or area of assembly/disassembly, closer than 20 feet to a power line during the process.

items.quote: If so, the employer must meet the requirements in Option (1), Option (2), or Option (3) of this section
items.statement: If any part of the equipment, load line or load could get closer than 20 feet to a power line during assembly/disassembly, the employer must meet the requirements of Option (1), Option (2) or Option (3).

items.quote: Confirm from the utility owner/operator that the power line has been deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite.
items.statement: Under Option (1), the employer must confirm from the utility owner/operator that the power line has been deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite.

items.quote: Ensure that no part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), gets closer than 20 feet to the power line by implementing the measures specified in paragraph (b) of this section.
items.statement: Under Option (2), the employer must ensure that no part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) gets closer than 20 feet to the power line, by implementing the measures in paragraph (b).

items.quote: Determine the line's voltage and the minimum clearance distance permitted under Table A (see § 1926.1408).
items.statement: Under Option (3), the employer must determine the line's voltage and the minimum clearance distance permitted under Table A.

items.quote: Determine if any part of the equipment, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), could get closer than the minimum clearance distance to the power line permitted under Table A (see § 1926.1408).
items.statement: Under Option (3), the employer must determine whether any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) could get closer to the power line than the Table A minimum clearance distance.

items.quote: If so, then the employer must follow the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section to ensure that no part of the equipment, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), gets closer to the line than the minimum clearance distance.
items.statement: Under Option (3), if any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) could get closer than the Table A minimum clearance distance, the employer must follow paragraph (b) to ensure that no such part gets closer to the line than that distance.

items.quote: Where encroachment precautions are required under Option (2), or Option (3) of this section, all of the following requirements must be met:
items.statement: Where encroachment precautions are required under Option (2) or Option (3), all of the requirements in paragraph (b) must be met.

items.quote: Conduct a planning meeting with the Assembly/Disassembly director (A/D director), operator, assembly/disassembly crew and the other workers who will be in the assembly/disassembly area to review the location of the power line(s) and the steps that will be implemented to prevent encroachment/electrocution.
items.statement: Where encroachment precautions are required, a planning meeting must be held with the A/D director, operator, assembly/disassembly crew and other workers who will be in the assembly/disassembly area to review the power line locations and the steps to prevent encroachment/electrocution.

items.quote: If tag lines are used, they must be nonconductive.
items.statement: Where encroachment precautions are required, any tag lines used must be nonconductive.

items.quote: At least one of the following additional measures must be in place.
items.statement: Where encroachment precautions are required, at least one of the additional measures listed in paragraph (b)(3) must be in place.

items.quote: The measure selected from this list must be effective in preventing encroachment.
items.statement: The additional measure selected from the paragraph (b)(3) list must be effective in preventing encroachment.

items.quote: Use a dedicated spotter who is in continuous contact with the equipment operator.
items.statement: If a dedicated spotter is the additional measure used, the spotter must be in continuous contact with the equipment operator.

items.quote: Be equipped with a visual aid to assist in identifying the minimum clearance distance.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must be equipped with a visual aid to assist in identifying the minimum clearance distance.

items.quote: Examples of a visual aid include, but are not limited to: A clearly visible line painted on the ground; a clearly visible line of stanchions; a set of clearly visible line-of-sight landmarks
items.statement: Examples of a spotter's visual aid include, but are not limited to, a clearly visible line painted on the ground, a clearly visible line of stanchions, or a set of clearly visible line-of-sight landmarks.

items.quote: Be positioned to effectively gauge the clearance distance.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must be positioned to effectively gauge the clearance distance.

items.quote: Where necessary, use equipment that enables the dedicated spotter to communicate directly with the operator.
items.statement: Where necessary, the dedicated spotter must use equipment that enables direct communication with the operator.

items.quote: Give timely information to the operator so that the required clearance distance can be maintained.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must give the operator timely information so the required clearance distance can be maintained.

items.quote: A proximity alarm set to give the operator sufficient warning to prevent encroachment.
items.statement: If a proximity alarm is the additional measure used, it must be set to give the operator sufficient warning to prevent encroachment.

items.quote: A device that automatically warns the operator when to stop movement, such as a range control warning device. Such a device must be set to give the operator sufficient warning to prevent encroachment.
items.statement: If a device that automatically warns the operator when to stop movement, such as a range control warning device, is the additional measure used, it must be set to give the operator sufficient warning to prevent encroachment.

items.quote: A device that automatically limits range of movement, set to prevent encroachment.
items.statement: If a device that automatically limits range of movement is the additional measure used, it must be set to prevent encroachment.

items.quote: An elevated warning line, barricade, or line of signs, in view of the operator, equipped with flags or similar high-visibility markings.
items.statement: If an elevated warning line, barricade or line of signs is the additional measure used, it must be in view of the operator and equipped with flags or similar high-visibility markings.

items.quote: No part of a crane/derrick, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), whether partially or fully assembled, is allowed below a power line unless the employer has confirmed that the utility owner/operator has deenergized and (at the worksite) visibly grounded the power line.
items.statement: No part of a crane/derrick, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), whether partially or fully assembled, is allowed below a power line unless the employer has confirmed that the utility owner/operator has deenergized and, at the worksite, visibly grounded the line.

items.quote: No part of a crane/derrick, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), whether partially or fully assembled, is allowed closer than the minimum approach distance under Table A (see § 1926.1408) to a power line unless the employer has confirmed that the utility owner/operator has deenergized and (at the worksite) visibly grounded the power line.
items.statement: No part of a crane/derrick, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), whether partially or fully assembled, is allowed closer to a power line than the Table A minimum approach distance unless the employer has confirmed that the utility owner/operator has deenergized and, at the worksite, visibly grounded the line.

items.quote: the utility owner/operator of the power lines must provide the requested voltage information within two working days of the employer's request.
items.statement: Where Option (3) is used, the power line's utility owner/operator must provide the requested voltage information within two working days of the employer's request.

items.quote: The employer must assume that all power lines are energized unless the utility owner/operator confirms that the power line has been and continues to be deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite.
items.statement: The employer must assume all power lines are energized unless the utility owner/operator confirms that the line has been and continues to be deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite.

items.quote: There must be at least one electrocution hazard warning conspicuously posted in the cab so that it is in view of the operator
items.statement: At least one electrocution hazard warning must be conspicuously posted in the cab so that it is in view of the operator.

items.quote: (except for overhead gantry and tower cranes) at least two on the outside of the equipment.
items.statement: At least two electrocution hazard warnings must be posted on the outside of the equipment, except for overhead gantry and tower cranes.

items.quote: Identify the work zone by either:
items.statement: Before beginning equipment operations, the employer must identify the work zone either by demarcating boundaries and prohibiting the operator from operating past them, or by defining it as the area 360 degrees around the equipment up to its maximum working radius.

items.quote: Demarcating boundaries (such as with flags, or a device such as a range limit device or range control warning device) and prohibiting the operator from operating the equipment past those boundaries
items.statement: If the employer identifies the work zone by demarcating boundaries (such as with flags, a range limit device or a range control warning device), the employer must prohibit the operator from operating the equipment past those boundaries.

items.quote: Defining the work zone as the area 360 degrees around the equipment, up to the equipment's maximum working radius.
items.statement: Under the alternative to demarcating boundaries, the work zone is defined as the area 360 degrees around the equipment, up to the equipment's maximum working radius.

items.quote: Determine if any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), if operated up to the equipment's maximum working radius in the work zone, could get closer than 20 feet to a power line.
items.statement: Before beginning equipment operations, the employer must determine whether any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), if operated up to maximum working radius in the work zone, could get closer than 20 feet to a power line.

items.quote: could get closer than 20 feet to a power line. If so, the employer must meet the requirements in Option (1), Option (2), or Option (3) of this section
items.statement: If any part of the equipment, load line or load could get closer than 20 feet to a power line, the employer must meet the requirements of Option (1), Option (2) or Option (3).

items.quote: Confirm from the utility owner/operator that the power line has been deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite.
items.statement: Under Option (1), the employer must confirm from the utility owner/operator that the power line has been deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite.

items.quote: Ensure that no part of the equipment, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), gets closer than 20 feet to the power line by implementing the measures specified in paragraph (b) of this section.
items.statement: Under Option (2), the employer must ensure no part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) gets closer than 20 feet to the power line by implementing the paragraph (b) measures.

items.quote: Determine the line's voltage and the minimum approach distance permitted under Table A
items.statement: Under Option (3), the employer must determine the line's voltage and the minimum approach distance permitted under Table A.

items.quote: Determine if any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), while operating up to the equipment's maximum working radius in the work zone, could get closer than the minimum approach distance of the power line permitted under Table A
items.statement: Under Option (3), the employer must determine whether any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), while operating up to maximum working radius in the work zone, could get closer to the power line than the Table A minimum approach distance.

items.quote: If so, then the employer must follow the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section to ensure that no part of the equipment, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), gets closer to the line than the minimum approach distance.
items.statement: If under Option (3) any part could get closer than the Table A minimum approach distance, the employer must follow paragraph (b) to ensure no part of the equipment, load line or load gets closer to the line than that distance.

items.quote: Where encroachment precautions are required under Option (2) or Option (3) of this section, all of the following requirements must be met:
items.statement: Where encroachment precautions are required under Option (2) or (3), all of the paragraph (b) requirements must be met.

items.quote: Conduct a planning meeting with the operator and the other workers who will be in the area of the equipment or load to review the location of the power line(s), and the steps that will be implemented to prevent encroachment/electrocution.
items.statement: Where Option (2) or (3) precautions are required, a planning meeting must be conducted with the operator and other workers who will be in the area of the equipment or load to review the power line locations and the steps to prevent encroachment and electrocution.

items.quote: If tag lines are used, they must be non-conductive.
items.statement: Where Option (2) or (3) precautions are required, any tag lines used must be non-conductive.

items.quote: Erect and maintain an elevated warning line, barricade, or line of signs, in view of the operator, equipped with flags or similar high-visibility markings, at 20 feet from the power line (if using Option (2) of this section) or at the minimum approach distance under Table A
items.statement: An elevated warning line, barricade or line of signs, in view of the operator and equipped with flags or similar high-visibility markings, must be erected and maintained at 20 feet from the power line under Option (2) or at the Table A minimum approach distance under Option (3).

items.quote: If the operator is unable to see the elevated warning line, a dedicated spotter must be used as described in § 1926.1408(b)(4)(ii) in addition to implementing one of the measures described in §§ 1926.1408(b)(4)(i), (iii), (iv) and (v).
items.statement: If the operator cannot see the elevated warning line, a dedicated spotter as described in (b)(4)(ii) must be used in addition to implementing one of the measures in (b)(4)(i), (iii), (iv) or (v).

items.quote: Implement at least one of the following measures:
items.statement: Where Option (2) or (3) precautions are required, at least one of the listed measures must be implemented: proximity alarm, dedicated spotter, automatic stop-warning device, automatic range-limiting device, or insulating link/device.

items.quote: A proximity alarm set to give the operator sufficient warning to prevent encroachment.
items.statement: A proximity alarm used as the (b)(4) measure must be set to give the operator sufficient warning to prevent encroachment.

items.quote: A dedicated spotter who is in continuous contact with the operator.
items.statement: A dedicated spotter used as the (b)(4) measure must be in continuous contact with the operator.

items.quote: Be equipped with a visual aid to assist in identifying the minimum clearance distance.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must be equipped with a visual aid to assist in identifying the minimum clearance distance, such as a painted line on the ground, a line of stanchions or line-of-sight landmarks, all clearly visible.

items.quote: Be positioned to effectively gauge the clearance distance.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must be positioned to effectively gauge the clearance distance.

items.quote: Where necessary, use equipment that enables the dedicated spotter to communicate directly with the operator.
items.statement: Where necessary, the dedicated spotter must use equipment that enables direct communication with the operator.

items.quote: Give timely information to the operator so that the required clearance distance can be maintained.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must give the operator timely information so the required clearance distance can be maintained.

items.quote: A device that automatically warns the operator when to stop movement, such as a range control warning device. Such a device must be set to give the operator sufficient warning to prevent encroachment.
items.statement: A device that automatically warns the operator when to stop movement, if used as the (b)(4) measure, must be set to give the operator sufficient warning to prevent encroachment.

items.quote: A device that automatically limits range of movement, set to prevent encroachment.
items.statement: A device that automatically limits range of movement, if used as the (b)(4) measure, must be set to prevent encroachment.

items.quote: An insulating link/device, as defined in § 1926.1401, installed at a point between the end of the load line (or below) and the load.
items.statement: An insulating link/device (as defined in § 1926.1401) used as the (b)(4) measure must be installed at a point between the end of the load line (or below) and the load.

items.quote: The requirements of paragraph (b)(4) of this section do not apply to work covered by subpart V of this part.
items.statement: Exception: the paragraph (b)(4) measures requirement does not apply to work covered by subpart V.

items.quote: the utility owner/operator of the power lines must provide the requested voltage information within two working days of the employer's request.
items.statement: Where Option (3) is used, the utility owner/operator must provide requested voltage information within two working days of the employer's request.

items.quote: No part of the equipment, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) is allowed below a power line unless the employer has confirmed that the utility owner/operator has deenergized and (at the worksite) visibly grounded the power line, except where one of the exceptions in paragraph (d)(2) of this section applies.
items.statement: No part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) is allowed below a power line unless the employer has confirmed that the utility owner/operator has deenergized and visibly grounded (at the worksite) the line, except where a (d)(2) exception applies.

items.quote:
Paragraph (d)(1) of this section is inapplicable where the employer demonstrates that one of the following applies:
(i) The work is covered by subpart V of this part.
items.statement: Exception: the below-power-line prohibition does not apply where the employer demonstrates that the work is covered by subpart V.

items.quote: For equipment with non-extensible booms: The uppermost part of the equipment, with the boom at true vertical, would be more than 20 feet below the plane of the power line or more than the Table A of this section minimum clearance distance below the plane of the power line.
items.statement: Exception: the below-power-line prohibition does not apply where the employer demonstrates that, for equipment with non-extensible booms, the uppermost part of the equipment with the boom at true vertical would be more than 20 feet, or more than the Table A minimum clearance distance, below the plane of the power line.

items.quote: For equipment with articulating or extensible booms: The uppermost part of the equipment, with the boom in the fully extended position, at true vertical, would be more than 20 feet below the plane of the power line or more than the Table A of this section minimum clearance distance below the plane of the power line.
items.statement: Exception: the below-power-line prohibition does not apply where the employer demonstrates that, for equipment with articulating or extensible booms, the uppermost part of the equipment with the boom fully extended at true vertical would be more than 20 feet, or more than the Table A minimum clearance distance, below the plane of the power line.

items.quote: The employer demonstrates that compliance with paragraph (d)(1) of this section is infeasible and meets the requirements of § 1926.1410.
items.statement: Exception: the below-power-line prohibition does not apply where the employer demonstrates that complying with it is infeasible and meets the requirements of § 1926.1410.

items.quote: The employer must assume that all power lines are energized unless the utility owner/operator confirms that the power line has been and continues to be deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite.
items.statement: The employer must assume all power lines are energized unless the utility owner/operator confirms that the line has been and continues to be deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite.

items.quote: When working near transmitter/communication towers where the equipment is close enough for an electrical charge to be induced in the equipment or materials being handled, the transmitter must be deenergized or the following precautions must be taken:
items.statement: When working near transmitter/communication towers where equipment is close enough for an electrical charge to be induced in the equipment or materials handled, either the transmitter must be deenergized or the (f)(1) and (f)(2) precautions must be taken.

items.quote: The equipment must be provided with an electrical ground.
items.statement: Near transmitter/communication towers where a charge can be induced, if the transmitter is not deenergized, the equipment must be provided with an electrical ground.

items.quote: If tag lines are used, they must be non-conductive.
items.statement: Near transmitter/communication towers where a charge can be induced, if the transmitter is not deenergized, any tag lines used must be non-conductive.

items.quote:
The employer must train each operator and crew member assigned to work with the equipment on all of the following:
(i) The procedures to be followed in the event of electrical contact with a power line.
items.statement: The employer must train each operator and crew member assigned to work with the equipment on the procedures to follow in the event of electrical contact with a power line.

items.quote: Information regarding the danger of electrocution from the operator simultaneously touching the equipment and the ground.
items.statement: Electrical-contact training must include information on the danger of electrocution from the operator simultaneously touching the equipment and the ground.

items.quote: The importance to the operator's safety of remaining inside the cab except where there is an imminent danger of fire, explosion, or other emergency that necessitates leaving the cab.
items.statement: Electrical-contact training must include the importance to the operator's safety of remaining inside the cab except where imminent danger of fire, explosion or another emergency necessitates leaving.

items.quote: The safest means of evacuating from equipment that may be energized.
items.statement: Electrical-contact training must include the safest means of evacuating from equipment that may be energized.

items.quote: The danger of the potentially energized zone around the equipment (step potential).
items.statement: Electrical-contact training must include the danger of the potentially energized zone around the equipment (step potential).

items.quote: The need for crew in the area to avoid approaching or touching the equipment and the load.
items.statement: Electrical-contact training must include the need for crew in the area to avoid approaching or touching the equipment and the load.

items.quote: Safe clearance distance from power lines.
items.statement: Electrical-contact training must include the safe clearance distance from power lines.

items.quote: Power lines are presumed to be energized unless the utility owner/operator confirms that the power line has been and continues to be deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite.
items.statement: Operators and crew members must be trained that power lines are presumed energized unless the utility owner/operator confirms the line has been and continues to be deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite.

items.quote: Power lines are presumed to be uninsulated unless the utility owner/operator or a registered engineer who is a qualified person with respect to electrical power transmission and distribution confirms that a line is insulated.
items.statement: Operators and crew members must be trained that power lines are presumed uninsulated unless the utility owner/operator, or a registered engineer who is a qualified person in electrical power transmission and distribution, confirms a line is insulated.

items.quote: The limitations of an insulating link/device, proximity alarm, and range control (and similar) device, if used.
items.statement: Operators and crew members must be trained on the limitations of insulating link/devices, proximity alarms, and range control (and similar) devices, if used.

items.quote: The procedures to be followed to properly ground equipment and the limitations of grounding.
items.statement: Operators and crew members must be trained on the procedures for properly grounding equipment and the limitations of grounding.

items.quote: Employees working as dedicated spotters must be trained to enable them to effectively perform their task, including training on the applicable requirements of this section.
items.statement: Employees working as dedicated spotters must be trained to perform their task effectively, including training on the applicable requirements of this section.

items.quote: Training under this section must be administered in accordance with § 1926.1430(g).
items.statement: Training under this section must be administered in accordance with § 1926.1430(g).

items.quote: Devices originally designed by the manufacturer for use as: A safety device (see § 1926.1415), operational aid, or a means to prevent power line contact or electrocution, when used to comply with this section, must meet the manufacturer's procedures for use and conditions of use.
items.statement: Devices originally designed by the manufacturer as a safety device, operational aid, or means to prevent power line contact or electrocution must, when used to comply with this section, meet the manufacturer's procedures and conditions of use.

items.quote: The value that follows “to” is up to and includes that value. For example, over 50 to 200 means up to and including 200kV.
items.statement: In Table A, the value following "to" is included in the range; for example, over 50 to 200 means up to and including 200 kV.

items.quote: The requirements of §§ 1926.1407 and 1926.1408 apply to power lines over 350 kV except:
items.statement: The requirements of §§ 1926.1407 and 1926.1408 apply to power lines over 350 kV, except as modified by paragraphs (a) and (b) of § 1926.1409.

items.quote: For power lines at or below 1000 kV, wherever the distance “20 feet” is specified, the distance “50 feet” must be substituted
items.statement: For power lines over 350 kV and at or below 1000 kV, wherever §§ 1926.1407 and 1926.1408 specify a distance of 20 feet, a distance of 50 feet must be substituted.

items.quote: For power lines over 1000 kV, the minimum clearance distance must be established by the utility owner/operator or registered professional engineer who is a qualified person with respect to electrical power transmission and distribution.
items.statement: For power lines over 1000 kV, the minimum clearance distance must be established by the utility owner/operator or a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person with respect to electrical power transmission and distribution.

items.quote: Equipment operations in which any part of the equipment, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) is closer than the minimum approach distance under Table A of § 1926.1408 to an energized power line is prohibited, except where the employer demonstrates that all of the following requirements are met:
items.statement: Equipment operations with any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) closer to an energized power line than the Table A (§ 1926.1408) minimum approach distance are prohibited, unless the employer demonstrates that all the requirements of § 1926.1410 are met.

items.quote: The employer determines that it is infeasible to do the work without breaching the minimum approach distance under Table A of § 1926.1408.
items.statement: To work closer than the Table A distance, the employer must determine that it is infeasible to do the work without breaching that minimum approach distance.

items.quote: The employer determines that, after consultation with the utility owner/operator, it is infeasible to deenergize and ground the power line or relocate the power line.
items.statement: To work closer than the Table A distance, the employer must determine, after consulting the utility owner/operator, that it is infeasible to deenergize and ground the power line or to relocate it.

items.quote: The power line owner/operator or registered professional engineer who is a qualified person with respect to electrical power transmission and distribution determines the minimum clearance distance that must be maintained to prevent electrical contact in light of the on-site conditions.
items.statement: The power line owner/operator, or a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person in electrical power transmission and distribution, must determine the minimum clearance distance needed to prevent electrical contact given on-site conditions, except for work covered by subpart V.

items.quote: The factors that must be considered in making this determination include, but are not limited to: Conditions affecting atmospheric conductivity; time necessary to bring the equipment, load line, and load (including rigging and lifting accessories) to a complete stop; wind conditions; degree of sway in the power line; lighting conditions, and other conditions affecting the ability to prevent electrical contact.
items.statement: The minimum clearance distance determination must consider at least these factors: conditions affecting atmospheric conductivity, time needed to bring the equipment, load line and load (including rigging and lifting accessories) to a complete stop, wind, power line sway, lighting, and other conditions affecting the ability to prevent electrical contact.

items.quote: Paragraph (c)(1) of this section does not apply to work covered by subpart V of this part; instead, for such work, the minimum approach distances established by the employer under § 1926.960(c)(1)(i) apply.
items.statement: Paragraph (c)(1) does not apply to work covered by subpart V; for that work, the minimum approach distances the employer established under § 1926.960(c)(1)(i) apply.

items.quote: A planning meeting with the employer and utility owner/operator (or registered professional engineer who is a qualified person with respect to electrical power transmission and distribution) is held to determine the procedures that will be followed to prevent electrical contact and electrocution.
items.statement: A planning meeting with the employer and the utility owner/operator (or a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person in electrical power transmission and distribution) must be held to determine the procedures for preventing electrical contact and electrocution.

items.quote: If the power line is equipped with a device that automatically reenergizes the circuit in the event of a power line contact, before the work begins, the automatic reclosing feature of the circuit interrupting device must be made inoperative if the design of the device permits.
items.statement: If the power line has a device that automatically reenergizes the circuit after a power line contact, the circuit interrupting device's automatic reclosing feature must be made inoperative before work begins, if the device's design permits.

items.quote: A dedicated spotter who is in continuous contact with the operator.
items.statement: The procedures must include a dedicated spotter who is in continuous contact with the operator.

items.quote: Be equipped with a visual aid to assist in identifying the minimum clearance distance.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must have a visual aid to help identify the minimum clearance distance, such as a painted ground line, a clearly visible line of stanchions, or clearly visible line-of-sight landmarks.

items.quote: Be positioned to effectively gauge the clearance distance.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must be positioned to effectively gauge the clearance distance.

items.quote: Where necessary, use equipment that enables the dedicated spotter to communicate directly with the operator.
items.statement: Where necessary, the dedicated spotter must use equipment that enables direct communication with the operator.

items.quote: Give timely information to the operator so that the required clearance distance can be maintained.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must give the operator timely information so the required clearance distance can be maintained.

items.quote: An elevated warning line, or barricade (not attached to the crane), in view of the operator (either directly or through video equipment), equipped with flags or similar high-visibility markings, to prevent electrical contact.
items.statement: The procedures must include an elevated warning line or barricade, not attached to the crane, in the operator's view (directly or by video equipment) and equipped with flags or similar high-visibility markings, to prevent electrical contact.

items.quote: However, this provision does not apply to work covered by subpart V of this part.
items.statement: The elevated warning line or barricade provision does not apply to work covered by subpart V.

items.quote: An insulating link/device installed at a point between the end of the load line (or below) and the load.
items.statement: An insulating link/device must be installed at a point between the end of the load line (or below) and the load, except for work covered by subpart V; time-limited substitute procedures were allowed under (d)(4)(iv) and (v).

items.quote: Paragraph (d)(4)(i) of this section does not apply to work covered by subpart V of this part.
items.statement: The insulating link/device requirement in paragraph (d)(4)(i) does not apply to work covered by subpart V.

items.quote: Until November 8, 2011, the following procedure may be substituted for the requirement in paragraph (d)(4)(i) of this section: All employees, excluding equipment operators located on the equipment, who may come in contact with the equipment, the load line, or the load must be insulated or guarded from the equipment, the load line, and the load.
items.statement: Until November 8, 2011, the (d)(4)(i) insulating link/device could be replaced by insulating or guarding all employees who might contact the equipment, load line or load from all three, excluding equipment operators located on the equipment.

items.quote: Insulating gloves rated for the voltage involved are adequate insulation for the purposes of this paragraph.
items.statement: For the (d)(4)(iv) substitute procedure, insulating gloves rated for the voltage involved are adequate insulation.

items.quote: The employer must use a link/device manufactured on or before November 8, 2011, that meets the definition of an insulating link/device, except that it has not been approved by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory
items.statement: Under the substitute procedure allowed until November 8, 2013, the employer had to use a link/device made on or before November 8, 2011 that met the insulating link/device definition except for Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory approval.

items.quote: that is maintained and used in accordance with manufacturer requirements and recommendations
items.statement: Under the substitute procedure allowed until November 8, 2013, the non-NRTL-approved link/device had to be maintained and used according to manufacturer requirements and recommendations.

items.quote: is installed at a point between the end of the load line (or below) and the load
items.statement: Under the substitute procedure allowed until November 8, 2013, the non-NRTL-approved link/device had to be installed at a point between the end of the load line (or below) and the load.

items.quote: All employees, excluding equipment operators located on the equipment, who may come in contact with the equipment, the load line, or the load must be insulated or guarded from the equipment, the load line, and the load through an additional means other than the device described in paragraph (d)(4)(v)(A) of this section.
items.statement: Under the (d)(4)(v) substitute procedure, all employees who might contact the equipment, load line or load, excluding equipment operators located on the equipment, had to be insulated or guarded from them by a means additional to the (d)(4)(v)(A) device.

items.quote: Insulating gloves rated for the voltage involved are adequate additional means of protection for the purposes of this paragraph.
items.statement: For the (d)(4)(v) substitute procedure, insulating gloves rated for the voltage involved are adequate additional protection.

items.quote: Until November 8, 2013, the following procedure may be substituted for the requirement in (d)(4)(i) of this section:
items.statement: The (d)(4)(v) substitute for the insulating link/device requirement was allowed only until November 8, 2013.

items.quote: Nonconductive rigging if the rigging may be within the Table A of § 1926.1408 distance during the operation.
items.statement: Nonconductive rigging must be used if the rigging may be within the Table A (§ 1926.1408) distance during the operation.

items.quote: If the equipment is equipped with a device that automatically limits range of movement, it must be used and set to prevent any part of the equipment, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) from breaching the minimum approach distance established under paragraph (c) of this section.
items.statement: If the equipment has a device that automatically limits range of movement, it must be used and set to keep any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) from breaching the minimum approach distance established under paragraph (c).

items.quote: If a tag line is used, it must be of the nonconductive type.
items.statement: Any tag line used must be nonconductive.

items.quote: Barricades forming a perimeter at least 10 feet away from the equipment to prevent unauthorized personnel from entering the work area.
items.statement: Barricades must form a perimeter at least 10 feet from the equipment to keep unauthorized personnel out of the work area, except where obstacles prevent that distance.

items.quote: In areas where obstacles prevent the barricade from being at least 10 feet away, the barricade must be as far from the equipment as feasible.
items.statement: Where obstacles prevent the barricade from being at least 10 feet from the equipment, it must be as far from the equipment as feasible.

items.quote: Workers other than the operator must be prohibited from touching the load line above the insulating link/device and crane.
items.statement: Workers other than the operator must be prohibited from touching the load line above the insulating link/device and crane.

items.quote: Operators remotely operating the equipment from the ground must use either wireless controls that isolate the operator from the equipment or insulating mats that insulate the operator from the ground.
items.statement: Operators remotely operating the equipment from the ground must use either wireless controls that isolate them from the equipment or insulating mats that insulate them from the ground.

items.quote: Only personnel essential to the operation are permitted to be in the area of the crane and load.
items.statement: Only personnel essential to the operation are permitted in the area of the crane and load.

items.quote: The equipment must be properly grounded.
items.statement: The equipment must be properly grounded.

items.quote: Insulating line hose or cover-up must be installed by the utility owner/operator except where such devices are unavailable for the line voltages involved.
items.statement: The utility owner/operator must install insulating line hose or cover-up, except where such devices are unavailable for the line voltages involved.

items.quote: The procedures developed to comply with paragraph (d) of this section are documented and immediately available on-site.
items.statement: The procedures developed to comply with paragraph (d) must be documented and immediately available on-site.

items.quote: The equipment user and utility owner/operator (or registered professional engineer) meet with the equipment operator and the other workers who will be in the area of the equipment or load to review the procedures that will be implemented to prevent breaching the minimum approach distance established in paragraph (c) of this section and prevent electrocution.
items.statement: The equipment user and utility owner/operator (or registered professional engineer) must meet with the equipment operator and other workers who will be near the equipment or load to review the procedures for preventing electrocution and breaches of the paragraph (c) minimum approach distance.

items.quote: The procedures developed to comply with paragraph (d) of this section are implemented.
items.statement: The procedures developed to comply with paragraph (d) must be implemented.

items.quote: The utility owner/operator (or registered professional engineer) and all employers of employees involved in the work must identify one person who will direct the implementation of the procedures.
items.statement: The utility owner/operator (or registered professional engineer) and all employers of employees involved in the work must identify one person to direct implementation of the procedures.

items.quote: The person identified in accordance with this paragraph must direct the implementation of the procedures
items.statement: The person identified to direct implementation must direct the implementation of the procedures.

items.quote: must have the authority to stop work at any time to ensure safety.
items.statement: The person identified to direct implementation must have the authority to stop work at any time to ensure safety.

items.quote: If a problem occurs implementing the procedures being used to comply with paragraph (d) of this section, or indicating that those procedures are inadequate to prevent electrocution, the employer must safely stop operations and either develop new procedures to comply with paragraph (d) of this section or have the utility owner/operator deenergize and visibly ground or relocate the power line before resuming work.
items.statement: If a problem occurs implementing the paragraph (d) procedures, or indicates they are inadequate to prevent electrocution, the employer must safely stop operations and, before resuming work, either develop new paragraph (d) procedures or have the utility owner/operator deenergize and visibly ground, or relocate, the power line.

items.quote: Devices originally designed by the manufacturer for use as a safety device (see § 1926.1415), operational aid, or a means to prevent power line contact or electrocution, when used to comply with this section, must comply with the manufacturer's procedures for use and conditions of use.
items.statement: Devices the manufacturer originally designed as a safety device (see § 1926.1415), operational aid, or means to prevent power line contact or electrocution must, when used to comply with this section, comply with the manufacturer's procedures and conditions of use.

items.quote: The employer must train each operator and crew member assigned to work with the equipment in accordance with § 1926.1408(g).
items.statement: The employer must train each operator and crew member assigned to work with the equipment in accordance with § 1926.1408(g).

items.quote: This section establishes procedures and criteria that must be met for equipment traveling under or near a power line on a construction site with no load.
items.statement: Section 1926.1411 sets the procedures and criteria that must be met for equipment traveling under or near a power line on a construction site with no load.

items.quote: Equipment traveling on a construction site with a load is governed by § 1926.1408, § 1926.1409 or § 1926.1410, whichever is appropriate, and § 1926.1417(u).
items.statement: Equipment traveling on a construction site with a load is excepted from this no-load section and is governed by § 1926.1408, § 1926.1409 or § 1926.1410, whichever is appropriate, and by § 1926.1417(u).

items.quote: The boom/mast and boom/mast support system are lowered sufficiently to meet the requirements of this paragraph.
items.statement: For equipment traveling under or near a power line with no load, the employer must ensure the boom/mast and boom/mast support system are lowered enough to meet the requirements of paragraph (b).

items.quote: The clearances specified in Table T of this section are maintained.
items.statement: For equipment traveling under or near a power line with no load, the employer must ensure the Table T clearances are maintained.

items.quote: The effects of speed and terrain on equipment movement (including movement of the boom/mast) are considered so that those effects do not cause the minimum clearance distances specified in Table T of this section to be breached.
items.statement: The employer must ensure the effects of speed and terrain on equipment movement, including boom/mast movement, are considered so they do not cause the Table T minimum clearance distances to be breached.

items.quote: If any part of the equipment while traveling will get closer than 20 feet to the power line, the employer must ensure that a dedicated spotter
items.statement: If any part of the equipment will get closer than 20 feet to the power line while traveling, the employer must ensure a dedicated spotter is used.

items.quote: If any part of the equipment while traveling will get closer than 20 feet to the power line, the employer must ensure that a dedicated spotter who is in continuous contact with the driver/operator is used.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter required when traveling equipment will get closer than 20 feet to a power line must be in continuous contact with the driver/operator.

items.quote: Be positioned to effectively gauge the clearance distance.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must be positioned to effectively gauge the clearance distance.

items.quote: Where necessary, use equipment that enables the dedicated spotter to communicate directly with the operator.
items.statement: Where necessary, the dedicated spotter must use equipment that enables the spotter to communicate directly with the operator.

items.quote: Give timely information to the operator so that the required clearance distance can be maintained.
items.statement: The dedicated spotter must give the operator timely information so the required clearance distance can be maintained.

items.quote: The power lines are illuminated or another means of identifying the location of the lines is used.
items.statement: When traveling at night or in poor visibility, in addition to the measures in paragraphs (b)(1) through (4), the employer must ensure the power lines are illuminated or another means of identifying their location is used.

items.quote: A safe path of travel is identified and used.
items.statement: When traveling at night or in poor visibility, in addition to the measures in paragraphs (b)(1) through (4), the employer must ensure a safe path of travel is identified and used.

items.statement: When traveling with no load, the minimum clearance from a power line of up to 0.75 kV (nominal, AC) is 4 feet.
