items.quote: Over 1,000 | (as established by the utility owner/operator or registered professional engineer who is a qualified person with respect to electrical power transmission and distribution).
items.statement: For power lines over 1,000 kV (nominal, AC), the minimum no-load travel clearance is as established by the utility owner/operator or by a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person with respect to electrical power transmission and distribution.

items.quote: Equipment that has had modifications or additions which affect the safe operation of the equipment (such as modifications or additions involving a safety device or operational aid, critical part of a control system, power plant, braking system, load-sustaining structural components, load hook, or in-use operating mechanism) or capacity must be inspected by a qualified person after such modifications/additions have been completed, prior to initial use.
items.statement: A qualified person must inspect equipment with modifications or additions that affect its safe operation or capacity, after the work is completed and before initial use.

items.quote: The inspection must assure that the modifications or additions have been done in accordance with the approval obtained pursuant to § 1926.1434 (Equipment modifications).
items.statement: The modified equipment inspection must assure that the modifications or additions were done in accordance with the approval obtained under § 1926.1434.

items.quote: The inspection must include functional testing of the equipment.
items.statement: The modified equipment inspection must include functional testing of the equipment.

items.quote: Equipment must not be used until an inspection under this paragraph demonstrates that the requirements of paragraph (a)(1)(i) of this section have been met.
items.statement: Modified equipment must not be used until an inspection demonstrates that the modifications or additions were done in accordance with the § 1926.1434 approval, as required by paragraph (a)(1)(i).

items.quote: Equipment that has had a repair or adjustment that relates to safe operation (such as: A repair or adjustment to a safety device or operator aid, or to a critical part of a control system, power plant, braking system, load-sustaining structural components, load hook, or in-use operating mechanism), must be inspected by a qualified person after such a repair or adjustment has been completed, prior to initial use.
items.statement: A qualified person must inspect equipment that has had a repair or adjustment relating to safe operation, after the work is completed and before initial use.

items.quote: The qualified person must determine if the repair/adjustment meets manufacturer equipment criteria (where applicable and available).
items.statement: Where manufacturer equipment criteria are applicable and available, the qualified person must determine whether the repair or adjustment meets them.

items.quote: (A) Determine if a registered professional engineer (RPE) is needed to develop criteria for the repair/adjustment.
items.statement: Where manufacturer equipment criteria are unavailable or inapplicable, the qualified person must determine whether a registered professional engineer (RPE) is needed to develop criteria for the repair or adjustment.

items.quote: If an RPE is not needed, the employer must ensure that the criteria are developed by the qualified person.
items.statement: If an RPE is not needed to develop repair or adjustment criteria where manufacturer criteria are unavailable or inapplicable, the employer must ensure the qualified person develops them.

items.quote: If an RPE is needed, the employer must ensure that they are developed by an RPE.
items.statement: If an RPE is needed to develop repair or adjustment criteria where manufacturer criteria are unavailable or inapplicable, the employer must ensure an RPE develops them.

items.quote: (B) Determine if the repair/adjustment meets the criteria developed in accordance with paragraph (b)(1)(ii)(A) of this section.
items.statement: Where manufacturer criteria are unavailable or inapplicable, the qualified person must determine whether the repair or adjustment meets the criteria developed by the qualified person or RPE.

items.quote: The inspection must include functional testing of the repaired/adjusted parts and other components that may be affected by the repair/adjustment.
items.statement: The repair or adjustment inspection must include functional testing of the repaired or adjusted parts and of other components the work may affect.

items.quote: Equipment must not be used until an inspection under this paragraph demonstrates that the repair/adjustment meets the requirements of paragraph (b)(1)(i) of this section (or, where applicable, paragraph (b)(1)(ii) of this section).
items.statement: Repaired or adjusted equipment must not be used until an inspection demonstrates that the work meets paragraph (b)(1)(i) (manufacturer criteria) or, where applicable, paragraph (b)(1)(ii) (developed criteria).

items.quote: Upon completion of assembly, the equipment must be inspected by a qualified person to assure that it is configured in accordance with manufacturer equipment criteria.
items.statement: When assembly is complete, a qualified person must inspect the equipment to assure it is configured in accordance with manufacturer equipment criteria.

items.quote: (i) Determine if a registered professional engineer (RPE) familiar with the type of equipment involved is needed to develop criteria for the equipment configuration.
items.statement: Where manufacturer equipment criteria are unavailable after assembly, a qualified person must determine whether an RPE familiar with the type of equipment is needed to develop configuration criteria.

items.quote: If an RPE is not needed, the employer must ensure that the criteria are developed by the qualified person.
items.statement: If an RPE is not needed to develop configuration criteria where manufacturer criteria are unavailable, the employer must ensure the qualified person develops them.

items.quote: If an RPE is needed, the employer must ensure that they are developed by an RPE.
items.statement: If an RPE is needed to develop configuration criteria where manufacturer criteria are unavailable, the employer must ensure an RPE develops them.

items.quote: (ii) Determine if the equipment meets the criteria developed in accordance with paragraph (c)(2)(i) of this section.
items.statement: Where manufacturer criteria are unavailable, a qualified person must determine whether the assembled equipment meets the developed configuration criteria.

items.quote: Equipment must not be used until an inspection under this paragraph demonstrates that the equipment is configured in accordance with the applicable criteria.
items.statement: Assembled equipment must not be used until a post-assembly inspection demonstrates it is configured in accordance with the applicable criteria.

items.quote: A competent person must begin a visual inspection prior to each shift the equipment will be used
items.statement: A competent person must begin a visual inspection before each shift in which the equipment will be used.

items.quote: which must be completed before or during that shift
items.statement: The each-shift visual inspection must be completed before or during that shift.

items.quote: The inspection must consist of observation for apparent deficiencies.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must consist of observation for apparent deficiencies.

items.quote: Taking apart equipment components and booming down is not required as part of this inspection unless the results of the visual inspection or trial operation indicate that further investigation necessitating taking apart equipment components or booming down is needed.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection does not require taking apart components or booming down, unless the visual inspection or trial operation results indicate further investigation requiring either is needed.

items.quote: Determinations made in conducting the inspection must be reassessed in light of observations made during operation.
items.statement: Determinations made during the each-shift inspection must be reassessed in light of observations made during operation.

items.quote: Control mechanisms for maladjustments interfering with proper operation.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must at minimum check control mechanisms for maladjustments that interfere with proper operation.

items.quote: Control and drive mechanisms for apparent excessive wear of components and contamination by lubricants, water or other foreign matter.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check control and drive mechanisms for apparent excessive component wear and for contamination by lubricants, water or other foreign matter.

items.quote: Air, hydraulic, and other pressurized lines for deterioration or leakage, particularly those which flex in normal operation.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check air, hydraulic and other pressurized lines for deterioration or leakage, particularly lines that flex in normal operation.

items.quote: Hydraulic system for proper fluid level.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check the hydraulic system for proper fluid level.

items.quote: Hooks and latches for deformation, cracks, excessive wear, or damage such as from chemicals or heat.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check hooks and latches for deformation, cracks, excessive wear, or damage such as from chemicals or heat.

items.quote: Wire rope reeving for compliance with the manufacturer's specifications.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check wire rope reeving for compliance with the manufacturer's specifications.

items.quote: Wire rope, in accordance with § 1926.1413(a).
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check wire rope in accordance with § 1926.1413(a).

items.quote: Electrical apparatus for malfunctioning, signs of apparent excessive deterioration, dirt or moisture accumulation.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check electrical apparatus for malfunctioning, signs of apparent excessive deterioration, and dirt or moisture accumulation.

items.quote: Tires (when in use) for proper inflation and condition.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check tires, when in use, for proper inflation and condition.

items.quote: Ground conditions around the equipment for proper support, including ground settling under and around outriggers/stabilizers and supporting foundations, ground water accumulation, or similar conditions.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check ground conditions around the equipment for proper support, including ground settling under and around outriggers/stabilizers and supporting foundations, ground water accumulation, or similar conditions.

items.quote: This paragraph does not apply to the inspection of ground conditions for railroad tracks and their underlying support when the railroad tracks are part of the general railroad system of transportation that is regulated pursuant to the Federal Railroad Administration under 49 CFR part 213.
items.statement: The ground-condition check does not apply to railroad tracks and their underlying support when the tracks are part of the general railroad system of transportation regulated by the Federal Railroad Administration under 49 CFR part 213.

items.quote: The equipment for level position within the tolerances specified by the equipment manufacturer's recommendations, both before each shift and after each move and setup.
items.statement: The equipment must be inspected for level position within the manufacturer's recommended tolerances, both before each shift and after each move and setup.

items.quote: Operator cab windows for significant cracks, breaks, or other deficiencies that would hamper the operator's view.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check operator cab windows for significant cracks, breaks, or other deficiencies that would hamper the operator's view.

items.quote: Rails, rail stops, rail clamps and supporting surfaces when the equipment has rail traveling.
items.statement: When the equipment has rail traveling, the each-shift inspection must check rails, rail stops, rail clamps and supporting surfaces.

items.quote: This paragraph does not apply to the inspection of rails, rail stops, rail clamps and supporting surfaces when the railroad tracks are part of the general railroad system of transportation that is regulated pursuant to the Federal Railroad Administration under 49 CFR part 213.
items.statement: The check of rails, rail stops, rail clamps and supporting surfaces does not apply when the railroad tracks are part of the general railroad system of transportation regulated by the Federal Railroad Administration under 49 CFR part 213.

items.quote: Safety devices and operational aids for proper operation.
items.statement: The each-shift inspection must check safety devices and operational aids for proper operation.

items.quote: If any deficiency in paragraphs (d)(1)(i) through (xiii) of this section (or in additional inspection items required to be checked for specific types of equipment in accordance with other sections of this standard) is identified, an immediate determination must be made by the competent person as to whether the deficiency constitutes a safety hazard.
items.statement: If a deficiency is found in items (d)(1)(i) through (xiii), or in additional items that other sections require for specific equipment types, the competent person must immediately determine whether it is a safety hazard.

items.quote: If the deficiency is determined to constitute a safety hazard, the equipment must be taken out of service until it has been corrected.
items.statement: If a deficiency covered by paragraph (d)(2) is determined to be a safety hazard, the equipment must be taken out of service until it is corrected.

items.quote: If any deficiency in paragraph (d)(1)(xiv) of this section (safety devices/operational aids) is identified, the action specified in §§ 1926.1415 and 1926.1416 must be taken prior to using the equipment.
items.statement: If a safety device or operational aid deficiency is identified, the action specified in §§ 1926.1415 and 1926.1416 must be taken before using the equipment.

items.quote: Each month the equipment is in service it must be inspected in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section (each shift).
items.statement: Each month the equipment is in service, it must be inspected in accordance with the each-shift requirements of paragraph (d).

items.quote: Equipment must not be used until an inspection under this paragraph demonstrates that no corrective action under paragraphs (d)(2) and (3) of this section is required.
items.statement: Equipment must not be used until a monthly inspection demonstrates that no corrective action under paragraphs (d)(2) and (d)(3) is required.

items.quote:
(i) The following information must be documented and maintained by the employer that conducts the inspection:
[29cfr1926.1412(e)(3)(i)(A)] (A) The items checked and the results of the inspection.
items.statement: The employer that conducts the monthly inspection must document and maintain the items checked and the inspection results.

items.quote: (B) The name and signature of the person who conducted the inspection and the date.
items.statement: The employer that conducts the monthly inspection must document and maintain the name and signature of the person who conducted it, along with the date.

items.quote: This document must be retained for a minimum of three months.
items.statement: The monthly inspection document must be retained for at least three months.

items.quote: At least every 12 months the equipment must be inspected by a qualified person in accordance with paragraph (d) of this section
items.statement: At least every 12 months, a qualified person must inspect the equipment in accordance with paragraph (d) (each shift) of this section.

items.quote: except that the corrective action set forth in paragraphs (f)(4), (f)(5), and (f)(6) of this section must apply in place of the corrective action required by paragraphs (d)(2) and (d)(3) of this section.
items.statement: For the inspection under paragraph (f)(1), the corrective actions in paragraphs (f)(4), (f)(5) and (f)(6) apply in place of the corrective action required by paragraphs (d)(2) and (d)(3).

items.quote: In addition, at least every 12 months, the equipment must be inspected by a qualified person.
items.statement: In addition to the paragraph (f)(1) inspection, a qualified person must inspect the equipment at least every 12 months for all items listed in paragraph (f)(2).

items.quote: Disassembly is required, as necessary, to complete the inspection.
items.statement: Equipment must be disassembled as necessary to complete the annual/comprehensive inspection.

items.quote: Structural members: Deformed, cracked, or significantly corroded.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check structural members of the equipment structure, including the boom and any jib, for deformation, cracks or significant corrosion.

items.quote: Bolts, rivets and other fasteners: loose, failed or significantly corroded.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check bolts, rivets and other fasteners in the equipment structure, including the boom and any jib, for being loose, failed or significantly corroded.

items.quote: Welds for cracks.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check welds in the equipment structure, including the boom and any jib, for cracks.

items.quote: Sheaves and drums for cracks or significant wear.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check sheaves and drums for cracks or significant wear.

items.quote: Parts such as pins, bearings, shafts, gears, rollers and locking devices for distortion, cracks or significant wear.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check parts such as pins, bearings, shafts, gears, rollers and locking devices for distortion, cracks or significant wear.

items.quote: Brake and clutch system parts, linings, pawls and ratchets for excessive wear.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check brake and clutch system parts, linings, pawls and ratchets for excessive wear.

items.quote: Safety devices and operational aids for proper operation (including significant inaccuracies).
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check safety devices and operational aids for proper operation, including significant inaccuracies.

items.quote: Gasoline, diesel, electric, or other power plants for safety-related problems (such as leaking exhaust and emergency shut-down feature) and conditions, and proper operation.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check gasoline, diesel, electric or other power plants for safety-related problems (such as leaking exhaust and emergency shut-down feature) and conditions, and for proper operation.

items.quote: Chains and chain drive sprockets for excessive wear of sprockets and excessive chain stretch.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check chains and chain drive sprockets for excessive sprocket wear and excessive chain stretch.

items.quote: Travel steering, brakes, and locking devices, for proper operation.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check travel steering, brakes and locking devices for proper operation.

items.quote: Tires for damage or excessive wear.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check tires for damage or excessive wear.

items.quote: Flexible hose or its junction with the fittings for indications of leaks.
items.statement: For hydraulic, pneumatic and other pressurized hoses, fittings and tubing, the annual/comprehensive inspection must check flexible hose or its junction with the fittings for indications of leaks.

items.quote: Threaded or clamped joints for leaks.
items.statement: For hydraulic, pneumatic and other pressurized hoses, fittings and tubing, the annual/comprehensive inspection must check threaded or clamped joints for leaks.

items.quote: Outer covering of the hose for blistering, abnormal deformation or other signs of failure/impending failure.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check the outer covering of pressurized hose for blistering, abnormal deformation or other signs of failure or impending failure.

items.quote: Outer surface of a hose, rigid tube, or fitting for indications of excessive abrasion or scrubbing.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check the outer surface of a pressurized hose, rigid tube or fitting for indications of excessive abrasion or scrubbing.

items.quote: Performance indicators: Unusual noises or vibration, low operating speed, excessive heating of the fluid, low pressure.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check hydraulic and pneumatic pumps and motors for these performance indicators: unusual noises or vibration, low operating speed, excessive fluid heating and low pressure.

items.quote: Loose bolts or fasteners.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check hydraulic and pneumatic pumps and motors for loose bolts or fasteners.

items.quote: Shaft seals and joints between pump sections for leaks.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check shaft seals and joints between sections of hydraulic and pneumatic pumps for leaks.

items.quote: Spools: Sticking, improper return to neutral, and leaks.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check hydraulic and pneumatic valve spools for sticking, improper return to neutral and leaks.

items.quote: (B) Leaks.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check hydraulic and pneumatic valves for leaks.

items.quote: Valve housing cracks.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check hydraulic and pneumatic valve housings for cracks.

items.quote: Relief valves: Failure to reach correct pressure
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check hydraulic and pneumatic relief valves for failure to reach correct pressure.

items.quote: if there is a manufacturer procedure for checking pressure, it must be followed
items.statement: If there is a manufacturer procedure for checking relief valve pressure, it must be followed.

items.quote: Drifting caused by fluid leaking across the piston.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check hydraulic and pneumatic cylinders for drifting caused by fluid leaking across the piston.

items.quote: Rod seals and welded joints for leaks.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check rod seals and welded joints of hydraulic and pneumatic cylinders for leaks.

items.quote: Cylinder rods for scores, nicks, or dents.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check hydraulic and pneumatic cylinder rods for scores, nicks or dents.

items.quote: Case (barrel) for significant dents.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check the case (barrel) of hydraulic and pneumatic cylinders for significant dents.

items.quote: Rod eyes and connecting joints: Loose or deformed.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check rod eyes and connecting joints of hydraulic and pneumatic cylinders for looseness or deformation.

items.quote: Outrigger or stabilizer pads/floats for excessive wear or cracks.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check outrigger or stabilizer pads/floats for excessive wear or cracks.

items.quote: Slider pads for excessive wear or cracks.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check slider pads for excessive wear or cracks.

items.quote: Electrical components and wiring for cracked or split insulation and loose or corroded terminations.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check electrical components and wiring for cracked or split insulation and loose or corroded terminations.

items.quote: Warning labels and decals originally supplied with the equipment by the manufacturer or otherwise required under this standard: Missing or unreadable.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check for missing or unreadable warning labels and decals that the manufacturer originally supplied with the equipment or that this standard otherwise requires.

items.quote: Originally equipped operator seat (or equivalent): Missing.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check whether the originally equipped operator seat (or equivalent) is missing.

items.quote: Operator seat: Unserviceable.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check whether the operator seat is unserviceable.

items.quote: Originally equipped steps, ladders, handrails, guards: Missing.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check for missing originally equipped steps, ladders, handrails and guards.

items.quote: Steps, ladders, handrails, guards: In unusable/unsafe condition.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must check whether steps, ladders, handrails and guards are in unusable or unsafe condition.

items.quote: This inspection must include functional testing to determine that the equipment as configured in the inspection is functioning properly.
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must include functional testing to determine that the equipment, as configured in the inspection, is functioning properly.

items.quote: If any deficiency is identified, an immediate determination must be made by the qualified person as to whether the deficiency constitutes a safety hazard or, though not yet a safety hazard, needs to be monitored in the monthly inspections.
items.statement: If any deficiency is identified, the qualified person must immediately determine whether it is a safety hazard or, though not yet a safety hazard, needs to be monitored in the monthly inspections.

items.quote: If the qualified person determines that a deficiency is a safety hazard, the equipment must be taken out of service until it has been corrected, except when temporary alternative measures are implemented as specified in § 1926.1416(d) or § 1926.1435(e).
items.statement: If the qualified person determines a deficiency is a safety hazard, the equipment must be taken out of service until it is corrected, except when temporary alternative measures are implemented as specified in § 1926.1416(d) or § 1926.1435(e).

items.quote: If the qualified person determines that, though not presently a safety hazard, the deficiency needs to be monitored, the employer must ensure that the deficiency is checked in the monthly inspections.
items.statement: If the qualified person determines that a deficiency is not presently a safety hazard but needs monitoring, the employer must ensure it is checked in the monthly inspections.

items.quote: The following information must be documented, maintained, and retained for a minimum of 12 months, by the employer that conducts the inspection:
items.statement: The employer that conducts the annual/comprehensive inspection must document, maintain and retain the required inspection information for at least 12 months.

items.quote: The items checked and the results of the inspection.
items.statement: The employer conducting the annual/comprehensive inspection must document the items checked and the results of the inspection.

items.quote: The name and signature of the person who conducted the inspection and the date.
items.statement: The employer conducting the annual/comprehensive inspection must document the inspector's name and signature and the date.

items.quote: Where the severity of use/conditions is such that there is a reasonable probability of damage or excessive wear (such as loading that may have exceeded rated capacity, shock loading that may have exceeded rated capacity, prolonged exposure to a corrosive atmosphere), the employer must stop using the equipment
items.statement: When severity of use or conditions creates a reasonable probability of damage or excessive wear (such as loading or shock loading that may have exceeded rated capacity, or prolonged exposure to a corrosive atmosphere), the employer must stop using the equipment.

items.quote: Inspect the equipment for structural damage to determine if the equipment can continue to be used safely.
items.statement: Under severe service conditions, a qualified person must inspect the equipment for structural damage to determine whether it can continue to be used safely.

items.quote: In light of the use/conditions determine whether any items/conditions listed in paragraph (f) of this section need to be inspected
items.statement: Under severe service conditions, a qualified person must determine, in light of the use or conditions, whether any items or conditions listed in paragraph (f) need to be inspected.

items.quote: if so, the qualified person must inspect those items/conditions.
items.statement: If the qualified person determines under severe service that paragraph (f) items or conditions need inspection, the qualified person must inspect them.

items.quote: If a deficiency is found, the employer must follow the requirements in paragraphs (f)(4) through (6) of this section.
items.statement: If a deficiency is found in a severe service inspection, the employer must follow paragraphs (f)(4) through (f)(6).

items.quote: Equipment that has been idle for 3 months or more must be inspected by a qualified person in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (e) (Monthly) of this section before initial use.
items.statement: Equipment idle for 3 months or more must be inspected by a qualified person under the paragraph (e) monthly inspection requirements before initial use.

items.quote: Any part of a manufacturer's procedures regarding inspections that relate to safe operation (such as to a safety device or operational aid, critical part of a control system, power plant, braking system, load-sustaining structural components, load hook, or in-use operating mechanism) that is more comprehensive or has a more frequent schedule of inspection than the requirements of this section must be followed.
items.statement: Any part of a manufacturer's inspection procedures relating to safe operation that is more comprehensive or has a more frequent inspection schedule than this section's requirements must be followed.

items.quote: All documents produced under this section must be available, during the applicable document retention period, to all persons who conduct inspections under this section.
items.statement: All documents produced under this section must be available, during the applicable retention period, to all persons who conduct inspections under this section.

items.quote: A competent person must begin a visual inspection prior to each shift the equipment is used
items.statement: A competent person must begin a visual wire rope inspection before each shift in which the equipment is used.

items.quote: which must be completed before or during that shift
items.statement: The shift visual inspection of wire rope must be completed before or during the shift.

items.quote: The inspection must consist of observation of wire ropes (running and standing) that are likely to be in use during the shift for apparent deficiencies, including those listed in paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
items.statement: The shift inspection must consist of observing the running and standing wire ropes likely to be used during the shift for apparent deficiencies, including those listed in paragraph (a)(2).

items.quote: Untwisting (opening) of wire rope or booming down is not required as part of this inspection.
items.statement: As an exception, the shift inspection does not require untwisting (opening) the wire rope or booming down.

items.quote: Significant distortion of the wire rope structure such as kinking, crushing, unstranding, birdcaging, signs of core failure or steel core protrusion between the outer strands.
items.statement: Category I apparent deficiencies include significant distortion of the wire rope structure, such as kinking, crushing, unstranding, birdcaging, signs of core failure, or steel core protrusion between the outer strands.

items.quote: (B) Significant corrosion.
items.statement: Significant corrosion is a Category I apparent deficiency.

items.quote: Electric arc damage (from a source other than power lines) or heat damage.
items.statement: Heat damage, or electric arc damage from a source other than power lines, is a Category I apparent deficiency.

items.quote: Improperly applied end connections.
items.statement: Improperly applied end connections are a Category I apparent deficiency.

items.quote: Significantly corroded, cracked, bent, or worn end connections (such as from severe service).
items.statement: Significantly corroded, cracked, bent, or worn end connections (such as from severe service) are a Category I apparent deficiency.

items.quote: In running wire ropes: Six randomly distributed broken wires in one rope lay
items.statement: In running wire ropes, six randomly distributed broken wires in one rope lay is a Category II apparent deficiency.
items.unit: broken wires in one rope lay

items.quote: three broken wires in one strand in one rope lay
items.statement: In running wire ropes, three broken wires in one strand in one rope lay is a Category II apparent deficiency.
items.unit: broken wires in one strand in one rope lay

items.quote: a rope lay is the length along the rope in which one strand makes a complete revolution around the rope
items.statement: A rope lay is the length along the rope in which one strand makes a complete revolution around the rope.

items.quote: In rotation resistant ropes: Two randomly distributed broken wires in six rope diameters
items.statement: In rotation resistant ropes, two randomly distributed broken wires in six rope diameters is a Category II apparent deficiency.
items.unit: broken wires in six rope diameters

items.quote: four randomly distributed broken wires in 30 rope diameters
items.statement: In rotation resistant ropes, four randomly distributed broken wires in 30 rope diameters is a Category II apparent deficiency.

items.quote: In pendants or standing wire ropes: More than two broken wires in one rope lay located in rope beyond end connections
items.statement: In pendants or standing wire ropes, more than two broken wires in one rope lay located in rope beyond end connections is a Category II apparent deficiency.
items.unit: broken wires in one rope lay

items.quote: more than one broken wire in a rope lay located at an end connection
items.statement: In pendants or standing wire ropes, more than one broken wire in a rope lay located at an end connection is a Category II apparent deficiency.
items.unit: broken wire in a rope lay

items.quote: A diameter reduction of more than 5% from nominal diameter.
items.statement: A wire rope diameter reduction of more than 5% from nominal diameter is a Category II apparent deficiency.

items.quote: In rotation resistant wire rope, core protrusion or other distortion indicating core failure.
items.statement: In rotation resistant wire rope, core protrusion or other distortion indicating core failure is a Category III apparent deficiency.

items.quote: Prior electrical contact with a power line.
items.statement: Prior electrical contact with a power line is a Category III apparent deficiency.

items.quote: A broken strand.
items.statement: A broken strand is a Category III apparent deficiency.

items.quote:
The competent person must give particular attention to all of the following:
[29cfr1926.1413(a)(3)(i)] (i) Rotation resistant wire rope in use.
items.statement: The competent person must give particular attention to rotation resistant wire rope in use.

items.quote: Wire rope being used for boom hoists and luffing hoists, particularly at reverse bends.
items.statement: The competent person must give particular attention to wire rope used for boom hoists and luffing hoists, particularly at reverse bends.

items.quote: Wire rope at flange points, crossover points and repetitive pickup points on drums.
items.statement: The competent person must give particular attention to wire rope at flange points, crossover points, and repetitive pickup points on drums.

items.quote: Wire rope at or near terminal ends.
items.statement: The competent person must give particular attention to wire rope at or near terminal ends.

items.quote: Wire rope in contact with saddles, equalizer sheaves or other sheaves where rope travel is limited.
items.statement: The competent person must give particular attention to wire rope in contact with saddles, equalizer sheaves, or other sheaves where rope travel is limited.

items.quote: an immediate determination must be made by the competent person as to whether the deficiency constitutes a safety hazard
items.statement: When a Category I deficiency is identified, the competent person must immediately determine whether it is a safety hazard.

items.quote: If the deficiency is determined to constitute a safety hazard, operations involving use of the wire rope in question must be prohibited until:
items.statement: If a Category I deficiency is determined to be a safety hazard, operations using that wire rope are prohibited until the rope is replaced or, if the deficiency is localized, corrected by severing as paragraph (a)(4)(i)(B) allows.

items.quote: If the deficiency is localized, the problem is corrected by severing the wire rope in two; the undamaged portion may continue to be used.
items.statement: A localized Category I safety hazard may be corrected by severing the wire rope in two, and the undamaged portion may continue to be used.

items.quote: Joining lengths of wire rope by splicing is prohibited.
items.statement: In correcting a Category I deficiency, joining lengths of wire rope by splicing is prohibited.

items.quote: the employer must ensure that the drum will still have two wraps of wire when the load and/or boom is in its lowest position
items.statement: If a rope is shortened to correct a Category I deficiency, the employer must ensure the drum still has two wraps of wire when the load and/or boom is in its lowest position.

items.quote: If a deficiency in Category II (see paragraph (a)(2)(ii) of this section) is identified, operations involving use of the wire rope in question must be prohibited until:
items.statement: When a Category II deficiency is identified, operations using that wire rope are prohibited until the employer meets an allowed removal criterion, the rope is replaced, or a localized deficiency is corrected by severing.

items.quote: The employer complies with the wire rope manufacturer's established criterion for removal from service or a different criterion that the wire rope manufacturer has approved in writing for that specific wire rope
items.statement: One way to lift the Category II operating prohibition is for the employer to comply with the wire rope manufacturer's established removal criterion, or a different criterion the manufacturer has approved in writing for that specific rope.

items.quote: If the deficiency is localized, the problem is corrected by severing the wire rope in two; the undamaged portion may continue to be used.
items.statement: A localized Category II deficiency may be corrected by severing the wire rope in two, and the undamaged portion may continue to be used.

items.quote: Joining lengths of wire rope by splicing is prohibited.
items.statement: In correcting a Category II deficiency, joining lengths of wire rope by splicing is prohibited.

items.quote: the employer must ensure that the drum will still have two wraps of wire when the load and/or boom is in its lowest position
items.statement: If a rope is shortened to correct a Category II deficiency, the employer must ensure the drum still has two wraps of wire when the load and/or boom is in its lowest position.

items.quote: If a deficiency in Category III is identified, operations involving use of the wire rope in question must be prohibited until:
items.statement: When a Category III deficiency is identified, operations using that wire rope are prohibited until it is replaced or, for a localized deficiency other than power line contact, corrected by severing.

items.quote: If the deficiency (other than power line contact) is localized, the problem is corrected by severing the wire rope in two; the undamaged portion may continue to be used.
items.statement: A localized Category III deficiency, other than power line contact, may be corrected by severing the wire rope in two, and the undamaged portion may continue to be used.

items.quote: Joining lengths of wire rope by splicing is prohibited.
items.statement: In correcting a Category III deficiency, joining lengths of wire rope by splicing is prohibited.

items.quote: Repair of wire rope that contacted an energized power line is also prohibited.
items.statement: Repairing wire rope that contacted an energized power line is prohibited.

items.quote: the employer must ensure that the drum will still have two wraps of wire when the load and/or boom is in its lowest position
items.statement: If a rope is shortened to correct a Category III deficiency, the employer must ensure the drum still has two wraps of wire when the load and/or boom is in its lowest position.

items.quote: either the equipment (as a whole) or the hoist with that wire rope must be tagged-out, in accordance with § 1926.1417(f)(1), until the wire rope is repaired or replaced
items.statement: When this section requires a wire rope to be removed from service, either the whole equipment or the hoist with that rope must be tagged out under § 1926.1417(f)(1) until the rope is repaired or replaced.

items.quote: Each month an inspection must be conducted in accordance with paragraph (a) (shift inspection) of this section.
items.statement: A wire rope inspection must be conducted each month in accordance with the shift inspection paragraph (a).

items.quote: The inspection must include any deficiencies that the qualified person who conducts the annual inspection determines under paragraph (c)(3)(ii) of this section must be monitored.
items.statement: The monthly inspection must include any deficiencies that the qualified person conducting the annual inspection determines under paragraph (c)(3)(ii) must be monitored.

items.quote: Wire ropes on equipment must not be used until an inspection under this paragraph demonstrates that no corrective action under paragraph (a)(4) of this section is required.
items.statement: Wire ropes on equipment must not be used until a monthly inspection shows that no corrective action under paragraph (a)(4) is required.

items.quote: The inspection must be documented according to § 1926.1412(e)(3) (monthly inspection documentation).
items.statement: The monthly inspection must be documented according to § 1926.1412(e)(3).

items.quote: At least every 12 months, wire ropes in use on equipment must be inspected by a qualified person in accordance with paragraph (a) of this section
items.statement: At least every 12 months, a qualified person must inspect wire ropes in use on equipment in accordance with the shift inspection paragraph (a).

items.quote: In addition, at least every 12 months, the wire ropes in use on equipment must be inspected by a qualified person
items.statement: In addition to the (c)(1) inspection, a qualified person must inspect wire ropes in use on equipment under the paragraph (c)(2) criteria at least every 12 months.

items.quote: The inspection must be for deficiencies of the types listed in paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
items.statement: The (c)(2) annual inspection must look for deficiencies of the types listed in paragraph (a)(2).

items.quote: The inspection must be complete and thorough, covering the surface of the entire length of the wire ropes
items.statement: The (c)(2) annual inspection must be complete and thorough, covering the surface of the entire length of the wire ropes.

items.quote:
with particular attention given to all of the following:
[29cfr1926.1413(c)(2)(ii)(A)] (A) Critical review items listed in paragraph (a)(3) of this section.
items.statement: The annual inspection must give particular attention to the critical review items listed in paragraph (a)(3).

items.quote: Those sections that are normally hidden during shift and monthly inspections.
items.statement: The annual inspection must give particular attention to rope sections normally hidden during shift and monthly inspections.

items.quote: Wire rope subject to reverse bends.
items.statement: The annual inspection must give particular attention to wire rope subject to reverse bends.

items.quote: Wire rope passing over sheaves.
items.statement: The annual inspection must give particular attention to wire rope passing over sheaves.

items.quote: such inspections must be conducted as soon as it becomes feasible, but no longer than an additional 6 months for running ropes
items.statement: As an exception, if the (c)(2) inspection is not feasible because of equipment set-up and configuration or site conditions, running ropes must be inspected as soon as feasible, but no longer than an additional 6 months.

items.quote: such inspections must be conducted as soon as it becomes feasible, but no longer than an additional 6 months for running ropes and, for standing ropes, at the time of disassembly
items.statement: As an exception, if the (c)(2) inspection is not feasible because of equipment set-up and configuration or site conditions, it must be done as soon as feasible but, for standing ropes, no later than at the time of disassembly.

items.quote: If a deficiency is identified, an immediate determination must be made by the qualified person as to whether the deficiency constitutes a safety hazard.
items.statement: If a deficiency is identified in the annual/comprehensive inspection, the qualified person must immediately determine whether it is a safety hazard.

items.quote: If the deficiency is determined to constitute a safety hazard, operations involving use of the wire rope in question must be prohibited until:
items.statement: If an annual inspection deficiency is determined to be a safety hazard, operations using that wire rope are prohibited until it is replaced or, if the deficiency is localized, corrected by severing.

items.quote: If the deficiency is localized, the problem is corrected by severing the wire rope in two; the undamaged portion may continue to be used.
items.statement: A localized safety hazard found in the annual inspection may be corrected by severing the wire rope in two, and the undamaged portion may continue to be used.

items.quote: Joining lengths of wire rope by splicing is prohibited.
items.statement: In correcting an annual inspection deficiency, joining lengths of wire rope by splicing is prohibited.

items.quote: the employer must ensure that the drum will still have two wraps of wire when the load and/or boom is in its lowest position
items.statement: If a rope is shortened to correct an annual inspection deficiency, the employer must ensure the drum still has two wraps of wire when the load and/or boom is in its lowest position.

items.quote: If the qualified person determines that, though not presently a safety hazard, the deficiency needs to be monitored, the employer must ensure that the deficiency is checked in the monthly inspections.
items.statement: If the qualified person determines that a deficiency is not presently a safety hazard but needs monitoring, the employer must ensure it is checked in the monthly inspections.

items.quote: The inspection must be documented according to § 1926.1412(f)(7) (annual/comprehensive inspection documentation).
items.statement: The annual/comprehensive inspection must be documented according to § 1926.1412(f)(7).

items.quote: Rope lubricants that are of the type that hinder inspection must not be used.
items.statement: Rope lubricants of the type that hinder inspection must not be used.

items.quote: All documents produced under this section must be available, during the applicable document retention period, to all persons who conduct inspections under this section.
items.statement: All documents produced under this section must be available, during the applicable retention period, to all persons who conduct inspections under this section.

items.quote: Original equipment wire rope and replacement wire rope must be selected and installed in accordance with the requirements of this section.
items.statement: Original equipment and replacement wire rope must be selected and installed in accordance with the requirements of § 1926.1414.

items.quote: Selection of replacement wire rope must be in accordance with the recommendations of the wire rope manufacturer, the equipment manufacturer, or a qualified person.
items.statement: Replacement wire rope must be selected according to the recommendations of the wire rope manufacturer, the equipment manufacturer, or a qualified person.

items.quote: Wire rope (other than rotation resistant rope) must comply with either Option (1) or Option (2) of this section
items.statement: Wire rope other than rotation resistant rope must comply with either Option (1) or Option (2) of the wire rope design criteria.

items.quote: Wire rope must comply with section 5-1.7.1 of ASME B30.5-2004 (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) except that section's paragraph (c) must not apply.
items.statement: Under design Option (1), wire rope must comply with section 5-1.7.1 of ASME B30.5-2004, except that paragraph (c) of that section must not apply.

items.quote: Wire rope must be designed to have, in relation to the equipment's rated capacity, a sufficient minimum breaking force and design factor so that compliance with the applicable inspection provisions in § 1926.1413 will be an effective means of preventing sudden rope failure.
items.statement: Under design Option (2), wire rope must be designed with a minimum breaking force and design factor, in relation to rated capacity, sufficient that complying with the applicable § 1926.1413 inspection provisions will effectively prevent sudden rope failure.

items.quote: Wire rope must be compatible with the safe functioning of the equipment.
items.statement: Wire rope must be compatible with the safe functioning of the equipment.

items.quote: Fiber core ropes must not be used for boom hoist reeving, except for derricks.
items.statement: Fiber core ropes must not be used for boom hoist reeving, except on derricks.

items.quote: Rotation resistant ropes must not be used for boom hoist reeving, except where the requirements of paragraph (e)(4)(ii) of this section are met.
items.statement: Rotation resistant ropes must not be used for boom hoist reeving except where the requirements of paragraph (e)(4)(ii) are met.

items.quote: Type I rotation resistant rope is stranded rope constructed to have little or no tendency to rotate or, if guided, transmits little or no torque.
items.statement: Type I rotation resistant rope is stranded rope constructed to have little or no tendency to rotate or, if guided, to transmit little or no torque.

items.quote: It has at least 15 outer strands
items.statement: Type I rotation resistant rope has at least 15 outer strands.

items.quote: comprises an assembly of at least three layers of strands laid helically over a center in two operations
items.statement: Type I rotation resistant rope comprises at least three layers of strands laid helically over a center in two operations.

items.quote: The direction of lay of the outer strands is opposite to that of the underlying layer.
items.statement: In Type I rope, the outer strands' direction of lay is opposite to that of the underlying layer.

items.quote: Type II rotation resistant rope is stranded rope constructed to have significant resistance to rotation.
items.statement: Type II rotation resistant rope is stranded rope constructed to have significant resistance to rotation.

items.quote: It has at least 10 outer strands
items.statement: Type II rotation resistant rope has at least 10 outer strands.

items.quote: comprises an assembly of two or more layers of strands laid helically over a center in two or three operations
items.statement: Type II rotation resistant rope comprises two or more layers of strands laid helically over a center in two or three operations.

items.quote: The direction of lay of the outer strands is opposite to that of the underlying layer.
items.statement: In Type II rope, the outer strands' direction of lay is opposite to that of the underlying layer.

items.quote: Type III rotation resistant rope is stranded rope constructed to have limited resistance to rotation.
items.statement: Type III rotation resistant rope is stranded rope constructed to have limited resistance to rotation.

items.quote: It has no more than nine outer strands
items.statement: Type III rotation resistant rope has no more than nine outer strands.

items.quote: comprises an assembly of two layers of strands laid helically over a center in two operations
items.statement: Type III rotation resistant rope comprises two layers of strands laid helically over a center in two operations.

items.quote: The direction of lay of the outer strands is opposite to that of the underlying layer.
items.statement: In Type III rope, the outer strands' direction of lay is opposite to that of the underlying layer.

items.quote: Types II and III with an operating design factor of less than 5 must not be used for duty cycle or repetitive lifts.
items.statement: Type II and III ropes with an operating design factor of less than 5 must not be used for duty cycle or repetitive lifts.

items.quote: Rotation resistant ropes (including Types I, II and III) must have an operating design factor of no less than 3.5.
items.statement: Rotation resistant ropes, including Types I, II and III, must have an operating design factor of at least 3.5.

items.quote: Type I must have an operating design factor of no less than 5, except where the wire rope manufacturer and the equipment manufacturer approves the design factor, in writing.
items.statement: Type I rope must have an operating design factor of at least 5, except where the wire rope manufacturer and the equipment manufacturer approve the design factor in writing.

items.quote: Types II and III must have an operating design factor of no less than 5, except where the requirements of paragraph (e)(3) of this section are met.
items.statement: Type II and III ropes must have an operating design factor of at least 5, except where the requirements of paragraph (e)(3) are met.

items.quote: A qualified person must inspect the rope in accordance with § 1926.1413(a).
items.statement: When Type II or III rope with an operating design factor below 5 is used for non-duty cycle, non-repetitive lifts, a qualified person must inspect the rope under § 1926.1413(a) for each lifting operation.

items.quote: The rope must be used only if the qualified person determines that there are no deficiencies constituting a hazard.
items.statement: For each lift with Type II or III rope with a design factor below 5, the rope may be used only if the qualified person determines it has no deficiencies constituting a hazard.

items.quote: more than one broken wire in any one rope lay must be considered a hazard
items.statement: When the qualified person evaluates Type II or III rope with a design factor below 5 before a lift, more than one broken wire in any one rope lay must be considered a hazard.
items.unit: broken wire in any one rope lay

items.quote: Operations must be conducted in such a manner and at such speeds as to minimize dynamic effects.
items.statement: For each lift using Type II or III rope with a design factor below 5 (non-duty cycle, non-repetitive), operations must be conducted in a manner and at speeds that minimize dynamic effects.

items.quote: Each lift made under § 1926.1414(e)(3) must be recorded in the monthly and annual inspection documents.
items.statement: Each lift made under § 1926.1414(e)(3) must be recorded in the monthly and annual inspection documents.

items.quote: Such prior uses must be considered by the qualified person in determining whether to use the rope again.
items.statement: The qualified person must consider prior uses under § 1926.1414(e)(3) when deciding whether to use the rope again.

items.quote: Rotation resistant ropes may be used as boom hoist reeving when load hoists are used as boom hoists for attachments such as luffing attachments or boom and mast attachment systems. Under these conditions, all of the following requirements must be met:
items.statement: Rotation resistant ropes may be used as boom hoist reeving when load hoists serve as boom hoists for attachments such as luffing or boom and mast attachment systems, provided all the requirements of (e)(4)(ii) are met.

items.quote: The drum must provide a first layer rope pitch diameter of not less than 18 times the nominal diameter of the rope used.
items.statement: When rotation resistant rope is used as boom hoist reeving under (e)(4)(ii), the drum must provide a first layer rope pitch diameter of at least 18 times the rope's nominal diameter.

items.quote: The requirements in § 1926.1426(a) (irrespective of the date of manufacture of the equipment), and § 1926.1426(b).
items.statement: Rotation resistant boom hoist reeving under (e)(4)(ii) must meet § 1926.1426(a), regardless of the equipment's date of manufacture, and § 1926.1426(b).

items.quote: The requirements in ASME B30.5-2004 sections 5-1.3.2(a), (a)(2) through (a)(4), (b) and (d) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6)
items.statement: Rotation resistant boom hoist reeving under (e)(4)(ii) must meet ASME B30.5-2004 sections 5-1.3.2(a), (a)(2) through (a)(4), (b) and (d), with the multiple-reeving sheave pitch diameter exception stated in this paragraph.

items.quote: the minimum pitch diameter for sheaves used in multiple rope reeving is 18 times the nominal diameter of the rope used (instead of the value of 16 specified in section 5-1.3.2(d))
items.statement: In applying the referenced ASME B30.5-2004 requirements, the minimum pitch diameter for sheaves in multiple rope reeving is 18 times the rope's nominal diameter instead of the 16 specified in section 5-1.3.2(d).
items.unit: times the nominal diameter of the rope

items.quote: All sheaves used in the boom hoist reeving system must have a rope pitch diameter of not less than 18 times the nominal diameter of the rope used.
items.statement: Under (e)(4)(ii), all sheaves in the boom hoist reeving system must have a rope pitch diameter of at least 18 times the rope's nominal diameter.

items.quote: The operating design factor for the boom hoist reeving system must be not less than five.
items.statement: Under (e)(4)(ii), the boom hoist reeving system's operating design factor must be at least five.

items.quote: The operating design factor for these ropes must be the total minimum breaking force of all parts of rope in the system divided by the load imposed on the rope system when supporting the static weights of the structure and the load within the equipment's rated capacity.
items.statement: The operating design factor for these ropes is the total minimum breaking force of all parts of rope in the system divided by the load on the rope system when supporting the static weights of the structure and the load within rated capacity.

items.quote: When provided, a power-controlled lowering system must be capable of handling rated capacities and speeds as specified by the manufacturer.
items.statement: Under (e)(4)(ii), a power-controlled lowering system, when provided, must be capable of handling the rated capacities and speeds specified by the manufacturer.

items.quote: Wire rope clips used in conjunction with wedge sockets must be attached to the unloaded dead end of the rope only
items.statement: Wire rope clips used with wedge sockets must be attached only to the unloaded dead end of the rope, subject to the exception for devices specifically designed for dead-ending rope in a wedge socket.

items.quote: except that the use of devices specifically designed for dead-ending rope in a wedge socket is permitted
items.statement: As an exception to the wedge socket clip rule, devices specifically designed for dead-ending rope in a wedge socket are permitted.

items.quote: Socketing must be done in the manner specified by the manufacturer of the wire rope or fitting.
items.statement: Socketing must be done in the manner specified by the wire rope or fitting manufacturer.

items.quote: Prior to cutting a wire rope, seizings must be placed on each side of the point to be cut.
items.statement: Before a wire rope is cut, seizings must be placed on each side of the cut point.

items.quote: The length and number of seizings must be in accordance with the wire rope manufacturer's instructions.
items.statement: The length and number of seizings used when cutting wire rope must follow the wire rope manufacturer's instructions.

items.quote: The following safety devices are required on all equipment covered by this subpart, unless otherwise specified:
items.statement: The safety devices listed in § 1926.1415 are required on all equipment covered by the subpart, unless otherwise specified.

items.quote: The equipment must have a crane level indicator that is either built into the equipment or is available on the equipment.
items.statement: The equipment must have a crane level indicator that is either built into the equipment or available on it.

items.quote: If a built-in crane level indicator is not working properly, it must be tagged-out or removed.
items.statement: A built-in crane level indicator that is not working properly must be tagged-out or removed.

items.quote: If a removable crane level indicator is not working properly, it must be removed.
items.statement: A removable crane level indicator that is not working properly must be removed.

items.quote: This requirement does not apply to portal cranes, derricks, floating cranes/derricks and land cranes/derricks on barges, pontoons, vessels or other means of flotation.
items.statement: The crane level indicator requirement does not apply to portal cranes, derricks, floating cranes/derricks, or land cranes/derricks on barges, pontoons, vessels or other means of flotation.

items.quote: Boom stops, except for derricks and hydraulic booms.
items.statement: Boom stops are a required safety device on covered equipment unless otherwise specified, except for derricks and hydraulic booms.

items.quote: Jib stops (if a jib is attached), except for derricks.
items.statement: If a jib is attached, jib stops are a required safety device, except for derricks.

items.quote: Equipment with foot pedal brakes must have locks.
items.statement: Equipment with foot pedal brakes must have locks.

items.quote: Hydraulic outrigger jacks and hydraulic stabilizer jacks must have an integral holding device/check valve.
items.statement: Hydraulic outrigger jacks and hydraulic stabilizer jacks must have an integral holding device/check valve.

items.quote: Equipment on rails must have rail clamps and rail stops, except for portal cranes.
items.statement: Equipment on rails must have rail clamps, except for portal cranes.

items.quote: Equipment on rails must have rail clamps and rail stops, except for portal cranes.
items.statement: Equipment on rails must have rail stops, except for portal cranes.

items.quote: The equipment must have a horn that is either built into the equipment or is on the equipment and immediately available to the operator.
items.statement: The equipment must have a horn that is either built into it, or is on it and immediately available to the operator.

items.quote: If a built-in horn is not working properly, it must be tagged-out or removed.
items.statement: A built-in horn that is not working properly must be tagged-out or removed.

items.quote: If a removable horn is not working properly, it must be removed.
items.statement: A removable horn that is not working properly must be removed.

items.quote: Operations must not begin unless all of the devices listed in this section are in proper working order.
items.statement: Operations must not begin unless all of the safety devices listed in § 1926.1415 are in proper working order.

items.quote: If a device stops working properly during operations, the operator must safely stop operations.
items.statement: If a safety device stops working properly during operations, the operator must safely stop operations.

items.quote: If any of the devices listed in this section are not in proper working order, the equipment must be taken out of service
items.statement: If any of the listed safety devices is not in proper working order, the equipment must be taken out of service.

items.quote: the equipment must be taken out of service and operations must not resume until the device is again working properly.
items.statement: When equipment is taken out of service because a listed safety device is not in proper working order, operations must not resume until the device is again working properly.

items.quote: Alternative measures are not permitted to be used.
items.statement: Alternative measures are not permitted to be used under the proper-operation requirement for the listed safety devices.

items.quote: The devices listed in this section (“listed operational aids”)
items.statement: "Listed operational aids" means the devices listed in § 1926.1416.

items.quote: are required on all equipment covered by this subpart, unless otherwise specified.
items.statement: The listed operational aids are required on all equipment covered by this subpart, unless otherwise specified.

items.quote: The requirements in paragraphs (e)(1), (e)(2), and (e)(3) of this section do not apply to articulating cranes.
items.statement: The requirements in paragraphs (e)(1), (e)(2) and (e)(3) do not apply to articulating cranes.

items.quote: The requirements in paragraphs (d)(3), (e)(1), and (e)(4) of this section apply only to those digger derricks manufactured after November 8, 2011.
items.statement: The requirements in paragraphs (d)(3), (e)(1) and (e)(4) apply only to those digger derricks manufactured after November 8, 2011.

items.quote: Operations must not begin unless the listed operational aids are in proper working order, except where an operational aid is being repaired the employer uses the specified temporary alternative measures.
items.statement: Operations must not begin unless the listed operational aids are in proper working order, except where an aid is being repaired and the employer uses the specified temporary alternative measures.

items.quote: More protective alternative measures specified by the crane/derrick manufacturer, if any, must be followed.
items.statement: If the crane/derrick manufacturer specifies more protective alternative measures, they must be followed.

items.quote: If a listed operational aid stops working properly during operations, the operator must safely stop operations until the temporary alternative measures are implemented or the device is again working properly.
items.statement: If a listed operational aid stops working properly during operations, the operator must safely stop operations until the temporary alternative measures are implemented or the device is again working properly.

items.quote: If a replacement part is no longer available, the use of a substitute device that performs the same type of function is permitted and is not considered a modification under § 1926.1434.
items.statement: If a replacement part is no longer available, a substitute device that performs the same type of function is permitted and is not considered a modification under § 1926.1434.

items.quote: Operational aids listed in this paragraph that are not working properly must be repaired no later than 7 calendar days after the deficiency occurs.
items.statement: Category I operational aids that are not working properly must be repaired no later than 7 calendar days after the deficiency occurs, subject to the parts-ordering exception.

items.quote: Exception: If the employer documents that it has ordered the necessary parts within 7 calendar days of the occurrence of the deficiency, the repair must be completed within 7 calendar days of receipt of the parts.
items.statement: As an exception for Category I aids, if the employer documents that it ordered the necessary parts within 7 calendar days of the deficiency occurring, the repair must be completed within 7 calendar days of receiving the parts.

items.quote: For equipment manufactured after December 16, 1969, a boom hoist limiting device is required.
items.statement: Equipment manufactured after December 16, 1969 must have a boom hoist limiting device.

items.quote: Temporary alternative measures (use at least one). One or more of the following methods must be used:
items.statement: As temporary alternative measures for a boom hoist limiting device, one or more of the methods in paragraphs (d)(1)(i)(A) through (C) must be used.

items.quote: Use a boom angle indicator.
items.statement: One temporary alternative method for a boom hoist limiting device is to use a boom angle indicator.

items.quote: Clearly mark the boom hoist cable (so that it can easily be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to keep the boom within the minimum allowable radius.
items.statement: One temporary alternative method for a boom hoist limiting device is to clearly mark the boom hoist cable, easily seen by the operator, at a point giving the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist and keep the boom within the minimum allowable radius.

items.quote: In addition, install mirrors or remote video cameras and displays if necessary for the operator to see the mark.
items.statement: When using the operator-visible boom hoist cable mark method, mirrors or remote video cameras and displays must also be installed if necessary for the operator to see the mark.

items.quote: Clearly mark the boom hoist cable (so that it can easily be seen by a spotter) at a point that will give the spotter sufficient time to signal the operator and have the operator stop the hoist to keep the boom within the minimum allowable radius.
items.statement: One temporary alternative method for a boom hoist limiting device is to clearly mark the boom hoist cable, easily seen by a spotter, at a point giving the spotter time to signal the operator and have the operator stop the hoist to keep the boom within the minimum allowable radius.

items.quote: If the equipment was manufactured on or before December 16, 1969, and is not equipped with a boom hoist limiting device, at least one of the measures in paragraphs (d)(1)(i)(A) through (C) of this section must be used.
items.statement: Equipment manufactured on or before December 16, 1969 that has no boom hoist limiting device must use at least one of the measures in paragraphs (d)(1)(i)(A) through (C).

items.quote: Equipment with a luffing jib must have a luffing jib limiting device.
items.statement: Equipment with a luffing jib must have a luffing jib limiting device.

items.quote: Temporary alternative measures are the same as in paragraph (d)(1)(i) of this section, except to limit the movement of the luffing jib rather than the boom hoist.
items.statement: Temporary alternative measures for a luffing jib limiting device are the same as in paragraph (d)(1)(i), except that they limit movement of the luffing jib rather than the boom hoist.

items.quote: Telescopic boom cranes manufactured after February 28, 1992, must be equipped with a device which automatically prevents damage from contact between the load block, overhaul ball, or similar component, and the boom tip (or fixed upper block or similar component).
items.statement: Telescopic boom cranes manufactured after February 28, 1992 must have a device that automatically prevents damage from contact between the load block, overhaul ball or similar component and the boom tip, fixed upper block or similar component.

items.quote: The device(s) must prevent such damage at all points where two-blocking could occur.
items.statement: On telescopic boom cranes manufactured after February 28, 1992, the anti two-blocking device(s) must prevent damage at all points where two-blocking could occur.

items.quote: Temporary alternative measures: Clearly mark the cable (so that it can easily be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, and use a spotter when extending the boom.
items.statement: The temporary alternative measures for the telescopic boom crane anti two-blocking device are to clearly mark the cable, easily seen by the operator, at a point giving the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, and also to use a spotter when extending the boom.

items.quote: Lattice boom cranes manufactured after Feb 28, 1992, must be equipped with a device that either automatically prevents damage and load failure from contact between the load block, overhaul ball, or similar component, and the boom tip (or fixed upper block or similar component), or warns the operator in time for the operator to prevent two-blocking.
items.statement: Lattice boom cranes manufactured after Feb 28, 1992 must have a device that either automatically prevents damage and load failure from two-block contact or warns the operator in time to prevent two-blocking, except for the uses excepted in paragraph (d)(3)(ii)(C).

items.quote: The device must prevent such damage/failure or provide adequate warning for all points where two-blocking could occur.
items.statement: On lattice boom cranes manufactured after Feb 28, 1992, the device must prevent the damage/failure or give adequate warning for all points where two-blocking could occur, except for the uses excepted in paragraph (d)(3)(ii)(C).

items.quote: Lattice boom cranes and derricks manufactured after November 8, 2011 must be equipped with a device which automatically prevents damage and load failure from contact between the load block, overhaul ball, or similar component, and the boom tip (or fixed upper block or similar component).
items.statement: Lattice boom cranes and derricks manufactured after November 8, 2011 must have a device that automatically prevents damage and load failure from two-block contact, except for the uses excepted in paragraph (d)(3)(ii)(C).

items.quote: The device(s) must prevent such damage/failure at all points where two-blocking could occur.
items.statement: On lattice boom cranes and derricks manufactured after November 8, 2011, the device(s) must prevent damage/failure at all points where two-blocking could occur, except for the uses excepted in paragraph (d)(3)(ii)(C).

items.quote: The requirements in paragraphs (d)(3)(ii)(A) and (B) of this section do not apply to such lattice boom equipment when used for dragline, clamshell (grapple), magnet, drop ball, container handling, concrete bucket, marine operations that do not involve hoisting personnel, and pile driving work.
items.statement: Paragraphs (d)(3)(ii)(A) and (B) do not apply to such lattice boom equipment when used for dragline, clamshell (grapple), magnet, drop ball, container handling, concrete bucket, marine operations that do not involve hoisting personnel, and pile driving work.

items.quote: Clearly mark the cable (so that it can easily be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, or use a spotter.
items.statement: The temporary alternative measures under the lattice boom provisions are to clearly mark the cable, easily seen by the operator, at a point giving the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, or to use a spotter.

items.quote: Articulating cranes manufactured after December 31, 1999, that are equipped with a load hoist must be equipped with a device that automatically prevents damage from contact between the load block, overhaul ball, or similar component, and the boom tip (or fixed upper block or similar component).
items.statement: Articulating cranes manufactured after December 31, 1999 that have a load hoist must have a device that automatically prevents damage from contact between the load block, overhaul ball or similar component and the boom tip, fixed upper block or similar component.

items.quote: The device must prevent such damage at all points where two-blocking could occur.
items.statement: On articulating cranes manufactured after December 31, 1999 with a load hoist, the device must prevent damage at all points where two-blocking could occur.

items.quote: When two-blocking could only occur with movement of the load hoist, clearly mark the cable (so that it can easily be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, or use a spotter.
items.statement: As a temporary alternative on these articulating cranes, when two-blocking could occur only with load hoist movement, clearly mark the cable so the operator can easily see it and has time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, or use a spotter.

items.quote: When two-blocking could occur without movement of the load hoist, clearly mark the cable (so that it can easily be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, and use a spotter when extending the boom.
items.statement: As a temporary alternative on these articulating cranes, when two-blocking could occur without load hoist movement, clearly mark the cable so the operator can easily see it and has time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, and also use a spotter when extending the boom.

items.quote: Operational aids listed in this paragraph that are not working properly must be repaired no later than 30 calendar days after the deficiency occurs.
items.statement: Category II operational aids that are not working properly must be repaired no later than 30 calendar days after the deficiency occurs, subject to the parts-ordering exception.

items.quote: Exception: If the employer documents that it has ordered the necessary parts within 7 calendar days of the occurrence of the deficiency, and the part is not received in time to complete the repair in 30 calendar days, the repair must be completed within 7 calendar days of receipt of the parts.
items.statement: As an exception for Category II aids, if the employer documents that it ordered the necessary parts within 7 calendar days of the deficiency, and the part does not arrive in time to complete the repair in 30 calendar days, the repair must be completed within 7 calendar days of receiving the parts.

items.quote: The equipment must have a boom angle or radius indicator readable from the operator's station.
