items.statement: Equipment must have a boom angle or radius indicator readable from the operator's station (this does not apply to articulating cranes, and applies to digger derricks only if manufactured after November 8, 2011).

items.quote: Radii or boom angle must be determined by measuring the radii or boom angle with a measuring device.
items.statement: As a temporary alternative to the boom angle or radius indicator, radii or boom angle must be determined by measuring them with a measuring device.

items.quote: Jib angle indicator if the equipment has a luffing jib.
items.statement: Equipment with a luffing jib must have a jib angle indicator (this does not apply to articulating cranes).

items.quote: Radii or jib angle must be determined by ascertaining the main boom angle and then measuring the radii or jib angle with a measuring device.
items.statement: As a temporary alternative to the jib angle indicator, radii or jib angle must be determined by ascertaining the main boom angle and then measuring the radii or jib angle with a measuring device.

items.quote: Boom length indicator if the equipment has a telescopic boom, except where the rated capacity is independent of the boom length.
items.statement: Equipment with a telescopic boom must have a boom length indicator, except where rated capacity is independent of boom length (this does not apply to articulating cranes).

items.quote: Temporary alternative measures. One or more of the following methods must be used:
items.statement: As temporary alternative measures for a boom length indicator, one or more of the methods in paragraphs (e)(3)(i) through (iii) must be used.

items.quote: Mark the boom with measured marks to calculate boom length
items.statement: One temporary alternative method for a boom length indicator is to mark the boom with measured marks to calculate boom length.

items.quote: Calculate boom length from boom angle and radius measurements
items.statement: One temporary alternative method for a boom length indicator is to calculate boom length from boom angle and radius measurements.

items.quote: Measure the boom with a measuring device.
items.statement: One temporary alternative method for a boom length indicator is to measure the boom with a measuring device.

items.quote: Equipment (other than derricks and articulating cranes) manufactured after March 29, 2003 with a rated capacity over 6,000 pounds must have at least one of the following: load weighing device, load moment (or rated capacity) indicator, or load moment (or rated capacity) limiter.
items.statement: Equipment other than derricks and articulating cranes, manufactured after March 29, 2003 with a rated capacity over 6,000 pounds, must have at least one of a load weighing device, load moment (or rated capacity) indicator, or load moment (or rated capacity) limiter.

items.quote: The weight of the load must be determined from a source recognized by the industry (such as the load's manufacturer) or by a calculation method recognized by the industry
items.statement: As a temporary alternative for the load weighing or similar device required by paragraph (e)(4)(i), the load weight must be determined from an industry-recognized source (such as the load's manufacturer) or by an industry-recognized calculation method.

items.quote: This information must be provided to the operator prior to the lift.
items.statement: Under the paragraph (e)(4)(i) temporary alternative measures, the load weight information must be provided to the operator before the lift.

items.quote: Articulating cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must have at least one of the following: automatic overload prevention device, load weighing device, load moment (or rated capacity) indicator, or load moment (rated capacity) limiter.
items.statement: Articulating cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must have at least one of an automatic overload prevention device, load weighing device, load moment (or rated capacity) indicator, or load moment (rated capacity) limiter.

items.quote: The weight of the load must be determined from a source recognized by the industry (such as the load's manufacturer) or by a calculation method recognized by the industry
items.statement: As a temporary alternative for the articulating crane devices in paragraph (e)(4)(ii), the load weight must be determined from an industry-recognized source (such as the load's manufacturer) or by an industry-recognized calculation method.

items.quote: This information must be provided to the operator prior to the lift.
items.statement: Under the articulating crane temporary alternative measures in paragraph (e)(4)(ii), the load weight information must be provided to the operator before the lift.

items.quote: Outrigger/stabilizer position (horizontal beam extension) sensor/monitor if the equipment has outriggers or stabilizers.
items.statement: Equipment manufactured after November 8, 2011 that has outriggers or stabilizers must have an outrigger/stabilizer position (horizontal beam extension) sensor/monitor.

items.quote: The operator must verify that the position of the outriggers or stabilizers is correct (in accordance with manufacturer procedures) before beginning operations requiring outrigger or stabilizer deployment.
items.statement: As a temporary alternative to the outrigger/stabilizer position sensor/monitor, the operator must verify under manufacturer procedures that the outrigger or stabilizer position is correct before beginning operations requiring their deployment.

items.quote: Hoist drum rotation indicator if the equipment has a hoist drum not visible from the operator's station.
items.statement: Equipment manufactured after November 8, 2011 with a hoist drum not visible from the operator's station must have a hoist drum rotation indicator.

items.quote: Mark the drum to indicate the rotation of the drum.
items.statement: As a temporary alternative to the hoist drum rotation indicator, the drum must be marked to indicate its rotation.

items.quote: In addition, install mirrors or remote video cameras and displays if necessary for the operator to see the mark.
items.statement: When using the drum mark as a temporary alternative, mirrors or remote video cameras and displays must also be installed if necessary for the operator to see the mark.

items.quote: The employer must comply with all manufacturer procedures applicable to the operational functions of equipment, including its use with attachments.
items.statement: The employer must comply with all manufacturer procedures applicable to the operational functions of equipment, including its use with attachments.

items.quote: Where the manufacturer procedures are unavailable, the employer must develop and ensure compliance with all procedures necessary for the safe operation of the equipment and attachments.
items.statement: Where manufacturer procedures are unavailable, the employer must develop all procedures necessary for the safe operation of the equipment and attachments.

items.quote: the employer must develop and ensure compliance with all procedures necessary for the safe operation of the equipment and attachments
items.statement: Where manufacturer procedures are unavailable, the employer must ensure compliance with all procedures necessary for the safe operation of the equipment and attachments.

items.quote: Procedures for the operational controls must be developed by a qualified person.
items.statement: Where manufacturer procedures are unavailable, procedures for the operational controls must be developed by a qualified person.

items.quote: Procedures related to the capacity of the equipment must be developed and signed by a registered professional engineer familiar with the equipment.
items.statement: Where manufacturer procedures are unavailable, procedures related to equipment capacity must be developed and signed by a registered professional engineer familiar with the equipment.

items.quote: The procedures applicable to the operation of the equipment, including rated capacities (load charts), recommended operating speeds, special hazard warnings, instructions, and operator's manual, must be readily available in the cab at all times for use by the operator.
items.statement: Procedures applicable to equipment operation, including rated capacities (load charts), recommended operating speeds, special hazard warnings, instructions and the operator's manual, must be readily available in the cab at all times for the operator's use.

items.quote: Where rated capacities are available in the cab only in electronic form: In the event of a failure which makes the rated capacities inaccessible, the operator must immediately cease operations or follow safe shut-down procedures until the rated capacities (in electronic or other form) are available.
items.statement: Where rated capacities are available in the cab only electronically and a failure makes them inaccessible, the operator must immediately cease operations or follow safe shut-down procedures until the rated capacities (in electronic or other form) are available.

items.quote: The operator must not engage in any practice or activity that diverts his/her attention while actually engaged in operating the equipment, such as the use of cellular phones (other than when used for signal communications).
items.statement: While actually operating the equipment, the operator must not engage in any practice or activity that diverts attention, such as using a cellular phone other than for signal communications.

items.quote: The operator must not leave the controls while the load is suspended, except where all of the following are met:
items.statement: The operator must not leave the controls while the load is suspended, except where all of the conditions in paragraphs (e)(1)(i) through (iv) are met.

items.quote: The operator remains adjacent to the equipment and is not engaged in any other duties.
items.statement: To qualify for the exception allowing the operator to leave the controls with a suspended load, the operator must remain adjacent to the equipment and not be engaged in any other duties.

items.quote: The load is to be held suspended for a period of time exceeding normal lifting operations.
items.statement: To qualify for the exception allowing the operator to leave the controls with a suspended load, the load must be held suspended for a period exceeding normal lifting operations.

items.quote: The competent person determines that it is safe to do so and implements measures necessary to restrain the boom hoist and telescoping, load, swing, and outrigger or stabilizer functions.
items.statement: Before the operator may leave the controls with a suspended load, the competent person must determine it is safe and implement measures necessary to restrain the boom hoist and telescoping, load, swing, and outrigger or stabilizer functions.

items.quote: Barricades or caution lines, and notices, are erected to prevent all employees from entering the fall zone.
items.statement: Before the operator may leave the controls with a suspended load, barricades or caution lines, and notices, must be erected to prevent all employees from entering the fall zone.

items.quote: No employees, including those listed in §§ 1926.1425(b)(1) through (3), § 1926.1425(d) or § 1926.1425(e), are permitted in the fall zone.
items.statement: When the operator leaves the controls with a suspended load under this exception, no employees, including those listed in §§ 1926.1425(b)(1) through (3), 1926.1425(d) or 1926.1425(e), are permitted in the fall zone.

items.quote: The provisions in § 1926.1417(e)(1) do not apply to working gear (such as slings, spreader bars, ladders, and welding machines) where the weight of the working gear is negligible relative to the lifting capacity of the equipment as positioned, and the working gear is suspended over an area other than an entrance or exit.
items.statement: Paragraph (e)(1) does not apply to working gear (such as slings, spreader bars, ladders and welding machines) when its weight is negligible relative to the equipment's lifting capacity as positioned and it is suspended over an area other than an entrance or exit.

items.quote: Where the employer has taken the equipment out of service, a tag must be placed in the cab stating that the equipment is out of service and is not to be used.
items.statement: Where the employer has taken equipment out of service, a tag must be placed in the cab stating that the equipment is out of service and is not to be used.

items.quote: Where the employer has taken a function(s) out of service, a tag must be placed in a conspicuous position stating that the function is out of service and is not to be used.
items.statement: Where the employer has taken a function out of service, a tag must be placed in a conspicuous position stating that the function is out of service and is not to be used.

items.quote:
the operator must not activate the switch or start the equipment until the sign has been removed by a person authorized to remove it, or until the operator has verified that:
[29cfr1926.1417(f)(2)(i)(A)] (A) No one is servicing, working on, or otherwise in a dangerous position on the machine.
[29cfr1926.1417(f)(2)(i)(B)] (B) The equipment has been repaired and is working properly.
items.statement: If a warning (tag-out or maintenance/do not operate) sign is on the equipment or starting control, the operator must not activate the switch or start the equipment until an authorized person removes the sign, or until the operator verifies both that no one is servicing, working on or otherwise dangerously positioned on the machine and that the equipment has been repaired and is working properly.

items.quote: If there is a warning (tag-out or maintenance/do not operate) sign on any other switch or control, the operator must not activate that switch or control until the sign has been removed by a person authorized to remove it, or until the operator has verified that the requirements in paragraphs (f)(2)(i)(A) and (B) of this section have been met.
items.statement: If a warning (tag-out or maintenance/do not operate) sign is on any other switch or control, the operator must not activate it until an authorized person removes the sign, or until the operator verifies that the requirements of (f)(2)(i)(A) and (B) have been met.

items.quote: Before starting the engine, the operator must verify that all controls are in the proper starting position
items.statement: Before starting the engine, the operator must verify that all controls are in the proper starting position.

items.quote: Before starting the engine, the operator must verify that all controls are in the proper starting position and that all personnel are in the clear.
items.statement: Before starting the engine, the operator must verify that all personnel are in the clear.

items.quote: When a local storm warning has been issued, the competent person must determine whether it is necessary to implement manufacturer recommendations for securing the equipment.
items.statement: When a local storm warning has been issued, the competent person must determine whether it is necessary to implement manufacturer recommendations for securing the equipment.

items.quote: The operator must, in writing, promptly inform the person designated by the employer to receive such information
items.statement: If equipment adjustments or repairs are necessary, the operator must promptly inform, in writing, the person the employer designated to receive such information.

items.quote: The operator must, in writing, promptly inform the person designated by the employer to receive such information and, where there are successive shifts, to the next operator
items.statement: If equipment adjustments or repairs are necessary and there are successive shifts, the operator must promptly inform the next operator in writing.

items.quote: The employer must notify all affected employees, at the beginning of each shift, of the necessary adjustments or repairs and all alternative measures.
items.statement: If equipment adjustments or repairs are necessary, the employer must notify all affected employees, at the beginning of each shift, of the necessary adjustments or repairs and all alternative measures.

items.quote: Safety devices and operational aids must not be used as a substitute for the exercise of professional judgment by the operator.
items.statement: Safety devices and operational aids must not be used as a substitute for the operator's exercise of professional judgment.

items.quote: If the competent person determines that there is a slack rope condition requiring re-spooling of the rope, it must be verified (before starting to lift) that the rope is seated on the drum and in the sheaves as the slack is removed.
items.statement: If the competent person determines there is a slack rope condition requiring re-spooling, it must be verified before starting to lift that the rope is seated on the drum and in the sheaves as the slack is removed.

items.quote: The competent person must adjust the equipment and/or operations to address the effect of wind, ice, and snow on equipment stability and rated capacity.
items.statement: The competent person must adjust the equipment and/or operations to address the effect of wind, ice and snow on equipment stability and rated capacity.

items.quote: The equipment must not be operated in excess of its rated capacity.
items.statement: The equipment must not be operated in excess of its rated capacity.

items.quote: The operator must not be required to operate the equipment in a manner that would violate paragraph (o)(1) of this section.
items.statement: The operator must not be required to operate the equipment in a manner that would exceed its rated capacity in violation of paragraph (o)(1).

items.quote: The operator must verify that the load is within the rated capacity of the equipment by at least one of the following methods:
items.statement: The operator must verify that the load is within the equipment's rated capacity by at least one of the methods in paragraph (o)(3)(i) or (ii).

items.quote: The weight of the load must be determined from a source recognized by the industry (such as the load's manufacturer), or by a calculation method recognized by the industry (such as calculating a steel beam from measured dimensions and a known per foot weight), or by other equally reliable means.
items.statement: Under the first load verification method, load weight must be determined from an industry-recognized source (such as the load's manufacturer), by an industry-recognized calculation method, or by other equally reliable means.

items.quote: In addition, when requested by the operator, this information must be provided to the operator prior to the lift
items.statement: Under the first load verification method, the load weight information must be provided to the operator before the lift when the operator requests it.

items.quote: The operator must begin hoisting the load to determine, using a load weighing device, load moment indicator, rated capacity indicator, or rated capacity limiter, if it exceeds 75 percent of the maximum rated capacity at the longest radius that will be used during the lift operation.
items.statement: Under the second load verification method, the operator must begin hoisting to determine, using a load weighing device, load moment indicator, rated capacity indicator or rated capacity limiter, whether the load exceeds 75 percent of the maximum rated capacity at the longest radius to be used during the lift.

items.quote: if it exceeds 75 percent of the maximum rated capacity at the longest radius that will be used during the lift operation. If it does, the operator must not proceed with the lift until he/she verifies the weight of the load in accordance with paragraph (o)(3)(i) of this section.
items.statement: If the load exceeds 75 percent of the maximum rated capacity at the longest radius to be used, the operator must not proceed with the lift until verifying the load weight under paragraph (o)(3)(i).

items.quote: The boom or other parts of the equipment must not contact any obstruction.
items.statement: The boom or other parts of the equipment must not contact any obstruction.

items.quote: The equipment must not be used to drag or pull loads sideways.
items.statement: The equipment must not be used to drag or pull loads sideways.

items.quote: On wheel-mounted equipment, no loads must be lifted over the front area, except as permitted by the manufacturer.
items.statement: On wheel-mounted equipment, no loads may be lifted over the front area except as permitted by the manufacturer.

items.quote: The operator must test the brakes each time a load that is 90% or more of the maximum line pull is handled by lifting the load a few inches and applying the brakes.
items.statement: The operator must test the brakes each time a load that is 90% or more of maximum line pull is handled, by lifting the load a few inches and applying the brakes.

items.quote: In duty cycle and repetitive lifts where each lift is 90% or more of the maximum line pull, this requirement applies to the first lift but not to successive lifts.
items.statement: In duty cycle and repetitive lifts where each lift is 90% or more of maximum line pull, the brake test applies to the first lift but not to successive lifts.

items.quote: Neither the load nor the boom must be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on their respective drums.
items.statement: Neither the load nor the boom may be lowered below the point where less than two full wraps of rope remain on their respective drums.

items.quote: Traveling with a load is prohibited if the practice is prohibited by the manufacturer.
items.statement: Traveling with a load is prohibited if the manufacturer prohibits the practice.

items.quote:
Where traveling with a load, the employer must ensure that:
[29cfr1926.1417(u)(2)(i)] (i) A competent person supervises the operation
items.statement: When traveling with a load, the employer must ensure that a competent person supervises the operation.

items.quote: A competent person supervises the operation, determines if it is necessary to reduce rated capacity
items.statement: When traveling with a load, the employer must ensure that a competent person determines whether it is necessary to reduce rated capacity.

items.quote: makes determinations regarding load position, boom location, ground support, travel route, overhead obstructions, and speed of movement necessary to ensure safety.
items.statement: When traveling with a load, the employer must ensure that a competent person makes the determinations necessary for safety on load position, boom location, ground support, travel route, overhead obstructions and speed of movement.

items.quote: The determinations of the competent person required in paragraph (u)(2)(i) of this section are implemented.
items.statement: When traveling with a load, the employer must ensure that the competent person's determinations required by (u)(2)(i) are implemented.

items.quote: For equipment with tires, tire pressure specified by the manufacturer is maintained.
items.statement: When traveling with a load on equipment with tires, the employer must ensure that the manufacturer-specified tire pressure is maintained.

items.quote: Rotational speed of the equipment must be such that the load does not swing out beyond the radius at which it can be controlled.
items.statement: The equipment's rotational speed must be such that the load does not swing out beyond the radius at which it can be controlled.

items.quote: A tag or restraint line must be used if necessary to prevent rotation of the load that would be hazardous.
items.statement: A tag or restraint line must be used if necessary to prevent hazardous rotation of the load.

items.quote: The brakes must be adjusted in accordance with manufacturer procedures to prevent unintended movement.
items.statement: The brakes must be adjusted in accordance with manufacturer procedures to prevent unintended movement.

items.quote: The operator must obey a stop (or emergency stop) signal, irrespective of who gives it.
items.statement: The operator must obey a stop or emergency stop signal, no matter who gives it.

items.quote: A locomotive crane must not be swung into a position where railway cars on an adjacent track could strike it, until it is determined that cars are not being moved on the adjacent track and that proper flag protection has been established.
items.statement: A locomotive crane must not be swung where railway cars on an adjacent track could strike it until it is determined that cars are not being moved on that track and that proper flag protection has been established.

items.quote:
The following applies to equipment other than tower cranes:
[29cfr1926.1417(aa)(1)(i)] (i) Equipment must not be operated without the counterweight or ballast in place as specified by the manufacturer.
items.statement: Equipment other than tower cranes must not be operated without the counterweight or ballast in place as specified by the manufacturer.

items.quote: The maximum counterweight or ballast specified by the manufacturer for the equipment must not be exceeded.
items.statement: For equipment other than tower cranes, the manufacturer-specified maximum counterweight or ballast must not be exceeded.

items.quote: Counterweight/ballast requirements for tower cranes are specified in § 1926.1435(b)(8).
items.statement: Counterweight and ballast requirements for tower cranes are specified in § 1926.1435(b)(8).

items.quote: Whenever there is a concern as to safety, the operator must have the authority to stop and refuse to handle loads until a qualified person has determined that safety has been assured.
items.statement: Whenever there is a concern as to safety, the operator must have the authority to stop and refuse to handle loads until a qualified person has determined that safety has been assured.

items.quote: The point of operation, meaning the load travel or the area near or at load placement, is not in full view of the operator.
items.statement: A signal person must be provided when the point of operation (the load travel or the area near or at load placement) is not in full view of the operator.

items.quote: The point of operation, meaning the load travel or the area near or at load placement
items.statement: The point of operation means the load travel or the area near or at load placement.

items.quote: When the equipment is traveling, the view in the direction of travel is obstructed.
items.statement: A signal person must be provided when the equipment is traveling and the view in the direction of travel is obstructed.

items.quote: Due to site specific safety concerns, either the operator or the person handling the load determines that it is necessary.
items.statement: A signal person must be provided when either the operator or the person handling the load determines it is necessary due to site specific safety concerns.

items.quote: Signals to operators must be by hand, voice, audible, or new signals.
items.statement: Signals to operators must be by hand, voice, audible, or new signals.

items.quote: When using hand signals, the Standard Method must be used (see appendix A of this subpart).
items.statement: When hand signals are used, the Standard Method (see appendix A of the subpart) must be used, subject to the exception for non-standard hand signals.

items.quote: Exception: Where use of the Standard Method for hand signals is infeasible, or where an operation or use of an attachment is not covered in the Standard Method, non-standard hand signals may be used in accordance with paragraph (c)(2) of this section.
items.statement: As an exception to the Standard Method, non-standard hand signals may be used in accordance with paragraph (c)(2) where the Standard Method is infeasible, or where an operation or use of an attachment is not covered in it.

items.quote: When using non-standard hand signals, the signal person, operator, and lift director (where there is one) must contact each other prior to the operation and agree on the non-standard hand signals that will be used.
items.statement: When non-standard hand signals are used, the signal person, operator, and lift director (where there is one) must contact each other before the operation and agree on the non-standard hand signals to be used.

items.quote:
Signals other than hand, voice, or audible signals may be used where the employer demonstrates that:
[29cfr1926.1419(d)(1)] (1) The new signals provide at least equally effective communication as voice, audible, or Standard Method hand signals, or
[29cfr1926.1419(d)(2)] (2) The new signals comply with a national consensus standard that provides at least equally effective communication
items.statement: Signals other than hand, voice, or audible signals may be used where the employer demonstrates either that they provide at least equally effective communication as voice, audible, or Standard Method hand signals, or that they comply with a national consensus standard that does so.

items.quote: The signals used (hand, voice, audible, or new), and means of transmitting the signals to the operator (such as direct line of sight, video, radio, etc.), must be appropriate for the site conditions.
items.statement: The signals used (hand, voice, audible, or new) must be appropriate for the site conditions.

items.quote: means of transmitting the signals to the operator (such as direct line of sight, video, radio, etc.), must be appropriate for the site conditions.
items.statement: The means of transmitting signals to the operator (such as direct line of sight, video, or radio) must be appropriate for the site conditions.

items.quote: During operations requiring signals, the ability to transmit signals between the operator and signal person must be maintained.
items.statement: During operations requiring signals, the ability to transmit signals between the operator and signal person must be maintained.

items.quote: If that ability is interrupted at any time, the operator must safely stop operations requiring signals until it is reestablished and a proper signal is given and understood.
items.statement: If the ability to transmit signals is interrupted at any time, the operator must safely stop operations requiring signals until it is reestablished and a proper signal is given and understood.

items.quote: If the operator becomes aware of a safety problem and needs to communicate with the signal person, the operator must safely stop operations.
items.statement: If the operator becomes aware of a safety problem and needs to communicate with the signal person, the operator must safely stop operations.

items.quote: Operations must not resume until the operator and signal person agree that the problem has been resolved.
items.statement: After the operator stops operations to communicate with the signal person about a safety problem, operations must not resume until both agree the problem has been resolved.

items.quote: Only one person may give signals to a crane/derrick at a time, except in circumstances covered by paragraph (j) of this section.
items.statement: Only one person may give signals to a crane/derrick at a time, except in circumstances covered by paragraph (j).

items.quote: Anyone who becomes aware of a safety problem must alert the operator or signal person by giving the stop or emergency stop signal.
items.statement: Anyone who becomes aware of a safety problem must alert the operator or signal person by giving the stop or emergency stop signal.

items.quote: § 1926.1417(y) requires the operator to obey a stop or emergency stop signal
items.statement: The operator is required by § 1926.1417(y) to obey a stop or emergency stop signal.

items.quote: All directions given to the operator by the signal person must be given from the operator's direction perspective.
items.statement: All directions the signal person gives the operator must be given from the operator's direction perspective.

items.quote:
Where a signal person(s) is in communication with more than one crane/derrick, a system must be used for identifying the crane/derrick each signal is for, as follows:
[29cfr1926.1419(m)(1)] (1) for each signal, prior to giving the function/direction, the signal person must identify the crane/derrick the signal is for, or
[29cfr1926.1419(m)(2)] (2) must use an equally effective method of identifying which crane/derrick the signal is for.
items.statement: A signal person in communication with more than one crane/derrick must use a system identifying which crane/derrick each signal is for: either identifying it before giving the function/direction for each signal, or using an equally effective identification method.

items.quote: The device(s) used to transmit signals must be tested on site before beginning operations to ensure that the signal transmission is effective, clear, and reliable.
items.statement: The device(s) used to transmit signals must be tested on site before beginning operations to ensure that signal transmission is effective, clear, and reliable.

items.quote: Signal transmission must be through a dedicated channel, except:
items.statement: Signal transmission must be through a dedicated channel, except in the situations listed in paragraphs (b)(1) and (b)(2).

items.quote: Multiple cranes/derricks and one or more signal persons may share a dedicated channel for the purpose of coordinating operations.
items.statement: As an exception to the dedicated channel requirement, multiple cranes/derricks and one or more signal persons may share a dedicated channel for the purpose of coordinating operations.

items.quote: Where a crane is being operated on or adjacent to railroad tracks, and the actions of the crane operator need to be coordinated with the movement of other equipment or trains on the same or adjacent tracks.
items.statement: The dedicated channel requirement is excepted where a crane is being operated on or adjacent to railroad tracks and the crane operator's actions need to be coordinated with the movement of other equipment or trains on the same or adjacent tracks.

items.quote: The operator's reception of signals must be by a hands-free system.
items.statement: The operator must receive signals by a hands-free system.

items.quote: Prior to beginning operations, the operator, signal person and lift director (if there is one), must contact each other and agree on the voice signals that will be used.
items.statement: Before beginning operations, the operator, signal person and lift director (if there is one) must contact each other and agree on the voice signals that will be used.

items.quote: Once the voice signals are agreed upon, these workers need not meet again to discuss voice signals unless another worker is added or substituted, there is confusion about the voice signals, or a voice signal is to be changed.
items.statement: Once the voice signals are agreed upon, the operator, signal person and lift director (if there is one) need not meet again to discuss them unless another worker is added or substituted, there is confusion about the voice signals, or a voice signal is to be changed.

items.quote: Each voice signal must contain the following three elements, given in the following order: function (such as hoist, boom, etc.), direction; distance and/or speed; function, stop command.
items.statement: Each voice signal must contain three elements in this order: function (such as hoist or boom), direction; distance and/or speed; and function, stop command.

items.quote: The operator, signal person and lift director (if there is one), must be able to effectively communicate in the language used.
items.statement: The operator, signal person and lift director (if there is one) must be able to communicate effectively in the language used.

items.quote: Hand signal charts must be either posted on the equipment or conspicuously posted in the vicinity of the hoisting operations.
items.statement: Hand signal charts must be either posted on the equipment or conspicuously posted in the vicinity of the hoisting operations.

items.quote: Paragraphs (b), (c)(3), (e) and (f) of this section apply to all equipment covered by this subpart except tower cranes.
items.statement: Paragraphs (b), (c)(3), (e) and (f) of §1926.1423 apply to all equipment covered by the subpart except tower cranes.

items.quote: Paragraphs (c)(1), (c)(2), (d), (g), (j) and (k) of this section apply to all equipment covered by this subpart.
items.statement: Paragraphs (c)(1), (c)(2), (d), (g), (j) and (k) of §1926.1423 apply to all equipment covered by the subpart.

items.quote: Paragraphs (c)(4) and (h) of this section apply only to tower cranes.
items.statement: Paragraphs (c)(4) and (h) of §1926.1423 apply only to tower cranes.

items.quote: Equipment manufactured after November 8, 2011 with lattice booms must be equipped with walkways on the boom(s) if the vertical profile of the boom (from cord centerline to cord centerline) is 6 or more feet.
items.statement: Equipment manufactured after November 8, 2011 with lattice booms must have walkways on the boom(s) if the boom's vertical profile, from cord centerline to cord centerline, is 6 or more feet.

items.quote: The walkways must be at least 12 inches wide.
items.statement: Boom walkways must be at least 12 inches wide.

items.quote:
Guardrails, railings and other permanent fall protection attachments along walkways are:
[29cfr1926.1423(b)(2)(ii)(A)] (A) Not required.
items.statement: Guardrails, railings and other permanent fall protection attachments are not required along boom walkways.

items.quote: Prohibited on booms supported by pendant ropes or bars if the guardrails/railings/attachments could be snagged by the ropes or bars.
items.statement: Guardrails, railings and other permanent fall protection attachments along walkways are prohibited on booms supported by pendant ropes or bars if the ropes or bars could snag them.

items.quote: Prohibited if of the removable type (designed to be installed and removed each time the boom is assembled/disassembled).
items.statement: Guardrails, railings and other permanent fall protection attachments along walkways are prohibited if they are the removable type, designed to be installed and removed each time the boom is assembled or disassembled.

items.quote: Where not prohibited, guardrails or railings may be of any height up to, but not more than, 45 inches.
items.statement: Where not prohibited, guardrails or railings along boom walkways may be any height up to, but not more than, 45 inches.

items.quote: Section 1926.502(b) does not apply to equipment covered by this subpart.
items.statement: Section 1926.502(b) does not apply to equipment covered by this subpart.

items.quote: The employer must maintain in good condition originally-equipped steps, handholds, ladders and guardrails/railings/grabrails.
items.statement: The employer must maintain originally-equipped steps, handholds, ladders and guardrails/railings/grabrails in good condition.

items.quote: Equipment manufactured after November 8, 2011 must be equipped so as to provide safe access and egress between the ground and the operator work station(s), including the forward and rear positions, by the provision of devices such as steps, handholds, ladders, and guardrails/railings/grabrails.
items.statement: Equipment (other than tower cranes) manufactured after November 8, 2011 must provide safe access and egress between the ground and the operator work station(s), including forward and rear positions, using devices such as steps, handholds, ladders and guardrails/railings/grabrails.

items.quote: Steps, handholds, ladders and guardrails/railings/grabrails must meet the criteria of SAE J185 (May 2003) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) or ISO 11660-2:1994(E) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) except where infeasible.
items.statement: The access devices required by (c)(3) must meet the criteria of SAE J185 (May 2003) or ISO 11660-2:1994(E), except where infeasible.

items.quote: Walking/stepping surfaces, except for crawler treads, must have slip-resistant features/properties
items.statement: Under (c)(3), walking/stepping surfaces, except crawler treads, must have slip-resistant features or properties.

items.quote: Tower cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must be equipped so as to provide safe access and egress between the ground and the cab, machinery platforms, and tower (mast), by the provision of devices such as steps, handholds, ladders, and guardrails/railings/grabrails.
items.statement: Tower cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must provide safe access and egress between the ground and the cab, machinery platforms and tower (mast), using devices such as steps, handholds, ladders and guardrails/railings/grabrails.

items.quote: Steps, handholds, ladders, and guardrails/railings/grabrails must meet the criteria of ISO 11660-1:2008(E) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) and ISO 11660-3:2008(E) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) or SAE J185 (May 2003) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) except where infeasible.
items.statement: Tower crane access devices must meet the criteria of both ISO 11660-1:2008(E) and ISO 11660-3:2008(E), or of SAE J185 (May 2003), except where infeasible.

items.quote: Walking/stepping surfaces must have slip-resistant features/properties
items.statement: Walking/stepping surfaces on tower cranes covered by (c)(4) must have slip-resistant features or properties.

items.quote: Personal fall arrest system components must be used in personal fall arrest and fall restraint systems
items.statement: Personal fall arrest system components must be used in personal fall arrest and fall restraint systems.

items.quote: must conform to the criteria in § 1926.502(d) except that § 1926.502(d)(15) does not apply to components used in personal fall arrest and fall restraint systems.
items.statement: Personal fall arrest system components used in fall arrest and fall restraint systems must conform to the criteria in §1926.502(d), except that §1926.502(d)(15) does not apply to them.

items.quote: Either body belts or body harnesses must be used in personal fall arrest and fall restraint systems.
items.statement: Either body belts or body harnesses must be used in personal fall arrest and fall restraint systems.

items.quote: For non-assembly/disassembly work, the employer must provide and ensure the use of fall protection equipment for employees who are on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge more than 6 feet above a lower level as follows:
items.statement: For non-assembly/disassembly work on equipment other than tower cranes, the employer must provide and ensure the use of fall protection for employees on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge more than 6 feet above a lower level, in the situations listed in (e)(1) and (e)(2).

items.quote:
When moving point-to-point:
[29cfr1926.1423(e)(1)(i)] (i) On non-lattice booms (whether horizontal or not horizontal).
items.statement: In non-assembly/disassembly work more than 6 feet above a lower level at an unprotected side or edge, fall protection is required when moving point-to-point on non-lattice booms, whether horizontal or not.

items.quote: On lattice booms that are not horizontal.
items.statement: In non-assembly/disassembly work more than 6 feet above a lower level at an unprotected side or edge, fall protection is required when moving point-to-point on lattice booms that are not horizontal.

items.quote: On horizontal lattice booms where the fall distance is 15 feet or more.
items.statement: In non-assembly/disassembly work, fall protection is required when moving point-to-point on horizontal lattice booms where the fall distance is 15 feet or more.

items.quote: While at a work station on any part of the equipment (including the boom, of any type), except when the employee is at or near draw-works (when the equipment is running), in the cab, or on the deck.
items.statement: In non-assembly/disassembly work more than 6 feet above a lower level at an unprotected side or edge, fall protection is required at a work station on any part of the equipment, including any type of boom, except when the employee is at or near draw-works while the equipment is running, in the cab, or on the deck.

items.quote: For assembly/disassembly work, the employer must provide and ensure the use of fall protection equipment for employees who are on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge more than 15 feet above a lower level, except when the employee is at or near draw-works (when the equipment is running), in the cab, or on the deck.
items.statement: For assembly/disassembly work on equipment other than tower cranes, the employer must provide and ensure the use of fall protection for employees on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge more than 15 feet above a lower level, except when the employee is at or near draw-works while the equipment is running, in the cab, or on the deck.

items.quote: Sections 1926.502(d)(15) and 1926.502(e)(2) apply to equipment covered by this subpart only to the extent delineated in paragraph (g)(2) of this section.
items.statement: Sections 1926.502(d)(15) and 1926.502(e)(2) apply to equipment covered by this subpart only to the extent set out in paragraph (g)(2).

items.quote: Personal fall arrest systems must be anchored to any apparently substantial part of the equipment unless a competent person, from a visual inspection, without an engineering analysis, would conclude that the criteria in § 1926.502(d)(15) would not be met.
items.statement: Personal fall arrest systems must be anchored to any apparently substantial part of the equipment unless a competent person would conclude from a visual inspection, without engineering analysis, that the §1926.502(d)(15) criteria would not be met.

items.quote: Positioning device systems must be anchored to any apparently substantial part of the equipment unless a competent person, from a visual inspection, without an engineering analysis, would conclude that the criteria in § 1926.502(e)(2) would not be met.
items.statement: Positioning device systems must be anchored to any apparently substantial part of the equipment unless a competent person would conclude from a visual inspection, without engineering analysis, that the §1926.502(e)(2) criteria would not be met.

items.quote: Attachable anchor devices (portable anchor devices that are attached to the equipment) must meet the anchorage criteria in § 1926.502(d)(15) for personal fall arrest systems
items.statement: Attachable anchor devices used for personal fall arrest systems must meet the anchorage criteria in §1926.502(d)(15).

items.quote: Attachable anchor devices (portable anchor devices that are attached to the equipment) must meet the anchorage criteria in § 1926.502(d)(15) for personal fall arrest systems and § 1926.502(e)(2) for positioning device systems.
items.statement: Attachable anchor devices used for positioning device systems must meet the anchorage criteria in §1926.502(e)(2).

items.quote: Attachable anchor devices (portable anchor devices that are attached to the equipment)
items.statement: Attachable anchor devices are portable anchor devices that are attached to the equipment.

items.quote: Fall restraint systems must be anchored to any part of the equipment that is capable of withstanding twice the maximum load that an employee may impose on it during reasonably anticipated conditions of use.
items.statement: Fall restraint systems must be anchored to a part of the equipment that can withstand twice the maximum load an employee may impose on it during reasonably anticipated conditions of use.

items.quote: For work other than erecting, climbing, and dismantling, the employer must provide and ensure the use of fall protection equipment for employees who are on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge more than 6 feet above a lower level, except when the employee is at or near draw-works (when the equipment is running), in the cab, or on the deck.
items.statement: On tower cranes, for work other than erecting, climbing and dismantling, the employer must provide and ensure the use of fall protection for employees on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge more than 6 feet above a lower level, except when the employee is at or near draw-works while the equipment is running, in the cab, or on the deck.

items.quote: For erecting, climbing, and dismantling work, the employer must provide and ensure the use of fall protection equipment for employees who are on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge more than 15 feet above a lower level.
items.statement: On tower cranes, for erecting, climbing and dismantling work, the employer must provide and ensure the use of fall protection for employees on a walking/working surface with an unprotected side or edge more than 15 feet above a lower level.

items.quote: A qualified person has determined that the set-up and rated capacity of the crane/derrick (including the hook, load line and rigging) meets or exceeds the requirements in § 1926.502(d)(15).
items.statement: A personal fall arrest system may be anchored to the crane/derrick's hook or other part of the load line only if a qualified person has determined that the set-up and rated capacity of the crane/derrick, including hook, load line and rigging, meets or exceeds the §1926.502(d)(15) requirements, and the other (j) conditions are also met.

items.quote: The equipment operator must be at the work site
items.statement: When a personal fall arrest system is anchored to the hook or load line, the equipment operator must be at the work site.

items.quote: The equipment operator must be at the work site and informed that the equipment is being used for this purpose.
items.statement: When a personal fall arrest system is anchored to the hook or load line, the equipment operator must be informed that the equipment is being used for this purpose.

items.quote: No load is suspended from the load line when the personal fall arrest system is anchored to the crane/derrick's hook (or other part of the load line).
items.statement: A personal fall arrest system may be anchored to the crane/derrick's hook or other part of the load line only if no load is suspended from the load line while it is so anchored.

items.quote:
The employer must train each employee who may be exposed to fall hazards while on, or hoisted by, equipment covered by this subpart on all of the following:
[29cfr1926.1423(k)(1)] (1) the requirements in this subpart that address fall protection.
items.statement: The employer must train each employee who may be exposed to fall hazards while on, or hoisted by, covered equipment on the subpart's fall protection requirements.

items.quote: the applicable requirements in §§ 1926.500 and 1926.502.
items.statement: The employer must train each employee who may be exposed to fall hazards while on, or hoisted by, covered equipment on the applicable requirements in §§1926.500 and 1926.502.

items.quote:
(1) The requirements in paragraph (a)(2) of this section apply where there are accessible areas in which the equipment's rotating superstructure (whether permanently or temporarily mounted) poses a reasonably foreseeable risk of:
[29cfr1926.1424(a)(1)(i)] (i) Striking and injuring an employee
items.statement: The swing radius requirements in paragraph (a)(2) apply where there are accessible areas in which the equipment's rotating superstructure, permanently or temporarily mounted, poses a reasonably foreseeable risk of striking and injuring an employee.

items.quote: (ii) Pinching/crushing an employee against another part of the equipment or another object.
items.statement: The swing radius requirements in paragraph (a)(2) also apply where there are accessible areas in which the rotating superstructure poses a reasonably foreseeable risk of pinching or crushing an employee against another part of the equipment or another object.

items.quote: each employee assigned to work on or near the equipment (“authorized personnel”)
items.statement: "Authorized personnel" are employees assigned to work on or near the equipment.

items.quote: (i) Train each employee assigned to work on or near the equipment (“authorized personnel”) in how to recognize struck-by and pinch/crush hazard areas posed by the rotating superstructure.
items.statement: To prevent employees from entering swing radius hazard areas, the employer must train each employee assigned to work on or near the equipment to recognize the struck-by and pinch/crush hazard areas posed by the rotating superstructure.

items.quote: (ii) Erect and maintain control lines, warning lines, railings or similar barriers to mark the boundaries of the hazard areas.
items.statement: To prevent employees from entering the hazard areas, the employer must erect and maintain control lines, warning lines, railings or similar barriers to mark their boundaries, subject to the infeasibility exception.

items.quote: Exception: When the employer can demonstrate that it is neither feasible to erect such barriers on the ground nor on the equipment, the hazard areas must be clearly marked by a combination of warning signs (such as “Danger—Swing/Crush Zone”) and high visibility markings on the equipment that identify the hazard areas.
items.statement: As an exception to barriers, when the employer can demonstrate that it is infeasible to erect them either on the ground or on the equipment, the hazard areas must be clearly marked by a combination of warning signs and high visibility markings on the equipment that identify the hazard areas.

items.quote: In addition, the employer must train each employee to understand what these markings signify.
items.statement: When the barrier infeasibility exception applies and signs and markings are used, the employer must also train each employee to understand what the markings signify.

items.quote: (i) Before an employee goes to a location in the hazard area that is out of view of the operator, the employee (or someone instructed by the employee) must ensure that the operator is informed that he/she is going to that location.
items.statement: Before an employee goes to a location in the hazard area that is out of the operator's view, the employee or someone instructed by the employee must ensure the operator is informed that the employee is going there.

items.quote: (ii) Where the operator knows that an employee went to a location covered by paragraph (a)(1) of this section, the operator must not rotate the superstructure until the operator is informed in accordance with a pre-arranged system of communication that the employee is in a safe position.
items.statement: Where the operator knows that an employee went to a location covered by paragraph (a)(1), the operator must not rotate the superstructure until informed, through a pre-arranged communication system, that the employee is in a safe position.

items.quote: (b) Where any part of a crane/derrick is within the working radius of another crane/derrick, the controlling entity must institute a system to coordinate operations.
items.statement: Where any part of a crane or derrick is within the working radius of another crane or derrick, the controlling entity must institute a system to coordinate operations.

items.quote: If there is no controlling entity, the employer (if there is only one employer operating the multiple pieces of equipment), or employers, must institute such a system.
items.statement: If cranes or derricks have overlapping working radius, there is no controlling entity, and only one employer operates the multiple pieces of equipment, that employer must institute the coordination system.

items.quote: If there is no controlling entity, the employer (if there is only one employer operating the multiple pieces of equipment), or employers, must institute such a system.
items.statement: If any part of a crane or derrick is within another's working radius, there is no controlling entity, and more than one employer is operating the equipment, the employers must institute the coordination system.

items.quote: Where available, hoisting routes that minimize the exposure of employees to hoisted loads must be used, to the extent consistent with public safety.
items.statement: Where available, hoisting routes that minimize employees' exposure to hoisted loads must be used, to the extent consistent with public safety.

items.quote: While the operator is not moving a suspended load, no employee must be within the fall zone, except for employees:
items.statement: While the operator is not moving a suspended load, no employee may be within the fall zone, except for the employees excepted in paragraphs (b)(1) through (b)(3).

items.quote: Engaged in hooking, unhooking or guiding a load;
items.statement: As an exception, employees engaged in hooking, unhooking or guiding a load may be within the fall zone while the operator is not moving a suspended load.

items.quote: Engaged in the initial attachment of the load to a component or structure; or
items.statement: As an exception, employees engaged in the initial attachment of the load to a component or structure may be within the fall zone while the operator is not moving a suspended load.

items.quote: Operating a concrete hopper or concrete bucket.
items.statement: As an exception, employees operating a concrete hopper or concrete bucket may be within the fall zone while the operator is not moving a suspended load.

items.quote: The materials being hoisted must be rigged to prevent unintentional displacement.
items.statement: When employees hooking, unhooking or guiding the load, or making the initial connection of a load to a component or structure, are within the fall zone, the materials being hoisted must be rigged to prevent unintentional displacement.

items.quote: Hooks with self-closing latches or their equivalent must be used.
items.statement: When employees hooking, unhooking or guiding the load, or making the initial connection of a load to a component or structure, are within the fall zone, hooks with self-closing latches or their equivalent must be used, except as allowed for "J" hooks when setting wooden trusses.

items.quote: Exception: “J” hooks are permitted to be used for setting wooden trusses.
items.statement: As an exception to the self-closing latch hook requirement, "J" hooks are permitted for setting wooden trusses.

items.quote: The materials must be rigged by a qualified rigger.
items.statement: When employees hooking, unhooking or guiding the load, or making the initial connection of a load to a component or structure, are within the fall zone, the materials must be rigged by a qualified rigger.

items.quote: Only employees needed to receive a load are permitted to be within the fall zone when a load is being landed.
items.statement: When a load is being landed, only employees needed to receive it are permitted within the fall zone.

items.quote: No employee must be directly under the load.
items.statement: During a tilt-up or tilt-down operation, no employee may be directly under the load.

items.quote: Only employees essential to the operation are permitted in the fall zone (but not directly under the load).
items.statement: During a tilt-up or tilt-down operation, only employees essential to the operation are permitted in the fall zone, and they may not be directly under the load.

items.quote: An employee is essential to the operation if the employee is conducting one of the following operations and the employer can demonstrate it is infeasible for the employee to perform that operation from outside the fall zone: (1) Physically guide the load; (2) closely monitor and give instructions regarding the load's movement; or (3) either detach it from or initially attach it to another component or structure (such as, but not limited to, making an initial connection or installing bracing).
items.statement: In a tilt-up or tilt-down operation, an employee is essential if the employee is physically guiding the load; closely monitoring and giving instructions about its movement; or detaching it from or initially attaching it to another component or structure (such as making an initial connection or installing bracing), and the employer can demonstrate that performing that operation from outside the fall zone is infeasible.

items.quote: Boom free fall is prohibited when an employee is in the fall zone of the boom or load
items.statement: Boom free fall is prohibited when an employee is in the fall zone of the boom or load.

items.quote: load line free fall is prohibited when an employee is directly under the load
items.statement: Load line free fall is prohibited when an employee is directly under the load.

items.quote: An employee is in the fall zone of the boom or load.
items.statement: Equipment with a boom designed to free fall (live boom) must not be used when an employee is in the fall zone of the boom or load.

items.quote: An employee is being hoisted.
items.statement: Equipment with a boom designed to free fall (live boom) must not be used when an employee is being hoisted.

items.quote: The load or boom is directly over a power line, or over any part of the area extending the Table A of § 1926.1408 clearance distance to each side of the power line
items.statement: Live boom equipment must not be used when the load or boom is directly over a power line, or over any part of the area extending the § 1926.1408 Table A clearance distance to each side of the line.

items.quote: any part of the area extending the Table A clearance distance to each side of the power line is within the radius of vertical travel of the boom or the load.
items.statement: Live boom equipment must not be used when any part of the area extending the Table A clearance distance to each side of a power line is within the radius of vertical travel of the boom or load.

items.quote: The load is over a shaft, except where there are no employees in the shaft.
items.statement: Live boom equipment must not be used when the load is over a shaft, except where no employees are in the shaft.

items.quote: The load is over a cofferdam, except where there are no employees in the fall zone of the boom or the load.
items.statement: Live boom equipment must not be used when the load is over a cofferdam, except where no employees are in the fall zone of the boom or load.

items.quote: Lifting operations are taking place in a refinery or tank farm.
items.statement: Live boom equipment must not be used when lifting operations are taking place in a refinery or tank farm.

items.quote: The equipment was manufactured prior to October 31, 1984
items.statement: Live boom equipment manufactured before October 31, 1984 is permitted to be used only where none of the paragraph (a)(1) prohibited circumstances are present.

items.quote: The equipment is a floating crane/derrick or a land crane/derrick on a vessel/flotation device.
items.statement: As an alternative to the pre-October 31, 1984 manufacture condition, live boom equipment may be used if it is a floating crane/derrick or a land crane/derrick on a vessel/flotation device, but only where none of the paragraph (a)(1) circumstances are present.

items.quote: Where the use of equipment with a boom that is designed to free fall (live boom) is prohibited, the boom hoist must have a secondary mechanism or device designed to prevent the boom from falling in the event the primary system used to hold or regulate the boom hoist fails
items.statement: Where use of live boom equipment is prohibited, the boom hoist must have a secondary mechanism or device designed to prevent the boom from falling if the primary system that holds or regulates the boom hoist fails.

items.quote: A friction clutch and, in addition, a braking device, to allow for controlled boom lowering.
items.statement: Where live boom use is prohibited, friction drums must have a friction clutch to allow for controlled boom lowering.

items.quote: in addition, a braking device, to allow for controlled boom lowering.
items.statement: Where live boom use is prohibited, friction drums must have a braking device, in addition to a friction clutch, to allow for controlled boom lowering.

items.quote: A secondary braking or locking device, which is manually or automatically engaged, to back-up the primary brake while the boom is held (such as a secondary friction brake or a ratchet and pawl device).
items.statement: Where live boom use is prohibited, friction drums must have a manually or automatically engaged secondary braking or locking device (such as a secondary friction brake or ratchet and pawl) to back up the primary brake while the boom is held.

items.quote: Hydraulic drums must have an integrally mounted holding device or internal static brake to prevent boom hoist movement in the event of hydraulic failure.
items.statement: Where live boom use is prohibited, hydraulic drums must have an integrally mounted holding device or internal static brake to prevent boom hoist movement in the event of hydraulic failure.

items.quote: Neither clutches nor hydraulic motors must be considered brake or locking devices for purposes of this subpart.
items.statement: For purposes of this subpart, neither clutches nor hydraulic motors are to be considered brake or locking devices.

items.quote: Hydraulic boom cylinders must have an integrally mounted holding device.
items.statement: Where live boom use is prohibited, hydraulic boom cylinders must have an integrally mounted holding device.

items.quote: Hydraulic telescoping booms must have an integrally mounted holding device to prevent the boom from retracting in the event of hydraulic failure.
items.statement: Hydraulic telescoping booms must have an integrally mounted holding device to prevent the boom from retracting in the event of hydraulic failure.

items.quote: An employee is directly under the load.
items.statement: When an employee is directly under the load, free fall of the load line hoist is prohibited and controlled load lowering is required.

items.quote: An employee is being hoisted.
items.statement: When an employee is being hoisted, free fall of the load line hoist is prohibited and controlled load lowering is required.

items.quote: The load is directly over a power line, or over any part of the area extending the Table A of § 1926.1408 clearance distance to each side of the power line
items.statement: When the load is directly over a power line, or over any part of the area extending the § 1926.1408 Table A clearance distance to each side of it, load line free fall is prohibited and controlled load lowering is required.

items.quote: any part of the area extending the Table A of § 1926.1408 clearance distance to each side of the power line is within the radius of vertical travel of the load.
items.statement: When any part of the area extending the § 1926.1408 Table A clearance distance to each side of a power line is within the load's radius of vertical travel, load line free fall is prohibited and controlled load lowering is required.

items.quote: The load is over a shaft.
items.statement: When the load is over a shaft, load line free fall is prohibited and controlled load lowering is required.

items.quote: The load is over a cofferdam, except where there are no employees in the fall zone of the load.
items.statement: When the load is over a cofferdam, load line free fall is prohibited and controlled load lowering is required, except where no employees are in the fall zone of the load.

items.quote: The employer must ensure that each operator is trained, certified/licensed, and evaluated in accordance with this section before operating any equipment covered under subpart CC, except for the equipment listed in paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
items.statement: The employer must ensure each operator is trained, certified/licensed and evaluated under §1926.1427 before operating any equipment covered by subpart CC, except the equipment listed in paragraph (a)(2).

items.quote: may only operate the equipment as an operator-in-training under supervision in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section.
items.statement: An employee not certified/licensed and evaluated to operate assigned equipment may operate it only as an operator-in-training under supervision in accordance with paragraph (b).

items.quote: Operators of derricks (see § 1926.1436), sideboom cranes (see § 1926.1440), or equipment with a maximum manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less (see § 1926.1441) are not required to comply with § 1926.1427.
items.statement: As an exception, operators of derricks are not required to comply with §1926.1427.

items.quote: Operators of derricks (see § 1926.1436), sideboom cranes (see § 1926.1440), or equipment with a maximum manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less (see § 1926.1441) are not required to comply with § 1926.1427.
items.statement: As an exception, operators of sideboom cranes are not required to comply with §1926.1427.

items.quote: equipment with a maximum manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less (see § 1926.1441) are not required to comply with § 1926.1427.
items.statement: As an exception, operators of equipment with a maximum manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less are not required to comply with §1926.1427.

items.quote: The training requirements in those other sections continue to apply
items.statement: The training requirements in the other sections for derricks, sideboom cranes and equipment rated 2,000 pounds or less continue to apply.

items.quote: for the training requirement for operators of sideboom cranes, follow section 1926.1430(c)
items.statement: For the training requirement for operators of sideboom cranes, section 1926.1430(c) is to be followed.

items.quote: an operator who is an employee of the U.S. military meets the requirements of this section if he/she has a current operator qualification issued by the U.S. military for operation of the equipment.
items.statement: An operator who is a U.S. military employee meets the requirements of §1926.1427 if he or she has a current U.S. military operator qualification for operation of the equipment.

items.quote: An employee of the U.S. military is a Federal employee of the Department of Defense or Armed Forces and does not include employees of private contractors.
items.statement: An employee of the U.S. military is a Federal employee of the Department of Defense or Armed Forces and does not include employees of private contractors.

items.quote: Not portable: Such a qualification meets the requirements of paragraph (a) of this section only where the operator is employed by (and operating the equipment for) the employer that issued the qualification.
items.statement: A U.S. military qualification is not portable: it meets paragraph (a) only where the operator is employed by, and operating the equipment for, the employer that issued it.

items.quote: Valid for the period of time stipulated by the issuing entity.
items.statement: A U.S. military qualification is valid for the period of time stipulated by the issuing entity.

items.quote: The employer must provide each operator-in-training with sufficient training, through a combination of formal and practical instruction, to ensure that the operator-in-training develops the skills, knowledge, and ability to recognize and avert risk necessary to operate the equipment safely for assigned work.
items.statement: The employer must give each operator-in-training sufficient training, combining formal and practical instruction, to develop the skills, knowledge, and ability to recognize and avert risk needed to operate the equipment safely for assigned work.

items.quote: The employer must provide instruction on the knowledge and skills listed in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2) of this section to the operator-in-training.
items.statement: The employer must instruct the operator-in-training on the knowledge and skills listed in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2).

items.quote: The operator-in-training must be continuously monitored on site by a trainer while operating equipment.
items.statement: A trainer must continuously monitor the operator-in-training on site while the operator-in-training operates equipment.

items.quote: The employer may only assign tasks within the operator-in-training's ability.
items.statement: The employer may only assign an operator-in-training tasks within his or her ability.

items.quote: could get within 20 feet of a power line that is up to 350 kV
items.statement: Unless certified under paragraph (c), an operator-in-training must not operate the equipment if any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), operated up to maximum working radius in the work zone, could get within 20 feet of a power line up to 350 kV.

items.quote: within 50 feet of a power line that is over 350 kV
items.statement: Unless certified under paragraph (c), an operator-in-training must not operate the equipment if any part of the equipment, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), operated up to maximum working radius in the work zone, could get within 50 feet of a power line over 350 kV.

items.quote: If the equipment is used to hoist personnel.
items.statement: Unless certified under paragraph (c), an operator-in-training must not operate the equipment when it is used to hoist personnel.

items.quote: In multiple-equipment lifts.
items.statement: Unless certified under paragraph (c), an operator-in-training must not operate the equipment in multiple-equipment lifts.

items.quote: If the equipment is used over a shaft, cofferdam, or in a tank farm.
items.statement: Unless certified under paragraph (c), an operator-in-training must not operate the equipment when it is used over a shaft, cofferdam, or in a tank farm.

items.quote: In multiple-lift rigging operations, except where the operator's trainer determines that the operator-in-training's skills are sufficient for this high-skill work.
items.statement: Unless certified under paragraph (c), an operator-in-training must not operate the equipment in multiple-lift rigging operations, except where the operator's trainer determines the operator-in-training's skills are sufficient for this high-skill work.

items.quote: While operating the equipment, the operator-in-training must be continuously monitored by an individual (“operator's trainer”) who meets all of the following requirements:
items.statement: The employer must ensure that, while operating subpart CC equipment, the operator-in-training is continuously monitored by an operator's trainer who meets all the requirements of paragraph (b)(4)(i).

items.quote: The operator's trainer is an employee or agent of the operator-in-training's employer.
items.statement: The operator's trainer must be an employee or agent of the operator-in-training's employer.

items.quote: The operator's trainer has the knowledge, training, and experience necessary to direct the operator-in-training on the equipment in use.
items.statement: The operator's trainer must have the knowledge, training, and experience necessary to direct the operator-in-training on the equipment in use.

items.quote: the operator's trainer performs no tasks that detract from the trainer's ability to monitor the operator-in-training.
items.statement: While monitoring, the operator's trainer must not perform tasks that detract from the ability to monitor the operator-in-training.

items.quote: For equipment other than tower cranes: The operator's trainer and the operator-in-training must be in direct line of sight of each other.
items.statement: For equipment other than tower cranes, the operator's trainer and operator-in-training must be in direct line of sight of each other.

items.quote: In addition, they must communicate verbally or by hand signals.
items.statement: For equipment other than tower cranes, the operator's trainer and operator-in-training must communicate verbally or by hand signals.

items.quote: For tower cranes: The operator's trainer and the operator-in-training must be in direct communication with each other.
items.statement: For tower cranes, the operator's trainer and operator-in-training must be in direct communication with each other.

items.quote: The operator-in-training must be monitored by the operator's trainer at all times, except for short breaks where all of the following are met:
items.statement: The operator's trainer must monitor the operator-in-training at all times, except during short breaks that meet all the conditions of paragraph (b)(4)(iv).

items.quote: The break lasts no longer than 15 minutes
items.statement: A trainer's break from monitoring may last no longer than 15 minutes.

items.quote: there is no more than one break per hour
items.statement: There may be no more than one trainer break per hour.

items.quote: Immediately prior to the break the operator's trainer informs the operator-in-training of the specific tasks that the operator-in-training is to perform and limitations to which he/she must adhere during the operator trainer's break.
items.statement: Immediately before a break, the operator's trainer must tell the operator-in-training the specific tasks to perform and the limitations to follow during the break.

items.quote: The specific tasks that the operator-in-training will perform during the operator trainer's break are within the operator-in-training's abilities.
items.statement: The specific tasks the operator-in-training performs during the trainer's break must be within the operator-in-training's abilities.

items.quote: The employer must provide retraining in relevant topics for each operator when, based on the performance of the operator or an evaluation of the operator's knowledge, there is an indication that retraining is necessary.
items.statement: The employer must retrain an operator in relevant topics when the operator's performance or an evaluation of the operator's knowledge indicates retraining is necessary.

items.quote: The employer must ensure that each operator is certified or licensed to operate the equipment as follows:
items.statement: The employer must ensure each operator is certified or licensed to operate the equipment as set out in paragraph (c).

items.quote: the equipment operator must be licensed by that government entity for operation of equipment within that entity's jurisdiction if that government licensing program meets the following requirements:
items.statement: When a state or local government issues licenses for subpart CC equipment and its program meets the paragraph (c)(1) requirements, the operator must be licensed by that government to operate equipment within its jurisdiction.

items.quote: The requirements for obtaining the license include an assessment, by written and practical tests, of the operator applicant regarding, at a minimum, the knowledge and skills listed in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2) of this section.
