items.statement: A qualifying government licensing program must assess applicants by written and practical tests on at least the knowledge and skills in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2).

items.quote: The testing meets industry-recognized criteria for written testing materials, practical examinations, test administration, grading, facilities/equipment, and personnel.
items.statement: A qualifying government licensing program's testing must meet industry-recognized criteria for written testing materials, practical examinations, test administration, grading, facilities/equipment, and personnel.

items.quote: The government authority that oversees the licensing department/office has determined that the requirements in paragraphs (c)(1)(i) and (ii) of this section have been met.
items.statement: For a government licensing program to qualify, the government authority overseeing the licensing department/office must have determined that the requirements of paragraphs (c)(1)(i) and (ii) are met.

items.quote: The licensing department/office has testing procedures for re-licensing designed to ensure that the operator continues to meet the technical knowledge and skills requirements in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2) of this section.
items.statement: A qualifying licensing department/office must have re-licensing testing procedures designed to ensure the operator still meets the knowledge and skills requirements in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2).

items.quote: a license is valid for the period of time stipulated by the licensing department/office, but no longer than 5 years.
items.statement: For compliance with §1926.1427, a government license is valid for the period the licensing department/office stipulates, but no longer than 5 years.

items.quote: When an operator is not required to be licensed under paragraph (c)(1) of this section, the operator must be certified in accordance with paragraph (d) or (e) of this section.
items.statement: An operator not required to be licensed under paragraph (c)(1) must be certified under paragraph (d) or (e).

items.quote: Whenever operator certification/licensure is required under this section, the employer must provide the certification/licensure at no cost to employees.
items.statement: Whenever certification/licensure is required under this section, the employer must provide it at no cost to employees.

items.quote: A testing entity is permitted to provide training as well as testing services as long as the criteria of the applicable governmental or accrediting agency (in the option selected) for an organization providing both services are met.
items.statement: A testing entity may provide both training and testing if it meets the applicable governmental or accrediting agency's criteria (in the option selected) for an organization providing both.

items.quote: Be accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency based on that agency's determination that industry-recognized criteria for written testing materials, practical examinations, test administration, grading, facilities/equipment, and personnel have been met.
items.statement: For its certification to satisfy §1926.1427, a crane operator testing organization must be accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency, based on that agency's determination that industry-recognized criteria for written testing materials, practical examinations, test administration, grading, facilities/equipment, and personnel are met.

items.quote: Assess the operator applicant regarding, at a minimum, the knowledge and skills listed in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2) of this section.
items.statement: The accredited testing organization must administer written and practical tests that assess applicants on at least the knowledge and skills in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2).

items.quote: Provide certification based on equipment type, or type and capacity.
items.statement: The accredited testing organization's written and practical tests must provide certification based on equipment type, or type and capacity.

items.quote: Have procedures for operators to re-apply and be re-tested in the event an operator applicant fails a test or is decertified.
items.statement: The accredited testing organization must have procedures for operators to re-apply and be re-tested if an applicant fails a test or is decertified.

items.quote: Have testing procedures for re-certification designed to ensure that the operator continues to meet the technical knowledge and skills requirements in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2) of this section.
items.statement: The accredited testing organization must have re-certification testing procedures designed to ensure the operator still meets the knowledge and skills requirements in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2).

items.quote: Have its accreditation reviewed by the nationally recognized accrediting agency at least every 3 years.
items.statement: The testing organization must have its accreditation reviewed by the nationally recognized accrediting agency at least every 3 years.

items.quote: If no accredited testing agency offers certification examinations for a particular type of equipment, an operator will be deemed to have complied with the certification requirements of this section for that equipment if the operator has been certified for the type that is most similar to that equipment and for which a certification examination is available.
items.statement: If no accredited testing agency offers certification exams for a particular equipment type, an operator is deemed to comply for that equipment if certified for the most similar type for which an exam is available.

items.quote: The operator's certificate must state the type of equipment for which the operator is certified.
items.statement: The operator's certificate must state the type of equipment for which the operator is certified.

items.quote: A certification issued under this option is portable among employers who are required to have operators certified under this option.
items.statement: A certification issued under the accredited testing organization option is portable among employers required to have operators certified under that option.

items.quote: A certification issued under this paragraph is valid for 5 years.
items.statement: A certification issued under paragraph (d) is valid for 5 years.

items.quote: The written and practical tests must be either:
items.statement: Under an audited employer program, the written and practical tests must be either developed by an accredited crane operator testing organization or approved by an auditor under the specified auditor-approval requirements.

items.quote: The auditor is certified to evaluate such tests by an accredited crane operator testing organization
items.statement: An auditor who approves an employer program's tests must be certified by an accredited crane operator testing organization to evaluate such tests.

items.quote: The auditor is not an employee of the employer.
items.statement: An auditor who approves an employer program's tests must not be an employee of the employer.

items.quote: The approval must be based on the auditor's determination that the written and practical tests meet nationally recognized test development criteria and are valid and reliable in assessing the operator applicants regarding, at a minimum, the knowledge and skills listed in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2) of this section.
items.statement: Auditor approval of tests must be based on a determination that the written and practical tests meet nationally recognized test development criteria and are valid and reliable in assessing operator applicants on at least the knowledge and skills in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2).

items.quote: The audit must be conducted in accordance with nationally recognized auditing standards.
items.statement: The audit for auditor approval of the tests must be conducted in accordance with nationally recognized auditing standards.

items.quote: The written and practical tests must be administered under circumstances approved by the auditor as meeting nationally recognized test administration standards.
items.statement: Under an audited employer program, the written and practical tests must be administered under circumstances the auditor approves as meeting nationally recognized test administration standards.

items.quote: The auditor must be certified to evaluate the administration of the written and practical tests by an accredited crane operator testing organization
items.statement: The auditor must be certified by an accredited crane operator testing organization to evaluate the administration of the written and practical tests.

items.quote: The auditor must not be an employee of the employer.
items.statement: The auditor for test administration must not be an employee of the employer.

items.quote: The audit must be conducted in accordance with nationally recognized auditing standards.
items.statement: The audit of test administration must be conducted in accordance with nationally recognized auditing standards.

items.quote: The employer program must be audited within 3 months of the beginning of the program
items.statement: The employer program must be audited within 3 months of the beginning of the program.

items.quote: at least every 3 years thereafter
items.statement: After the initial audit, the employer program must be audited at least every 3 years.

items.quote: The employer program must have testing procedures for re-qualification designed to ensure that the operator continues to meet the technical knowledge and skills requirements in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2) of this section.
items.statement: The employer program must have re-qualification testing procedures designed to ensure the operator continues to meet the technical knowledge and skills requirements in paragraphs (j)(1) and (2).

items.quote: The re-qualification procedures must be audited in accordance with paragraphs (e)(1) and (2) of this section.
items.statement: The employer program's re-qualification procedures must be audited in accordance with paragraphs (e)(1) and (2).

items.quote: No operator is qualified until the auditor confirms that the deficiency has been corrected.
items.statement: If the auditor determines the program has a significant deficiency, the employer must ensure no operator is qualified until the auditor confirms it has been corrected.

items.quote: The program is audited again within 180 days of the confirmation that the deficiency was corrected.
items.statement: If the auditor determines there is a significant deficiency, the employer must ensure the program is audited again within 180 days of the confirmation that it was corrected.

items.quote: The auditor files a documented report of the deficiency to the appropriate Regional Office of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration within 15 days of the auditor's determination that there is a deficiency.
items.statement: If the auditor determines there is a significant deficiency, the employer must ensure the auditor files a documented report of it with the appropriate OSHA Regional Office within 15 days of that determination.

items.quote: Records of the audits of the employer's program are maintained by the auditor for 3 years
items.statement: If the auditor determines there is a significant deficiency, the employer must ensure the auditor maintains records of the program audits for 3 years.

items.quote: are made available by the auditor to the Secretary of Labor or the Secretary's designated representative upon request
items.statement: If the auditor determines there is a significant deficiency, the employer must ensure the auditor makes the program audit records available on request to the Secretary of Labor or the Secretary's designated representative.

items.quote: Not portable: Such a certification meets the requirements of paragraph (c) of this section only where the operator is employed by (and operating the equipment for) the employer that issued the certification.
items.statement: An audited-program certification is not portable: it meets paragraph (c) only while the operator is employed by, and operating the equipment for, the employer that issued it.

items.quote: Valid for 5 years.
items.statement: An audited-program certification is valid for 5 years.

items.quote: The skills and knowledge, as well as the ability to recognize and avert risk, necessary to operate the equipment safely, including those specific to the safety devices, operational aids, software, and the size and configuration of the equipment.
items.statement: Through an evaluation, the employer must ensure each operator is qualified by demonstrating the skills, knowledge, and ability to recognize and avert risk needed to operate the equipment safely, including those specific to its safety devices, operational aids, software, size and configuration.

items.quote: Size and configuration includes, but is not limited to, lifting capacity, boom length, attachments, luffing jib, and counterweight set-up.
items.statement: For operator evaluation, equipment size and configuration includes, but is not limited to, lifting capacity, boom length, attachments, luffing jib, and counterweight set-up.

items.quote: The ability to perform the hoisting activities required for assigned work, including, if applicable, blind lifts, personnel hoisting, and multi-crane lifts.
items.statement: Through an evaluation, the employer must ensure each operator demonstrates the ability to perform the hoisting activities required for assigned work, including, if applicable, blind lifts, personnel hoisting, and multi-crane lifts.

items.quote: For operators employed prior to December 10, 2018, the employer may rely on its previous assessments of the operator in lieu of conducting a new evaluation of that operator's existing knowledge and skills.
items.statement: For operators employed before December 10, 2018, the employer may rely on its previous assessments instead of newly evaluating their existing knowledge and skills.

items.quote: The definition of “qualified” in § 1926.32 does not apply to paragraph (f)(1) of this section
items.statement: The § 1926.32 definition of "qualified" does not apply to paragraph (f)(1).

items.quote: Possession of a certificate or degree cannot, by itself, cause a person to be qualified for purposes of paragraph (f)(1).
items.statement: Possessing a certificate or degree cannot, by itself, make a person qualified for purposes of paragraph (f)(1).

items.quote: The evaluation required under paragraph (f)(1) of this section must be conducted by an individual who has the knowledge, training, and experience necessary to assess equipment operators.
items.statement: The paragraph (f)(1) evaluation must be conducted by an individual with the knowledge, training, and experience necessary to assess equipment operators.

items.quote: The evaluator must be an employee or agent of the employer.
items.statement: The evaluator must be an employee or agent of the employer.

items.quote: Employers that assign evaluations to an agent retain the duty to ensure that the requirements in paragraph (f) are satisfied.
items.statement: An employer that assigns evaluations to an agent retains the duty to ensure the paragraph (f) requirements are satisfied.

items.quote: Once the evaluation is completed successfully, the employer may allow the operator to operate other equipment that the employer can demonstrate does not require substantially different skills, knowledge, or ability to recognize and avert risk to operate.
items.statement: After a successful evaluation, the employer may allow the operator to operate other equipment that the employer can demonstrate does not require substantially different skills, knowledge, or ability to recognize and avert risk.

items.quote: The employer must document the completion of the evaluation.
items.statement: The employer must document the completion of the operator evaluation.

items.quote: This document must provide: The operator's name; the evaluator's name and signature; the date; and the make, model, and configuration of equipment used in the evaluation.
items.statement: The evaluation document must provide the operator's name, the evaluator's name and signature, the date, and the make, model, and configuration of equipment used in the evaluation.

items.quote: The employer must make the document available at the worksite while the operator is employed by the employer.
items.statement: The employer must make the evaluation document available at the worksite while the operator is employed by the employer.

items.quote: For operators assessed per paragraph (f)(2) of this section, the documentation must reflect the date of the employer's determination of the operator's abilities and the make, model and configuration of equipment on which the operator has previously demonstrated competency.
items.statement: For operators assessed under paragraph (f)(2), the documentation must reflect the date of the employer's determination of the operator's abilities and the make, model and configuration of equipment on which the operator previously demonstrated competency.

items.quote: When an employer is required to provide an operator with retraining under paragraph (b)(5) of this section, the employer must re-evaluate the operator with respect to the subject of the retraining.
items.statement: When an employer must retrain an operator under paragraph (b)(5), the employer must re-evaluate the operator on the subject of the retraining.

items.quote:
Tests under this section may be administered verbally, with answers given verbally, where the operator candidate:
[29cfr1926.1427(h)(1)(i)] (i) Passes a written demonstration of literacy relevant to the work.
items.statement: For tests under this section to be given and answered verbally, the operator candidate must pass a written demonstration of literacy relevant to the work.

items.quote: Demonstrates the ability to use the type of written manufacturer procedures applicable to the class/type of equipment for which the candidate is seeking certification.
items.statement: For tests under this section to be given verbally, the operator candidate must demonstrate the ability to use the type of written manufacturer procedures applicable to the class/type of equipment for which certification is sought.

items.quote: Tests under this section may be administered in any language the operator candidate understands
items.statement: Tests under this section may be administered in any language the operator candidate understands.

items.quote: the operator's certification documentation must note the language in which the test was given
items.statement: The operator's certification documentation must note the language in which the test was given.

items.quote: The operator is only permitted to operate equipment that is furnished with materials required by this subpart, such as operations manuals and load charts, that are written in the language of the certification.
items.statement: An operator may operate only equipment furnished with materials required by this subpart, such as operations manuals and load charts, written in the language of the certification.

items.quote: The individual knows the information necessary for safe operation of the specific type of equipment the individual will operate, including all of the following:
items.statement: Certification must be based on a written test determining that the individual knows the information necessary for safe operation of the specific type of equipment they will operate, including all the listed subjects.

items.quote: The controls and operational/performance characteristics.
items.statement: The certification written test must determine that the individual knows the controls and operational/performance characteristics of the specific equipment type.

items.quote: Use of, and the ability to calculate (manually or with a calculator), load/capacity information on a variety of configurations of the equipment.
items.statement: The certification written test must determine that the individual knows how to use, and can calculate manually or with a calculator, load/capacity information for a variety of equipment configurations.

items.quote: Procedures for preventing and responding to power line contact.
items.statement: The certification written test must determine that the individual knows procedures for preventing and responding to power line contact.

items.quote: Technical knowledge of the subject matter criteria listed in appendix C of this subpart applicable to the specific type of equipment the individual will operate.
items.statement: The certification written test must determine that the individual has technical knowledge of the appendix C subject matter criteria applicable to the specific equipment type they will operate.

items.quote: Use of the appendix C criteria meets the requirements of this provision.
items.statement: Using the appendix C criteria meets the requirement for technical knowledge of the applicable subject matter criteria.

items.quote: Technical knowledge applicable to the suitability of the supporting ground and surface to handle expected loads, site hazards, and site access.
items.statement: The certification written test must determine that the individual has technical knowledge applicable to whether the supporting ground and surface are suitable to handle expected loads, and to site hazards and site access.

items.quote: This subpart, including applicable incorporated materials.
items.statement: The certification written test must determine that the individual knows this subpart, including applicable incorporated materials.

items.quote: The individual is able to read and locate relevant information in the equipment manual and other materials containing information referred to in paragraph (j)(1)(i) of this section.
items.statement: The certification written test must determine that the individual can read and locate relevant information in the equipment manual and other materials containing the information referred to in paragraph (j)(1)(i).

items.quote: A determination through a practical test that the individual has the skills necessary for safe operation of the equipment
items.statement: Certification must be based on a practical test determining that the individual has the skills necessary for safe operation of the equipment.

items.quote: Ability to recognize, from visual and auditory observation, the items listed in § 1926.1412(d) (shift inspection).
items.statement: The certification practical test must assess the ability to recognize, by sight and sound, the shift inspection items listed in § 1926.1412(d).

items.quote: Operational and maneuvering skills.
items.statement: The certification practical test must assess operational and maneuvering skills.

items.quote: Application of load chart information.
items.statement: The certification practical test must assess application of load chart information.

items.quote: Application of safe shut-down and securing procedures.
items.statement: The certification practical test must assess application of safe shut-down and securing procedures.

items.quote: Apart from the evaluation and documentation requirements in paragraphs (a) and (f), this section is effective on December 10, 2018.
items.statement: Except for the evaluation and documentation requirements in paragraphs (a) and (f), this section is effective December 10, 2018.

items.quote: The evaluation and documentation requirements in paragraphs (a) and (f) are effective on February 7, 2019.
items.statement: The evaluation and documentation requirements in paragraphs (a) and (f) are effective February 7, 2019.

items.quote: The employer of the signal person must ensure that each signal person meets the Qualification Requirements (paragraph (c) of this section) prior to giving any signals.
items.statement: The employer of the signal person must ensure that each signal person meets the Qualification Requirements of paragraph (c) before giving any signals.

items.quote: This requirement must be met by using either Option (1) or Option (2) of this section.
items.statement: The employer must meet the signal person qualification requirement by using either Option (1), a third party qualified evaluator, or Option (2), the employer's qualified evaluator.

items.quote: The signal person has documentation from a third party qualified evaluator (see Qualified Evaluator (third party), § 1926.1401 for definition) showing that the signal person meets the Qualification Requirements
items.statement: Under Option (1), the signal person has documentation from a third party qualified evaluator showing that the signal person meets the Qualification Requirements.

items.quote: The employer's qualified (see Qualified Evaluator (not a third party), § 1926.1401 for definition) evaluator assesses the individual and determines that the individual meets the Qualification Requirements
items.statement: Under Option (2), the employer's qualified evaluator (not a third party) assesses the individual and determines that the individual meets the Qualification Requirements.

items.quote: and provides documentation of that determination.
items.statement: Under Option (2), the employer's qualified evaluator provides documentation of the determination that the individual meets the Qualification Requirements.

items.quote: An assessment by an employer's qualified evaluator under this option is not portable—other employers are not permitted to use it to meet the requirements of this section.
items.statement: An assessment by an employer's qualified evaluator under Option (2) is not portable, so other employers are not permitted to use it to meet the requirements of this section.

items.quote: The employer must make the documentation for whichever option is used available at the site while the signal person is employed by the employer.
items.statement: The employer must make the documentation for whichever option is used available at the site while the signal person is employed by the employer.

items.quote: The documentation must specify each type of signaling (e.g. hand signals, radio signals, etc.) for which the signal person meets the requirements of paragraph (c) of this section.
items.statement: The qualification documentation must specify each type of signaling, such as hand or radio signals, for which the signal person meets the paragraph (c) requirements.

items.quote: If subsequent actions by the signal person indicate that the individual does not meet the Qualification Requirements (see paragraph (c) of this section), the employer must not allow the individual to continue working as a signal person until re-training is provided and a re-assessment is made in accordance with paragraph (a) of this section that confirms that the individual meets the Qualification Requirements.
items.statement: If a signal person's subsequent actions indicate they do not meet the Qualification Requirements, the employer must not allow them to continue working as a signal person until re-training is provided and a re-assessment under paragraph (a) confirms they meet the requirements.

items.quote: Know and understand the type of signals used.
items.statement: Each signal person must know and understand the type of signals used.

items.quote: If hand signals are used, the signal person must know and understand the Standard Method for hand signals.
items.statement: If hand signals are used, the signal person must know and understand the Standard Method for hand signals.

items.quote: Be competent in the application of the type of signals used.
items.statement: Each signal person must be competent in the application of the type of signals used.

items.quote: Have a basic understanding of equipment operation and limitations, including the crane dynamics involved in swinging and stopping loads and boom deflection from hoisting loads.
items.statement: Each signal person must have a basic understanding of equipment operation and limitations, including the crane dynamics involved in swinging and stopping loads and boom deflection from hoisting loads.

items.quote: Know and understand the relevant requirements of §§ 1926.1419 through 1926.1422 and 1926.1428.
items.statement: Each signal person must know and understand the relevant requirements of §§ 1926.1419 through 1926.1422 and 1926.1428.

items.quote: Demonstrate that he/she meets the requirements in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4) of this section through an oral or written test, and through a practical test.
items.statement: Each signal person must demonstrate through an oral or written test that he or she meets the requirements in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4).

items.quote: Demonstrate that he/she meets the requirements in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4) of this section through an oral or written test, and through a practical test.
items.statement: Each signal person must also demonstrate through a practical test that he or she meets the requirements in paragraphs (c)(1) through (4).

items.quote: The operation is limited to those functions necessary to perform maintenance, inspect the equipment, or verify its performance.
items.statement: Maintenance, inspection and repair personnel may operate the equipment only where the operation is limited to functions necessary to perform maintenance, inspect the equipment, or verify its performance, and all other requirements of paragraph (a) are also met.

items.quote:
(2) The personnel either:
[29cfr1926.1429(a)(2)(i)] (i) Operate the equipment under the direct supervision of an operator who meets the requirements of § 1926.1427 (Operator qualification and certification); or
[29cfr1926.1429(a)(2)(ii)] (ii) Are familiar with the operation, limitations, characteristics and hazards associated with the type of equipment.
items.statement: To operate the equipment, maintenance, inspection and repair personnel must either operate it under the direct supervision of an operator who meets the requirements of § 1926.1427, or be familiar with the operation, limitations, characteristics and hazards associated with the type of equipment; the other requirements of paragraph (a) must also be met.

items.quote: Maintenance and repair personnel must meet the definition of a qualified person with respect to the equipment and maintenance/repair tasks performed.
items.statement: Maintenance and repair personnel must meet the definition of a qualified person with respect to the equipment and the maintenance/repair tasks performed.

items.quote: The employer must train each employee specified in § 1926.1408(g) and § 1926.1410(m) in the topics listed in § 1926.1408(g).
items.statement: The employer must train each employee specified in § 1926.1408(g) and § 1926.1410(m) on overhead powerlines, covering the topics listed in § 1926.1408(g).

items.quote: The employer must train each employee who will be assigned to work as a signal persons who does not meet the requirements of § 1926.1428(c) in the areas addressed in that paragraph.
items.statement: The employer must train each employee who will be assigned to work as a signal person and does not meet the requirements of § 1926.1428(c) in the areas addressed in that paragraph.

items.quote: The employer must train each operator in accordance with § 1926.1427(a) and (b), on the safe operation of the equipment the operator will be using.
items.statement: The employer must train each operator, in accordance with § 1926.1427(a) and (b), on the safe operation of the equipment the operator will be using.

items.quote: The employer must train each operator covered under the exception of § 1926.1427(a)(2) on the safe operation of the equipment the operator will be using.
items.statement: The employer must train each operator covered under the exception of § 1926.1427(a)(2) on the safe operation of the equipment the operator will be using.

items.quote: On friction equipment, whenever moving a boom off a support, first raise the boom a short distance (sufficient to take the load of the boom) to determine if the boom hoist brake needs to be adjusted.
items.statement: The employer must train each operator of subpart-covered equipment that, on friction equipment, whenever moving a boom off a support, the boom is first raised a short distance (sufficient to take the load of the boom) to determine whether the boom hoist brake needs adjustment.

items.quote: On other types of equipment with a boom, the same practice is applicable, except that typically there is no means of adjusting the brake; if the brake does not hold, a repair is necessary.
items.statement: The employer must train each operator of subpart-covered equipment that the same short boom-raise practice applies to other types of equipment with a boom, except that typically the brake cannot be adjusted, so a repair is necessary if the brake does not hold.

items.quote: Where available, the manufacturer's emergency procedures for halting unintended equipment movement.
items.statement: The employer must train each operator of subpart-covered equipment in the manufacturer's emergency procedures for halting unintended equipment movement, where available.

items.quote: The employer must train each competent person and each qualified person regarding the requirements of this subpart applicable to their respective roles.
items.statement: The employer must train each competent person and each qualified person on the subpart's requirements that apply to their respective roles.

items.quote: The employer must train each employee who works with the equipment to keep clear of holes, and crush/pinch points and the hazards addressed in § 1926.1424 (Work area control).
items.statement: The employer must train each employee who works with the equipment to keep clear of holes and crush/pinch points, and on the hazards addressed in § 1926.1424 (Work area control).

items.quote: The employer must train each operator and each additional employee authorized to start/energize equipment or operate equipment controls (such as maintenance and repair employees), in the tag-out and start-up procedures in §§ 1926.1417(f) and (g).
items.statement: The employer must train each operator, and each additional employee authorized to start/energize equipment or operate equipment controls (such as maintenance and repair employees), in the tag-out and start-up procedures in § 1926.1417(f) and (g).

items.quote: The employer must evaluate each employee required to be trained under this subpart to confirm that the employee understands the information provided in the training.
items.statement: The employer must evaluate each employee required to be trained under the subpart to confirm that the employee understands the training information.

items.quote: The employer must provide refresher training in relevant topics for each employee when, based on the conduct of the employee or an evaluation of the employee's knowledge, there is an indication that retraining is necessary.
items.statement: The employer must provide each employee refresher training in relevant topics when the employee's conduct or an evaluation of the employee's knowledge indicates that retraining is necessary.

items.quote: Whenever training is required under subpart CC, the employer must provide the training at no cost to the employee.
items.statement: Whenever training is required under subpart CC, the employer must provide it at no cost to the employee.

items.quote: The requirements of this section are supplemental to the other requirements in this subpart and apply when one or more employees are hoisted.
items.statement: The requirements of this section supplement the other requirements in the subpart and apply when one or more employees are hoisted.

items.quote: The use of equipment to hoist employees is prohibited except where the employer demonstrates that the erection, use, and dismantling of conventional means of reaching the work area, such as a personnel hoist, ladder, stairway, aerial lift, elevating work platform, or scaffold, would be more hazardous, or is not possible because of the project's structural design or worksite conditions.
items.statement: Using equipment to hoist employees is prohibited unless the employer demonstrates that erecting, using and dismantling conventional means of reaching the work area (such as a personnel hoist, ladder, stairway, aerial lift, elevating work platform or scaffold) would be more hazardous, or is not possible because of the project's structural design or worksite conditions.

items.quote: This paragraph does not apply to work covered by subpart R (Steel Erection) of this part
items.statement: Exception: paragraph (a), which restricts using equipment to hoist employees, does not apply to work covered by subpart R (Steel Erection).

items.quote: also does not apply to routine personnel access to an underground worksite via shaft as covered by § 1926.800 (Underground Construction) of this part.
items.statement: Exception: paragraph (a), which restricts using equipment to hoist employees, does not apply to routine personnel access to an underground worksite via shaft as covered by § 1926.800 (Underground Construction).

items.quote: When using equipment to hoist employees, the employees must be in a personnel platform that meets the requirements of paragraph (e) of this section.
items.statement: When equipment is used to hoist employees, they must be in a personnel platform that meets the requirements of paragraph (e).

items.quote: Into and out of drill shafts that are up to and including 8 feet in diameter
items.statement: Exception: a personnel platform is not required for hoisting employees into and out of drill shafts up to and including 8 feet in diameter (paragraph (o) sets the requirements for hoisting them).

items.quote: In pile driving operations (see paragraph (p) of this section for requirements for hoisting these employees).
items.statement: Exception: a personnel platform is not required for hoisting employees in pile driving operations (paragraph (p) sets the requirements for hoisting them).

items.quote: Solely for transfer to or from a marine worksite in a marine-hoisted personnel transfer device
items.statement: Exception: a personnel platform is not required for hoisting employees solely for transfer to or from a marine worksite in a marine-hoisted personnel transfer device (paragraph (r) sets the requirements for hoisting them).

items.quote: In storage-tank (steel or concrete), shaft and chimney operations
items.statement: Exception: a personnel platform is not required for hoisting employees in storage-tank (steel or concrete), shaft and chimney operations (paragraph (s) sets the requirements for hoisting them).

items.quote: The equipment must be uniformly level, within one percent of level grade
items.statement: The equipment must be uniformly level, within one percent of level grade.

items.quote: located on footing that a qualified person has determined to be sufficiently firm and stable.
items.statement: The equipment must be located on footing that a qualified person has determined to be sufficiently firm and stable.

items.quote: Equipment with outriggers or stabilizers must have them all extended and locked.
items.statement: Equipment with outriggers or stabilizers must have all of them extended and locked.

items.quote: The amount of extension must be the same for all outriggers and stabilizers
items.statement: The amount of extension must be the same for all outriggers and stabilizers.

items.quote: The amount of extension must be the same for all outriggers and stabilizers and in accordance with manufacturer procedures and load charts.
items.statement: Outrigger and stabilizer extension must be in accordance with manufacturer procedures and load charts.

items.quote: The total load (with the platform loaded, including the hook, load line and rigging) must not exceed 50 percent of the rated capacity for the radius and configuration of the equipment, except during proof testing.
items.statement: With suspended personnel platforms, the total load (loaded platform, including hook, load line and rigging) must not exceed 50 percent of the equipment's rated capacity for the radius and configuration, except during proof testing.

items.quote: The total weight of the loaded personnel platform must not exceed 50 percent of the rated capacity for the radius and configuration of the equipment (except during proof testing).
items.statement: With boom-attached personnel platforms, the total weight of the loaded platform must not exceed 50 percent of the equipment's rated capacity for the radius and configuration, except during proof testing.

items.quote: the total load (including the hook, load line, rigging and any other equipment that imposes a load) must not exceed 50 percent of the rated capacity for the radius and configuration of the equipment, except during proof testing.
items.statement: When hoisting personnel without a platform under paragraph (b)(2), the total load (including hook, load line, rigging and any other equipment that imposes a load) must not exceed 50 percent of the rated capacity for the radius and configuration, except during proof testing.

items.quote: When the occupied personnel platform is in a stationary working position, the load and boom hoist brakes, swing brakes, and operator actuated secondary braking and locking features (such as pawls or dogs) or automatic secondary brakes must be engaged.
items.statement: When the occupied personnel platform is in a stationary working position, the load and boom hoist brakes, swing brakes, and either operator-actuated secondary braking and locking features (such as pawls or dogs) or automatic secondary brakes must be engaged.

items.quote:
Equipment (except for derricks and articulating cranes) with a variable angle boom must be equipped with all of the following:
(A) A boom angle indicator, readily visible to the operator
items.statement: Equipment with a variable angle boom, except derricks and articulating cranes, must have a boom angle indicator readily visible to the operator.

items.quote:
Equipment (except for derricks and articulating cranes) with a variable angle boom must be equipped with all of the following:
(A) A boom angle indicator, readily visible to the operator, and
(B) A boom hoist limiting device.
items.statement: Equipment with a variable angle boom, except derricks and articulating cranes, must have a boom hoist limiting device.

items.quote: Articulating cranes must be equipped with a properly functioning automatic overload protection device.
items.statement: Articulating cranes must have a properly functioning automatic overload protection device.

items.quote:
Equipment with a luffing jib must be equipped with:
(A) A jib angle indicator, readily visible to the operator
items.statement: Equipment with a luffing jib must have a jib angle indicator readily visible to the operator.

items.quote:
Equipment with a luffing jib must be equipped with:
(A) A jib angle indicator, readily visible to the operator, and.
(B) A jib hoist limiting device.
items.statement: Equipment with a luffing jib must have a jib hoist limiting device.

items.quote: Equipment with telescoping booms must be equipped with a device to indicate the boom's extended length clearly to the operator, or must have measuring marks on the boom.
items.statement: Equipment with telescoping booms must have either a device that clearly indicates the boom's extended length to the operator or measuring marks on the boom.

items.quote: A device which automatically prevents damage and load failure from contact between the load block, overhaul ball, or similar component, and the boom tip (or fixed upper block or similar component) must be used.
items.statement: A device must be used that automatically prevents damage and load failure from contact between the load block, overhaul ball or similar component and the boom tip, fixed upper block or similar component.

items.quote: The device(s) must prevent such damage/failure at all points where two-blocking could occur.
items.statement: The anti two-block device(s) must prevent damage or failure at all points where two-blocking could occur.

items.quote: Exception: This device is not required when hoisting personnel in pile driving operations. Instead, paragraph (p)(2) of this section specifies how to prevent two-blocking during such operations.
items.statement: Exception: the anti two-block device is not required when hoisting personnel in pile driving operations; paragraph (p)(2) instead specifies how to prevent two-blocking.

items.quote: The load line hoist drum must have a system, other than the load line hoist brake, which regulates the lowering rate of speed of the hoist mechanism.
items.statement: The load line hoist drum must have a system, other than the load line hoist brake, that regulates the hoist mechanism's lowering speed.

items.quote: This system or device must be used when hoisting personnel.
items.statement: The controlled load lowering system or device must be used when hoisting personnel.

items.quote: Free fall of the load line hoist is prohibited
items.statement: Free fall of the load line hoist is prohibited.

items.quote: the use of equipment in which the boom hoist mechanism can free fall is also prohibited
items.statement: Using equipment in which the boom hoist mechanism can free fall is prohibited.

items.quote: Personnel hoisting operations must not begin unless the devices listed in this section are in proper working order.
items.statement: Personnel hoisting operations must not begin unless the devices listed in this section are in proper working order.

items.quote: If a device stops working properly during such operations, the operator must safely stop operations.
items.statement: If a device stops working properly during personnel hoisting, the operator must safely stop operations.

items.quote: Personnel hoisting operations must not resume until the device is again working properly.
items.statement: Personnel hoisting operations must not resume until the failed device is again working properly.

items.quote: Alternative measures are not permitted.
items.statement: Alternative measures are not permitted in place of a properly working required device for personnel hoisting.

items.quote: Direct attachment of a personnel platform to a luffing jib is prohibited.
items.statement: A personnel platform must not be attached directly to a luffing jib.

items.quote: A qualified person familiar with structural design must design the personnel platform and attachment/suspension system used for hoisting personnel.
items.statement: A qualified person familiar with structural design must design the personnel platform and the attachment/suspension system used for hoisting personnel.

items.quote: must allow the platform to remain within 10 degrees of level, regardless of boom angle.
items.statement: The system connecting the personnel platform to the equipment must allow the platform to remain within 10 degrees of level regardless of boom angle.

items.quote: The suspension system must be designed to minimize tipping of the platform due to movement of employees occupying the platform.
items.statement: The suspension system must be designed to minimize platform tipping caused by movement of the employees occupying it.

items.quote: The personnel platform itself (excluding the guardrail system and personal fall arrest system anchorages), must be capable of supporting, without failure, its own weight and at least five times the maximum intended load.
items.statement: The personnel platform itself, excluding the guardrail system and personal fall arrest anchorages, must be able to support without failure its own weight plus at least five times the maximum intended load.

items.quote: All welding of the personnel platform and its components must be performed by a certified welder familiar with the weld grades, types and material specified in the platform design.
items.statement: All welding of the personnel platform and its components must be done by a certified welder familiar with the weld grades, types and material specified in the platform design.

items.quote: The personnel platform must be equipped with a guardrail system which meets the requirements of subpart M of this part
items.statement: The personnel platform must have a guardrail system that meets the requirements of subpart M.

items.quote: must be enclosed at least from the toeboard to mid-rail with either solid construction material or expanded metal having openings no greater than 1/2 inch (1.27 cm).
items.statement: The platform must be enclosed at least from toeboard to mid-rail with solid construction material or expanded metal with openings no greater than 1/2 inch (1.27 cm).

items.quote: Points to which personal fall arrest systems are attached must meet the anchorage requirements in subpart M of this part.
items.statement: Points to which personal fall arrest systems are attached on the platform must meet the subpart M anchorage requirements.

items.quote: A grab rail must be installed inside the entire perimeter of the personnel platform except for access gates/doors.
items.statement: A grab rail must be installed inside the entire perimeter of the personnel platform, except at access gates/doors.

items.quote: (i) Not swing outward.
items.statement: Installed access gates/doors of any type must not swing outward, except as allowed where inward swing with safe entry is infeasible because of platform size.

items.quote: If due to the size of the personnel platform, such as a 1-person platform, it is infeasible for the door to swing inward and allow safe entry for the platform occupant, then the access gate/door may swing outward.
items.statement: Exception: an access gate/door may swing outward if, because of platform size (such as a 1-person platform), it is infeasible for it to swing inward and allow the occupant to enter safely.

items.quote: Be equipped with a device that prevents accidental opening.
items.statement: Installed access gates/doors of any type must have a device that prevents accidental opening.

items.quote: Headroom must be sufficient to allow employees to stand upright in the platform.
items.statement: Platform headroom must be sufficient for employees to stand upright.

items.quote: In addition to the use of hard hats, employees must be protected by overhead protection on the personnel platform when employees are exposed to falling objects.
items.statement: When employees are exposed to falling objects, they must be protected by overhead protection on the personnel platform in addition to using hard hats.

items.quote: The platform overhead protection must not obscure the view of the operator or platform occupants (such as wire mesh that has up to 1/2 inch openings), unless full protection is necessary.
items.statement: Platform overhead protection must not obscure the view of the operator or platform occupants (such as wire mesh with openings up to 1/2 inch), unless full protection is necessary.

items.quote: All edges exposed to employee contact must be smooth enough to prevent injury.
items.statement: All platform edges exposed to employee contact must be smooth enough to prevent injury.

items.quote: The weight of the platform and its rated capacity must be conspicuously posted on the platform with a plate or other permanent marking.
items.statement: The platform's weight and rated capacity must be conspicuously posted on it with a plate or other permanent marking.

items.quote: The personnel platform must not be loaded in excess of its rated capacity.
items.statement: The personnel platform must not be loaded beyond its rated capacity.

items.quote: Personnel platforms must be used only for employees, their tools, and the materials necessary to do their work.
items.statement: Personnel platforms must be used only for employees, their tools and the materials necessary for their work.

items.quote: Platforms must not be used to hoist materials or tools when not hoisting personnel.
items.statement: Personnel platforms must not be used to hoist materials or tools when not hoisting personnel, subject to the trial lift exception.

items.quote: Materials and tools to be used during the lift, if secured and distributed in accordance with paragraph (f)(3) of this section may be in the platform for trial lifts.
items.statement: Exception: materials and tools to be used during the lift may be in the platform for trial lifts if secured and distributed in accordance with paragraph (f)(3).

items.quote:
(3) Materials and tools must be:
(i) Secured to prevent displacement.
items.statement: Materials and tools must be secured to prevent displacement.

items.quote: Evenly distributed within the confines of the platform while it is suspended.
items.statement: Materials and tools must be evenly distributed within the platform while it is suspended.

items.quote: The number of employees occupying the personnel platform must not exceed the maximum number the platform was designed to hold or the number required to perform the work, whichever is less.
items.statement: The number of employees in the personnel platform must not exceed the lesser of the maximum number it was designed to hold or the number required to perform the work.

items.quote: Of a type that can be closed and locked, eliminating the throat opening.
items.statement: Hooks used in the connection between the hoist line and the personnel platform, including those on overhaul ball assemblies, lower load blocks, bridle legs or other attachment assemblies or components, must be of a type that can be closed and locked, eliminating the throat opening.

items.quote: Closed and locked when attached.
items.statement: Hooks used in the connection between the hoist line and the personnel platform must be closed and locked when attached.

items.quote: Shackles used in place of hooks must be of the alloy anchor type
items.statement: Shackles used in place of hooks must be of the alloy anchor type.

items.quote:
with either:
[29cfr1926.1431(g)(1)(ii)(A)] (A) A bolt, nut and retaining pin, in place; or
[29cfr1926.1431(g)(1)(ii)(B)] (B) Of the screw type, with the screw pin secured from accidental removal.
items.statement: Shackles used in place of hooks must have either a bolt, nut and retaining pin in place, or be of the screw type with the screw pin secured from accidental removal.

items.quote: Where other detachable devices are used, they must be of the type that can be closed and locked to the same extent as the devices addressed in paragraphs (g)(1)(i) and (ii) of this section.
items.statement: Other detachable devices, where used, must be of a type that can be closed and locked to the same extent as the hooks and shackles addressed in paragraphs (g)(1)(i) and (ii).

items.quote: Such devices must be closed and locked when attached.
items.statement: Other detachable devices must be closed and locked when attached.

items.quote: each bridle leg must be connected to a master link or shackle (see paragraph (g)(1) of this section) in a manner that ensures that the load is evenly divided among the bridle legs.
items.statement: When a rope bridle suspends the personnel platform, each bridle leg must be connected to a master link or shackle in a manner that ensures the load is evenly divided among the bridle legs.

items.quote: must be capable of supporting, without failure, at least five times the maximum intended load applied or transmitted to that component.
items.statement: Rigging hardware (including wire rope, shackles, rings and master links) and hooks must be capable of supporting, without failure, at least five times the maximum intended load applied or transmitted to that component.

items.quote: Where rotation resistant rope is used, the slings must be capable of supporting without failure at least ten times the maximum intended load.
items.statement: Where rotation resistant rope is used, the slings must be capable of supporting without failure at least ten times the maximum intended load.

items.quote: Eyes in wire rope slings must be fabricated with thimbles.
items.statement: Eyes in wire rope slings must be fabricated with thimbles.

items.quote: Bridles and associated rigging for suspending the personnel platform must be used only for the platform and the necessary employees, their tools and materials necessary to do their work.
items.statement: Bridles and associated rigging for suspending the personnel platform must be used only for the platform, the necessary employees, and the tools and materials necessary to do their work.

items.quote: The bridles and associated rigging must not have been used for any purpose other than hoisting personnel.
items.statement: The bridles and associated rigging for suspending the personnel platform must not have been used for any purpose other than hoisting personnel.

items.quote: A trial lift with the unoccupied personnel platform loaded at least to the anticipated liftweight must be made from ground level, or any other location where employees will enter the platform, to each location at which the platform is to be hoisted and positioned.
items.statement: A trial lift with the unoccupied personnel platform loaded at least to the anticipated liftweight must be made from ground level, or any other location where employees will enter the platform, to each location at which the platform will be hoisted and positioned.

items.quote: Where there is more than one location to be reached from a single set-up position, either individual trial lifts for each location, or a single trial lift, in which the platform is moved sequentially to each location, must be performed
items.statement: When more than one location is to be reached from a single set-up position, either an individual trial lift to each location or a single trial lift moving the platform sequentially to each location must be performed.

items.quote: the method selected must be the same as the method that will be used to hoist the personnel.
items.statement: For multiple locations from one set-up position, the trial lift method selected must be the same as the method that will be used to hoist the personnel.

items.quote: The trial lift must be performed immediately prior to each shift in which personnel will be hoisted.
items.statement: The trial lift must be performed immediately prior to each shift in which personnel will be hoisted.

items.quote:
In addition, the trial lift must be repeated prior to hoisting employees in each of the following circumstances:
[29cfr1926.1431(h)(2)(i)] (i) The equipment is moved and set up in a new location or returned to a previously used location.
items.statement: The trial lift must be repeated before hoisting employees when the equipment is moved and set up in a new location or returned to a previously used location.

items.quote: The lift route is changed, unless the competent person determines that the new route presents no new factors affecting safety.
items.statement: The trial lift must be repeated before hoisting employees when the lift route is changed, unless the competent person determines that the new route presents no new factors affecting safety.

items.quote: Safety devices and operational aids required by this section are activated and functioning properly.
items.statement: For the trial lift, the competent person must determine that safety devices and operational aids required by this section are activated and functioning properly.

items.quote: Other safety devices and operational aids must meet the requirements of §§ 1926.1415 and 1926.1416.
items.statement: Other safety devices and operational aids must meet the requirements of §§ 1926.1415 and 1926.1416.

items.quote: Nothing interferes with the equipment or the personnel platform in the course of the trial lift.
items.statement: The competent person must determine that nothing interferes with the equipment or the personnel platform in the course of the trial lift.

items.quote: The lift will not exceed 50 percent of the equipment's rated capacity at any time during the lift.
items.statement: The competent person must determine that the lift will not exceed 50 percent of the equipment's rated capacity at any time during the lift.
items.unit: percent of the equipment's rated capacity

items.quote: The load radius to be used during the lift has been accurately determined.
items.statement: The competent person must determine that the load radius to be used during the lift has been accurately determined.

items.quote: Conduct a visual inspection of the equipment, base support or ground, and personnel platform, to determine whether the trial lift has exposed any defect or problem or produced any adverse effect.
items.statement: Immediately after the trial lift, the competent person must visually inspect the equipment, base support or ground, and personnel platform to determine whether the trial lift exposed any defect or problem or produced any adverse effect.

items.quote: Confirm that, upon the completion of the trial lift process, the test weight has been removed.
items.statement: Immediately after the trial lift, the competent person must confirm that the test weight has been removed upon completion of the trial lift process.

items.quote: The platform must be hoisted a few inches with the personnel and materials/tools on board and inspected by a competent person to ensure that it is secure and properly balanced.
items.statement: Immediately before each lift, the platform must be hoisted a few inches with personnel and materials/tools on board and inspected by a competent person to ensure it is secure and properly balanced.

items.quote: Hoist ropes must be free of deficiencies in accordance with § 1926.1413(a).
items.statement: Immediately before each lift and before the personnel lift proceeds, a competent person must determine that hoist ropes are free of deficiencies in accordance with § 1926.1413(a).

items.quote: Multiple part lines must not be twisted around each other.
items.statement: Immediately before each lift and before the personnel lift proceeds, a competent person must determine that multiple part lines are not twisted around each other.

items.quote: The primary attachment must be centered over the platform.
items.statement: Immediately before each lift and before the personnel lift proceeds, a competent person must determine that the primary attachment is centered over the platform.

items.quote: If the load rope is slack, the hoisting system must be inspected to ensure that all ropes are properly seated on drums and in sheaves.
items.statement: If the load rope is slack immediately before a lift, the hoisting system must be inspected to ensure all ropes are properly seated on drums and in sheaves before the personnel lift proceeds.

items.quote: Any condition found during the trial lift and subsequent inspection(s) that fails to meet a requirement of this standard or otherwise creates a safety hazard must be corrected before hoisting personnel.
items.statement: Any condition found during the trial lift and subsequent inspections that fails to meet a requirement of the standard or otherwise creates a safety hazard must be corrected before hoisting personnel.

items.quote: At each jobsite, prior to hoisting employees on the personnel platform, and after any repair or modification, the platform and rigging must be proof tested to 125 percent of the platform's rated capacity.
items.statement: At each jobsite, before hoisting employees on the personnel platform, the platform and rigging must be proof tested to 125 percent of the platform's rated capacity.
items.unit: percent of the platform's rated capacity

items.quote: after any repair or modification, the platform and rigging must be proof tested to 125 percent of the platform's rated capacity.
items.statement: After any repair or modification, the platform and rigging must be proof tested to 125 percent of the platform's rated capacity.
items.unit: percent of the platform's rated capacity

items.quote: The proof test may be done concurrently with the trial lift.
items.statement: The proof test is permitted to be done concurrently with the trial lift.

items.quote: The platform must be lowered by controlled load lowering, braked
items.statement: For proof testing, the platform must be lowered by controlled load lowering and braked.

items.quote: held in a suspended position for a minimum of five minutes with the test load evenly distributed on the platform.
items.statement: For proof testing, the platform must be held in a suspended position for at least five minutes with the test load evenly distributed on it.

items.quote: After proof testing, a competent person must inspect the platform and rigging to determine if the test has been passed.
items.statement: After proof testing, a competent person must inspect the platform and rigging to determine whether the test has been passed.

items.quote: If any deficiencies are found that pose a safety hazard, the platform and rigging must not be used to hoist personnel unless the deficiencies are corrected, the test is repeated, and a competent person determines that the test has been passed.
items.statement: If deficiencies posing a safety hazard are found after proof testing, the platform and rigging must not be used to hoist personnel unless the deficiencies are corrected, the test is repeated, and a competent person determines the test has been passed.

items.quote: Personnel hoisting must not be conducted until the competent person determines that the platform and rigging have successfully passed the proof test.
items.statement: Personnel hoisting must not be conducted until the competent person determines that the platform and rigging have passed the proof test.

items.quote: Hoisting of the personnel platform must be performed in a slow, controlled, cautious manner, with no sudden movements of the equipment or the platform.
items.statement: The personnel platform must be hoisted in a slow, controlled, cautious manner, with no sudden movements of the equipment or the platform.

items.quote: Keep all parts of the body inside the platform during raising, lowering, and horizontal movement.
items.statement: Platform occupants must keep all body parts inside the platform during raising, lowering and horizontal movement.

items.quote: This provision does not apply to an occupant of the platform when necessary to position the platform or while performing the duties of a signal person.
items.statement: The rule to keep all body parts inside the platform does not apply to an occupant when necessary to position the platform or while performing the duties of a signal person.

items.quote: Not stand, sit on, or work from the top or intermediate rail or toeboard
items.statement: Platform occupants must not stand on, sit on, or work from the top or intermediate rail or toeboard.

items.quote: or use any other means/device to raise their working height.
items.statement: Platform occupants must not use any other means or device to raise their working height.

items.quote: Not pull the platform out of plumb in relation to the hoisting equipment.
items.statement: Platform occupants must not pull the platform out of plumb in relation to the hoisting equipment.

items.quote: Before employees exit or enter a hoisted personnel platform that is not landed, the platform must be secured to the structure where the work is to be performed, unless the employer can demonstrate that securing to the structure would create a greater hazard.
items.statement: Before employees exit or enter a hoisted personnel platform that is not landed, the platform must be secured to the structure where the work is to be performed, unless the employer can demonstrate that securing it would create a greater hazard.

items.quote: If the platform is tied to the structure, the operator must not move the platform until the operator receives confirmation that it is freely suspended.
items.statement: If the platform is tied to the structure, the operator must not move it until receiving confirmation that it is freely suspended.

items.quote: Tag lines must be used when necessary to control the platform.
items.statement: Tag lines must be used when necessary to control the platform.

items.quote: Where the platform is not equipped with controls, the equipment operator must remain at the equipment controls, on site, and in view of the equipment, at all times while the platform is occupied.
items.statement: For a platform without controls, the equipment operator must remain at the equipment controls, on site and in view of the equipment, at all times while the platform is occupied.

items.quote: The occupant using the controls in the platform must be a qualified person with respect to their use, including the safe limitations of the equipment and hazards associated with its operation.
items.statement: For a platform with controls, at all times while it is occupied, the occupant using them must be a qualified person on their use, including the equipment's safe limitations and operating hazards.

items.quote: The equipment operator must be at a set of equipment controls that include boom and swing functions of the equipment
items.statement: For a platform with controls, while it is occupied, the equipment operator must be at a set of equipment controls that include the boom and swing functions.

items.quote: The equipment operator must be at a set of equipment controls that include boom and swing functions of the equipment, and must be on site and in view of the equipment.
items.statement: For a platform with controls, while it is occupied, the equipment operator must be on site and in view of the equipment.

items.quote: The platform operating manual must be in the platform or on the equipment.
items.statement: For a platform with controls, while it is occupied, the platform operating manual must be in the platform or on the equipment.

items.quote: When wind speed (sustained or gusts) exceeds 20 mph at the personnel platform, a qualified person must determine if, in light of the wind conditions, it is not safe to lift personnel.
items.statement: When sustained or gust wind speed at the personnel platform exceeds 20 mph, a qualified person must determine whether the wind conditions make it unsafe to lift personnel.

items.quote: If it is not, the lifting operation must not begin (or, if already in progress, must be terminated).
items.statement: If the qualified person determines that wind makes lifting personnel unsafe, the lift must not begin, or must be terminated if already in progress.

items.quote: A qualified person must determine if, in light of indications of dangerous weather conditions, or other impending or existing danger, it is not safe to lift personnel.
items.statement: A qualified person must determine whether indications of dangerous weather, or other impending or existing danger, make it unsafe to lift personnel.

items.quote: If it is not, the lifting operation must not begin (or, if already in progress, must be terminated).
items.statement: If dangerous weather or other impending or existing danger is determined to make lifting personnel unsafe, the lift must not begin, or must be terminated if already in progress.

items.quote: Employees being hoisted must remain in direct communication with the signal person (where used), or the operator.
items.statement: Employees being hoisted must remain in direct communication with the signal person (where used) or the operator.

items.quote: Except over water, employees occupying the personnel platform must be provided and use a personal fall arrest system.
items.statement: Except over water, employees occupying the personnel platform must be provided with and use a personal fall arrest system.

items.quote: The system must be attached to a structural member within the personnel platform.
items.statement: The personal fall arrest system for platform occupants, required except over water, must be attached to a structural member within the personnel platform.

items.quote: When working over or near water, the requirements of § 1926.106 apply.
items.statement: When working over or near water, the requirements of § 1926.106 apply.

items.quote: The fall arrest system, including the attachment point (anchorage) used to comply with paragraph (i) of this section, must meet the requirements in § 1926.502.
items.statement: The fall arrest system used to comply with paragraph (k)(10)(i), including its anchorage, must meet the requirements in § 1926.502.

items.quote: No lifts must be made on any other of the equipment's load lines while personnel are being hoisted, except in pile driving operations.
items.statement: No lifts may be made on any of the equipment's other load lines while personnel are being hoisted, except in pile driving operations.

items.quote: Loads are permitted to be hoisted by such a winch while employees occupy the personnel platform only where the load on the winch line does not exceed 500 pounds
items.statement: A winch that is original equipment on a factory-produced boom-mounted personnel platform may hoist loads while employees occupy the platform only if the winch line load does not exceed 500 pounds.

items.quote: only where the load on the winch line does not exceed 500 pounds and does not exceed the rated capacity of the winch and platform.
items.statement: A winch that is original equipment on a factory-produced boom-mounted personnel platform may hoist loads while employees occupy the platform only if the winch line load does not exceed the rated capacity of the winch and platform.

items.quote: Hoisting of employees while the equipment is traveling is prohibited, except for:
items.statement: For equipment other than derricks, hoisting employees while the equipment is traveling is prohibited unless an exception in paragraph (k)(12)(i) applies.

items.quote: Equipment that travels on fixed rails; or
items.statement: Equipment that travels on fixed rails is excepted from the ban on hoisting employees while traveling.

items.quote: Where the employer demonstrates that there is no less hazardous way to perform the work.
items.statement: The ban on hoisting employees while equipment travels is excepted where the employer demonstrates there is no less hazardous way to perform the work.

items.quote: This exception does not apply to rubber-tired equipment.
items.statement: The exception stated in paragraph (k)(12)(i) for hoisting employees while traveling does not apply to rubber-tired equipment.

items.quote: Equipment travel must be restricted to a fixed track or runway.
items.statement: When employees are hoisted while the equipment travels, travel must be restricted to a fixed track or runway.

items.quote: Where a runway is used, it must be a firm, level surface designed, prepared and designated as a path of travel for the weight and configuration of the equipment being used to lift and travel with the personnel platform.
items.statement: A runway used for traveling with hoisted employees must be a firm, level surface designed, prepared and designated as a travel path for the weight and configuration of the equipment used to lift and travel with the platform.

items.quote: An existing surface may be used as long as it meets these criteria.
items.statement: An existing surface may be used as a runway as long as it meets the runway criteria.

items.quote: Equipment travel must be limited to boom length.
items.statement: When employees are hoisted while the equipment travels, travel must be limited to boom length.

items.quote: The boom must be parallel to the direction of travel, except where it is safer to do otherwise.
items.statement: When employees are hoisted while the equipment travels, the boom must be parallel to the direction of travel, except where it is safer to do otherwise.

items.quote: A complete trial run must be performed to test the route of travel before employees are allowed to occupy the platform.
items.statement: When employees are to be hoisted while the equipment travels, a complete trial run testing the travel route must be performed before employees may occupy the platform.

items.quote: This trial run can be performed at the same time as the trial lift required by paragraph (h) of this section which tests the lift route.
items.statement: The travel trial run may be performed at the same time as the paragraph (h) trial lift, which tests the lift route.

items.quote: Derricks are prohibited from traveling while personnel are hoisted.
items.statement: Derricks are prohibited from traveling while personnel are hoisted.

items.quote: Held to review the applicable requirements of this section and the procedures that will be followed.
items.statement: A pre-lift meeting must be held to review the applicable requirements of this section and the procedures that will be followed.

items.quote: Attended by the equipment operator, signal person (if used for the lift), employees to be hoisted, and the person responsible for the task to be performed.
items.statement: The pre-lift meeting must be attended by the equipment operator, the signal person (if used for the lift), the employees to be hoisted and the person responsible for the task.

items.quote: Held prior to the trial lift at each new work location
items.statement: The pre-lift meeting must be held before the trial lift at each new work location.

items.quote: must be repeated for any employees newly assigned to the operation.
items.statement: The pre-lift meeting must be repeated for any employees newly assigned to the operation.

items.quote: Hoisting personnel within 20 feet of a power line that is up to 350 kV, and hoisting personnel within 50 feet of a power line that is over 350 kV, is prohibited, except for work covered by subpart V of this part
items.statement: Hoisting personnel within 20 feet of a power line up to 350 kV is prohibited, except for work covered by subpart V (Power Transmission and Distribution).

items.quote: hoisting personnel within 50 feet of a power line that is over 350 kV, is prohibited, except for work covered by subpart V of this part
items.statement: Hoisting personnel within 50 feet of a power line over 350 kV is prohibited, except for work covered by subpart V (Power Transmission and Distribution).

items.quote: When hoisting employees into and out of drill shafts that are up to and including 8 feet in diameter, all of the following requirements must be met:
items.statement: All the paragraph (o) requirements must be met when hoisting employees into and out of drill shafts up to and including 8 feet in diameter.

items.quote: The employee must be in either a personnel platform or on a boatswain's chair.
items.statement: An employee hoisted into or out of a drill shaft up to and including 8 feet in diameter must be in a personnel platform or on a boatswain's chair.

items.quote: If using a personnel platform, paragraphs (a) through (n) of this section apply.
items.statement: If a personnel platform is used for drill shaft hoisting under paragraph (o), paragraphs (a) through (n) apply.

If a boatswain's chair is used for drill shaft hoisting, paragraphs (a), (c), (d)(1), (d)(3), (d)(4), (e)(1)-(3), (f)(1), (f)(2)(i), (f)(3)(i), (g), (h), (k)(1), (k)(6), (k)(8), (k)(9), (k)(11)(i), (m) and (n) apply.

items.quote: Where the terms “personnel platform” or “platform” are used in these paragraphs, substitute them with “boatswain's chair.”
