items.statement: In the paragraphs applied to drill shaft boatswain's chair hoisting, "boatswain's chair" is substituted for "personnel platform" or "platform".

items.quote: A signal person must be stationed at the shaft opening.
items.statement: For drill shaft hoisting in a boatswain's chair, a signal person must be stationed at the shaft opening.

items.quote: The employee must be hoisted in a slow, controlled descent and ascent.
items.statement: For drill shaft hoisting in a boatswain's chair, the employee must be hoisted in a slow, controlled descent and ascent.

items.quote: The employee must use personal fall protection equipment, including a full body harness, attached independent of the crane/derrick.
items.statement: For drill shaft hoisting in a boatswain's chair, the employee must use personal fall protection equipment, including a full body harness, attached independent of the crane/derrick.

items.quote: The fall protection equipment must meet the applicable requirements in § 1926.502.
items.statement: For drill shaft hoisting in a boatswain's chair, the fall protection equipment must meet the applicable requirements in § 1926.502.

items.quote: must be capable of supporting, without failure, its own weight and at least five times the maximum intended load.
items.statement: For drill shaft hoisting, the boatswain's chair itself (excluding personal fall arrest system anchorages) must support without failure its own weight and at least five times the maximum intended load.

items.quote: No more than one person must be hoisted at a time.
items.statement: For drill shaft hoisting in a boatswain's chair, no more than one person may be hoisted at a time.

items.quote: The employee must be in a personnel platform or boatswain's chair.
items.statement: An employee hoisted in pile driving operations must be in a personnel platform or boatswain's chair.

items.quote: For lattice boom cranes: Clearly mark the cable (so that it can easily be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, or use a spotter who is in direct communication with the operator to inform the operator when this point is reached.
items.statement: When hoisting an employee in pile driving with a lattice boom crane, either the cable must be clearly marked, easily seen by the operator, at a point giving time to stop the hoist and prevent two-blocking, or a spotter in direct communication with the operator must say when that point is reached.

items.quote: For telescopic boom cranes: Clearly mark the cable (so that it can be easily seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking
items.statement: When hoisting an employee in pile driving with a telescopic boom crane, the cable must be clearly marked, easily seen by the operator, at a point giving the operator time to stop the hoist and prevent two-blocking.

items.quote: and use a spotter who is in direct communication with the operator to inform the operator when this point is reached.
items.statement: When hoisting an employee in pile driving with a telescopic boom crane, a spotter in direct communication with the operator must also be used to inform the operator when the marked point is reached.

items.quote: If using a personnel platform, paragraphs (b) through (n) of this section apply.
items.statement: If a personnel platform is used in pile driving operations, paragraphs (b) through (n) apply.

If a boatswain's chair is used in pile driving, paragraphs (a), (c), (d)(1), (d)(3), (d)(4), (e)(1)-(3), (f)(1), (f)(2)(i), (f)(3)(i), (g), (h), (j), (k)(1), (k)(6), (k)(8), (k)(9), (k)(11)(i), (m) and (n) apply.

items.quote: Where the terms “personnel platform” or “platform” are used in these paragraphs, substitute them with “boatswains chair.”
items.statement: In the paragraphs applied to pile driving boatswain's chair hoisting, "boatswains chair" is substituted for "personnel platform" or "platform".

items.quote: The employee must be hoisted in a slow, controlled descent and ascent.
items.statement: For pile driving hoisting in a boatswain's chair, the employee must be hoisted in a slow, controlled descent and ascent.

items.quote: The employee must use personal fall protection equipment, including a full body harness, independently attached to the lower load block or overhaul ball.
items.statement: For pile driving hoisting in a boatswain's chair, the employee must use personal fall protection equipment, including a full body harness, independently attached to the lower load block or overhaul ball.

items.quote: The fall protection equipment must meet the applicable requirements in § 1926.502.
items.statement: For pile driving hoisting in a boatswain's chair, the fall protection equipment must meet the applicable requirements in § 1926.502.

items.quote: must be capable of supporting, without failure, its own weight and at least five times the maximum intended load.
items.statement: For pile driving hoisting, the boatswain's chair itself (excluding personal fall arrest system anchorages) must support without failure its own weight and at least five times the maximum intended load.

items.quote: No more than one person must be hoisted at a time.
items.statement: For pile driving hoisting in a boatswain's chair, no more than one person may be hoisted at a time.

items.quote: The employee must be in either a personnel platform or a marine-hoisted personnel transfer device.
items.statement: When employees are hoisted solely for transfer to or from a marine worksite, each employee must be in either a personnel platform or a marine-hoisted personnel transfer device.

items.quote: If using a personnel platform, paragraphs (a) through (n) of this section apply.
items.statement: When a personnel platform is used to hoist employees solely for transfer to or from a marine worksite, paragraphs (a) through (n) of this section apply.

items.quote: The following paragraphs of this section apply: (a), (c)(2), (d)(1), (d)(3), (d)(4), (e)(1) through (5), (e)(12), (f)(1), (g), (h), (j), (k)(1), (k)(8), (k)(9), (k)(10)(ii), (k)(11)(i), (k)(12), (m), and (n).
items.statement: When a marine-hoisted personnel transfer device is used for marine transfer, these paragraphs of this section apply: (a), (c)(2), (d)(1), (d)(3), (d)(4), (e)(1) through (5), (e)(12), (f)(1), (g), (h), (j), (k)(1), (k)(8), (k)(9), (k)(10)(ii), (k)(11)(i), (k)(12), (m), and (n).

items.quote: Where the terms “personnel platform” or “platform” are used in these paragraphs, substitute them with “marine-hoisted personnel transfer device.”
items.statement: In the paragraphs that apply to a marine-hoisted personnel transfer device, that term is substituted wherever "personnel platform" or "platform" is used.

items.quote: The transfer device must be used only for transferring workers.
items.statement: A marine-hoisted personnel transfer device used for marine transfer must be used only for transferring workers.

items.quote: The number of workers occupying the transfer device must not exceed the maximum number it was designed to hold.
items.statement: The number of workers occupying a marine-hoisted personnel transfer device must not exceed the maximum number it was designed to hold.

items.quote: Each employee must wear a U.S. Coast Guard personal flotation device approved for industrial use.
items.statement: When a marine-hoisted personnel transfer device is used for marine transfer, each employee must wear a U.S. Coast Guard personal flotation device approved for industrial use.

items.quote: The employee must be in a personnel platform except when the employer can demonstrate that use of a personnel platform is infeasible
items.statement: An employee hoisted in storage tank (steel or concrete), shaft and chimney operations must be in a personnel platform, except when the employer can demonstrate that using one is infeasible.

items.quote: except when the employer can demonstrate that use of a personnel platform is infeasible; in such a case, a boatswain's chair must be used.
items.statement: In storage tank, shaft and chimney operations, if the employer can demonstrate that using a personnel platform is infeasible, a boatswain's chair must be used.

items.quote: If using a personnel platform, paragraphs (a) through (n) of this section apply.
items.statement: When a personnel platform is used for hoisting in storage tank, shaft and chimney operations, paragraphs (a) through (n) of this section apply.

When a boatswain's chair is used in storage tank, shaft and chimney operations, these paragraphs of this section apply: (a), (c), (d)(1), (d)(3), (d)(4), (e)(1), (e)(2), (e)(3), (f)(1), (f)(2)(i), (f)(3)(i), (g), (h), (k)(1), (k)(6), (k)(8), (k)(9), (k)(11)(i), (m), (n).

items.quote: Where the terms “personnel platform” or “platform” are used in these paragraphs, substitute them with “boatswains chair.”
items.statement: In the paragraphs that apply to a boatswain's chair, "boatswains chair" is substituted wherever "personnel platform" or "platform" is used.

items.quote: The employee must be hoisted in a slow, controlled descent and ascent.
items.statement: An employee using a boatswain's chair in storage tank, shaft and chimney operations must be hoisted in a slow, controlled descent and ascent.

items.quote: The employee must use personal fall protection equipment, including a full body harness
items.statement: An employee using a boatswain's chair must use personal fall protection equipment, including a full body harness.

items.quote: The employee must use personal fall protection equipment, including a full body harness, attached independent of the crane/derrick.
items.statement: The personal fall protection equipment of an employee in a boatswain's chair must be attached independent of the crane/derrick, subject to the exception for when there is no adequate structure for attachment as required in § 1926.502(d)(15).

items.quote: When there is no adequate structure for attachment of personal fall arrest equipment as required in § 1926.502(d)(15), the attachment must be to the lower load block or overhaul ball.
items.statement: For an employee in a boatswain's chair, when there is no adequate structure for attaching personal fall arrest equipment as required in § 1926.502(d)(15), the attachment must be to the lower load block or overhaul ball.

items.quote: The fall protection equipment must meet the applicable requirements in § 1926.502.
items.statement: Fall protection equipment used with a boatswain's chair must meet the applicable requirements in § 1926.502.

items.quote: The boatswain's chair itself (excluding the personal fall arrest system anchorages), must be capable of supporting, without failure, its own weight and at least five times the maximum intended load.
items.statement: The boatswain's chair itself, excluding the personal fall arrest system anchorages, must be capable of supporting without failure its own weight and at least five times the maximum intended load.

items.quote: No more than one person must be hoisted at a time.
items.statement: When a boatswain's chair is used, no more than one person may be hoisted at a time.

items.quote: Before beginning a crane/derrick operation in which more than one crane/derrick will be supporting the load, the operation must be planned.
items.statement: Before beginning a crane/derrick operation in which more than one crane or derrick will be supporting the load, the operation must be planned.

items.quote: The plan must be developed by a qualified person.
items.statement: The plan for a multiple-crane/derrick lift must be developed by a qualified person.

items.quote: The plan must be designed to ensure that the requirements of this subpart are met.
items.statement: The multiple-crane/derrick lift plan must be designed to ensure that the requirements of this subpart are met.

items.quote: Where the qualified person determines that engineering expertise is needed for the planning, the employer must ensure that it is provided.
items.statement: Where the qualified person determines that engineering expertise is needed for the planning, the employer must ensure that it is provided.

items.quote: The multiple-crane/derrick lift must be directed by a person who meets the criteria for both a competent person and a qualified person, or by a competent person who is assisted by one or more qualified persons (lift director).
items.statement: The multiple-crane/derrick lift must be directed by a lift director, who is either a person meeting the criteria for both a competent person and a qualified person, or a competent person assisted by one or more qualified persons.

items.quote: The lift director must review the plan in a meeting with all workers who will be involved with the operation.
items.statement: The lift director must review the plan in a meeting with all workers who will be involved with the multiple-crane/derrick operation.

items.quote: The following requirements apply to equipment that has a manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of more than 2,000 pounds.
items.statement: The requirements of §1926.1433 apply to equipment with a manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of more than 2,000 pounds.

items.quote: Crawler, truck and locomotive cranes manufactured prior to November 8, 2010 must meet the applicable requirements for design, construction, and testing as prescribed in ANSI B30.5-1968 (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6), PCSA Std. No. 2 (1968) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6), the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section, or the applicable DIN standards that were in effect at the time of manufacture.
items.statement: Crawler, truck and locomotive cranes manufactured before November 8, 2010 must meet the applicable design, construction and testing requirements of ANSI B30.5-1968, PCSA Std. No. 2 (1968), paragraph (b) of this section, or the applicable DIN standards in effect at the time of manufacture.

items.quote: Mobile (including crawler and truck) and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet the following portions of ASME B30.5-2004 (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) as applicable:
items.statement: Mobile (including crawler and truck) and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet the listed portions of ASME B30.5-2004 as applicable.

items.quote: In section 5-1.1.1 (“Load Ratings—Where Stability Governs Lifting Performance”), paragraphs (a)-(d) (including subparagraphs).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, paragraphs (a)-(d), including subparagraphs, of ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.1.1 (load ratings where stability governs lifting performance).

items.quote: In section 5-1.1.2 (“Load Ratings—Where Structural Competence Governs Lifting Performance”), paragraph (b).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, paragraph (b) of ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.1.2 (load ratings where structural competence governs lifting performance).

items.quote: Section 5-1.2 (“Stability (Backward and Forward)”).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.2 (backward and forward stability).

items.quote: In section 5-1.3.1 (“Boom Hoist Mechanism”), paragraphs (a), (b)(1) and (b)(2)
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, paragraphs (a), (b)(1) and (b)(2) of ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.3.1 (boom hoist mechanism), subject to an exception for rotation resistant rope.

items.quote: except that when using rotation resistant rope, § 1926.1414(c)(4)(ii)(A) applies.
items.statement: As an exception within the boom hoist mechanism requirements taken from ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.3.1, § 1926.1414(c)(4)(ii)(A) applies when rotation resistant rope is used.

items.quote: In section 5-1.3.2 (“Load Hoist Mechanism”), paragraphs (a)(2) through (a)(4) (including subparagraphs), (b) (including subparagraphs), (c) (first sentence only) and (d).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, these parts of ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.3.2 (load hoist mechanism): paragraphs (a)(2) through (a)(4) and (b), both including subparagraphs, the first sentence only of (c), and (d).

items.quote: Section 5-1.3.3 (“Telescoping Boom”).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.3.3 (telescoping boom).

items.quote: Section 5-1.4 (“Swing Mechanism”).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.4 (swing mechanism).

items.quote: In section 5-1.5 (“Crane Travel”), all provisions except 5-1.5.3(d).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, all provisions of ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.5 (crane travel) except 5-1.5.3(d).

items.quote: In section 5-1.6 (“Controls”), all provisions except 5-1.6.1 (c).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, all provisions of ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.6 (controls) except 5-1.6.1(c).

items.quote: Section 5-1.7.4 (“Sheaves”).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.7.4 (sheaves).

items.quote: Section 5-1.7.5 (“Sheave sizes”).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.7.5 (sheave sizes).

items.quote: In section 5-1.9.1 (“Booms”), paragraph (f).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, paragraph (f) of ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.9.1 (booms).

items.quote: Section 5-1.9.3 (“Outriggers”).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.9.3 (outriggers).

items.quote: Section 5-1.9.4 (“Locomotive Crane Equipment”).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.9.4 (locomotive crane equipment).

items.quote: Section 5-1.9.7 (“Clutch and Brake Protection”).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.9.7 (clutch and brake protection).

items.quote: In section 5-1.9.11 (“Miscellaneous equipment”), paragraphs (a), (c), (e), and (f).
items.statement: Mobile and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet, as applicable, paragraphs (a), (c), (e) and (f) of ASME B30.5-2004 section 5-1.9.11 (miscellaneous equipment).

items.quote: mobile (including crawler and truck) and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet the prototype testing requirements in Test Option A or Test Option B of this section.
items.statement: Mobile (including crawler and truck) and locomotive cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet the prototype testing requirements of either Test Option A or Test Option B.

items.quote: Tower cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet the prototype testing requirements in BS EN 14439:2006
items.statement: Tower cranes manufactured on or after November 8, 2010 must meet the prototype testing requirements in BS EN 14439:2006.

items.quote: Prototype testing of crawler, locomotive and truck cranes manufactured prior to November 8, 2010 must conform to paragraph (a) of this section.
items.statement: Prototype testing of crawler, locomotive and truck cranes manufactured before November 8, 2010 must conform to paragraph (a) of this section.

items.quote: The following applies to equipment with cantilevered booms (such as hydraulic boom cranes): All the tests listed in SAE J1063 (Nov. 1993) Table 1 (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) must be performed to load all critical structural elements to their respective limits.
items.statement: Under Test Option A, for equipment with cantilevered booms (such as hydraulic boom cranes), all tests in SAE J1063 (Nov. 1993) Table 1 must be performed to load all critical structural elements to their respective limits.

items.quote: All the strength margins listed in SAE J1063 (Nov. 1993) Table 2 (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) must be met.
items.statement: Under Test Option A, for equipment with cantilevered booms (such as hydraulic boom cranes), all strength margins in SAE J1063 (Nov. 1993) Table 2 must be met.

items.quote: The following applies to equipment with pendant supported lattice booms: All the tests listed in SAE J987 (Jun. 2003) Table 1 (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) must be performed to load all critical structural elements to their respective limits.
items.statement: Under Test Option A, for equipment with pendant supported lattice booms, all tests in SAE J987 (Jun. 2003) Table 1 must be performed to load all critical structural elements to their respective limits.

items.quote: All the strength margins listed in SAE J987 (Jun. 2003) Table 2 (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) must be met.
items.statement: Under Test Option A, for equipment with pendant supported lattice booms, all strength margins in SAE J987 (Jun. 2003) Table 2 must be met.

items.quote: Test Option B. The testing and verification requirements of BS EN 13000:2004 (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) must be met. In applying BS EN 13000:2004, the following additional requirements must be met:
items.statement: Under Test Option B, the testing and verification requirements of BS EN 13000:2004 must be met, along with the additional requirements this section specifies for applying that standard.

items.quote: The following applies to equipment with cantilevered booms (such as hydraulic boom cranes): The analysis methodology (computer modeling) must demonstrate that all load cases listed in SAE J1063 (Nov. 1993) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) meet the strength margins listed in SAE J1063 (Nov. 1993) Table 2.
items.statement: Under Test Option B, for equipment with cantilevered booms (such as hydraulic boom cranes), the analysis methodology (computer modeling) must demonstrate that all SAE J1063 (Nov. 1993) load cases meet the strength margins in SAE J1063 Table 2.

items.quote: The following applies to equipment with pendant supported lattice booms: The analysis methodology (computer modeling) must demonstrate that all load cases listed in SAE J987 (Jun. 2003) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) meet the strength margins listed in SAE J987 (Jun. 2003) Table 2.
items.statement: Under Test Option B, for equipment with pendant supported lattice booms, the analysis methodology (computer modeling) must demonstrate that all SAE J987 (Jun. 2003) load cases meet the strength margins in SAE J987 Table 2.

items.quote: The physical testing requirements under SAE J1063 (Nov. 1993) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) and SAE J987 (Jun. 2003) (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) must be met unless the reliability of the analysis methodology (computer modeling) has been demonstrated by a documented history of verification through strain gauge measuring or strain gauge measuring in combination with other physical testing.
items.statement: Under Test Option B, the physical testing requirements of SAE J1063 (Nov. 1993) and SAE J987 (Jun. 2003) must be met unless the reliability of the analysis methodology (computer modeling) has been demonstrated by a documented history of verification through strain gauge measuring, alone or combined with other physical testing.

items.quote: At all manufacturer approved operating radii, boom angles, work areas, boom lengths and configurations, jib lengths and angles (or offset).
items.statement: For all equipment covered by the subpart, the rated capacity information available in the cab must include at least the manufacturer's complete range of equipment rated capacities at all manufacturer-approved operating radii, boom angles, work areas, boom lengths and configurations, and jib lengths and angles (or offset).

items.quote: Alternate ratings for use and nonuse of option equipment which affects rated capacities, such as outriggers, stabilizers, and extra counterweights.
items.statement: The in-cab rated capacity information must include alternate ratings for use and nonuse of optional equipment that affects rated capacities, such as outriggers, stabilizers and extra counterweights.

items.quote: A work area chart for which capacities are listed in the load chart.
items.statement: The in-cab information must include a work area chart for which capacities are listed in the load chart.

items.quote: The work area figure and load chart must clearly indicate the areas where no load is to be handled.
items.statement: The work area figure and load chart must clearly indicate the areas where no load is to be handled.

items.quote: Recommended reeving for the hoist lines must be shown.
items.statement: The in-cab information must show the recommended reeving for the hoist lines.

items.quote: Recommended parts of hoist reeving, size, and type of wire rope for various equipment loads.
items.statement: The in-cab information must include the recommended parts of hoist reeving, and the size and type of wire rope, for various equipment loads.

items.quote: Recommended boom hoist reeving diagram, where applicable
items.statement: Where applicable, the in-cab information must include a recommended boom hoist reeving diagram.

items.quote: Recommended boom hoist reeving diagram, where applicable; size, type and length of wire rope.
items.statement: The in-cab information must include the size, type and length of wire rope, listed with the boom hoist reeving item.

items.quote: Tire pressure (where applicable).
items.statement: Where applicable, the in-cab information must include tire pressure.

items.quote: Caution or warnings relative to limitations on equipment and operating procedures
items.statement: The in-cab information must include cautions or warnings about limitations on equipment and operating procedures.

items.quote: including an indication of the least stable direction
items.statement: The in-cab cautions or warnings must include an indication of the least stable direction.

items.quote: Position of the gantry and requirements for intermediate boom suspension (where applicable).
items.statement: Where applicable, the in-cab information must include the position of the gantry.

items.quote: requirements for intermediate boom suspension (where applicable)
items.statement: Where applicable, the in-cab information must include the requirements for intermediate boom suspension.

items.quote: Instructions for boom erection
items.statement: The in-cab information must include instructions for boom erection.

items.quote: conditions under which the boom, or boom and jib combinations, may be raised or lowered
items.statement: The in-cab information must include the conditions under which the boom, or boom and jib combinations, may be raised or lowered.

items.quote: Whether the hoist holding mechanism is automatically or manually controlled, whether free fall is available, or any combination of these.
items.statement: The in-cab information must state whether the hoist holding mechanism is automatically or manually controlled, whether free fall is available, or any combination of these.

items.quote: The maximum telescopic travel length of each boom telescopic section.
items.statement: The in-cab information must include the maximum telescopic travel length of each boom telescopic section.

items.quote: Whether sections are telescoped manually or with power.
items.statement: The in-cab information must state whether boom sections are telescoped manually or with power.

items.quote: The sequence and procedure for extending and retracting the telescopic boom section.
items.statement: The in-cab information must include the sequence and procedure for extending and retracting the telescopic boom section.

items.quote: Maximum loads permitted during the boom extending operation
items.statement: The in-cab information must include the maximum loads permitted during the boom extending operation.

items.quote: Maximum loads permitted during the boom extending operation, and any limiting conditions or cautions.
items.statement: The in-cab information must include any limiting conditions or cautions for the boom extending operation.

items.quote: Hydraulic relief valve settings specified by the manufacturer.
items.statement: The in-cab information must include the hydraulic relief valve settings specified by the manufacturer.

items.quote: Load hooks (including latched and unlatched types), ball assemblies and load blocks must be of sufficient weight to overhaul the line from the highest hook position for boom or boom and jib lengths and the number of parts of the line in use.
items.statement: Load hooks (latched and unlatched), ball assemblies and load blocks must be heavy enough to overhaul the line from the highest hook position for the boom or boom and jib lengths and the number of parts of line in use.

items.quote: Hook and ball assemblies and load blocks must be marked with their rated capacity
items.statement: Hook and ball assemblies and load blocks must be marked with their rated capacity.

items.quote: Hook and ball assemblies and load blocks must be marked with their rated capacity and weight.
items.statement: Hook and ball assemblies and load blocks must be marked with their weight.

items.quote: Hooks must be equipped with latches, except where the requirements of paragraph (d)(4)(ii) of this section are met.
items.statement: Hooks must have latches, except where the requirements of paragraph (d)(4)(ii) are met.

items.quote: Hooks without latches, or with latches removed or disabled, must not be used unless:
items.statement: Hooks without latches, or with latches removed or disabled, must not be used unless a qualified person has determined it is safer to hoist and place the load that way and load routes are pre-planned so that no employee must work in the fall zone except those needed to hook or unhook the load.

items.quote: A qualified person has determined that it is safer to hoist and place the load without latches (or with the latches removed/tied-back).
items.statement: To use a hook without a latch or with its latch removed or disabled, a qualified person must have determined that it is safer to hoist and place the load without latches or with them removed or tied back.

items.quote: Routes for the loads are pre-planned to ensure that no employee is required to work in the fall zone except for employees necessary for the hooking or unhooking of the load.
items.statement: To use a hook without a latch or with its latch removed or disabled, load routes must be pre-planned so that no employee is required to work in the fall zone, except employees needed to hook or unhook the load.

items.quote: The latch must close the throat opening
items.statement: A hook latch must close the throat opening.

items.quote: be designed to retain slings or other lifting devices/accessories in the hook when the rigging apparatus is slack
items.statement: A hook latch must be designed to retain slings or other lifting devices or accessories in the hook when the rigging apparatus is slack.

items.quote: Posted warnings required by this subpart as well as those originally supplied with the equipment by the manufacturer must be maintained in legible condition.
items.statement: Posted warnings required by the subpart, and those originally supplied with the equipment by the manufacturer, must be kept legible.

items.quote: An accessible fire extinguisher must be on the equipment.
items.statement: An accessible fire extinguisher must be on the equipment.

items.quote: Cabs must be designed with a form of adjustable ventilation and method for clearing the windshield for maintaining visibility and air circulation.
items.statement: Equipment cabs must be designed with a form of adjustable ventilation for air circulation.

items.quote: method for clearing the windshield for maintaining visibility
items.statement: Equipment cabs must be designed with a method for clearing the windshield to maintain visibility.

items.quote: Examples of means for adjustable ventilation include air conditioner or window that can be opened (for ventilation and air circulation)
items.statement: Examples of adjustable cab ventilation include an air conditioner or a window that can be opened.

items.quote: examples of means for maintaining visibility include heater (for preventing windshield icing), defroster, fan, windshield wiper
items.statement: Examples of means for maintaining cab visibility include a heater (to prevent windshield icing), defroster, fan and windshield wiper.

items.quote: Cab doors (swinging, sliding) must be designed to prevent inadvertent opening or closing while traveling or operating the machine.
items.statement: Swinging and sliding cab doors must be designed to prevent inadvertent opening or closing while the machine is traveling or operating.

items.quote: Swinging doors adjacent to the operator must open outward.
items.statement: Swinging cab doors adjacent to the operator must open outward.

items.quote: Sliding operator doors must open rearward.
items.statement: Sliding operator doors must open rearward.

items.quote: The cab must have windows in front and on both sides of the operator.
items.statement: The cab must have windows in front of the operator and on both sides.

items.quote: Forward vertical visibility must be sufficient to give the operator a view of the boom point at all times.
items.statement: Forward vertical visibility from the cab must be enough for the operator to see the boom point at all times.

items.quote: Windows with sections designed to be opened must be designed so that they can be secured to prevent inadvertent closure.
items.statement: Cab windows with sections designed to be opened must be designed so those sections can be secured to prevent inadvertent closure.

items.quote: Windows must be of safety glass or material with similar optical and safety properties
items.statement: Cab windows must be safety glass or a material with similar optical and safety properties.

items.quote: that introduce no visible distortion or otherwise obscure visibility that interferes with the safe operation of the equipment
items.statement: Cab window material must introduce no visible distortion or otherwise obscure visibility in a way that interferes with safe operation of the equipment.

items.quote: A clear passageway must be provided from the operator's station to an exit door on the operator's side.
items.statement: A clear passageway must be provided from the operator's station to an exit door on the operator's side.

items.quote: Areas of the cab roof that serve as a workstation for rigging, maintenance or other equipment-related tasks must be capable of supporting 250 pounds without permanent distortion.
items.statement: Cab roof areas used as a workstation for rigging, maintenance or other equipment-related tasks must be able to support 250 pounds without permanent distortion.

items.quote: Belts, gears, shafts, pulleys, sprockets, spindles, drums, fly wheels, chains, and other parts or components that reciprocate, rotate or otherwise move must be guarded where contact by employees (except for maintenance and repair employees) is possible in the performance of normal duties.
items.statement: Belts, gears, shafts, pulleys, sprockets, spindles, drums, fly wheels, chains and other reciprocating, rotating or moving parts must be guarded where employees, other than maintenance and repair employees, could contact them while performing normal duties.

items.quote: All exhaust pipes, turbochargers, and charge air coolers must be insulated or guarded where contact by employees (except for maintenance and repair employees) is possible in the performance of normal duties.
items.statement: All exhaust pipes, turbochargers and charge air coolers must be insulated or guarded where employees, other than maintenance and repair employees, could contact them while performing normal duties.

items.quote: Hydraulic and pneumatic lines must be protected from damage to the extent feasible.
items.statement: Hydraulic and pneumatic lines must be protected from damage to the extent feasible.

items.quote: The equipment must be designed so that exhaust fumes are not discharged in the cab
items.statement: The equipment must be designed so that exhaust fumes are not discharged in the cab.

items.quote: are discharged in a direction away from the operator
items.statement: The equipment must be designed so that exhaust fumes are discharged in a direction away from the operator.

items.quote: Of a size and thermal capacity sufficient to control all rated loads with the minimum recommended reeving.
items.statement: Friction mechanisms, such as brakes and clutches, used to control the boom hoist or load line hoist must have enough size and thermal capacity to control all rated loads with the minimum recommended reeving.

items.quote: Adjustable to permit compensation for lining wear to maintain proper operation.
items.statement: Friction mechanisms used to control the boom hoist or load line hoist must be adjustable to compensate for lining wear and maintain proper operation.

items.quote: Hydraulic drums must have an integrally mounted holding device or internal static brake to prevent load hoist movement in the event of hydraulic failure.
items.statement: Hydraulic drums must have an integrally mounted holding device or internal static brake to prevent load hoist movement if the hydraulics fail.

items.quote: The employer's obligations under paragraphs (a) through (c) and (d)(7) through (13) of this section are met where the equipment has not changed (except in accordance with § 1926.1434 (Equipment modifications)) and it can refer to documentation from the manufacturer showing that the equipment has been designed, constructed and tested in accordance with those paragraphs.
items.statement: The employer's obligations under paragraphs (a) through (c) and (d)(7) through (13) are met where the equipment has not changed (except under § 1926.1434, Equipment modifications) and the employer can refer to manufacturer documentation showing it was designed, constructed and tested in accordance with those paragraphs.

items.quote: Modifications or additions which affect the capacity or safe operation of the equipment are prohibited except where the requirements of paragraphs (a)(1), (a)(2), (a)(3), (a)(4), or (a)(5) of this section are met.
items.statement: Modifications or additions that affect the equipment's capacity or safe operation are prohibited unless the requirements of paragraph (a)(1), (a)(2), (a)(3), (a)(4), or (a)(5) are met.

items.quote: The manufacturer approves the modifications/additions in writing.
items.statement: Under the manufacturer review and approval option, the manufacturer must approve the modifications or additions in writing.

items.quote: The load charts, procedures, instruction manuals and instruction plates/tags/decals are modified as necessary to accord with the modification/addition.
items.statement: Under the manufacturer review and approval option, load charts, procedures, instruction manuals and instruction plates/tags/decals must be modified as necessary to accord with the modification or addition.

items.quote: The original safety factor of the equipment is not reduced.
items.statement: Under the manufacturer review and approval option, the equipment's original safety factor must not be reduced.

items.quote: The manufacturer is provided a detailed description of the proposed modification/addition, is asked to approve the modification/addition, but it declines to review the technical merits of the proposal or fails, within 30 days, to acknowledge the request or initiate the review, and all of the following are met:
items.statement: The manufacturer refusal option applies when the manufacturer, given a detailed description of the proposed modification or addition and asked to approve it, declines to review the proposal's technical merits, and all of the (a)(2) conditions must then be met.

items.quote: fails, within 30 days, to acknowledge the request or initiate the review
items.statement: The manufacturer refusal option also applies when the manufacturer, given a detailed description and asked to approve the proposal, fails within 30 days to acknowledge the request or initiate the review, and all of the (a)(2) conditions must then be met.

items.quote:
(i) A registered professional engineer who is a qualified person with respect to the equipment involved:
[29cfr1926.1434(a)(2)(i)(A)] (A) Approves the modification/addition
items.statement: Under the manufacturer refusal option, a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person with respect to the equipment involved must approve the modification or addition.

items.quote: specifies the equipment configurations to which that approval applies
items.statement: Under the manufacturer refusal option, the qualified registered professional engineer must specify the equipment configurations to which the approval applies.

items.quote: Modifies load charts, procedures, instruction manuals and instruction plates/tags/decals as necessary to accord with the modification/addition.
items.statement: Under the manufacturer refusal option, the qualified registered professional engineer must modify load charts, procedures, instruction manuals and instruction plates/tags/decals as necessary to accord with the modification or addition.

items.quote: The original safety factor of the equipment is not reduced.
items.statement: Under the manufacturer refusal option, the equipment's original safety factor must not be reduced.

items.quote: The manufacturer is unavailable and the requirements of paragraphs (a)(2)(i) and (ii) of this section are met.
items.statement: The unavailable manufacturer option requires that the manufacturer be unavailable and that the requirements of paragraphs (a)(2)(i) and (ii) be met.

items.quote: agrees to review the technical merits of the proposal, but fails to complete the review of the proposal within 120 days of the date it was provided the detailed description of the proposed modification/addition, and the requirements of paragraphs (a)(2)(i) and (ii) of this section are met.
items.statement: A modification may proceed under (a)(4) when the manufacturer, given a detailed description and asked to approve it, agrees to review its technical merits but fails to complete the review within 120 days of the date it was provided the description, and the requirements of (a)(2)(i) and (ii) are met.

items.quote: The equipment is designed for marine work sites, contains major structural components from more than one manufacturer, and the requirements of paragraphs (a)(2)(i) and (ii) of this section are met.
items.statement: The multiple-manufacturer option applies to equipment designed for marine work sites that contains major structural components from more than one manufacturer, provided the requirements of paragraphs (a)(2)(i) and (ii) are met.

items.quote: Modifications or additions which affect the capacity or safe operation of the equipment are prohibited where the manufacturer, after a review of the technical safety merits of the proposed modification/addition, rejects the proposal and explains the reasons for the rejection in a written response.
items.statement: Modifications or additions affecting capacity or safe operation are prohibited where the manufacturer, after reviewing the technical safety merits, rejects the proposal and explains the reasons in a written response.

items.quote: If the manufacturer rejects the proposal but does not explain the reasons for the rejection in writing, the employer may treat this as a manufacturer refusal to review the request under paragraph (a)(2) of this section.
items.statement: If the manufacturer rejects the proposal but does not explain the reasons in writing, the employer may treat this as a manufacturer refusal to review the request under paragraph (a)(2).

items.quote: The provisions in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section do not apply to modifications made or approved by the U.S. military.
items.statement: Paragraphs (a) and (b) do not apply to modifications made or approved by the U.S. military.

items.quote: This section contains supplemental requirements for tower cranes; all sections of this subpart apply to tower cranes unless specified otherwise.
items.statement: Section 1926.1435 contains supplemental requirements for tower cranes, and all sections of the subpart apply to tower cranes unless specified otherwise.

items.quote: apply to tower cranes (except as otherwise specified)
items.statement: Sections 1926.1403, 1926.1404, 1926.1405 and 1926.1406 on assembly/disassembly apply to tower cranes, except as otherwise specified and with the stated term replacements.

items.quote: the term “assembly/disassembly” is replaced by “erecting, climbing and dismantling,”
items.statement: When §§ 1926.1403 through 1926.1406 are applied to tower cranes, the term “assembly/disassembly” is replaced by “erecting, climbing and dismantling.”

items.quote: the term “disassembly” is replaced by “dismantling.”
items.statement: When §§ 1926.1403 through 1926.1406 are applied to tower cranes, the term “disassembly” is replaced by “dismantling.”

items.quote: Employees must not be in or under the tower, jib, or rotating portion of the crane during erecting, climbing and dismantling operations until the crane is secured in a locked position and the competent person in charge indicates it is safe to enter this area, unless the manufacturer's instructions direct otherwise and only the necessary personnel are permitted in this area.
items.statement: In addition to § 1926.1404(e), employees must not be in or under the tower, jib or rotating portion of a self-erecting tower crane during erecting, climbing and dismantling until the crane is secured in a locked position and the competent person in charge indicates it is safe to enter, unless the manufacturer's instructions direct otherwise and only the necessary personnel are permitted in the area.

items.quote: Tower crane foundations and structural supports (including both the portions of the structure used for support and the means of attachment) must be designed by the manufacturer or a registered professional engineer.
items.statement: Tower crane foundations and structural supports, including the portions of the structure used for support and the means of attachment, must be designed by the manufacturer or a registered professional engineer.

items.quote: The requirements in § 1926.1404(h)(1) through (9) apply.
items.statement: The requirements in § 1926.1404(h)(1) through (9) on addressing specific hazards apply to tower cranes.

items.quote: The A/D director must determine that tower crane foundations and structural supports are installed in accordance with their design.
items.statement: The A/D director must determine that tower crane foundations and structural supports are installed in accordance with their design.

items.quote: Backward stability before swinging self erecting cranes or cranes on traveling or static undercarriages.
items.statement: The A/D director must address backward stability before swinging self-erecting cranes or cranes on traveling or static undercarriages.

items.quote: Wind must not exceed the speed recommended by the manufacturer or, where manufacturer does not specify this information, the speed determined by a qualified person.
items.statement: As a hazard the A/D director must address, wind must not exceed the speed recommended by the manufacturer or, where the manufacturer does not specify it, the speed determined by a qualified person.

items.quote: Towers must be erected plumb to the manufacturer's tolerance
items.statement: Towers must be erected plumb to the manufacturer's tolerance.

items.quote: Towers must be erected plumb to the manufacturer's tolerance and verified by a qualified person.
items.statement: A qualified person must verify that towers are erected plumb to tolerance.

items.quote: Where the manufacturer does not specify plumb tolerance, the crane tower must be plumb to a tolerance of at least 1:500 (approximately 1 inch in 40 feet).
items.statement: Where the manufacturer does not specify a plumb tolerance, the crane tower must be plumb to a tolerance of at least 1:500 (approximately 1 inch in 40 feet).

items.quote: On jobsites where more than one fixed jib (hammerhead) tower crane is installed, the cranes must be located such that no crane can come in contact with the structure of another crane.
items.statement: On jobsites with more than one fixed jib (hammerhead) tower crane, the cranes must be located so that no crane can contact the structure of another crane.

items.quote: Cranes are permitted to pass over one another.
items.statement: On multiple tower crane jobsites, cranes are permitted to pass over one another.

items.quote:
Prior to, and during, all climbing procedures (including inside climbing and top climbing), the employer must:
[29cfr1926.1435(b)(7)(i)] (i) Comply with all manufacturer prohibitions.
items.statement: Before and during all climbing procedures, including inside climbing and top climbing, the employer must comply with all manufacturer prohibitions.

items.quote: Have a registered professional engineer verify that the host structure is strong enough to sustain the forces imposed through the braces, brace anchorages and supporting floors.
items.statement: Before and during all climbing procedures, the employer must have a registered professional engineer verify that the host structure is strong enough to sustain the forces imposed through the braces, brace anchorages and supporting floors.

items.quote: Equipment must not be erected, dismantled or operated without the amount and position of counterweight and/or ballast in place as specified by the manufacturer or a registered professional engineer familiar with the equipment.
items.statement: Equipment must not be erected, dismantled or operated without the amount and position of counterweight and/or ballast in place as specified by the manufacturer or a registered professional engineer familiar with the equipment.

items.quote: The maximum counterweight and/or ballast specified by the manufacturer or registered professional engineer familiar with the equipment must not be exceeded.
items.statement: The maximum counterweight and/or ballast specified by the manufacturer or a registered professional engineer familiar with the equipment must not be exceeded.

items.quote: The size and location of signs installed on tower cranes must be in accordance with manufacturer specifications.
items.statement: The size and location of signs installed on tower cranes must be in accordance with manufacturer specifications.

items.quote: Where these are unavailable, a registered professional engineer familiar with the type of equipment involved must approve in writing the size and location of any signs.
items.statement: Where manufacturer sign specifications are unavailable, a registered professional engineer familiar with the type of equipment must approve in writing the size and location of any signs.

items.quote: Section 1926.1415 does not apply to tower cranes.
items.statement: Section 1926.1415 does not apply to tower cranes.

items.quote: Boom stops on luffing boom type tower cranes.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, luffing boom type tower cranes are required to have boom stops.

items.quote: Jib stops on luffing boom type tower cranes if equipped with a jib attachment.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, luffing boom type tower cranes equipped with a jib attachment are required to have jib stops.

items.quote: Travel rail end stops at both ends of travel rail.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes are required to have travel rail end stops at both ends of the travel rail.

items.quote: Travel rail clamps on all travel bogies.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes are required to have travel rail clamps on all travel bogies.

items.quote: Integrally mounted check valves on all load supporting hydraulic cylinders.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes are required to have integrally mounted check valves on all load supporting hydraulic cylinders.

items.quote: Hydraulic system pressure limiting device.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes are required to have a hydraulic system pressure limiting device.

items.quote:
The following brakes, which must automatically set in the event of pressure loss or power failure, are required:
[29cfr1926.1435(d)(2)(vii)(A)] (A) A hoist brake on all hoists.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes must have a hoist brake on all hoists that automatically sets in the event of pressure loss or power failure.

items.quote: Swing brake.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes must have a swing brake that automatically sets in the event of pressure loss or power failure.

items.quote: Trolley brake.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes must have a trolley brake that automatically sets in the event of pressure loss or power failure.

items.quote: Rail travel brake.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes must have a rail travel brake that automatically sets in the event of pressure loss or power failure.

items.quote: Deadman control or forced neutral return control (hand) levers.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes are required to have deadman control or forced neutral return control (hand) levers.

items.quote: Emergency stop switch at the operator's station.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes are required to have an emergency stop switch at the operator's station.

items.quote: Trolley end stops must be provided at both ends of travel of the trolley.
items.statement: Unless otherwise specified, tower cranes must have trolley end stops at both ends of travel of the trolley.

items.quote: Operations must not begin unless the devices listed in this section are in proper working order.
items.statement: Operations must not begin unless the safety devices listed in this section are in proper working order.

items.quote: If a device stops working properly during operations, the operator must safely stop operations.
items.statement: If a listed safety device stops working properly during operations, the operator must safely stop operations.

items.quote: The equipment must be taken out of service
items.statement: If a listed safety device stops working properly during operations, the equipment must be taken out of service.

items.quote: operations must not resume until the device is again working properly.
items.statement: After a safety device stops working properly, operations must not resume until the device is again working properly.

items.quote: Alternative measures are not permitted to be used.
items.statement: Alternative measures are not permitted in place of a safety device that is not working properly.

items.quote: Section 1926.1416 does not apply to tower cranes.
items.statement: As an exclusion, §1926.1416 does not apply to tower cranes.

items.quote: The devices listed in this section (“operational aids”) are required on all tower cranes covered by this subpart, unless otherwise specified.
items.statement: The operational aids listed in this section are required on all tower cranes covered by this subpart, unless otherwise specified.

items.quote: Operations must not begin unless the operational aids are in proper working order, except where the employer meets the specified temporary alternative measures.
items.statement: Operations must not begin unless the operational aids are in proper working order, except where the employer meets the specified temporary alternative measures.

items.quote: More protective alternative measures specified by the tower crane manufacturer, if any, must be followed.
items.statement: Any more protective alternative measures specified by the tower crane manufacturer must be followed.

items.quote: If an operational aid stops working properly during operations, the operator must safely stop operations until the temporary alternative measures are implemented or the device is again working properly.
items.statement: If an operational aid stops working properly during operations, the operator must safely stop operations until the temporary alternative measures are implemented or the device is again working properly.

items.quote: If a replacement part is no longer available, the use of a substitute device that performs the same type of function is permitted and is not considered a modification under § 1926.1434.
items.statement: If a replacement part for an operational aid is no longer available, a substitute device that performs the same type of function is permitted and is not considered a modification under §1926.1434.

items.quote: must be repaired no later than 7 calendar days after the deficiency occurs
items.statement: A Category I operational aid that is not working properly must be repaired no later than 7 calendar days after the deficiency occurs, unless the parts-ordering exception applies.

items.quote: Exception: If the employer documents that it has ordered the necessary parts within 7 calendar days of the occurrence of the deficiency, the repair must be completed within 7 calendar days of receipt of the parts.
items.statement: As an exception for Category I aids, if the employer documents that it ordered the necessary parts within 7 calendar days of the deficiency occurring, the repair must be completed within 7 calendar days of receiving the parts.

items.quote: The travel of the trolley must be restricted at both ends of the jib by a trolley travel limiting device to prevent the trolley from running into the trolley end stops.
items.statement: A trolley travel limiting device must restrict trolley travel at both ends of the jib to prevent the trolley from running into the trolley end stops.

items.quote: The trolley rope must be marked (so it can be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the trolley prior to the end stops.
items.statement: Under temporary alternative Option A for the trolley travel limiting device, the trolley rope must be marked, visibly to the operator, at a point giving the operator sufficient time to stop the trolley before the end stops.

items.quote: A spotter who is in direct communication with the operator must be used when operations are conducted within 10 feet of the outer or inner trolley end stops.
items.statement: Under temporary alternative Option B for the trolley travel limiting device, a spotter in direct communication with the operator must be used when operating within 10 feet of the outer or inner trolley end stops.

items.quote: The range of the boom must be limited at the minimum and maximum radius.
items.statement: The range of the boom must be limited at both the minimum and maximum radius by a boom hoist limiting device.

items.quote: Clearly mark the cable (so it can be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the boom hoist within the minimum and maximum boom radius, or use a spotter who is in direct communication with the operator to inform the operator when this point is reached.
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for the boom hoist limiting device, either clearly mark the cable, visibly to the operator, at a point giving sufficient time to stop the boom hoist within the minimum and maximum boom radius, or use a spotter in direct communication with the operator to say when this point is reached.

items.quote: The tower crane must be equipped with a device which automatically prevents damage from contact between the load block, overhaul ball, or similar component, and the boom tip (or fixed upper block or similar component).
items.statement: A tower crane must have an anti two-blocking device that automatically prevents damage from contact between the load block, overhaul ball or similar component and the boom tip, fixed upper block or similar component.

items.quote: The device(s) must prevent such damage at all points where two-blocking could occur.
items.statement: The anti two-blocking device or devices must prevent damage at all points where two-blocking could occur.

items.quote: Clearly mark the cable (so it can be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, or use a spotter who is in direct communication with the operator to inform the operator when this point is reached.
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for the anti two-blocking device, either clearly mark the cable, visibly to the operator, at a point giving sufficient time to stop the hoist to prevent two-blocking, or use a spotter in direct communication with the operator to say when this point is reached.

items.quote: Tower cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must be equipped with a device that prevents the last 2 wraps of hoist cable from being spooled off the drum.
items.statement: Tower cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must have a hoist drum lower limiting device that prevents the last 2 wraps of hoist cable from being spooled off the drum.

items.quote: Mark the cable (so it can be seen by the operator) at a point that will give the operator sufficient time to stop the hoist prior to last 2 wraps of hoist cable being spooled off the drum, or use a spotter who is in direct communication with the operator to inform the operator when this point is reached
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for the hoist drum lower limiting device, either mark the cable, visibly to the operator, at a point giving sufficient time to stop the hoist before the last 2 wraps spool off the drum, or use a spotter in direct communication with the operator to say when this point is reached.

items.quote: The tower crane must have a device that prevents moment overloading.
items.statement: A tower crane must have a load moment limiting device that prevents moment overloading.

items.quote: A radius indicating device must be used (if the tower crane is not equipped with a radius indicating device, the radius must be measured to ensure the load is within the rated capacity of the crane).
items.statement: As a temporary alternative for the load moment limiting device, a radius indicating device must be used, or if the crane has none, the radius must be measured to ensure the load is within the crane's rated capacity.

items.quote: In addition, the weight of the load must be determined from a source recognized by the industry (such as the load's manufacturer), or by a calculation method recognized by the industry (such as calculating a steel beam from measured dimensions and a known per foot weight), or by other equally reliable means.
items.statement: As a temporary alternative for the load moment limiting device, the load weight must also be determined from an industry-recognized source, by an industry-recognized calculation method, or by other equally reliable means.

items.quote: This information must be provided to the operator prior to the lift.
items.statement: Under the load moment limiting device temporary alternative, this load weight information must be provided to the operator before the lift.

items.quote: The capacity of the hoist must be limited to prevent overloading, including each individual gear ratio if equipped with a multiple speed hoist transmission.
items.statement: A hoist line pull limiting device must limit hoist capacity to prevent overloading, including for each individual gear ratio on a multiple speed hoist transmission.

items.quote: The operator must ensure that the weight of the load does not exceed the capacity of the hoist (including for each individual gear ratio if equipped with a multiple speed hoist transmission).
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for the hoist line pull limiting device, the operator must ensure the load weight does not exceed hoist capacity, including for each individual gear ratio on a multiple speed hoist transmission.

items.quote: The travel distance in each direction must be limited to prevent the travel bogies from running into the end stops or buffers.
items.statement: A rail travel limiting device must limit travel distance in each direction to prevent the travel bogies from running into the end stops or buffers.

items.quote: A spotter who is in direct communication with the operator must be used when operations are conducted within 10 feet of either end of the travel rail end stops
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for the rail travel limiting device, a spotter in direct communication with the operator must be used when operating within 10 feet of either end of the travel rail end stops.

items.quote: the spotter must inform the operator of the distance of the travel bogies from the end stops or buffers.
items.statement: The spotter used as the rail travel limiting alternative must inform the operator of the distance of the travel bogies from the end stops or buffers.

items.quote: The boom hoist drum must be equipped with a control that will enable the operator to positively lock the boom hoist drum from the cab.
items.statement: The boom hoist drum must have a control that enables the operator to positively lock the drum from the cab.

items.quote: The device must be manually set when required if an electric, hydraulic or automatic control is not functioning.
items.statement: As the temporary alternative, if an electric, hydraulic or automatic boom hoist drum locking control is not functioning, the device must be manually set when required.

items.quote: must be repaired no later than 30 calendar days after the deficiency occurs
items.statement: A Category II operational aid that is not working properly must be repaired no later than 30 calendar days after the deficiency occurs, unless the parts-ordering exception applies.

items.quote: Exception: If the employer documents that it has ordered the necessary parts within 7 calendar days of the occurrence of the deficiency, and the part is not received in time to complete the repair in 30 calendar days, the repair must be completed within 7 calendar days of receipt of the parts.
items.statement: As an exception for Category II aids, if the employer documents that it ordered the necessary parts within 7 calendar days of the deficiency and the part does not arrive in time to repair within 30 calendar days, the repair must be completed within 7 calendar days of receiving the parts.

items.quote: Luffing boom tower cranes must have a boom angle indicator readable from the operator's station.
items.statement: Luffing boom tower cranes must have a boom angle indicator readable from the operator's station.

items.quote: Hammerhead tower cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must have a hook radius indicator readable from the operator's station.
items.statement: Hammerhead tower cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must have a hook radius indicator readable from the operator's station.

items.quote: Hook radii or boom angle must be determined by measuring the hook radii or boom angle with a measuring device.
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for the boom angle or hook radius indicator, hook radii or boom angle must be determined by measuring them with a measuring device.

items.quote: The trolley speed must be automatically reduced prior to the trolley reaching the end limit in both directions.
items.statement: A trolley travel deceleration device must automatically reduce trolley speed before the trolley reaches the end limit in both directions.

items.quote: The employer must post a notice in the cab of the crane notifying the operator that the trolley travel deceleration device is malfunctioning and instructing the operator to take special care to reduce the trolley speed when approaching the trolley end limits.
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for a malfunctioning trolley travel deceleration device, the employer must post a cab notice telling the operator of the malfunction and to take special care to reduce trolley speed when approaching the trolley end limits.

items.quote: The boom speed must be automatically reduced prior to the boom reaching the minimum or maximum radius limit.
items.statement: A boom hoist deceleration device must automatically reduce boom speed before the boom reaches the minimum or maximum radius limit.

items.quote: The employer must post a notice in the cab of the crane notifying the operator that the boom hoist deceleration device is malfunctioning and instructing the operator to take special care to reduce the boom speed when approaching the minimum or maximum radius limits.
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for a malfunctioning boom hoist deceleration device, the employer must post a cab notice telling the operator of the malfunction and to take special care to reduce boom speed when approaching the minimum or maximum radius limits.

items.quote: The load speed must be automatically reduced prior to the hoist reaching the upper limit.
items.statement: A load hoist deceleration device must automatically reduce load speed before the hoist reaches the upper limit.

items.quote: The employer must post a notice in the cab of the crane notifying the operator that the load hoist deceleration device is malfunctioning and instructing the operator to take special care to reduce the load speed when approaching the upper limits.
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for a malfunctioning load hoist deceleration device, the employer must post a cab notice telling the operator of the malfunction and to take special care to reduce load speed when approaching the upper limits.

items.quote: A device must be provided to display the wind speed
items.statement: A wind speed indicating device must be provided to display the wind speed.

items.quote: must be mounted above the upper rotating structure on tower cranes
items.statement: On tower cranes, the wind speed indicator must be mounted above the upper rotating structure, while self erecting cranes have their own mounting location.

items.quote: On self erecting cranes, it must be mounted at or above the jib level.
items.statement: On self erecting cranes, the wind speed indicator must be mounted at or above the jib level.

items.quote: Temporary alternative measures: Use of wind speed information from a properly functioning indicating device on another tower crane on the same site, or a qualified person estimates the wind speed.
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for the wind speed indicator, use wind speed information from a properly functioning indicator on another tower crane on the same site, or have a qualified person estimate the wind speed.

items.quote: Cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must have a device that displays the magnitude of the load on the hook.
items.statement: Cranes manufactured after November 8, 2011 must have a load indicating device that displays the magnitude of the load on the hook.

items.quote: Displays that are part of load moment limiting devices that display the load on the hook meet this requirement.
items.statement: Displays that are part of load moment limiting devices and display the load on the hook meet the load indicating device requirement.

items.quote: The weight of the load must be determined from a source recognized by the industry (such as the load's manufacturer), or by a calculation method recognized by the industry (such as calculating a steel beam from measured dimensions and a known per foot weight), or by other equally reliable means.
items.statement: As the temporary alternative for the load indicating device, the load weight must be determined from an industry-recognized source, by an industry-recognized calculation method, or by other equally reliable means.

items.quote: This information must be provided to the operator prior to the lift.
items.statement: Under the load indicating device temporary alternative, the load weight information must be provided to the operator before the lift.

items.quote: Section 1926.1412 (Inspections) applies to tower cranes, except that the term “assembly” is replaced by “erection.”
items.statement: Section 1926.1412 (Inspections) applies to tower cranes, except that the term "assembly" is replaced by "erection."

items.quote: Section 1926.1413 (Wire rope—inspection) applies to tower cranes.
items.statement: Section 1926.1413 (Wire rope—inspection) applies to tower cranes.

items.quote: Before each crane component is erected, it must be inspected by a qualified person for damage or excessive wear.
items.statement: Before each tower crane component is erected, a qualified person must inspect it for damage or excessive wear.

items.quote: The qualified person must pay particular attention to components that will be difficult to inspect thoroughly during shift inspections.
items.statement: In the pre-erection inspection, the qualified person must pay particular attention to components that will be difficult to inspect thoroughly during shift inspections.

items.quote: that component must not be erected on the crane unless it is repaired and, upon reinspection by the qualified person, found to no longer create a safety hazard.
items.statement: If the qualified person determines that a component is damaged or worn enough to create a safety hazard if used on the crane, it must not be erected on the crane unless it is repaired and, upon reinspection by the qualified person, found to no longer create a safety hazard.

items.quote: If the qualified person determines that, though not presently a safety hazard, the component needs to be monitored, the employer must ensure that the component is checked in the monthly inspections.
items.statement: If the qualified person determines that a component is not presently a safety hazard but needs monitoring, the employer must ensure it is checked in the monthly inspections.

items.quote: Any such determination must be documented
items.statement: Any determination by the qualified person that a component not presently a safety hazard needs monitoring must be documented.

items.quote: the documentation must be available to any individual who conducts a monthly inspection.
items.statement: The documentation of a determination that a component needs monitoring must be available to any individual who conducts a monthly inspection.

items.quote: In addition to the requirements in § 1926.1412(c), the following requirements must be met:
items.statement: For the tower crane post-erection inspection, the requirements of § 1926.1435(f)(3) must be met in addition to those in § 1926.1412(c).

items.quote: A load test using certified weights, or scaled weights using a certified scale with a current certificate of calibration, must be conducted after each erection.
items.statement: A load test must be conducted after each erection of a tower crane, using certified weights or scaled weights from a certified scale with a current certificate of calibration.

items.quote: The load test must be conducted in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions when available.
items.statement: The post-erection load test must be conducted according to the manufacturer's instructions when they are available.

items.quote: Where these instructions are unavailable, the test must be conducted in accordance with written load test procedures developed by a registered professional engineer familiar with the type of equipment involved.
items.statement: When the manufacturer's instructions are unavailable, the load test must follow written load test procedures developed by a registered professional engineer familiar with the type of equipment involved.

items.quote: Tower (mast) bolts and other structural bolts (for loose or dislodged condition) from the base of the tower crane up or, if the crane is tied to or braced by the structure, those above the upper-most brace support.
items.statement: Monthly tower crane inspections must additionally check tower (mast) bolts and other structural bolts for loose or dislodged condition, from the crane base up or, if the crane is tied to or braced by the structure, those above the upper-most brace support.

items.quote: The upper-most tie-in, braces, floor supports and floor wedges where the tower crane is supported by the structure, for loose or dislodged components.
items.statement: Where the structure supports the tower crane, monthly inspections must additionally check the upper-most tie-in, braces, floor supports and floor wedges for loose or dislodged components.

items.quote: In addition to the items that must be inspected under § 1926.1412(f), all turntable and tower bolts must be inspected for proper condition and torque.
items.statement: In annual tower crane inspections, in addition to the items required under § 1926.1412(f), all turntable and tower bolts must be inspected for proper condition and torque.

items.quote: This section contains supplemental requirements for derricks, whether temporarily or permanently mounted; all sections of this subpart apply to derricks unless specified otherwise.
items.statement: Section 1926.1436 contains supplemental requirements for derricks, whether temporarily or permanently mounted, and all sections of the subpart apply to derricks unless specified otherwise.

items.quote: A derrick is powered equipment consisting of a mast or equivalent member that is held at or near the end by guys or braces, with or without a boom, and its hoisting mechanism.
items.statement: A derrick is powered equipment consisting of a mast or equivalent member held at or near the end by guys or braces, with or without a boom, and its hoisting mechanism.

items.quote: The mast/equivalent member and/or the load is moved by the hoisting mechanism (typically base-mounted) and operating ropes.
items.statement: In a derrick, the mast or equivalent member and/or the load is moved by the hoisting mechanism (typically base-mounted) and operating ropes.

items.quote: Derricks include: A-frame, basket, breast, Chicago boom, gin pole (except gin poles used for erection of communication towers), guy, shearleg, stiffleg, and variations of such equipment.
items.statement: Derricks include A-frame, basket, breast, Chicago boom, gin pole (except gin poles used to erect communication towers), guy, shearleg and stiffleg derricks, and variations of such equipment.

items.quote: Section 1926.1417 (Operation) applies except for § 1926.1417(c) (Accessibility of procedures).
