items.statement: Section 1926.1417 (Operation) applies to derricks, except for § 1926.1417(c) (Accessibility of procedures).

items.quote: Rated capacity at corresponding ranges of boom angle or operating radii.
items.statement: Derrick load charts must contain at least the rated capacity at corresponding ranges of boom angle or operating radii.

items.quote: Specific lengths of components to which the rated capacities apply.
items.statement: Derrick load charts must contain at least the specific lengths of components to which the rated capacities apply.

items.quote: Required parts for hoist reeving.
items.statement: Derrick load charts must contain at least the required parts for hoist reeving.

items.quote: Size and construction of rope must be included on the load chart or in the operating manual.
items.statement: The size and construction of rope must be included on the derrick load chart or in the operating manual.

items.quote: For permanently installed derricks with fixed lengths of boom, guy, and mast, a load chart must be posted where it is visible to personnel responsible for the operation of the equipment.
items.statement: For permanently installed derricks with fixed lengths of boom, guy and mast, a load chart must be posted where it is visible to personnel responsible for operating the equipment.

items.quote: For derricks that are not permanently installed, the load chart must be readily available at the job site to personnel responsible for the operation of the equipment.
items.statement: For derricks that are not permanently installed, the load chart must be readily available at the job site to personnel responsible for operating the equipment.

items.quote: Derricks must be constructed to meet all stresses imposed on members and components when installed and operated in accordance with the manufacturer's/builder's procedures and within its rated capacity.
items.statement: Derricks must be constructed to meet all stresses imposed on members and components when installed and operated according to the manufacturer's/builder's procedures and within rated capacity.

items.quote: Welding of load sustaining members must conform to recommended practices in ANSI/AWS D14.3-94 (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) or AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2002
items.statement: Welding of derrick load sustaining members must conform to recommended practices in ANSI/AWS D14.3-94 or AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2002.

items.quote: The minimum number of guys must be 6, with equal spacing, except where a qualified person or derrick manufacturer approves variations from these requirements and revises the rated capacity to compensate for such variations.
items.statement: A guy derrick must have at least 6 guys, except where a qualified person or derrick manufacturer approves a variation and revises the rated capacity to compensate.

items.quote: with equal spacing, except where a qualified person or derrick manufacturer approves variations from these requirements and revises the rated capacity to compensate for such variations.
items.statement: Guy derrick guys must be equally spaced, except where a qualified person or derrick manufacturer approves a variation and revises the rated capacity to compensate.

items.quote: Guy derricks must not be used unless the employer has the following guy information from the manufacturer or a qualified person, when not available from the manufacturer:
items.statement: Guy derricks must not be used unless the employer has the required guy information from the manufacturer, or from a qualified person when it is not available from the manufacturer.

items.quote: The number of guys.
items.statement: Before a guy derrick is used, the employer must have information on the number of guys, from the manufacturer or, if unavailable from the manufacturer, a qualified person.

items.quote: The spacing around the mast.
items.statement: Before a guy derrick is used, the employer must have information on the guy spacing around the mast, from the manufacturer or, if unavailable from the manufacturer, a qualified person.

items.quote: The size, grade, and construction of rope to be used for each guy.
items.statement: Before a guy derrick is used, the employer must have the size, grade and construction of rope to be used for each guy, from the manufacturer or, if unavailable from the manufacturer, a qualified person.

items.quote: The amount of initial sag or tension.
items.statement: For guy derricks manufactured after December 18, 1970, in addition to the (c)(2)(ii) information, the employer must have the amount of initial sag or tension, from the manufacturer or, if unavailable from the manufacturer, a qualified person.

items.quote: The amount of tension in guy line rope at anchor.
items.statement: For guy derricks manufactured after December 18, 1970, in addition to the (c)(2)(ii) information, the employer must have the amount of tension in the guy line rope at the anchor, from the manufacturer or, if unavailable from the manufacturer, a qualified person.

items.quote: The mast base must permit the mast to rotate freely with allowance for slight tilting of the mast caused by guy slack.
items.statement: A guy derrick mast base must permit the mast to rotate freely, with allowance for slight tilting of the mast caused by guy slack.

items.quote: Permit the mast to rotate freely.
items.statement: A guy derrick mast cap must permit the mast to rotate freely.

items.quote: Withstand tilting and cramping caused by the guy loads.
items.statement: A guy derrick mast cap must withstand tilting and cramping caused by the guy loads.

items.quote: Be secured to the mast to prevent disengagement during erection.
items.statement: A guy derrick mast cap must be secured to the mast to prevent disengagement during erection.

items.quote: Be provided with means for attaching guy ropes.
items.statement: A guy derrick mast cap must be provided with means for attaching guy ropes.

items.quote: The mast must be supported in the vertical position by at least two stifflegs
items.statement: A stiffleg derrick mast must be supported vertically by at least two stifflegs.

items.quote: one end of each must be connected to the top of the mast and the other end securely anchored.
items.statement: Each stiffleg must have one end connected to the top of the mast and the other end securely anchored.

items.quote: The stifflegs must be capable of withstanding the loads imposed at any point of operation within the load chart range.
items.statement: Stifflegs must be capable of withstanding the loads imposed at any point of operation within the load chart range.

items.quote: Permit the mast to rotate freely (when necessary).
items.statement: A stiffleg derrick mast base must permit the mast to rotate freely (when necessary).

items.quote: Permit deflection of the mast without binding.
items.statement: A stiffleg derrick mast base must permit the mast to deflect without binding.

items.quote: The mast must be prevented from lifting out of its socket when the mast is in tension.
items.statement: A stiffleg derrick mast must be prevented from lifting out of its socket when the mast is in tension.

items.quote: Permit the mast to rotate freely (when necessary).
items.statement: The stiffleg connecting member at the top of the mast must permit the mast to rotate freely (when necessary).

items.quote: Withstand the loads imposed by the action of the stifflegs.
items.statement: The stiffleg connecting member at the top of the mast must withstand the loads imposed by the action of the stifflegs.

items.quote: Be secured so as to oppose separating forces.
items.statement: The stiffleg connecting member at the top of the mast must be secured so as to oppose separating forces.

items.quote: Guy lines must be sized and spaced so as to make the gin pole stable in both boomed and vertical positions.
items.statement: Gin pole guy lines must be sized and spaced to make the gin pole stable in both boomed and vertical positions, subject to the exception for configurations that do not achieve this.

items.quote: Exception: Where the size and/or spacing of guy lines do not result in the gin pole being stable in both boomed and vertical positions, the employer must ensure that the derrick is not used in an unstable position.
items.statement: As an exception, where guy line size and/or spacing do not make the gin pole stable in both boomed and vertical positions, the employer must ensure the derrick is not used in an unstable position.

items.quote: The base of the gin pole must permit movement of the pole (when necessary).
items.statement: The base of a gin pole must permit movement of the pole (when necessary).

items.quote: The gin pole must be anchored at the base against horizontal forces (when such forces are present).
items.statement: A gin pole must be anchored at the base against horizontal forces when such forces are present.

items.quote: Permit the derrick to swing at all permitted operating radii and mounting heights between fittings.
items.statement: Chicago boom derrick fittings for stepping the boom and attaching the topping lift must be arranged to permit the derrick to swing at all permitted operating radii and mounting heights between fittings.

items.quote: Accommodate attachment to the upright member of the host structure.
items.statement: Chicago boom derrick fittings for stepping the boom and attaching the topping lift must be arranged to accommodate attachment to the upright member of the host structure.

items.quote: Withstand the forces applied when configured and operated in accordance with the manufacturer's/builder's procedures and within its rated capacity.
items.statement: Chicago boom derrick fittings for stepping the boom and attaching the topping lift must be arranged to withstand the forces applied when configured and operated according to the manufacturer's/builder's procedures and within rated capacity.

items.quote: Prevent the boom or topping lift from lifting out under tensile forces.
items.statement: Chicago boom derrick fittings for stepping the boom and attaching the topping lift must be arranged to prevent the boom or topping lift from lifting out under tensile forces.

items.quote: Load anchoring data developed by the manufacturer or a qualified person must be used.
items.statement: Load anchoring data developed by the manufacturer or a qualified person must be used.

items.quote: The mast base must be anchored.
items.statement: A guy derrick mast base must be anchored.

items.quote: The guys must be secured to the ground or other firm anchorage.
items.statement: Guy derrick guys must be secured to the ground or other firm anchorage.

items.quote: The anchorage and guying must be designed to withstand maximum horizontal and vertical forces encountered when operating within rated capacity with the particular guy slope and spacing specified for the application.
items.statement: Guy derrick anchorage and guying must be designed to withstand the maximum horizontal and vertical forces encountered when operating within rated capacity with the guy slope and spacing specified for the application.

items.quote: The mast base and stifflegs must be anchored.
items.statement: A stiffleg derrick's mast base and stifflegs must be anchored.

items.quote: The mast base and stifflegs must be designed to withstand maximum horizontal and vertical forces encountered when operating within rated capacity with the particular stiffleg spacing and slope specified for the application.
items.statement: A stiffleg derrick's mast base and stifflegs must be designed to withstand the maximum horizontal and vertical forces encountered when operating within rated capacity with the stiffleg spacing and slope specified for the application.

items.quote: The boom, swinger mechanisms and hoists must be suitable for the derrick work intended
items.statement: The boom, swinger mechanisms and hoists must be suitable for the intended derrick work.

items.quote: must be anchored to prevent displacement from the imposed loads.
items.statement: The boom, swinger mechanisms and hoists must be anchored to prevent displacement from imposed loads.

items.quote: Sections 7-1.1 (“Load ratings and markings”).
items.statement: Base mounted drum hoists must meet Section 7-1.1 (Load ratings and markings) of ASME B30.7-2001.

items.quote: Section 7-1.2 (“Construction”), except: 7-1.2.13 (“Operator's cab”); 7-1.2.15 (“Fire extinguishers”).
items.statement: Base mounted drum hoists must meet Section 7-1.2 (Construction) of ASME B30.7-2001, except 7-1.2.13 (Operator's cab) and 7-1.2.15 (Fire extinguishers).

items.quote: Section 7-1.3 (“Installation”).
items.statement: Base mounted drum hoists must meet Section 7-1.3 (Installation) of ASME B30.7-2001.

items.quote: Applicable terms in section 7-0.2 (“Definitions”).
items.statement: Base mounted drum hoists must meet the applicable terms in section 7-0.2 (Definitions) of ASME B30.7-2001.

items.quote: The employer must ensure that new hoists are load tested to a minimum of 110% of rated capacity, but not more than 125% of rated capacity, unless otherwise recommended by the manufacturer.
items.statement: The employer must ensure new hoists are load tested to at least 110% of rated capacity, unless the manufacturer recommends otherwise.

items.quote: but not more than 125% of rated capacity, unless otherwise recommended by the manufacturer.
items.statement: New hoist load tests must not exceed 125% of rated capacity, unless the manufacturer recommends otherwise.

items.quote: This requirement is met where the manufacturer has conducted this testing.
items.statement: The new-hoist load test requirement is met where the manufacturer has conducted the testing.

items.quote: Hoists that have had repairs, modifications or additions affecting their capacity or safe operation must be evaluated by a qualified person to determine if a load test is necessary.
items.statement: Hoists with repairs, modifications or additions affecting capacity or safe operation must be evaluated by a qualified person to determine if a load test is necessary.

items.quote: If it is, load testing must be conducted in accordance with paragraphs (e)(2)(ii) and (iv) of this section.
items.statement: If a qualified person determines a repaired or modified hoist needs a load test, it must be conducted according to paragraphs (e)(2)(ii) and (iv).

items.quote: The test load must be hoisted a vertical distance to assure that the load is supported by the hoist and held by the hoist brake(s).
items.statement: In load tests of new or repaired/modified hoists, the test load must be hoisted a vertical distance that assures it is supported by the hoist and held by the hoist brake(s).

items.quote: The test load must be lowered, stopped and held with the brake(s).
items.statement: In load tests of new or repaired/modified hoists, the test load must be lowered, stopped and held with the brake(s).

items.quote: The hoist must not be used unless a competent person determines that the test has been passed.
items.statement: A load-tested hoist must not be used unless a competent person determines that the test has been passed.

items.quote: Section 1926.1416 (Operational aids) applies, except for § 1926.1416(d)(1) (Boom hoist limiting device), § 1926.1416(e)(1) (Boom angle or radius indicator), and § 1926.1416(e)(4) (Load weighing and similar devices).
items.statement: Section 1926.1416 (Operational aids) applies to derricks, except § 1926.1416(d)(1) (boom hoist limiting device), (e)(1) (boom angle or radius indicator) and (e)(4) (load weighing and similar devices).

items.quote: A boom angle indicator is not required but if the derrick is not equipped with a functioning one, the employer must ensure that either:
items.statement: A boom angle indicator is not required, but if a derrick lacks a functioning one, the employer must ensure that one of the two specified alternatives (boom hoist cable marks or a signaling/preventing device) is used.

items.quote: The boom hoist cable must be marked with caution and stop marks.
items.statement: Under the cable-marking alternative for a derrick without a functioning boom angle indicator, the boom hoist cable must be marked with caution and stop marks.

items.quote: The stop marks must correspond to maximum and minimum allowable boom angles.
items.statement: Under the cable-marking alternative, the stop marks must correspond to the maximum and minimum allowable boom angles.

items.quote: The caution and stop marks must be in view of the operator, or a spotter who is in direct communication with the operator
items.statement: Under the cable-marking alternative, the caution and stop marks must be in view of the operator or of a spotter in direct communication with the operator.

items.quote: An electronic or other device that signals the operator in time to prevent the boom from moving past its maximum and minimum angles, or automatically prevents such movement, is used.
items.statement: As the alternative to cable marks, an electronic or other device must be used that signals the operator in time to prevent the boom moving past its maximum and minimum angles, or automatically prevents such movement.

items.quote: Derricks manufactured more than one year after November 8, 2010 with a maximum rated capacity over 6,000 pounds must have at least one of the following: load weighing device, load moment indicator, rated capacity indicator, or rated capacity limiter.
items.statement: Derricks manufactured more than one year after November 8, 2010 with a maximum rated capacity over 6,000 pounds must have at least one of a load weighing device, load moment indicator, rated capacity indicator or rated capacity limiter.

items.quote: Temporary alternative measures: The weight of the load must be determined from a source recognized by the industry (such as the load's manufacturer), or by a calculation method recognized by the industry (such as calculating a steel beam from measured dimensions and a known per foot weight), or by other equally reliable means.
items.statement: As a temporary alternative measure to the load weight/capacity device, load weight must be determined from an industry-recognized source (such as the load's manufacturer), an industry-recognized calculation method, or other equally reliable means.

items.quote: This information must be provided to the operator prior to the lift.
items.statement: Under the temporary alternative measures, the load weight information must be provided to the operator before the lift.

items.quote: A load weight/capacity device that is not working properly must be repaired no later than 30 days after the deficiency occurs.
items.statement: A load weight/capacity device that is not working properly must be repaired no later than 30 days after the deficiency occurs, subject to the parts-delay exception.

items.quote: Exception: If the employer documents that it has ordered the necessary parts within 7 days of the occurrence of the deficiency, and the part is not received in time to complete the repair in 30 days, the repair must be completed within 7 days of receipt of the parts.
items.statement: As an exception to the 30-day deadline, if the employer documents ordering the necessary parts within 7 days of the deficiency and the part does not arrive in time to finish within 30 days, the repair must be completed within 7 days of receiving the parts.

items.quote: Anchorages, including the structure to which the derrick is attached (if applicable), must be approved by a qualified person.
items.statement: For new or reinstalled derricks, a qualified person must approve the anchorages, including the structure to which the derrick is attached, if applicable.

items.quote: If using a rock or hairpin anchorage, the qualified person must determine if any special testing of the anchorage is needed.
items.statement: If a new or reinstalled derrick uses a rock or hairpin anchorage, the qualified person must determine whether the anchorage needs any special testing.

items.quote: If so, it must be tested accordingly.
items.statement: If the qualified person determines that a rock or hairpin anchorage needs special testing, it must be tested accordingly.

items.quote: Prior to initial use, new or reinstalled derricks must be tested by a competent person with no hook load to verify proper operation.
items.statement: Before initial use, a competent person must functionally test new or reinstalled derricks with no hook load to verify proper operation.

items.quote: Lifting and lowering the hook(s) through the full range of hook travel.
items.statement: The functional test of a new or reinstalled derrick must include lifting and lowering the hook or hooks through the full range of hook travel.

items.quote: Raising and lowering the boom through the full range of boom travel.
items.statement: The functional test of a new or reinstalled derrick must include raising and lowering the boom through the full range of boom travel.

items.quote: Swinging in each direction through the full range of swing.
items.statement: The functional test of a new or reinstalled derrick must include swinging in each direction through the full range of swing.

items.quote: Actuating the anti two-block and boom hoist limit devices (if provided).
items.statement: The functional test of a new or reinstalled derrick must include actuating the anti two-block and boom hoist limit devices, if provided.

items.quote: Actuating locking, limiting and indicating devices (if provided).
items.statement: The functional test of a new or reinstalled derrick must include actuating locking, limiting and indicating devices, if provided.

items.quote: Prior to initial use, new or reinstalled derricks must be load tested by a competent person.
items.statement: Before initial use, a competent person must load test new or reinstalled derricks.

items.quote: Test loads must be at least 100% and no more than 110% of the rated capacity, unless otherwise recommended by the manufacturer or qualified person
items.statement: Load test loads for new or reinstalled derricks must be at least 100% and no more than 110% of rated capacity unless the manufacturer or a qualified person recommends otherwise, but never less than the maximum anticipated load.
items.value: at least 100% and no more than 110%

items.quote: but in no event must the test load be less than the maximum anticipated load.
items.statement: In no event may a derrick's test load be less than the maximum anticipated load, even if the manufacturer or a qualified person recommends a different test load.

items.quote: Hoisting the test load a few inches and holding to verify that the load is supported by the derrick and held by the hoist brake(s).
items.statement: The load test must include hoisting the test load a few inches and holding it to verify that the derrick supports it and the hoist brake or brakes hold it.

items.quote: Swinging the derrick, if applicable, the full range of its swing, at the maximum allowable working radius for the test load.
items.statement: The load test must include swinging the derrick, if applicable, through its full range of swing at the maximum allowable working radius for the test load.

items.quote: Booming the derrick up and down within the allowable working radius for the test load.
items.statement: The load test must include booming the derrick up and down within the allowable working radius for the test load.

items.quote: Lowering, stopping and holding the load with the brake(s).
items.statement: The load test must include lowering, stopping and holding the load with the brake or brakes.

items.quote: The derrick must not be used unless the competent person determines that the test has been passed.
items.statement: A new or reinstalled derrick must not be used unless the competent person determines that it has passed the load test.

items.quote: Tests conducted under this paragraph must be documented.
items.statement: Tests conducted under the post-assembly approval and testing paragraph for derricks must be documented.

items.quote: The document must contain the date, test results and the name of the tester.
items.statement: The derrick test document must contain the date, the test results and the name of the tester.

items.quote: The document must be retained until the derrick is re-tested or dismantled, whichever occurs first.
items.statement: The derrick test document must be kept until the derrick is re-tested or dismantled, whichever occurs first.

items.quote: All such documents must be available, during the applicable document retention period, to all persons who conduct inspections in accordance with § 1926.1412.
items.statement: During the retention period, derrick test documents must be available to all persons who conduct inspections under § 1926.1412.

items.quote: Derricks that have had repairs, modifications or additions affecting the derrick's capacity or safe operation must be evaluated by a qualified person to determine if a load test is necessary.
items.statement: A qualified person must evaluate a derrick with repairs, modifications or additions affecting its capacity or safe operation to determine whether a load test is necessary.

items.quote: If it is, load testing must be conducted and documented in accordance with paragraph (g) of this section.
items.statement: If the qualified person's evaluation of a repaired or modified derrick finds a load test necessary, the test must be conducted and documented according to paragraph (g).

items.quote: If power fails during operations, the derrick operator must safely stop operations.
items.statement: If power fails during operations, the derrick operator must safely stop operations.

items.quote: Setting all brakes or locking devices.
items.statement: When stopping operations after a power failure, the derrick operator's procedure must include setting all brakes or locking devices.

items.quote: Moving all clutch and other power controls to the off position.
items.statement: When stopping operations after a power failure, the derrick operator's procedure must include moving all clutch and other power controls to the off position.

items.quote: Ropes must not be handled on a winch head without the knowledge of the operator.
items.statement: Ropes must not be handled on a winch head without the operator's knowledge.

items.quote: While a winch head is being used, the operator must be within reach of the power unit control lever.
items.statement: While a winch head is being used, the operator must be within reach of the power unit control lever.

items.quote: When the boom is being held in a fixed position, dogs, pawls, or other positive holding mechanisms on the boom hoist must be engaged.
items.statement: When the boom is held in a fixed position, dogs, pawls or other positive holding mechanisms on the boom hoist must be engaged.

items.quote: When taken out of service for 30 days or more, the boom must be secured by one of the following methods:
items.statement: When a derrick is taken out of service for 30 days or more, its boom must be secured by one of the listed methods.

items.quote: Laid down.
items.statement: For an out-of-service period of 30 days or more, one permitted way to secure the boom is to lay it down.

items.quote: Secured to a stationary member, as nearly under the head as possible, by attachment of a sling to the load block.
items.statement: For an out-of-service period of 30 days or more, one permitted method is securing the boom to a stationary member, as nearly under the head as possible, by attaching a sling to the load block.

items.quote: For guy derricks, lifted to a vertical position and secured to the mast.
items.statement: For an out-of-service period of 30 days or more, one permitted method for guy derricks is lifting the boom to a vertical position and securing it to the mast.

items.quote: For stiffleg derricks, secured against the stiffleg.
items.statement: For an out-of-service period of 30 days or more, one permitted method for stiffleg derricks is securing the boom against the stiffleg.

items.quote: The process of jumping the derrick must be supervised by the A/D director.
items.statement: The A/D director must supervise the process of jumping the derrick.

items.quote: Derrick operations must be supervised by a competent person.
items.statement: A competent person must supervise derrick operations.

items.quote: In addition to the requirements in § 1926.1412, the following additional items must be included in the inspections:
items.statement: Derrick inspections must include the additional items listed for derricks, in addition to meeting the requirements of § 1926.1412.

items.quote: Daily: Guys for proper tension.
items.statement: Daily derrick inspections must include checking the guys for proper tension.

items.quote:
Annual.
[29cfr1926.1436(p)(2)(i)] (i) Gudgeon pin for cracks, wear, and distortion.
items.statement: Annual derrick inspections must include checking the gudgeon pin for cracks, wear and distortion.

items.quote: Foundation supports for continued ability to sustain the imposed loads.
items.statement: Annual derrick inspections must include checking foundation supports for continued ability to sustain the imposed loads.

items.quote: The employer must train each operator of a derrick on the safe operation of equipment the individual will operate.
items.statement: The employer must train each derrick operator on the safe operation of the equipment that person will operate.

items.quote: Section 1926.1427 of this subpart (Operator qualification and certification) does not apply.
items.statement: As an exception, § 1926.1427 (Operator qualification and certification) does not apply to derricks.

items.quote: This section contains supplemental requirements for floating cranes/derricks and land cranes/derricks on barges, pontoons, vessels or other means of flotation (i.e., vessel/flotation device).
items.statement: Section 1926.1437 contains supplemental requirements for floating cranes/derricks and for land cranes/derricks on barges, pontoons, vessels or other means of flotation (vessel/flotation device).

items.quote: The sections of this subpart apply to floating cranes/derricks and land cranes/derricks on barges, pontoons, vessels or other means of flotation, unless specified otherwise.
items.statement: The sections of this subpart apply to floating cranes/derricks and land cranes/derricks on means of flotation unless specified otherwise.

items.quote: The requirements of this section do not apply when using jacked barges when the jacks are deployed to the river, lake, or sea bed and the barge is fully supported by the jacks.
items.statement: As an exception, this section's requirements do not apply when using jacked barges with the jacks deployed to the river, lake or sea bed and the barge fully supported by the jacks.

items.quote: The requirements in paragraphs (c) through (k) of this section apply to both floating cranes/derricks and land cranes/derricks on barges, pontoons, vessels or other means of flotation.
items.statement: The requirements in paragraphs (c) through (k) apply to both floating cranes/derricks and land cranes/derricks on means of flotation.

items.quote: The requirements of § 1926.1424 (Work area control) apply, except for § 1926.1424(a)(2)(ii).
items.statement: The work area control requirements of § 1926.1424 apply, except for § 1926.1424(a)(2)(ii).

items.quote:
(2) The employer must either:
[29cfr1926.1437(c)(2)(i)] (i) Erect and maintain control lines, warning lines, railings or similar barriers to mark the boundaries of the hazard areas; or
[29cfr1926.1437(c)(2)(ii)] (ii) Clearly mark the hazard areas by a combination of warning signs (such as, “Danger—Swing/Crush Zone”) and high visibility markings on the equipment that identify the hazard areas.
items.statement: The employer must either erect and maintain control lines, warning lines, railings or similar barriers to mark hazard area boundaries, or clearly mark the hazard areas with a combination of warning signs and high visibility equipment markings (with employee training on the markings).

items.quote: In addition, the employer must train each employee to understand what these markings signify.
items.statement: When the employer marks hazard areas with warning signs and high visibility markings, it must train each employee to understand what the markings signify.

items.quote: Keeping clear of the load. Section 1926.1425 does not apply.
items.statement: As an exception, § 1926.1425 (keeping clear of the load) does not apply.

items.quote:
In addition to the safety devices listed in § 1926.1415, the following safety devices are required:
[29cfr1926.1437(e)(1)] (1) Barge, pontoon, vessel or other means of flotation list and trim device.
items.statement: In addition to the safety devices in § 1926.1415, a list and trim device for the barge, pontoon, vessel or other means of flotation is required.

items.quote: The safety device must be located in the cab or, when there is no cab, at the operator's station.
items.statement: The list and trim device must be located in the cab or, when there is no cab, at the operator's station.

items.quote:
In addition to the safety devices listed in § 1926.1415, the following safety devices are required:
[29cfr1926.1437(e)(1)] (1) Barge, pontoon, vessel or other means of flotation list and trim device. The safety device must be located in the cab or, when there is no cab, at the operator's station.
[29cfr1926.1437(e)(2)] (2) Positive equipment house lock.
items.statement: A positive equipment house lock is a required additional safety device.

items.quote: A competent person must determine if wind is a factor that needs to be considered
items.statement: A competent person must determine whether wind is a factor that needs to be considered.

items.quote: if wind needs to be considered, a wind speed and direction indicator must be used.
items.statement: If wind needs to be considered, a wind speed and direction indicator must be used.

items.quote: An anti two-block device is required only when hoisting personnel or hoisting over an occupied cofferdam or shaft.
items.statement: An anti two-block device is required only when hoisting personnel or hoisting over an occupied cofferdam or shaft.

items.quote: Section 1926.1416(e)(4) (Load weighing and similar devices) does not apply to dragline, clamshell (grapple), magnet, drop ball, container handling, concrete bucket, and pile driving work performed under this section.
items.statement: As an exception, § 1926.1416(e)(4) (load weighing and similar devices) does not apply to dragline, clamshell (grapple), magnet, drop ball, container handling, concrete bucket and pile driving work performed under this section.

items.quote: If the crane/derrick has a cab, the requirements of § 1926.1417(c) apply.
items.statement: If the crane/derrick has a cab, the requirements of § 1926.1417(c) on accessibility of procedures apply.

items.quote:
If the crane/derrick does not have a cab, the employer must ensure that:
[29cfr1926.1437(g)(1)] (1) Rated capacities (load charts) are posted at the operator's station.
items.statement: If the crane/derrick has no cab, the employer must ensure rated capacities (load charts) are posted at the operator's station.

items.quote: If the operator's station is moveable (such as with pendant-controlled equipment), the load charts are posted on the equipment.
items.statement: For a crane/derrick without a cab, if the operator's station is moveable (such as with pendant-controlled equipment), the load charts are posted on the equipment.

items.quote: Procedures applicable to the operation of the equipment (other than load charts), recommended operating speeds, special hazard warnings, instructions and operators manual, must be readily available on board the vessel/flotation device.
items.statement: For a crane/derrick without a cab, the employer must ensure that operating procedures (other than load charts), recommended operating speeds, special hazard warnings, instructions and the operator's manual are readily available on board the vessel/flotation device.

items.quote: In addition to meeting the requirements of § 1926.1412 for inspecting the crane/derrick, the employer must inspect the barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation used to support a floating crane/derrick or land crane/derrick
items.statement: In addition to inspecting the crane/derrick under § 1926.1412, the employer must inspect the barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation supporting it.

items.quote: For each shift inspection, the means used to secure/attach the equipment to the vessel/flotation device is in proper condition, including wear, corrosion, loose or missing fasteners, defective welds, and (when applicable) insufficient tension.
items.statement: At each shift inspection, the employer must ensure the means securing the equipment to the vessel/flotation device is in proper condition, including wear, corrosion, loose or missing fasteners, defective welds and, when applicable, insufficient tension.

items.quote: The means used to secure/attach the equipment to the vessel/flotation device is in proper condition, including inspection for wear, corrosion, and, when applicable, insufficient tension.
items.statement: At each monthly inspection, the means securing the equipment to the vessel/flotation device must be in proper condition, including inspection for wear, corrosion and, when applicable, insufficient tension.

items.quote: The vessel/flotation device is not taking on water.
items.statement: At each monthly inspection, the employer must ensure the vessel/flotation device is not taking on water.

items.quote: The deckload is properly secured.
items.statement: At each monthly inspection, the employer must ensure the deckload is properly secured.

items.quote: The vessel/flotation device is watertight based on the condition of the chain lockers, storage, fuel compartments, and hatches.
items.statement: At each monthly inspection, the employer must ensure the vessel/flotation device is watertight based on the condition of the chain lockers, storage, fuel compartments and hatches.

items.quote: The firefighting and lifesaving equipment is in place and functional.
items.statement: At each monthly inspection, the employer must ensure firefighting and lifesaving equipment is in place and functional.

items.quote: The shift and monthly inspections are conducted by a competent person
items.statement: A competent person conducts the shift and monthly vessel/flotation device inspections.

items.quote: If any deficiency is identified, an immediate determination is made by a qualified person whether the deficiency constitutes a hazard.
items.statement: If a shift or monthly inspection identifies any deficiency, a qualified person immediately determines whether it constitutes a hazard.

items.quote: If the deficiency is determined to constitute a hazard, the vessel/flotation device is removed from service until the deficiency has been corrected.
items.statement: If a deficiency from a shift or monthly inspection is determined to be a hazard, the vessel/flotation device is removed from service until the deficiency is corrected.

items.quote: The external portion of the barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation used is inspected annually by a qualified person who has expertise with respect to vessels/flotation devices
items.statement: The external portion of the means of flotation must be inspected annually by a qualified person with expertise in vessels/flotation devices.

items.quote: The items identified in paragraphs (h)(1) (Shift) and (h)(2) (Monthly) of this section.
items.statement: The annual external inspection includes the items in the shift (h)(1) and monthly (h)(2) inspections.

items.quote: Cleats, bitts, chocks, fenders, capstans, ladders, and stanchions, for significant corrosion, wear, deterioration, or deformation that could impair the function of these items.
items.statement: The annual external inspection checks cleats, bitts, chocks, fenders, capstans, ladders and stanchions for significant corrosion, wear, deterioration or deformation that could impair their function.

items.quote: External evidence of leaks and structural damage
items.statement: The annual external inspection includes external evidence of leaks and structural damage.

items.quote: evidence of leaks and damage below the waterline may be determined through internal inspection of the vessel/flotation device.
items.statement: Evidence of leaks and damage below the waterline may be determined through internal inspection of the vessel/flotation device.

items.quote: Four-corner draft readings.
items.statement: The annual external inspection includes four-corner draft readings.

items.quote: Firefighting equipment for serviceability.
items.statement: The annual external inspection includes checking firefighting equipment for serviceability.

items.quote: Rescue skiffs, lifelines, work vests, life preservers and ring buoys are inspected for proper condition.
items.statement: At each annual inspection, rescue skiffs, lifelines, work vests, life preservers and ring buoys are inspected for proper condition.

items.quote: If any deficiency is identified, an immediate determination is made by the qualified person whether the deficiency constitutes a hazard or, though not yet a hazard, needs to be monitored in the monthly inspections.
items.statement: If the annual inspection identifies any deficiency, the qualified person immediately determines whether it is a hazard or, though not yet a hazard, needs monitoring in the monthly inspections.

items.quote: If the qualified person determines that the deficiency constitutes a hazard, the vessel/flotation device is removed from service until it has been corrected.
items.statement: If the qualified person determines an annual-inspection deficiency is a hazard, the vessel/flotation device is removed from service until it is corrected.

items.quote: If the qualified person determines that, though not presently a hazard, the deficiency needs to be monitored, the deficiency is checked in the monthly inspections.
items.statement: If the qualified person determines an annual-inspection deficiency is not presently a hazard but needs monitoring, it is checked in the monthly inspections.

items.quote:
Four-year: internal vessel/flotation device inspection. For each four-year inspection:
[29cfr1926.1437(h)(5)(i)] (i) A marine engineer, marine architect, licensed surveyor, or other qualified person who has expertise with respect to vessels/flotation devices surveys the internal portion of the barge, pontoons, vessel, or other means of flotation.
items.statement: Every four years, the internal portion of the means of flotation is surveyed by a marine engineer, marine architect, licensed surveyor or other qualified person with expertise in vessels/flotation devices.

items.quote: If the surveyor identifies a deficiency, an immediate determination is made by the surveyor as to whether the deficiency constitutes a hazard or, though not yet a hazard, needs to be monitored in the monthly or annual inspections, as appropriate.
items.statement: If the surveyor identifies a deficiency in the four-year inspection, the surveyor immediately determines whether it is a hazard or, though not yet a hazard, needs monitoring in the monthly or annual inspections, as appropriate.

items.quote: If the surveyor determines that the deficiency constitutes a hazard, the vessel/flotation device is removed from service until it has been corrected.
items.statement: If the surveyor determines a deficiency is a hazard, the vessel/flotation device is removed from service until it is corrected.

items.quote: If the surveyor determines that, though not presently a hazard, the deficiency needs to be monitored, the deficiency is checked in the monthly or annual inspections, as appropriate.
items.statement: If the surveyor determines a deficiency is not presently a hazard but needs monitoring, it is checked in the monthly or annual inspections, as appropriate.

items.quote: The monthly and annual inspections required in paragraphs (h)(2) and (h)(4) of this section are documented in accordance with §§ 1926.1412 (e)(3) and 1926.1412(f)(7), respectively
items.statement: Monthly vessel/flotation device inspections are documented in accordance with § 1926.1412(e)(3), and annual ones in accordance with § 1926.1412(f)(7).

items.quote: the four-year inspection required in paragraph (h)(5) of this section is documented in accordance with § 1926.1412(f)(7), except that
items.statement: The four-year inspection is documented in accordance with § 1926.1412(f)(7), except for its retention period.

items.quote: the documentation for that inspection must be retained for a minimum of 4 years
items.statement: Documentation of the four-year inspection must be retained for at least 4 years.

items.quote: All such documents must be made available, during the applicable document retention period, to all persons who conduct inspections in accordance with § 1926.1412.
items.statement: All these inspection documents must be made available, during the applicable retention period, to all persons who conduct inspections under § 1926.1412.

items.quote: If a crane/derrick is used to get a diver into and out of the water, it must not be used for any other purpose until the diver is back on board.
items.statement: When working with a diver, a crane/derrick used to get a diver into and out of the water must not be used for any other purpose until the diver is back on board.

items.quote: When used for more than one diver, it must not be used for any other purpose until all divers are back on board.
items.statement: A crane/derrick used to get more than one diver into and out of the water must not be used for any other purpose until all divers are back on board.

items.quote: The operator must remain at the controls of the crane/derrick at all times.
items.statement: When working with a diver in the water, the operator must remain at the crane/derrick controls at all times.

items.quote:
In addition to the requirements in §§ 1926.1419 through 1926.1422 (Signals), either:
[29cfr1926.1437(j)(3)(i)] (i) A clear line of sight must be maintained between the operator and tender; or
[29cfr1926.1437(j)(3)(ii)] (ii) The signals between the operator and tender must be transmitted electronically.
items.statement: When working with a diver, in addition to the signal requirements of §§ 1926.1419 through 1926.1422, either a clear line of sight must be maintained between operator and tender or their signals must be transmitted electronically.

items.quote: must not allow any amount of shifting in any direction.
items.statement: When working with a diver, the means securing the crane/derrick to the vessel/flotation device must not allow any shifting in any direction.

items.quote: The employer must ensure that the barge, pontoons, vessel, or other means of flotation must be capable of withstanding imposed environmental, operational and in-transit loads when used in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and limitations.
items.statement: The employer must ensure the means of flotation is capable of withstanding imposed environmental, operational and in-transit loads when used in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and limitations.

items.quote: The employer must ensure that the manufacturer's specifications and limitations with respect to environmental, operational, and in-transit loads for a barge, pontoon, vessel, or other means of flotation are not exceeded or violated.
items.statement: The employer must ensure the manufacturer's specifications and limitations on environmental, operational and in-transit loads for the means of flotation are not exceeded or violated.

items.quote: When the manufacturer's specifications and limitations are unavailable, the employer must ensure that the specifications and limitations established by a qualified person with respect to environmental, operational and in-transit loads for the barge, pontoons, vessel, or other means of flotation are not exceeded or violated.
items.statement: When the manufacturer's specifications and limitations are unavailable, the employer must ensure those established by a qualified person for environmental, operational and in-transit loads on the means of flotation are not exceeded or violated.

items.quote: For equipment designed by the manufacturer (or employer) for marine use by permanent attachment to barges, pontoons, vessels or other means of flotation
items.statement: Paragraph (m), on floating cranes/derricks, covers equipment designed by the manufacturer or employer for marine use by permanent attachment to barges, pontoons, vessels or other means of flotation.

items.quote: The employer must not exceed the manufacturer load charts applicable to operations on water.
items.statement: For floating cranes/derricks, the employer must not exceed the manufacturer load charts applicable to operations on water.

items.quote: When using these charts, the employer must comply with all parameters and limitations (such as dynamic and environmental parameters) applicable to the use of the charts.
items.statement: When using the manufacturer load charts for operations on water, the employer must comply with all parameters and limitations, such as dynamic and environmental parameters, that apply to the use of the charts.

items.quote: load charts take into consideration a minimum wind speed of 40 miles per hour
items.statement: For floating cranes/derricks, the employer must ensure that load charts take into consideration a minimum wind speed of 40 miles per hour.

items.quote: The employer must ensure that the requirements for maximum allowable list and maximum allowable trim as specified in Table M1 of this section are met.
items.statement: The employer must ensure that floating cranes/derricks meet the maximum allowable list and maximum allowable trim requirements in Table M1.

items.quote:

Equipment designed for marine use by permanent attachment (other than derricks): | |
25 tons or less | 5 | 5
items.statement: For equipment other than derricks that is designed for marine use by permanent attachment and rated at 25 tons or less, the maximum allowable list is 5 degrees.

items.quote:
Rated capacity | Maximum allowable list (degrees) | Maximum allowable trim (degrees)
Equipment designed for marine use by permanent attachment (other than derricks): | |
25 tons or less | 5 | 5
items.statement: For equipment other than derricks that is designed for marine use by permanent attachment and rated at 25 tons or less, the maximum allowable trim is 5 degrees.

Equipment designed for marine use by permanent attachment (other than derricks): | |

Over 25 tons | 7 | 7
items.statement: For equipment other than derricks that is designed for marine use by permanent attachment and rated over 25 tons, the maximum allowable list is 7 degrees.

items.quote:
Rated capacity | Maximum allowable list (degrees) | Maximum allowable trim (degrees)
Equipment designed for marine use by permanent attachment (other than derricks): | |
25 tons or less | 5 | 5
Over 25 tons | 7 | 7
items.statement: For equipment other than derricks that is designed for marine use by permanent attachment and rated over 25 tons, the maximum allowable trim is 7 degrees.

items.statement: For derricks of any rated capacity designed for marine use by permanent attachment, the maximum allowable list is 10 degrees.
