items.statement: For derricks of any rated capacity designed for marine use by permanent attachment, the maximum allowable trim is 10 degrees.

items.quote: The employer must ensure that the equipment is stable under the conditions specified in Tables M2 and M3 of this section.
items.statement: The employer must ensure that floating cranes/derricks are stable under the conditions in Tables M2 and M3.

items.quote: Freeboard is the vertical distance between the water line and the main deck of the vessel.
items.statement: Freeboard is the vertical distance between the water line and the main deck of the vessel.

items.quote:
Operated at | Wind speed (mph) | Minimum freeboard (ft)
Rated capacity | 60 | 2
items.statement: When operated at rated capacity in a 60 mph wind, floating equipment must be stable with a minimum freeboard of 2 ft.

items.quote:
Operated at | Wind speed (mph) | Minimum freeboard (ft)
Rated capacity | 60 | 2
Rated capacity plus 25% | 60 | 1
items.statement: When operated at rated capacity plus 25% in a 60 mph wind, floating equipment must be stable with a minimum freeboard of 1 ft.

items.quote:
Operated at | Wind speed (mph) | Minimum freeboard (ft)
Rated capacity | 60 | 2
Rated capacity plus 25% | 60 | 1
High boom, no load | 60 | 2
items.statement: With a high boom and no load in a 60 mph wind, floating equipment must be stable with a minimum freeboard of 2 ft.

items.quote:
For backward stability of the boom: |
High boom, no load, full back list (least stable condition) | 90 mph.
items.statement: For backward stability of the boom, floating equipment must be stable in a 90 mph wind with a high boom, no load and full back list (the least stable condition).

items.quote: If the equipment is employer-made, it must not be used unless the employer has documents demonstrating that the load charts and applicable parameters for use meet the requirements of paragraphs (m)(1) through (3) of this section.
items.statement: Employer-made floating equipment must not be used unless the employer has documents demonstrating that its load charts and applicable parameters for use meet paragraphs (m)(1) through (3).

items.quote: Such documents must be signed by a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person with respect to the design of this type of equipment (including the means of flotation).
items.statement: The documents for employer-made floating equipment must be signed by a registered professional engineer who is a qualified person for the design of this type of equipment, including the means of flotation.

items.quote: Are structurally sufficient to withstand the static and dynamic loads of the crane/derrick when operating at the crane/derrick's maximum rated capacity with all planned and actual deck loads and ballasted compartments.
items.statement: For floating cranes/derricks, the employer must ensure the means of flotation is structurally sufficient to withstand the crane/derrick's static and dynamic loads at maximum rated capacity with all planned and actual deck loads and ballasted compartments.

items.quote: Have a subdivided hull with one or more longitudinal watertight bulkheads for reducing the free-surface effect.
items.statement: For floating cranes/derricks, the employer must ensure the means of flotation has a subdivided hull with one or more longitudinal watertight bulkheads to reduce the free-surface effect.

items.quote: Have access to void compartments to allow for inspection and pumping.
items.statement: For floating cranes/derricks, the employer must ensure the means of flotation has access to void compartments for inspection and pumping.

items.quote:
The rated capacity of the equipment (including but not limited to modification of load charts) applicable for use on land is reduced to:
(i) Account for increased loading from list, trim, wave action, and wind.
items.statement: For land cranes/derricks used on means of flotation, the employer must ensure the land-use rated capacity, including load chart modifications, is reduced to account for increased loading from list, trim, wave action and wind.

items.quote: Be applicable to a specified location(s) on the specific barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation that will be used, under the environmental conditions expected and encountered.
items.statement: For land cranes/derricks on means of flotation, the employer must ensure the reduced rated capacity applies to specified locations on the specific vessel or flotation device to be used, under the expected and encountered environmental conditions.

items.quote: The conditions required in paragraphs (n)(3) and (n)(4) of this section are met.
items.statement: For land cranes/derricks on means of flotation, the employer must ensure the rated capacity is reduced so that the conditions required in paragraphs (n)(3) and (n)(4) are met.

items.quote: The rated capacity modification required in paragraph (n)(1) of this section is performed by the equipment manufacturer, or a qualified person who has expertise with respect to both land crane/derrick capacity and the stability of vessels/flotation devices.
items.statement: The employer must ensure the (n)(1) rated capacity modification is performed by the equipment manufacturer or a qualified person with expertise in both land crane/derrick capacity and the stability of vessels/flotation devices.

items.quote: The maximum allowable list and the maximum allowable trim for the barge, pontoon, vessel or other means of flotation must not exceed the amount necessary to ensure that the conditions in paragraph (n)(4) of this section are met.
items.statement: With a land crane/derrick aboard, the maximum allowable list and trim of the means of flotation must not exceed the amount necessary to ensure the (n)(4) conditions are met.

items.quote: the maximum allowable list and the maximum allowable trim does not exceed the least of the following: 5 degrees, the amount specified by the crane/derrick manufacturer, or, when, an amount is not so specified, the amount specified by the qualified person.
items.statement: With a land crane/derrick aboard, the maximum allowable list and trim of the means of flotation must not exceed the least of 5 degrees, the crane/derrick manufacturer's amount, or, when the manufacturer specifies none, the qualified person's amount.

items.quote: The maximum allowable list and the maximum allowable trim for the land crane/derrick does not exceed the amount specified by the crane/derrick manufacturer, or, when, an amount is not so specified, the amount specified by the qualified person.
items.statement: The land crane/derrick's maximum allowable list and trim must not exceed the amount specified by its manufacturer or, when the manufacturer specifies none, by the qualified person.

items.quote: All deck surfaces of the barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation used are above water.
items.statement: For land cranes/derricks on means of flotation, the employer must ensure all deck surfaces of the means of flotation used are above water.

items.quote: The entire bottom area of the barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation used is submerged.
items.statement: For land cranes/derricks on means of flotation, the employer must ensure the entire bottom area of the means of flotation used is submerged.

items.quote: Physical attachment, corralling, rails system and centerline cable system meet the requirements in Option (1), Option (2), Option (3), or Option (4) of this section, and that whichever option is used also meets the requirements of paragraph (n)(5)(v) of this section.
items.statement: For land cranes/derricks on means of flotation, the employer must ensure that physical attachment, corralling, rails or a centerline cable system meets Option (1), (2), (3) or (4), and that the option used also meets paragraph (n)(5)(v).

items.quote: The crane/derrick is physically attached to the barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation. Methods of physical attachment include crossed-cable systems attached to the crane/derrick and vessel/flotation device, bolting or welding the crane/derrick to the vessel/flotation device, strapping the crane/derrick to the vessel/flotation device with chains, or other methods of physical attachment.
items.statement: Option (1), physical attachment, means the crane/derrick is physically attached to the means of flotation, by methods such as crossed cables attached to both, bolting or welding, strapping with chains, or other physical attachment.

items.quote: The crane/derrick is prevented from shifting by installing barricade restraints (i.e., a corralling system).
items.statement: Option (2), corralling, prevents the crane/derrick from shifting by installing barricade restraints.

items.quote: Employers must ensure that corralling systems do not allow the equipment to shift by any amount of shifting in any direction.
items.statement: Employers must ensure that corralling systems do not allow the equipment to shift by any amount in any direction.

items.quote: The crane/derrick must be prevented from shifting by being mounted on a rail system.
items.statement: Under Option (3), the crane/derrick must be prevented from shifting by being mounted on a rail system.

items.quote: Employers must ensure that rail clamps and rail stops are used unless the system is designed to prevent movement during operation by other means.
items.statement: Under the rail option, employers must ensure rail clamps and rail stops are used unless the system is designed to prevent movement during operation by other means.

items.quote: The crane/derrick is prevented from shifting by being mounted to a wire rope system.
items.statement: Option (4), the centerline cable system, prevents the crane/derrick from shifting by mounting it to a wire rope system.

items.quote: The wire rope and attachments are of sufficient size and strength to support the side load of crane/derrick.
items.statement: In a centerline cable system, the employer must ensure the wire rope and attachments are of sufficient size and strength to support the crane/derrick's side load.

items.quote: The wire rope is attached physically to the vessel/flotation device.
items.statement: In a centerline cable system, the employer must ensure the wire rope is physically attached to the vessel/flotation device.

items.quote: The wire rope is attached to the crane/derrick by appropriate attachment methods (such as shackles or sheaves) on the undercarriage, and that the method used will allow the crew to secure the crane/derrick from movement during operation and to move the crane/derrick longitudinally along the vessel/flotation device for repositioning.
items.statement: In a centerline cable system, the employer must ensure the wire rope is attached to the crane/derrick undercarriage by appropriate methods, such as shackles or sheaves, that let the crew secure it from movement during operation and move it longitudinally along the vessel for repositioning.

items.quote: Means are installed to prevent the crane/derrick from passing the forward or aft end of the wire rope attachments.
items.statement: In a centerline cable system, the employer must ensure means are installed to prevent the crane/derrick from passing the forward or aft end of the wire rope attachments.

items.quote: The crane/derrick is secured from movement during operation.
items.statement: In a centerline cable system, the employer must ensure the crane/derrick is secured from movement during operation.

items.quote: The systems/means used to comply with Option (1), Option (2), Option (3), or Option (4) of this section are designed by a marine engineer, registered professional engineer familiar with floating crane/derrick design, or qualified person familiar with floating crane/derrick design.
items.statement: The systems or means used to comply with Options (1) through (4) must be designed by a marine engineer, or a registered professional engineer or qualified person familiar with floating crane/derrick design.

items.quote: For mobile auxiliary cranes used on the deck of a floating crane/derrick, the requirement specified by paragraph (n)(5) of this section to use Option (1), Option (2), Option (3), or Option (4) does not apply when the employer demonstrates implementation of a plan and procedures that meet the following requirements
items.statement: As an exception, mobile auxiliary cranes used on the deck of a floating crane/derrick need not use an (n)(5) option when the employer demonstrates implementation of a plan and procedures meeting the (n)(6) requirements.

items.quote: A marine engineer or registered professional engineer familiar with floating crane/derrick design develops and signs a written plan for the use of the mobile auxiliary crane.
items.statement: To use the mobile auxiliary crane exception, a marine engineer or registered professional engineer familiar with floating crane/derrick design must develop and sign a written plan for the crane's use.

items.quote: The plan is designed so that the applicable requirements of this section are met despite the position, travel, operation, and lack of physical attachment (or corralling, use of rails or cable system) of the mobile auxiliary crane.
items.statement: The mobile auxiliary crane plan must be designed so the section's applicable requirements are met despite the crane's position, travel, operation, and lack of physical attachment, corralling, rails or cable system.

items.quote: The plan specifies the areas of the deck where the mobile auxiliary crane is permitted to be positioned, travel, and operate
items.statement: The plan must specify the deck areas where the mobile auxiliary crane is permitted to be positioned, travel and operate.

items.quote: The plan specifies the areas of the deck where the mobile auxiliary crane is permitted to be positioned, travel, and operate, and the parameters and limitations of such movements and operation.
items.statement: The plan must specify the parameters and limitations of the mobile auxiliary crane's permitted movements and operation.

items.quote: The deck is marked to identify the permitted areas for positioning, travel, and operation.
items.statement: Under the mobile auxiliary crane plan, the deck must be marked to identify the permitted areas for positioning, travel and operation.

items.quote: The plan specifies the dynamic and environmental conditions that must be present for use of the plan.
items.statement: The mobile auxiliary crane plan must specify the dynamic and environmental conditions that must be present for its use.

items.quote: If the dynamic and environmental conditions in paragraph (n)(6)(v) of this section are exceeded, the mobile auxiliary crane is attached physically or corralled in accordance with Option (1), Option (2) or Option (4) of paragraph (n)(5) of this section.
items.statement: If the plan's dynamic and environmental conditions are exceeded, the mobile auxiliary crane must be physically attached or corralled in accordance with Option (1), (2) or (4) of paragraph (n)(5).

items.quote: Are structurally sufficient to withstand the static and dynamic loads of the crane/derrick when operating at the crane/derrick's maximum rated capacity with all anticipated deck loads and ballasted compartments.
items.statement: For land cranes/derricks on means of flotation, the employer must ensure the means of flotation is structurally sufficient to withstand the crane/derrick's static and dynamic loads at maximum rated capacity with all anticipated deck loads and ballasted compartments.

items.quote: Have a subdivided hull with one or more longitudinal watertight bulkheads for reducing the free surface effect.
items.statement: For land cranes/derricks on means of flotation, the employer must ensure the means of flotation has a subdivided hull with one or more longitudinal watertight bulkheads to reduce the free surface effect.

items.quote: Have access to void compartments to allow for inspection and pumping.
items.statement: For land cranes/derricks on means of flotation, the employer must ensure the means of flotation has access to void compartments for inspection and pumping.

items.quote: The requirements of § 1910.179, except for § 1910.179(b)(1), and not the requirements of this subpart CC, apply to the following equipment when used in construction and permanently installed in a facility
items.statement: The requirements of § 1910.179, other than § 1910.179(b)(1), apply to overhead and gantry cranes and the other equipment listed in § 1926.1438(a) when used in construction and permanently installed in a facility.

items.quote: The requirements of § 1910.179, except for § 1910.179(b)(1)
items.statement: § 1910.179(b)(1) is excepted from the § 1910.179 requirements that apply to permanently installed overhead and gantry cranes and the other listed equipment used in construction.

items.quote: not the requirements of this subpart CC, apply to the following equipment when used in construction and permanently installed in a facility
items.statement: The requirements of subpart CC do not apply to overhead and gantry cranes and the other equipment listed in § 1926.1438(a) when used in construction and permanently installed in a facility.

items.quote: overhead and gantry cranes, including semigantry, cantilever gantry, wall cranes, storage bridge cranes, and others having the same fundamental characteristics.
items.statement: The permanently installed equipment covered by § 1926.1438(a) is overhead and gantry cranes, including semigantry, cantilever gantry, wall cranes, storage bridge cranes, and others having the same fundamental characteristics.

items.quote: This paragraph applies to the following equipment when used in construction and not permanently installed in a facility: Overhead and gantry cranes, overhead/bridge cranes, semigantry, cantilever gantry, wall cranes, storage bridge cranes, launching gantry cranes, and similar equipment having the same fundamental characteristics, irrespective of whether it travels on tracks, wheels, or other means.
items.statement: Paragraph (b) applies to overhead and gantry, overhead/bridge, semigantry, cantilever gantry, wall, storage bridge, launching gantry cranes and similar equipment with the same fundamental characteristics, when used in construction and not permanently installed in a facility, whether it travels on tracks, wheels or other means.

items.quote: Sections 1926.1400 through 1926.1414
items.statement: Sections 1926.1400 through 1926.1414 apply to overhead and gantry cranes and similar equipment identified in paragraph (b)(1) (used in construction and not permanently installed).
Sections 1926.1417 through 1926.1425 apply to equipment identified in paragraph (b)(1).
Section 1926.1426(d) applies to equipment identified in paragraph (b)(1).
Sections 1926.1427 through 1926.1434 apply to equipment identified in paragraph (b)(1).
Sections 1926.1437, 1926.1439 and 1926.1441 apply to equipment identified in paragraph (b)(1).
Paragraphs (b)(5), (6), (7); (e)(1), (3), (5), (6); (f)(1), (4); (g); (h)(1), (3); (k); and (n) of § 1910.179 apply to equipment identified in paragraph (b)(1).

items.quote: The definitions in § 1910.179(a) except for “hoist” and “load.”
items.statement: The definitions in § 1910.179(a), except those for "hoist" and "load," apply to equipment identified in paragraph (b)(1).

items.quote: For those words, the definitions in § 1926.1401 apply.
items.statement: For equipment identified in paragraph (b)(1), the definitions of "hoist" and "load" in § 1926.1401 apply.

items.quote: Section 1910.179(b)(2), but only where the equipment identified in paragraph (b)(1) of this section (§ 1926.1438) was manufactured before September 19, 2001.
items.statement: Section 1910.179(b)(2) applies only where the equipment identified in paragraph (b)(1) was manufactured before September 19, 2001.

items.quote: For equipment manufactured on or after September 19, 2001, the following sections of ASME B30.2-2005 (incorporated by reference, see § 1926.6) apply: 2-1.3.1; 2-1.3.2; 2-1.4.1; 2-1.6; 2-1.7.2; 2-1.8.2; 2-1.9.1; 2-1.9.2; 2-1.11; 2-1.12.2; 2-1.13.7; 2-1.14.2; 2-1.14.3; 2-1.14.5; 2-1.15.; 2-2.2.2; 2-3.2.1.1. In addition, 2-3.5 applies
items.statement: For paragraph (b)(1) equipment manufactured on or after September 19, 2001, section 2-3.5 of ASME B30.2-2005 also applies, subject to a substitution in 2-3.5.1(b).

items.quote: except in 2-3.5.1(b), “29 CFR 1910.147” is substituted for “ANSI Z244.1.”
items.statement: When applying section 2-3.5 to paragraph (b)(1) equipment manufactured on or after September 19, 2001, "29 CFR 1910.147" is substituted for "ANSI Z244.1" in 2-3.5.1(b).

items.quote: The provisions of subpart CC apply to dedicated pile drivers, except as specified in this section.
items.statement: The provisions of subpart CC apply to dedicated pile drivers, except as specified in § 1926.1439.

items.quote: Section 1926.1416(d)(3) (Anti two-blocking device) does not apply.
items.statement: As an exception for dedicated pile drivers, § 1926.1416(d)(3) (Anti two-blocking device) does not apply to them.

items.quote: Section 1926.1416(e)(4) (Load weighing and similar devices) applies only to dedicated pile drivers manufactured after November 8, 2011.
items.statement: For dedicated pile drivers, § 1926.1416(e)(4) (Load weighing and similar devices) applies only to those manufactured after November 8, 2011.

items.quote: In § 1926.1433, only §§ 1926.1433(d) and (e) apply to dedicated pile drivers.
items.statement: In § 1926.1433, only paragraphs (d) and (e) apply to dedicated pile drivers.

items.quote: The provisions of this standard apply, except § 1926.1402 (Ground conditions)
items.statement: The provisions of this standard apply to sideboom cranes, except that § 1926.1402 (Ground conditions) is excluded.

items.quote: The provisions of this standard apply, except § 1926.1402 (Ground conditions), § 1926.1415 (Safety devices)
items.statement: The provisions of this standard apply to sideboom cranes, except that § 1926.1415 (Safety devices) is excluded.

items.quote: The provisions of this standard apply, except § 1926.1402 (Ground conditions), § 1926.1415 (Safety devices), § 1926.1416 (Operational aids)
items.statement: The provisions of this standard apply to sideboom cranes, except that § 1926.1416 (Operational aids) is excluded.

items.quote: The provisions of this standard apply, except § 1926.1402 (Ground conditions), § 1926.1415 (Safety devices), § 1926.1416 (Operational aids), and § 1926.1427 (Operator qualification and certification).
items.statement: The provisions of this standard apply to sideboom cranes, except that § 1926.1427 (Operator qualification and certification) is excluded.

items.quote: Section 1926.1426 (Free fall and controlled load lowering) applies, except § 1926.1426(a)(2)(i).
items.statement: Section 1926.1426 (Free fall and controlled load lowering) applies to sideboom cranes, except for § 1926.1426(a)(2)(i).

items.quote: Sideboom cranes in which the boom is designed to free fall (live boom) are permitted only if manufactured prior to November 8, 2010.
items.statement: Sideboom cranes with a boom designed to free fall (live boom) are permitted only if they were manufactured prior to November 8, 2010.

items.quote: Section 14-1.1 (“Load Ratings”).
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet Section 14-1.1 (“Load Ratings”) of ASME B30.14-2004.

items.quote: Section 14-1.3 (“Side Boom Tractor Travel”).
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet Section 14-1.3 (“Side Boom Tractor Travel”) of ASME B30.14-2004.

items.quote: Section 14-1.5 (“Ropes and Reeving Accessories”).
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet Section 14-1.5 (“Ropes and Reeving Accessories”) of ASME B30.14-2004.

items.quote: Section 14-1.7.1 (“Booms”).
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet Section 14-1.7.1 (“Booms”) of ASME B30.14-2004.

items.quote: Section 14-1.7.2 (“General Requirements—Exhaust Gases”).
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet Section 14-1.7.2 (“General Requirements—Exhaust Gases”) of ASME B30.14-2004.

items.quote: Section 14-1.7.3 (“General Requirements—Stabilizers (Wheel-Type Side Boom Tractors)”).
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet Section 14-1.7.3 (“General Requirements—Stabilizers (Wheel-Type Side Boom Tractors)”) of ASME B30.14-2004.

items.quote: Section 14-1.7.4 (“General Requirements—Welded Construction”).
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet Section 14-1.7.4 (“General Requirements—Welded Construction”) of ASME B30.14-2004.

items.quote: Section 14-1.7.6 (“General Requirements—Clutch and Brake Protection”).
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet Section 14-1.7.6 (“General Requirements—Clutch and Brake Protection”) of ASME B30.14-2004.

items.quote: Section 14-2.2.2 (“Testing—Rated Load Test”), except that it applies only to equipment that has been altered or modified.
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet Section 14-2.2.2 (“Testing—Rated Load Test”) of ASME B30.14-2004, except that it applies only to equipment that has been altered or modified.

items.quote: In section 14-3.1.2 (“Operator Qualifications”), paragraph (a), except the phrase “When required by law.”
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet paragraph (a) of ASME B30.14-2004 section 14-3.1.2 (“Operator Qualifications”), except for the phrase “When required by law.”

items.quote: In section 14-3.1.3 (“Operating Practices”), paragraphs (e), (f)(1)-(f)(4), (f)(6), (f)(7), (h), and (i).
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet paragraphs (e), (f)(1)-(f)(4), (f)(6), (f)(7), (h), and (i) of ASME B30.14-2004 section 14-3.1.3 (“Operating Practices”).

items.quote: In section 14-3.2.3 (“Moving the Load”), paragraphs (j), (l), and (m).
items.statement: Sideboom cranes mounted on wheel or crawler tractors must meet paragraphs (j), (l), and (m) of ASME B30.14-2004 section 14-3.2.3 (“Moving the Load”).

items.quote: requirements for employers using equipment with a maximum rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less
items.statement: The requirements of §1926.1441 apply to employers using equipment with a maximum rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less.
An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §1926.1400 (Scope).

items.quote: § 1926.1401 (Definitions)
items.statement: An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §1926.1401 (Definitions).

items.quote: § 1926.1402 (Ground conditions)
items.statement: An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §1926.1402 (Ground conditions).

items.quote: § 1926.1403 (Assembly/disassembly—selection of manufacturer or employer procedures)
items.statement: An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §1926.1403 (selection of manufacturer or employer assembly/disassembly procedures).

items.quote: § 1926.1406 (Assembly/disassembly—employer procedures)
items.statement: An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §1926.1406 (employer procedures for assembly/disassembly).

items.quote: §§ 1926.1407 through 1926.1411 (Power line safety)
items.statement: An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §§1926.1407 through 1926.1411 (Power line safety).

items.quote: § 1926.1412(c) (Post-assembly)
items.statement: An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §1926.1412(c) (Post-assembly).

items.quote: §§ 1926.1413 through 1926.1414 (Wire rope)
items.statement: An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §§1926.1413 through 1926.1414 (Wire rope).

items.quote: § 1926.1418 (Authority to stop operation)
items.statement: An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §1926.1418 (Authority to stop operation).
An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §§1926.1419 through 1926.1422 (Signals).

items.quote: § 1926.1423 (Fall protection)
items.statement: An employer using equipment rated at 2,000 pounds or less must comply with §1926.1423 (Fall protection).

items.quote: § 1926.1425 (Keeping clear of the load) (except for § 1926.1425(c)(3) (qualified rigger))

items.quote: when pins (or similar devices) are being removed, employees must not be under the boom, jib, or other components, except where the requirements of § 1926.1404(f)(2) are met.

items.quote: The exception in § 1926.1404(f)(2) applies when the employer demonstrates that site constraints require one or more employees to be under the boom, jib, or other components when pins (or similar devices) are being removed.
items.statement: The § 1926.1404(f)(2) exception applies when the employer demonstrates that site constraints require one or more employees to be under the boom, jib, or other components while pins or similar devices are being removed.

items.quote: In such a situation, the A/D director must implement procedures that minimize the risk of unintended dangerous movement
items.statement: When the § 1926.1404(f)(2) exception applies because site constraints require employees to be under the boom, jib, or other components during pin removal, the A/D director must implement procedures that minimize the risk of unintended dangerous movement.

items.quote: the A/D director must implement procedures that minimize the risk of unintended dangerous movement and minimize the duration and extent of exposure under the boom.
items.statement: When the § 1926.1404(f)(2) exception applies because site constraints require employees to be under the boom, jib, or other components during pin removal, the A/D director must implement procedures that minimize the duration and extent of exposure under the boom.

items.quote: To minimize the risk of unintended dangerous movement while the pins are removed, the A/D director uses an assist crane that is rigged to support the boom section that is being detached
items.statement: In the appendix's example of in-air boom disassembly with employees under the boom, the A/D director minimizes the risk of unintended dangerous movement during pin removal by using an assist crane rigged to support the boom section being detached.

items.quote: using particular care to ensure that the section end that is near the employee(s) removing the pins is well supported.
items.statement: In the appendix's in-air boom disassembly example, the A/D director uses particular care to ensure that the end of the detaching section near the employees removing the pins is well supported by the assist crane rigging.

items.quote: The duration and extent of exposure is minimized by removing the far side pins first
items.statement: In the appendix's example, where the aerial lift basket must go under the boom to reach the far side pins, exposure is minimized by removing the far side pins first.

items.quote: moving the aerial lift basket as soon as possible to the near side so that the employees are no longer under the boom
items.statement: In the appendix's example, after the far side pins are removed first, the aerial lift basket is moved to the near side as soon as possible so that employees are no longer under the boom.

items.quote: removing the far side pins first, moving the aerial lift basket as soon as possible to the near side so that the employees are no longer under the boom, and then removing the near side pins.
items.statement: In the appendix's example, the near side pins are removed after the far side pins have been removed and the aerial lift basket has been moved to the near side.

items.quote: during assembly/disassembly, the center of gravity of the load must be identified if that is necessary for the method used for maintaining stability.

items.quote: where there is insufficient information to accurately identify the center of gravity, measures designed to prevent unintended dangerous movement resulting from an inaccurate identification of the center of gravity must be used.
items.statement: Under § 1926.1404(h)(6)(ii), where there is insufficient information to accurately identify the center of gravity, measures designed to prevent unintended dangerous movement resulting from an inaccurate identification must be used.

items.quote: In this situation, before raising the section, all personnel are kept clear of the section
items.statement: In the appendix's example, where the A/D director cannot determine where to attach the assist crane hoist line above the center of gravity of the non-symmetrical top boom section, all personnel are kept clear of the section before it is raised.

items.quote: the section is first raised a few inches to determine whether it tips when raised
items.statement: In the appendix's unknown center of gravity example, the boom section is first raised a few inches to determine whether it tips.

items.quote: if it did tip, it would indicate it is not rigged over the center of gravity
items.statement: In the appendix's example, a boom section that tips when raised is indicated not to be rigged over its center of gravity.

items.quote: If this occurs, the hoist line is repositioned and the procedure repeated (with employees kept clear of the section while it is raised) until the A/D director determines that it is rigged over the center of gravity and can be moved into place without dangerous movement.
items.statement: In the appendix's example, if the section tips, the hoist line is repositioned and the test-raise procedure is repeated until the A/D director determines that the section is rigged over the center of gravity and can be moved into place without dangerous movement.

items.quote: the procedure repeated (with employees kept clear of the section while it is raised)
items.statement: In the appendix's example, employees are kept clear of the boom section while it is raised during each repeat of the test-raise procedure.
